# Roadmap: arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions

**Summary.** Build counting and averaging theorems for arithmetic families by passing from integral orbits to lattice counts, controlling the cusps, and then imposing local conditions with a uniform large-prime tail. The principal results are the Davenport–Heilbronn field and class-group means, their secondary terms, low-degree field asymptotics, and the Bhargava–Shankar mean of three for the size of the 2-Selmer group. Higher Selmer averages, twist-family consequences, random-group laws and function-field moments extend the same framework. Every result keeps its own height, equivalence relation, local specifications and weighting.

## Purpose and scope

A finite list of congruences gives a finite residue calculation. An arithmetic density requires more: finiteness of the height denominator, a fundamental-domain count with its multiplicities, and a bound uniform in the primes left out of the finite calculation. This roadmap builds that passage explicitly. It also separates probabilistic model theorems from conjectures that identify those models with arithmetic distributions.

The layers treat binary cubic and quartic forms, pairs of ternary quadratic forms, quintic rings and their resolvents, general symmetric pencils, squarefree discriminants, quadratic and low-degree field families, Selmer coverings, local masses and finite-group moments. Additional strands treat primitive hypersurface equations, finite-field abelian varieties, Picard-quotient bundle probabilities, and marked nonabelian extensions. Their source-specific denominators are part of the mathematics; they do not become a common quotient family merely because they share coefficient coordinates.

The roadmap does not prove every heuristic it formulates. Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet, Malle, Poonen–Rains and BKLPR arithmetic identifications are named conjectural propositions. The bad-type Wood ordinary-limit assertion is distinguished from the proved liminf bound. Conditional ppav statements retain the model-ring and polarization-growth assumptions. A supplied orbit dictionary is also distinguished from a pinned Lean declaration implementing it.

## Conventions

1. **Families and counts.** A family has a specified carrier, equivalence relation and height with finite sublevels. `N(S;X)` always refers to that stated carrier. Inclusive `H≤X` and strict `H<X` cutoffs are kept distinct. Empty finite denominators give zero finite ratios; a limiting mean must specify an inhabited sequence or eventual positive denominator. Embedded degree-n fields weight isomorphism classes by `n/#Aut`, while rigid extensions retain their labels.
2. **Coefficients and discriminants.** A binary degree-n form is `Σ a_i x^(n−i)y^i`. Its universal integral discriminant keeps degree n even when `a₀=0`. Dehomogenization agrees with the affine polynomial discriminant only with the exact-degree hypotheses. Layer 0 owns this universal object and strong/weak coefficient-perturbation loci; Layer 1 transports them to its orbit coordinates. The monic family perturbs only its free coefficients.
3. **Quartics and heights.** Ordinary binary-quartic coefficients give `I=12ae−3bd+c²`, `J=72ace+9bcd−27ad²−27eb²−2c³` and `27Δ=4I³−J²`. The quartic invariant height is `H′=max(|I|³,J²/4)`. For a minimal short model `y²=x³+Ax+B`, use `(I,J)=(−3A,−27B)`, `H_E=max(4|A|³,27B²)` and `27H_E=4H′`. Twisted and untwisted actions retain their stated determinant characters.
4. **Measures and local specifications.** Coefficient Haar measure assigns volume one to the integral lattice. Orbital measures have their separately stated Jacobian and Tamagawa normalization. A finite condition has its actual CRT residue density. A product of marginal densities is justified only by independent prime-power conditions. Infinite products require convergence and a uniform large-prime tail; convergence of the product alone gives no global density theorem.
5. **Groups and ranks.** Ordinary, narrow and relative class groups are distinct; relative means retain norm kernels and their base factors. Prime-power rank is the rank of p-torsion in the preceding power image. Selmer groups, reduced Selmer ranks, torsor Selmer sets, Mordell–Weil rank and p-infinity corank are kept separate. A locally soluble degree-one divisor class is weaker than a point.
6. **Characteristic and limits.** Projective root tests retain the odd-prime caveat. Characteristic-2/3 coefficient-height Weierstrass families are not silently replaced by minimal short models over Q. Function-field statements keep q, degree, infinity type and order of limits; liminf, limsup and ordinary limits are not interchanged.
7. **Names.** API names below are proposed library interfaces. The companion representative file uses the common root `TauCetiRoadmap.ArithmeticStatistics`, with `Coefficients`, `BinaryQuartic`, `Orbits`, `Counting`, `FieldStatistics`, `Selmer` and `Distributions` subnamespaces. Only definitions with native carriers and real bodies occur there; the full definition/API/Check specifications remain here.

## Sources and reading guide

The core route uses Bhargava–Shankar's binary-quartic paper (arXiv:1006.1002v3), Bhargava–Shankar–Tsimerman's Davenport–Heilbronn paper (arXiv:1005.0672), Bhargava's composition-law and quartic/quintic density papers, and Bhargava–Shankar–Wang's discriminant sieves. The distribution strands use Fouvry–Klüners, Ellenberg–Venkatesh–Westerland, Wood, Poonen–Rains, BKLPR and BKLOS. Bundle and finite-field comparisons use Shende–Tsimerman and Lipnowski–Tsimerman. Every target below carries theorem/section/page locators to the exact version in the bibliography.

The original Cohen–Lenstra, Davenport–Heilbronn and some descent/classical inputs have source-access or proof-interface gaps. Later public accounts do not certify an unread original argument. The explicit limitations below remain part of those targets. No source passage is reproduced here; formulas, theorem specifications and proof routes are stated in the roadmap's own language.

## Layer 0: Families, heights and measures

The height and the denominator are fixed before introducing any limiting statistic. Quotient families carry a Northcott obligation; a coefficient cube or a weighted monic box carries its own finite cardinality. The invariant pair interface connects binary quartics to the minimal elliptic-curve family, while the discriminant interface also covers forms whose root lies at infinity.

Three further coefficient regimes need their own carriers. Primitive hypersurface equations divide by the correct projective sign relation and use the source's real-root height. Hyperelliptic equation models keep fixed coordinates. Finite-field abelian varieties and principal polarizations use separate counting functions. The Picard quotient by the hyperelliptic pencil controls a joint bundle pushforward, with a parity carry; it is not an independent product law. Marked nonabelian extensions use a fixed embedded wreath type and a specified infinity completion.

**Worked checks.** The form `x⁴−y⁴` has `(I,J,Δ)=(−12,0,−256)`. The leading-zero cubic `xy(x−y)` still has binary discriminant 1; applying a degree-dropped affine discriminant would lose the fixed-degree convention. For `y²=x³−x`, `(I,J)=(3,0)` gives `H′=27` and `H_E=4`. The monic degree-zero polynomial is 1 and its weighted height is zero. These checks distinguish the coefficient conventions before any counting theorem is invoked.

The monic Euler product below is a local constant, not a global density. Its global use depends on Layer 2's tail and Layer 3's sieve theorem. The general monic order comparison, projective root criterion and hyperelliptic geometric adapter remain separately specified supplier obligations.

<a id="st0-arithmetic-family"></a>

### 0.1 Arithmetic families: objects up to equivalence, ordered by a Northcott height, with weighted and unweighted counting functions

An arithmetic family is a pair (ι, H) in which ι is a type of arithmetic objects already taken up to the family's equivalence relation — a quotient type Quotient s of a type of representatives by a setoid s (integral models up to change of variables, number fields up to ℚ-isomorphism) or an orbit type Γ\V = MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient Γ V of a group action (integral binary quartic forms up to GL₂(ℤ)) — and H : ι → ℝ is a height with Mathlib's Northcott property: {i : H(i) ≤ B} is finite for every real B. For a weight w : ι → M into an additive commutative monoid, the weighted counting function is N_H(w; X) := Σ_{H(i) ≤ X} w(i), a finite sum over heightLE X = {i : H(i) ≤ X}; the unweighted count of a subfamily S ⊆ ι is N_H(S; X) := #{i ∈ S : H(i) ≤ X} = N_H(1_S; X); the strict-cutoff count written by the sources is N_H^<(S; X) := #{i ∈ S : H(i) < X}. Constructions: ofQuotient, from a class-invariant height on representatives whose induced height is Northcott; comap along a map f : κ → ι with finite fibres (Northcott by Mathlib's Northcott.comp_of_finite_fibers), with the multiplicity formula N_{H∘f}(f⁻¹S; X) = N_H(#f⁻¹(·)·1_S; X), which is how an isomorphism multiplicity is made explicit; rescale by c > 0, with N_{cH}(S; X) = N_H(S; X/c); ofNat for a natural-valued Northcott height N, whose carrier heightLE is Tau Ceti's normLE N and whose weighted count is Tau Ceti's summatory N w; ofMulHeight, the elements of a number field ordered by Mathlib's multiplicative Weil height mulHeight₁ (Northcott by NumberField.finite_setOfPred_mulHeight₁_le). Proposed declaration: the structure ArithmeticFamily ι with fields height and northcott.

**Hypotheses.** The equivalence relation is built into the type ι: counts are counts of classes, never of representatives, unless comap is used with its explicit fibre multiplicities.; Heights are real-valued. A natural-valued height enters through ofNat and then agrees with Tau Ceti's normLE/summatory carrier, so Tau Ceti's counting lemmas apply unchanged.; The cutoff is inclusive (H(i) ≤ X), as in Tau Ceti's normLE. The strict cutoff H(i) < X of the sources is countLT; relative densities do not depend on the choice (ST.0/relative-density).

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:Northcott`; `mathlib:Northcott.comp_of_finite_fibers`; `mathlib:Filter.TendstoCofinite`; `mathlib:Set.ncard`; `mathlib:Height.mulHeight₁`; `mathlib:NumberField.finite_setOfPred_mulHeight₁_le`; `tauceti:TauCeti.normLE`; `tauceti:TauCeti.coe_normLE`; `tauceti:TauCeti.summatory`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), §2, paragraph after (6), printed p. 7. The counting function of an orbit family ordered by a height, with the strict cutoff; count and countLT of this node. [P/bhargava-threeisogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-threeisogeny-2019), §2, printed p. 2. A weighted count divided by an unweighted count over the same family ordered by a height: weightedCount and count.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticFamily.finite_height_le` (characterisation): {i : H(i) ≤ X} is finite for every real X.
- `ArithmeticFamily.heightLE` (data): The finset of members of height at most X (inclusive cutoff).
- `ArithmeticFamily.mem_heightLE` (simp): i ∈ heightLE X ↔ H(i) ≤ X.
- `ArithmeticFamily.weightedCount` (data): N_H(w; X) = Σ_{i ∈ heightLE X} w(i) for w : ι → M, M an additive commutative monoid.
- `ArithmeticFamily.count` (data): N_H(S; X) = #{i ∈ S : H(i) ≤ X} for a subfamily S ⊆ ι.
- `ArithmeticFamily.countLT` (data): The strict-cutoff count #{i ∈ S : H(i) < X}.
- `ArithmeticFamily.count_eq_weightedCount_indicator` (characterisation): N_H(S; X) = N_H(1_S; X) (as reals).
- `ArithmeticFamily.count_mono_set` (relation): S ⊆ T ⇒ N_H(S; X) ≤ N_H(T; X).
- `ArithmeticFamily.count_mono` (relation): X ≤ Y ⇒ N_H(S; X) ≤ N_H(S; Y).
- `ArithmeticFamily.count_union_of_disjoint` (simp): For disjoint S, T: N_H(S ∪ T; X) = N_H(S; X) + N_H(T; X).
- `ArithmeticFamily.count_eq_zero_of_lt` (simp): If every height is ≥ b and X < b then N_H(S; X) = 0.
- `ArithmeticFamily.tendsto_count_atTop` (characterisation): For infinite S, N_H(S; X) → ∞ as X → ∞.
- `ArithmeticFamily.countLT_le_count` (relation): N_H^<(S; X) ≤ N_H(S; X).
- `ArithmeticFamily.ofQuotient` (constructor): The family on Quotient s from an s-invariant height on representatives whose induced height is Northcott.
- `ArithmeticFamily.comap` (functoriality): Pull-back along f : κ → ι with finite fibres; height H ∘ f.
- `ArithmeticFamily.count_comap` (compatibility): Isomorphism multiplicity: N_{H∘f}(f⁻¹S; X) = Σ_{i ∈ S, H(i) ≤ X} #f⁻¹(i).
- `ArithmeticFamily.rescale` (functoriality): The family (ι, cH) for c > 0.
- `ArithmeticFamily.count_rescale` (simp): N_{cH}(S; X) = N_H(S; X/c).
- `ArithmeticFamily.ofNat` (constructor): The family of a natural-valued Northcott height N, heights (N i : ℝ).
- `ArithmeticFamily.heightLE_ofNat` (compatibility): The finite height sublevel set for ofNat N equals the imported TauCeti.normLE N X.
- `ArithmeticFamily.ofMulHeight` (example): The elements of a number field K ordered by Mathlib's mulHeight₁ (Northcott by NumberField.finite_setOfPred_mulHeight₁_le).
- `ArithmeticFamily.weightedCount_ofNat` (compatibility): The weighted count for a natural Northcott height equals the imported TauCeti.summatory N w X, with inclusive cutoff.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ArithmeticFamily.test_count_int` (computation): The integers ordered by |n| (a Northcott height) have count 7 at X = 3.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ArithmeticFamily.test_count_empty` (degenerate): For every family and every X, the count of the empty subfamily is 0.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ArithmeticFamily.test_not_northcott_abs_rat` (non-example): The function x ↦ |x| on ℚ is not Northcott, so the rationals ordered by absolute value are not an arithmetic family.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ArithmeticFamily.test_count_nat` (compatibility): For ℕ ordered by n (ofNat id) and X ≥ 0, the count of all members is ⌊X⌋₊ + 1, the cardinality of Tau Ceti's normLE id X.

**Proof route.**

1. heightLE X is the toFinset of the finite set {i : H(i) ≤ X} given by the northcott field; weightedCount is the finite sum over it and count is Set.ncard of {i ∈ S : H(i) ≤ X}.
2. count_eq_weightedCount_indicator, count_mono_set, count_mono, count_union_of_disjoint and count_eq_zero_of_lt are finite-set identities.
3. tendsto_count_atTop: an infinite S is not contained in any bounded-height set (those are finite), so its members have unbounded height and the monotone count tends to infinity.
4. comap is Northcott by mathlib:Northcott.comp_of_finite_fibers (the instance Filter.TendstoCofinite f is exactly finiteness of fibres); count_comap splits {k : f(k) ∈ S, H(f(k)) ≤ X} into the fibres over heightLE X.
5. rescale: {i : cH(i) ≤ B} = {i : H(i) ≤ B/c}. ofNat: {i : (N i : ℝ) ≤ B} ⊆ {i : N i ≤ ⌊B⌋₊}, finite by Northcott N; its heightLE has the members of tauceti:TauCeti.normLE (tauceti:TauCeti.coe_normLE), so weightedCount (ofNat N) w = tauceti:TauCeti.summatory N w.
6. ofMulHeight: the northcott field is mathlib:NumberField.finite_setOfPred_mulHeight₁_le.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The integers ordered by |n| have exactly 7 members of height at most 3.
- The rationals ordered by |x| are rejected: the absolute value of a representative is not Northcott. The same mistake in arithmetic form is ordering rational Weierstrass equations instead of ℚ-isomorphism classes (EllipticCurves Layer 8 records that bounded-height finiteness fails there).
- For ofNat N, weightedCount agrees with TauCeti.summatory N w at every X, so eventually_summatory_indicator_sub_eq and the Abel-summation interface of Tau Ceti apply to every natural-valued family.
- Representatives against classes: for the squareclass twist family of y² = x³ − x over ℚ the twist map has fibres {t, t + [−1]} (ST.0/isomorphism-multiplicity-of-the-twist-family), and count_comap records the factor 2 between counting squareclasses and counting isomorphism classes of twists.

**Consumers.** Bhargava–Shankar §2, (7), (10)–(11) — GL₂(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary quartic forms ordered by H form a family on MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient GL₂(ℤ) V_ℤ; N(S; X) is count and the weighted counts of Theorem 2.12 are weightedCount; Bhargava–Shankar §3, Theorem 3.1 and the proof of Theorem 3.19 — elliptic curves over ℚ ordered by H(E_{A,B}) (ST.0/elliptic-curves-over-q-ordered-by-height); the average of #S₂(E) is weightedCount divided by count; Burungale–Tian Theorem 1.2, Proposition 1.3, Theorems 3.3 and 3.5; BKLOS §2 — squareclasses t ∈ F×/F×² ordered by H(t), each counted once, and positive squarefree n ordered by n (ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family, ST.0/positive-squarefree-family-over-q); Bhargava–Shankar–Tsimerman Theorems 1 and 3 and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields — number fields up to isomorphism ordered by |Disc| (ST.0/number-fields-ordered-by-discriminant); ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4/average-size-of-the-2-selmer-group-is-three — the counts N(S; X), N_φ(S; X) of Theorems 2.11, 2.12, 2.21 and 3.19 are count and weightedCount of this carrier; extraction items PAPER-SKOROBOGATOV-SOFOS-23/2, PAPER-BROWNING-LEBOUDEC-SAWIN-23/family, PAPER-WOOD-19/11 (routed to ST.0) — coefficient-box families, families of embedded equations and discriminant slices are instances of ofQuotient and ofNat
