### 0.25 The eligible invariant pairs ordered by H(I, J), with the curve normalisation 27·H_E = 4·H′ (the binary-quartic invariant and height interface)

This interface packages ST.0's binary-quartic interface, consumed by ST.1–ST.4 and by AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.8: the invariants I, J with weights (det γ)⁴, (det γ)⁶ (ST.0/binary-quartic-invariants, ST.0/relative-invariance-of-i-and-j), the discriminant with 27Δ = 4I³ − J², equal to the polynomial discriminant (ST.0/quartic-discriminant-is-the-polynomial-discriminant), the height H(I, J) = max{|I|³, J²/4} (ST.0/binary-quartic-height), the eligible pairs characterised modulo 27 (ST.0/eligibility-criterion-modulo-27; nine translates of 9ℤ × 27ℤ, ST.0/eligible-pairs-are-nine-lattice-translates) and the normalisation to curves (ST.0/quartic-to-curve-height-normalisation). Definition: the arithmetic family eligibleFamily of eligible pairs (I, J) ∈ ℤ² ordered by H(I, J) (Northcott because H is Northcott on ℤ²), with the map ofCurve sending E_{A,B} (EllipticCurves Layer 8's minimal pair) to its eligible invariant pair (−3A, −27B), for which 27·H(E) = 4·H(ofCurve E). The sign of Δ(I, J) splits eligible pairs of nonzero discriminant into those counted by Proposition 2.10(a) (Δ > 0: forms with four or no real roots) and (b) (Δ < 0: two real roots). Proposed declarations: BinaryQuartic.eligibleFamily, BinaryQuartic.ofCurve.

**Hypotheses.** Eligible pairs include degenerate ones with 4I³ = J²: (0, 0) (the zero form) and (1, ±2) (x³y ∓ x²y² = x²y(x ∓ y), a double root); the three eligible pairs of height ≤ 1 are all of this kind. Counts in Theorem 1.8 restrict to (−1)^iΔ > 0.; The map ofCurve is not surjective: curve invariants lie in 3ℤ × 27ℤ.

<a id="st0-squareclass-height"></a>

### 0.26 The squareclass height H(t) = ∏_{ord_v(t) odd} N v on F×/F×²

Let F be a number field, O_F its ring of integers and t ∈ F×/F×² a squareclass (Tau Ceti's SquareClassGroup F). For a finite prime v (Mathlib's HeightOneSpectrum O_F) the parity of ord_v(u) for a representative u ∈ F× (Mathlib's valuationOfNeZero) depends only on t. The odd support of t is the finite set of v with ord_v(t) odd (finite by Tau Ceti's finite_setOfPred_valuation_ne_one), its support ideal is the squarefree integral ideal 𝔞(t) := ∏_{v odd} v, and the squareclass height is H(t) := ∏_{v : ord_v(t) odd} N v = N(𝔞(t)) ∈ ℕ (Ideal.absNorm). Properties: H(0) = 1 (trivial class); H(s + t)·g² = H(s)·H(t) with g = N(gcd(𝔞(s), 𝔞(t))) (the odd support of a product is the symmetric difference); H(t) = 1 iff every ord_v(t) is even, i.e. t lies in the Selmer group K(∅, 2) (Mathlib's selmerGroup with S = ∅, n = 2), which contains the classes of units and of generators of squares of ideals and is nontrivial in general; for F = ℚ the class of a squarefree integer n has H = |n|, so [1] and [−1] both have height 1 (BKLOS §2: 'the squareclasses of all squarefree integers of absolute value less than X'). H is not the norm of a representative and not the discriminant of F(√t). Proposed declarations: squareclassHeight, oddSupport, supportIdeal.

**Hypotheses.** F is a number field; only finite primes enter H (infinite places are local conditions, not height factors).; The height is defined on squareclasses; representatives are used only through parities of valuations.

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum`; `mathlib:IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuationOfNeZero`; `mathlib:Ideal.absNorm`; `mathlib:IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup`; `tauceti:TauCeti.SquareClassGroup`; `tauceti:TauCeti.squareClass`; `tauceti:TauCeti.squareClass_eq_iff_isSquare_mul`; `tauceti:IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.finite_setOfPred_valuation_ne_one`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-threeisogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-threeisogeny-2019), §2, printed p. 2 (author version). Verbatim the height. [P/bhargava-threeisogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-threeisogeny-2019), §2, printed p. 2. The rational case H([n]) = |n| for squarefree n. [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), Proposition 1.3, printed p. 2. The squareclasses of Proposition 1.3 are ordered by this height (the ordering is not printed there: ArithmeticStatistics/E105).

**API.**

- `oddSupport` (data): The finite primes at which a unit has odd valuation.
- `oddSupport_finite` (characterisation): The odd support is finite.
- `unitHeight` (data): ∏_{v ∈ oddSupport(u)} N v for a unit u.
- `squareclassHeight` (data): H(t), the unit height of any representative.
- `supportIdeal` (data): 𝔞(u) = ∏_{v ∈ oddSupport(u)} v.
- `squareclassHeight_mk` (simp): H([u]) = unitHeight(u).
- `squareclassHeight_zero` (simp): H(trivial class) = 1.
- `unitHeight_eq_absNorm_supportIdeal` (characterisation): unitHeight(u) = N(𝔞(u)).
- `squareclassHeight_add_mul_sq` (relation): H(s + t)·g² = H(s)·H(t) for g = N(gcd(𝔞(s), 𝔞(t))).
- `squareclassHeight_eq_one_iff` (characterisation): Height 1 iff all valuations even, i.e. the class lies in K(∅, 2).
- `squareclassHeight_rat` (example): Over ℚ, the class of a squarefree integer n has height |n|.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.test_squareclassHeight_rat_twelve` (computation): Over ℚ, H([12]) = 3.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.test_squareclassHeight_rat_neg_one` (degenerate): Over ℚ, H([−1]) = 1, as H([1]).
- `ArithmeticStatistics.test_squareclassHeight_not_disc` (non-example): Over ℚ, H([3]) = 3, not the discriminant 12 of ℚ(√3).

**Proof route.**

1. oddSupport is a subset of the finite set of v with ord_v(u) ≠ 0 (tauceti:IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.finite_setOfPred_valuation_ne_one).
2. Independence of the representative: u′ = u·w² changes every ord_v by an even number (valuationOfNeZero is a homomorphism; tauceti:TauCeti.squareClass_eq_iff_isSquare_mul).
3. squareclassHeight_add_mul_sq: the odd support of uu′ is the symmetric difference of the odd supports, and N is multiplicative on coprime products.
4. squareclassHeight_rat: for squarefree n the odd support is the set of primes dividing n, and N(pℤ) = p.

**Acceptance checks.**

- ℚ: H([12]) = 3, H([−1]) = 1, H([3]) = 3 (the discriminant of ℚ(√3) is 12).
- ℚ(i): K(∅, 2) = {[1], [i]} (−1 = i² is a square, the class number is 1) and [2] = [−i(1 + i)²] = [i] has height 1.

**Consumers.** Burungale–Tian Proposition 1.3 and Theorem 3.5 — the ordering of K×/(K×)² in 'at least 50%'; BKLOS §2, Theorems 2.1–2.7 — Σ(X) = {s ∈ Σ : H(s) < X} (ST.5 bklos-density); extraction item PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26/number-field-twist-height — is this definition, with bounded-height finiteness ST.0/finiteness-of-squareclasses-of-bounded-height; Part II CMRankZeroConverse (cm-twist-density, nondescent-density) — proportions of squareclasses of K ordered by H

<a id="st0-squareclass-height-fibres-are-selmer-cosets"></a>

### 0.27 Squareclasses with the same support ideal differ by an element of the Selmer group K(∅, 2)

For u, u′ ∈ F×: 𝔞(u) = 𝔞(u′) iff ord_v(u/u′) is even for every finite prime v, i.e. iff the class of u/u′ lies in the Selmer group K(∅, 2) = {x ∈ F×/F×² : ord_v(x) ≡ 0 (mod 2) for all v} (Mathlib's selmerGroup with S = ∅). Hence the fibres of t ↦ 𝔞(t) on F×/F×² are the cosets of K(∅, 2). Proposed declaration: supportIdeal_eq_iff.

**Hypotheses.** The squarefree ideal 𝔞(u) determines the odd support (unique factorisation of ideals).

**Dependencies.** [The squareclass height H(t) = ∏_{ord_v(t) odd} N v on F×/F×²](#st0-squareclass-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/squareclass-height`); `mathlib:IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup`; `mathlib:IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuationOfNeZeroMod`; `tauceti:IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuationOfNeZeroMod_mk_eq_one_iff`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-threeisogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-threeisogeny-2019), §2, printed p. 2. The height depends only on the odd support; this lemma identifies the classes sharing it.

**Proof route.**

1. 𝔞(u) = 𝔞(u′) iff the odd supports agree iff ord_v(u) ≡ ord_v(u′) (mod 2) for every v iff ord_v(u/u′) is even for every v.
2. Membership of the class of u/u′ in selmerGroup ∅ 2 is the vanishing of valuationOfNeZeroMod 2 at every v, which tauceti:IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuationOfNeZeroMod_mk_eq_one_iff turns into 2 | ord_v.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Over ℚ, K(∅, 2) = {[1], [−1]}, so each positive squarefree n and −n have the same support ideal.

<a id="st0-finiteness-of-squareclasses-of-bounded-height"></a>

### 0.28 Bounded-height finiteness for squareclasses of a number field

For every number field F the squareclass height is Northcott: {t ∈ F×/F×² : H(t) ≤ X} is finite for every X. Precisely, t ↦ 𝔞(t) maps onto the squarefree ideals whose class lies in Cl(F)², with fibres the cosets of K(∅, 2), so #{t : H(t) ≤ X} = #K(∅, 2)·#{squarefree 𝔞 : N𝔞 ≤ X, [𝔞] ∈ Cl(F)²} ≤ #K(∅, 2)·#{ideals of norm ≤ X}. Proposed declaration: northcott_squareclassHeight.

**Hypotheses.** The finiteness is for squareclasses under their height, not for representatives: each class has infinitely many representatives in F×.

**Dependencies.** [The squareclass height H(t) = ∏_{ord_v(t) odd} N v on F×/F×²](#st0-squareclass-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/squareclass-height`); [Squareclasses with the same support ideal differ by an element of the Selmer group K(∅, 2)](#st0-squareclass-height-fibres-are-selmer-cosets) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/squareclass-height-fibres-are-selmer-cosets`); [Arithmetic families: objects up to equivalence, ordered by a Northcott height, with weighted and unweighted counting functions](#st0-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/arithmetic-family`); `tauceti:IsDedekindDomain.finite_selmerGroup_of_numberField`; `tauceti:TauCeti.instNorthcottAbsNormNonZeroDivisors`; `mathlib:Ring.HasFiniteQuotients.finite_absNorm_le`; `mathlib:Northcott.comp_of_finite_fibers`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-threeisogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-threeisogeny-2019), §2, printed p. 2. The averages presuppose that Σ(X) is finite; this theorem supplies it.

**Proof route.**

1. K(∅, 2) is finite: tauceti:IsDedekindDomain.finite_selmerGroup_of_numberField (class number theorem and Dirichlet's unit theorem, via the exact sequence 1 → O_F×/O_F×² → K(∅, 2) → Cl(F)[2] → 0).
2. The fibres of t ↦ 𝔞(t) are cosets of K(∅, 2) (ST.0/squareclass-height-fibres-are-selmer-cosets), hence finite.
3. The absolute norm is Northcott on nonzero ideals (tauceti:TauCeti.instNorthcottAbsNormNonZeroDivisors, from mathlib:Ring.HasFiniteQuotients.finite_absNorm_le).
4. H = N ∘ 𝔞 is Northcott by mathlib:Northcott.comp_of_finite_fibers.
5. Image: (u) = 𝔞(u)·𝔟² for a fractional ideal 𝔟, so [𝔞(u)] = [𝔟]⁻² ∈ Cl²; conversely if 𝔞𝔟² = (u) then 𝔞(u) = 𝔞 for squarefree 𝔞.

**Acceptance checks.**

- F = ℚ: #{t : H(t) ≤ X} = 2·#{1 ≤ n ≤ X squarefree} ~ (12/π²)X.
- F = ℚ(i): K(∅, 2) = {[1], [i]}, so every squarefree ideal of norm ≤ X is 𝔞(t) for exactly two classes.

<a id="st0-quadratic-twist-squareclass-family"></a>

### 0.29 The unweighted squareclass-height family of quadratic twists E^(t), t ∈ F×/F×²

Let F be a number field and E : y² = x³ + Ax + B an elliptic curve over F in short form (Tau Ceti's shortCurve A B; every elliptic curve over F has one, Mathlib's exists_variableChange_isShortNF). For a squareclass t ∈ F×/F×² with representative u, the quadratic twist E^(t) is the class of the model u y² = x³ + Ax + B, equivalently E^(u) : y² = x³ + u²A x + u³B, modulo F-isomorphism (Mathlib's orbit type of the VariableChange action). It is well defined: replacing u by us² changes the model by the change of variables with u_C = s; the trivial class gives E; E^(u) is Tau Ceti's quadraticTwistOf 0 (−u) (the model y² = x³ + 16u²A x + 64u³B) after the change of variables with u_C = 2 (the inverse change u_C = 1/2 sends the standard twist to Tau Ceti’s model), and for u ∉ F×² it is F-isomorphic to Tau Ceti's quadraticTwist E F(√u) (exists_smul_quadraticTwist_eq with the generator √u, of trace 0 and norm −u); Δ(E^(u)) = u⁶Δ(E) and j(E^(u)) = j(E). The squareclass twist family of E is the arithmetic family (F×/F×², H) with H the squareclass height (ST.0/squareclass-height; Northcott by ST.0/finiteness-of-squareclasses-of-bounded-height), together with the twist map t ↦ [E^(t)]. It is unweighted: each squareclass is counted once, whatever the multiplicity of the twist map (ST.0/isomorphism-multiplicity-of-the-twist-family). Proportions of twists 'ordered by H(t)' (Burungale–Tian Proposition 1.3 and Theorem 3.5; BKLOS Theorems 2.1–2.7) are relative densities in this family, and its subfamilies defined by local conditions on F_v×/F_v×² are instances of ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions. Proposed declarations: twistModel, twistClass, twistFamily.

**Hypotheses.** F has characteristic 0, so the short model exists and the twist is elliptic exactly when E is (Δ(E^(u)) = u⁶Δ(E)).; The trivial class is included.; The family counts squareclasses. Distinct squareclasses yield isomorphic twists exactly when j = 1728 and −1 is nonsquare in F; in that case the two classes t and −t have the same image.; For F = ℚ the family is ordered by |n| for squarefree n of both signs; Burungale–Tian's congruent-number family is its positive part (ST.0/positive-squarefree-family-over-q).

**Dependencies.** [Arithmetic families: objects up to equivalence, ordered by a Northcott height, with weighted and unweighted counting functions](#st0-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/arithmetic-family`); [The squareclass height H(t) = ∏_{ord_v(t) odd} N v on F×/F×²](#st0-squareclass-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/squareclass-height`); [Bounded-height finiteness for squareclasses of a number field](#st0-finiteness-of-squareclasses-of-bounded-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/finiteness-of-squareclasses-of-bounded-height`); `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.shortCurve`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistOf`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.exists_smul_quadraticTwistOf_eq`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.exists_smul_eq_quadraticTwistOf_add_mul`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwist`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.exists_smul_quadraticTwist_eq`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.VariableChange`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.variableChange_a₄`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.variableChange_a₆`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.variableChange_j`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.Δ_of_isShortNF`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.exists_variableChange_isShortNF`; `mathlib:MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-threeisogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-threeisogeny-2019), §1, printed p. 1. Twists indexed by squareclasses with the model s̃y² = f(x). [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), §1.0.2, printed p. 2. Twists indexed by integers, i.e. by their squareclasses. [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), Proposition 1.3, printed p. 2. The family of twists over K indexed by squareclasses, counted once each.

**API.**

- `twistModel` (data): E^(u) : y² = x³ + u²A x + u³B.
- `twistClass` (data): t ↦ [E^(t)] ∈ F-isomorphism classes.
- `twistFamily` (constructor): The family (F×/F×², H) of twists.
- `twistModel_one` (simp): E^(1) = E.
- `twistClass_zero` (simp): The trivial class gives [E].
- `exists_smul_twistModel_mul_sq` (extensionality): E^(us²) ≅ E^(u) by the change of variables u_C = s.
- `twistModel_Δ` (simp): Δ(E^(u)) = u⁶Δ(E).
- `twistModel_j` (simp): j(E^(u)) = j(E).
- `exists_smul_twistModel_eq_quadraticTwistOf` (compatibility): E^(u) ≅ (16u²A, 64u³B), the value of Tau Ceti's quadraticTwistOf 0 (−u) on shortCurve A B.
- `twistModel_rat_congruent` (example): Over ℚ, the twist of y² = x³ − x by n is y² = x³ − n²x.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.test_twistFamily_height_zero` (degenerate): The trivial squareclass has height 1.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.test_twistModel_congruent_five` (computation): Over ℚ, the twist of y² = x³ − x by 5 is y² = x³ − 25x.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.test_twistModel_sq_iso` (characterisation): Over ℚ, the twist by 4 is isomorphic to E (a square class is trivial).

**Proof route.**

1. twistModel is the short curve with coefficients u²A, u³B; exists_smul_twistModel_mul_sq: the change of variables with u_C = s sends (u²s⁴A, u³s⁶B) to (u²A, u³B) (mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.variableChange_a₄, variableChange_a₆).
2. twistClass is the lift of u ↦ [twistModel u] to F×/F×², well defined by the previous step.
3. twistModel_Δ: mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.Δ_of_isShortNF gives −16(4u⁶A³ + 27u⁶B²); twistModel_j: j = 6912·a₄³/(4a₄³ + 27a₆²) is unchanged by (A, B) ↦ (u²A, u³B).
4. Compatibility with Tau Ceti's twist: tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistOf with (t, n) = (0, −u) gives (16u²A, 64u³B); the change of variables with u_C = 2 returns (u²A, u³B); tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.exists_smul_quadraticTwistOf_eq (generator change a = s, b = 0) and tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.exists_smul_eq_quadraticTwistOf_add_mul (the split case u = 1) give the same well-definedness on Tau Ceti's side; tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.exists_smul_quadraticTwist_eq with θ = √u (trace 0, norm −u) relates Tau Ceti's quadraticTwist E F(√u) to E^(u) for u ∉ F×².
5. twistFamily is the family of ST.0/finiteness-of-squareclasses-of-bounded-height.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Over ℚ, the twist of y² = x³ − x by 5 is y² = x³ − 25x, Burungale–Tian's E^(5) : 5y² = x³ − x.
- The twist by 4 = 2² is isomorphic to E; the trivial class has height 1.
- Over ℚ the classes of height ≤ X are the squareclasses of squarefree n with |n| ≤ X.

<a id="st0-isomorphism-multiplicity-of-the-twist-family"></a>

### 0.30 Isomorphism multiplicity of the twist map: injective unless j = 1728, fibres {t, t + [−1]} at j = 1728

Let F be a number field and E : y² = x³ + Ax + B with 4A³ + 27B² ≠ 0. (a) If B ≠ 0 (so j(E) ≠ 1728; j = 0 included), the twist map t ↦ [E^(t)] on F×/F×² is injective: E^(u) ≅_F E^(u′) iff u′/u ∈ F×². (b) If B = 0 (j = 1728), E^(−u) and E^(u) are the same model y² = x³ + u²A x, and E^(u) ≅_F E^(u′) iff u′/u ∈ ±F×²; so when −1 ∉ F×² every fibre of the twist map is {t, t + [−1]}, of size 2, and the unweighted squareclass count counts each isomorphism class of twists twice (count_comap of ST.0/arithmetic-family). In particular for y² = x³ − x over ℚ, E^(n) = E^(−n), which is why Burungale–Tian index their family by positive squarefree n. Proposed declaration: twistClass_injective_or_neg.

**Hypotheses.** Characteristic 0 (a number field): short models and the shape of changes of variables between them use 2, 3 invertible.

**Dependencies.** [The unweighted squareclass-height family of quadratic twists E^(t), t ∈ F×/F×²](#st0-quadratic-twist-squareclass-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family`); [Arithmetic families: objects up to equivalence, ordered by a Northcott height, with weighted and unweighted counting functions](#st0-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/arithmetic-family`); `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.variableChange_a₁`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.variableChange_a₂`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.variableChange_a₃`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.variableChange_a₄`; `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.variableChange_a₆`; `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.not_exists_smul_quadraticTwist_eq`

**Sources.** [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), Abstract, printed p. 1. The congruent-number family is indexed by positive n; E^(n) and E^(−n) coincide, which this lemma makes explicit.

**Proof route.**

1. A change of variables between two short models over F has s = r = t = 0: a₁′ = u_C⁻¹·2s, then a₂′ = u_C⁻²·3r and a₃′ = u_C⁻³·2t must vanish (mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.variableChange_a₁, variableChange_a₂, variableChange_a₃); then (a₄′, a₆′) = (u_C⁻⁴a₄, u_C⁻⁶a₆) (variableChange_a₄, variableChange_a₆).
2. So E^(u) ≅ E^(u′) iff there is w ∈ F× with u′²A = w⁴u²A and u′³B = w⁶u³B. Let q = u′/u. If A, B ≠ 0: q² = w⁴ and q³ = w⁶ give q = q³/q² = w² ∈ F×². If A = 0 (then B ≠ 0): q³ = w⁶ gives q = ζw² with ζ³ = 1, and ζ = (ζ²)² is a square. If B = 0 (then A ≠ 0): q² = w⁴ gives q = ±w².
3. Conversely q = w² (and, when B = 0, q = −w²) gives the isomorphism with u_C = w⁻¹.
4. Cross-check (not needed for the proof): Tau Ceti's tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.not_exists_smul_quadraticTwist_eq says that for j ∉ {0, 1728} a twist by a nontrivial quadratic extension is not F-isomorphic to E.

**Acceptance checks.**

- y² = x³ − x over ℚ: E^(n) = E^(−n) = y² = x³ − n²x; over ℚ(i) (−1 a square) the twist map is injective.
- y² = x³ + 1 (j = 0) over ℚ: E^(u) ≅ E^(u′) only for u′/u ∈ ℚ×², although Aut(E over ℚ̄) has order 6.

<a id="st0-positive-squarefree-family-over-q"></a>

### 0.31 The positive squarefree integers ordered by n, and Burungale–Tian's subfamily n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8)

Over ℚ, squareclasses correspond to squarefree integers n ↦ [n], with H([n]) = |n| (ST.0/squareclass-height). Burungale–Tian's families are P, the positive squarefree integers ordered by n — the squareclasses of ℚ positive at the real place (local condition Σ_∞ = {+1} ⊂ ℝ×/ℝ×²) — and S ⊆ P, the positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8): the squareclasses with Σ_∞ = {+1} and Σ_2 = {[1], [3], [2], [10]} ⊂ ℚ₂×/ℚ₂×² (for squarefree n the class of n in ℚ₂×/ℚ₂×² determines n mod 8 when n is odd and n/2 mod 8 when n is even, and n ≡ 2 (mod 8) iff n/2 ≡ 1 or 5 (mod 8)). Both are ordered by n with the cutoff n ≤ X (Burungale–Tian's S(X) = {0 < n ≤ X}), realised as subsets of ℕ in the family natFamily = (ℕ, n); 'density one in this family' is HasDensity A S 1 (ST.0/relative-density). No positive squarefree n is ≡ 0 or 4 (mod 8). S is the family of positive squarefree n for which the twist E^(n) of y² = x³ − x has root number +1 (Burungale–Tian footnote 2, from Birch–Stephens; RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0 owns that computation). Proposed declarations: SquarefreeFamily.natFamily, posSquarefree, evenParityClasses.

**Hypotheses.** Positive n only: the class [−n] gives the same curve (ST.0/isomorphism-multiplicity-of-the-twist-family) and is excluded, not identified.; The ordering is by n, not by the fundamental discriminant (n or 4n); the comparison is ST.0/piecewise-rescaling-of-a-height.

**Dependencies.** [Arithmetic families: objects up to equivalence, ordered by a Northcott height, with weighted and unweighted counting functions](#st0-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/arithmetic-family`); [Families defined by local conditions, local densities and largeness](#st0-family-defined-by-local-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions`); [The squareclass height H(t) = ∏_{ord_v(t) odd} N v on F×/F×²](#st0-squareclass-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/squareclass-height`); `mathlib:Squarefree`

**Sources.** [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), Theorem 3.3, printed p. 6. The family S and 'density one' within it. [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), Footnote 2, printed p. 2. Why the classes 1, 2, 3 mod 8 (for positive squarefree n; see PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26/E9).

**API.**

- `SquarefreeFamily.natFamily` (constructor): ℕ ordered by n.
- `SquarefreeFamily.posSquarefree` (data): P = {n > 0 squarefree}.
- `SquarefreeFamily.evenParityClasses` (data): S = {n ∈ P : n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8)}.
- `SquarefreeFamily.evenParityClasses_subset` (relation): S ⊆ P.
- `SquarefreeFamily.posSquarefree_mod_eight` (relation): n ∈ P ⇒ n ≢ 0, 4 (mod 8).
- `SquarefreeFamily.posSquarefree_infinite` (relation): P is infinite.
- `SquarefreeFamily.unitHeight_posSquarefree` (compatibility): For n ∈ P the squareclass height of [n] is n.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.SquarefreeFamily.test_evenParity_members` (computation): 1, 2, 11 ∈ S and 5, 9 ∉ S.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.SquarefreeFamily.test_count_evenParity_twenty` (computation): S has 7 members up to 20.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.SquarefreeFamily.test_count_posSquarefree_one` (non-example): Only n = 1 has height ≤ 1 in P: the class [−1], also of height 1, is not in the positive family.

**Proof route.**

1. natFamily is ofNat id; posSquarefree and evenParityClasses are subsets of ℕ; evenParityClasses_subset and posSquarefree_mod_eight (4 | n contradicts squarefreeness) are immediate.
2. posSquarefree_infinite: the primes are squarefree.
3. unitHeight_posSquarefree: ST.0/squareclass-height (squareclassHeight_rat).
4. The local description at 2: ℚ₂×/ℚ₂×² is represented by ±1, ±3, ±2, ±6 (unit classes mod 8 times {1, 2}); for n odd, [n] = [n mod 8]; for n = 2m, [n] = [2]·[m mod 8].

**Acceptance checks.**

- The members up to 20 are 1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 17, 19 (7 of the 13 positive squarefree n ≤ 20).
- [−1] has height 1 but is not in P.

<a id="st0-squarefree-indicator-as-a-moebius-sum"></a>

### 0.32 The squarefree indicator as a Möbius sum over square divisors

For every integer n ≥ 1, Σ_{d ≥ 1, d² | n} μ(d) = 1 if n is squarefree and 0 otherwise. Proposed declaration: SquarefreeFamily.sum_moebius_sq_dvd.

**Hypotheses.** n ≥ 1.

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius`; `mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius_mul_coe_zeta`; `mathlib:exists_sq_mul_squarefree`; `mathlib:Squarefree`

**Sources.** [P/nunes-squarefree-2015](#source-p-nunes-squarefree-2015), §1, (1.1), printed p. 1 (arXiv v2). The count of squarefree integers is the sum of µ² = the squarefree indicator, which this identity expands.

**Proof route.**

1. Write n = b²m with m squarefree (mathlib:exists_sq_mul_squarefree).
2. d² | n iff d | b: if p^(2k) | b²m with m squarefree then p^k | b (compare p-adic valuations, v_p(m) ≤ 1).
3. Σ_{d | b} μ(d) = [b = 1] (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius_mul_coe_zeta), and b = 1 iff n is squarefree.

**Acceptance checks.**

- n = 12 = 2²·3: the divisors d with d² | 12 are 1, 2 and μ(1) + μ(2) = 0.

<a id="st0-squarefree-integers-in-residue-classes"></a>

### 0.33 Squarefree integers in a coprime residue class: (6/π²)·q⁻¹·∏_{p|q}(1 − p⁻²)⁻¹·X + O_q(√X)

For integers q ≥ 1 and a with gcd(a, q) = 1 there is C_q such that for all X ≥ 1: |#{1 ≤ n ≤ X : n squarefree, n ≡ a (mod q)} − (6/π²)·q⁻¹·∏_{p | q}(1 − p⁻²)⁻¹·X| ≤ C_q·√X. Proposed declaration: SquarefreeFamily.squarefree_residue_count.

**Hypotheses.** q is fixed (the constant depends on q; Hooley's bound O((X/q)^(1/2) + q^(1/2+ε)) is uniform but not needed here).; gcd(a, q) = 1; non-coprime classes reduce to coprime ones by factoring out the common part (for q = 8, a = 2: n = 2m with m ≡ 1 (mod 4)).

**Dependencies.** [The squarefree indicator as a Möbius sum over square divisors](#st0-squarefree-indicator-as-a-moebius-sum) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/squarefree-indicator-as-a-moebius-sum`); [The positive squarefree integers ordered by n, and Burungale–Tian's subfamily n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8)](#st0-positive-squarefree-family-over-q) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/positive-squarefree-family-over-q`); [Arithmetic families: objects up to equivalence, ordered by a Northcott height, with weighted and unweighted counting functions](#st0-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/arithmetic-family`); `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LSeries.mul_mu_eq_one`; `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LFunction_eq_LSeries`; `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LFunctionTrivChar_eq_mul_riemannZeta`; `mathlib:riemannZeta_two`

**Sources.** [P/nunes-squarefree-2015](#source-p-nunes-squarefree-2015), §1, (1.1), printed p. 1 (arXiv v2). The main term of this lemma. [P/nunes-squarefree-2015](#source-p-nunes-squarefree-2015), §1, (1.3), printed p. 1. The error term; for fixed q it is O(√X), which the elementary argument above also gives.

**Proof route.**

1. By ST.0/squarefree-indicator-as-a-moebius-sum the count is Σ_{d ≤ √X} μ(d)·#{n ≤ X : d² | n, n ≡ a (mod q)}.
2. If gcd(d, q) > 1 the inner set is empty (d² | n and gcd(n, q) = 1 force gcd(d, q) = 1); otherwise it is one residue class modulo qd² and has X/(qd²) + θ elements with |θ| ≤ 1.
3. Hence the count is (X/q)·Σ_{d ≤ √X, (d,q)=1} μ(d)d⁻² + O(√X), and the tail Σ_{d > √X} d⁻² ≤ 2/√X costs another O(√X).
4. Σ_{d ≥ 1, (d,q)=1} μ(d)d⁻² = L(χ₀μ, 2) = 1/L(χ₀, 2) for the trivial Dirichlet character χ₀ mod q (mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LSeries.mul_mu_eq_one and mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LFunction_eq_LSeries at s = 2), and L(χ₀, 2) = ∏_{p|q}(1 − p⁻²)·ζ(2) (mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LFunctionTrivChar_eq_mul_riemannZeta) with ζ(2) = π²/6 (mathlib:riemannZeta_two).

**Acceptance checks.**

- q = 8: each odd class has main term (6/π²)(1/8)(4/3)X = X/π².
- q = 1: 6X/π² + O(√X).
- Numerically to 2·10⁶ the classes 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 (mod 8) each contain (1.000 ± 0.001)·X/π² squarefree integers.

<a id="st0-even-parity-classes-have-half-density"></a>

### 0.34 The classes n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8) have relative density 1/2 among positive squarefree integers

Among the positive squarefree integers ordered by n, Burungale–Tian's family S of n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8) has relative density 1/2: #{n ≤ X : n ∈ S}/#{n ≤ X : n ∈ P} → 1/2. Proposed declaration: SquarefreeFamily.hasDensity_evenParityClasses.

**Hypotheses.** The six squarefree classes modulo 8 (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7) have equal density 1/6; the eight residue classes do not (0 and 4 contain no squarefree integer).

**Dependencies.** [Squarefree integers in a coprime residue class: (6/π²)·q⁻¹·∏_{p|q}(1 − p⁻²)⁻¹·X + O_q(√X)](#st0-squarefree-integers-in-residue-classes) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/squarefree-integers-in-residue-classes`); [The positive squarefree integers ordered by n, and Burungale–Tian's subfamily n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8)](#st0-positive-squarefree-family-over-q) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/positive-squarefree-family-over-q`); [Upper, lower and limiting relative densities of a subfamily in a height-ordered family](#st0-relative-density) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/relative-density`)

**Sources.** [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), Abstract and Theorem 1.2, printed pp. 1–2. The comparison between the density-one statement in S and the abstract's 50% of all positive squarefree n rests on this density.

**Proof route.**

1. Classes 1 and 3 (mod 8): ST.0/squarefree-integers-in-residue-classes with q = 8 gives X/π² + O(√X) each.
2. Class 2 (mod 8): n = 2m with m squarefree and m ≡ 1 (mod 4); the count is #{m ≤ X/2 : m squarefree, m ≡ 1 (mod 4)} = (6/π²)(1/4)(4/3)(X/2) + O(√X) = X/π² + O(√X) (q = 4).
3. So #S(X) = 3X/π² + O(√X), while #P(X) = 6X/π² + O(√X) (q = 1); the ratio tends to 1/2 (ST.0/relative-density).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Up to 20: 7 members of S among 13 positive squarefree integers; to 2·10⁶ the proportion is 0.49999.
- Counting all eight residue classes with equal weight would give 3/8, the wrong answer.

<a id="st0-density-one-in-the-even-parity-classes-is-half-of-all-squarefree"></a>

### 0.35 A density-one subset of the even-parity classes has density 1/2 among all positive squarefree integers

If A ⊆ S has relative density one in S (positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8), ordered by n), then A has relative density 1/2 in the positive squarefree integers P. Proposed declaration: SquarefreeFamily.hasDensity_half_of_hasDensity_one.

**Hypotheses.** A ⊆ S; the conclusion is an exact limit 1/2, not a lower bound.

**Dependencies.** [The classes n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8) have relative density 1/2 among positive squarefree integers](#st0-even-parity-classes-have-half-density) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/even-parity-classes-have-half-density`); [Relative densities multiply along a tower of subfamilies](#st0-relative-density-is-multiplicative-in-towers) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/relative-density-is-multiplicative-in-towers`)

**Sources.** [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), Abstract, printed p. 1. The proportion 50% in P follows from density one in S by this lemma.

**Proof route.**

1. ST.0/relative-density-is-multiplicative-in-towers with S ⊆ P, α = 1 and β = 1/2 (ST.0/even-parity-classes-have-half-density).

**Acceptance checks.**

- This is the passage from Burungale–Tian's Theorem 1.2 (density one in S) to the '50% of the positive square-free integers' of their abstract, for the set of n with analytic rank zero; the complementary statement (analytic rank nonzero on P ∖ S, by root number −1) is the consumer's (Part II CMRankZeroConverse, goldfeld, with RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0).

<a id="st0-number-fields-ordered-by-discriminant"></a>

### 0.36 Number fields ordered by |Disc|: embedded fields, isomorphism classes, degree and automorphism weights

Fix a field A of characteristic 0 (an algebraic closure of ℚ for counting). The embedded number fields are the intermediate fields ℚ ⊆ K ⊆ A that are finite-dimensional over ℚ; ordered by |Disc(K)| they form an arithmetic family (embeddedFamily), Northcott by Hermite's theorem (Mathlib's NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd; Tau Ceti's explicit bound NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le). ℚ-isomorphism is an equivalence relation on embedded fields (isoSetoid); its classes ordered by |Disc| form the family of number fields up to isomorphism (isoFamily; Northcott because each class of bounded discriminant has a representative among the finitely many embedded fields of bounded discriminant). A class carries its degree n = [K : ℚ] (isoDegree) and its automorphism weight w(K) := n/#Aut(K/ℚ) (autWeight). This is the convention of Bhargava–Shankar–Tsimerman's Theorems 1 and 3 ('cubic fields K, up to isomorphism') and of the Davenport–Heilbronn count at ST.3. Proposed declarations: NumberFieldFamily.embeddedFamily, isoFamily, autWeight.

**Hypotheses.** The counted objects are isomorphism classes; embedded subfields of ℚ̄ are counted with multiplicity n/#Aut(K) (ST.0/embedded-and-isomorphism-class-counts-of-number-fields).; The discriminant is Mathlib's NumberField.discr of the ring of integers, an isomorphism invariant.; Restricting further by the Galois group of the normal closure (as in N_n(G, X)) is not part of this node.

**Dependencies.** [Arithmetic families: objects up to equivalence, ordered by a Northcott height, with weighted and unweighted counting functions](#st0-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/arithmetic-family`); `mathlib:IntermediateField`; `mathlib:NumberField.discr`; `mathlib:NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd`; `tauceti:NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Theorem 1 (Davenport–Heilbronn), printed p. 1 (arXiv v3). Fields counted up to isomorphism, ordered by discriminant. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), §1.2, printed p. 3. The objects of the classical counts are isomorphism classes.

**API.**

- `NumberFieldFamily.Embedded` (data): Finite-dimensional intermediate fields ℚ ⊆ K ⊆ A.
- `NumberFieldFamily.embeddedFamily` (constructor): Embedded number fields ordered by |Disc|.
- `NumberFieldFamily.isoSetoid` (relation): ℚ-isomorphism of embedded fields.
- `NumberFieldFamily.isoFamily` (constructor): Number fields up to isomorphism ordered by |Disc|.
- `NumberFieldFamily.degree` (data): The degree-n subfamily of embedded fields.
- `NumberFieldFamily.isoDegree` (data): The degree of an isomorphism class.
- `NumberFieldFamily.autWeight` (data): w(K) = [K : ℚ]/#Aut(K/ℚ).

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.NumberFieldFamily.test_rat_discr` (degenerate): The bottom field ℚ has height 1.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.NumberFieldFamily.test_autWeight_galois` (computation): A Galois field of degree n ≥ 1 has automorphism weight 1.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.NumberFieldFamily.test_autWeight_noncyclic_cubic` (non-example): A cubic field with trivial automorphism group has weight 3, not 1: counting embedded cubic fields is not counting isomorphism classes.

**Proof route.**

1. embeddedFamily: height K ↦ |discr K|, northcott from mathlib:NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd (monotone in the bound).
2. isoSetoid: AlgEquiv is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; isoFamily's height is well defined since isomorphic fields have equal discriminants.
3. isoFamily is Northcott: every class of height ≤ X contains an embedded field of height ≤ X, and there are finitely many of those.
4. autWeight and isoDegree are well defined: isomorphic fields have the same degree and isomorphic automorphism groups.

**Acceptance checks.**

- ℚ has height 1; a Galois field of degree n has weight 1; a cubic field with trivial automorphism group has weight 3.
- Bhargava–Shankar–Tsimerman Theorem 1: N₃(0, X) counts totally real cubic fields up to isomorphism with 0 < Disc < X.

**Consumers.** ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields and Bhargava–Shankar–Tsimerman Theorems 1 and 3 — cubic fields up to isomorphism ordered by |Disc|, split by signature; ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/quoted-classical-counts-for-binary-quadratic-and-cubic-forms — orders in cubic fields up to isomorphism (Delone–Faddeev, ST.1); extraction item PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-TANIGUCHI-ETAL-20/field-count-carrier (routed to ST.0) — N_n(G, X) counts ℚ-isomorphism classes of degree-n fields; the degree and isomorphism conventions are this node's, the Galois-group restriction is listed as remaining

<a id="st0-embedded-and-isomorphism-class-counts-of-number-fields"></a>

### 0.37 Counting embedded degree-n fields is counting isomorphism classes with weight n/#Aut(K)

Let A be algebraically closed of characteristic 0. For every n and X: #{embedded K ⊆ A : [K : ℚ] = n, |Disc(K)| ≤ X} = Σ_{[K] : [K : ℚ] = n, |Disc(K)| ≤ X} n/#Aut(K/ℚ). Equivalently, each isomorphism class of degree n has exactly n/#Aut(K) embedded representatives. Proposed declaration: NumberFieldFamily.count_degree_eq_weightedCount.

**Hypotheses.** A algebraically closed (so every degree-n field has exactly n embeddings into A).

**Dependencies.** [Number fields ordered by |Disc|: embedded fields, isomorphism classes, degree and automorphism weights](#st0-number-fields-ordered-by-discriminant) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/number-fields-ordered-by-discriminant`); [Arithmetic families: objects up to equivalence, ordered by a Northcott height, with weighted and unweighted counting functions](#st0-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/arithmetic-family`); `mathlib:AlgHom.card`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Theorem 3, printed p. 2 (arXiv v3). Counts are of isomorphism classes; Mathlib's Hermite finiteness is for embedded fields, and this lemma converts.

**Proof route.**

1. The ℚ-embeddings K → A number n (mathlib:AlgHom.card).
2. Aut(K/ℚ) acts freely on Hom(K, A) by precomposition, and two embeddings have the same image iff they differ by an automorphism; so the embedded copies of K, the images, number n/#Aut(K).
3. Sum over the classes of bounded discriminant (the discriminant is an isomorphism invariant) using count_comap of ST.0/arithmetic-family for the map from embedded fields to classes.

**Acceptance checks.**

- A non-Galois cubic field has three embedded copies in ℚ̄, a cyclic cubic field one: counting subfields of ℚ̄ weights S₃-cubic fields by 3.
- Degree 2: every quadratic field is Galois, so embedded and isomorphism-class counts agree.

<a id="st0-coefficient-box"></a>

### 0.38 Integral coefficient boxes

For n≥0 use integral vectors a∈Z^(n+1), representing Σ a_i x^(n−i)y^i. H_box(a)=max_i |a_i| is natural valued and Northcott. The inclusive box has (2B+1)^(n+1) elements at natural cutoff B; it counts vectors, without quotienting by a change-of-variables group.

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:Northcott`; `tauceti:TauCeti.normLE`

**Sources.** [S0/bsw25-published](#source-s0-bsw25-published), §1 p.1, height convention. Coefficient maximum and fixed-degree integral models.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.boxHeight_le` (characterisation): H_box(a)≤B iff every coordinate has absolute value at most B.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.boxHeight_northcott` (instance): The maximum height on a fixed finite coefficient vector is Northcott.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.boxHeight_count` (characterisation): The inclusive box has (2B+1)^m vectors.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.boxHeight_neg` (characterisation): Changing all signs preserves height.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.box_test_three` (computation): A single integer has seven choices in the box of height 3.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.box_test_zero` (degenerate): Only the zero vector has height 0.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.box_test_negative_cutoff` (compatibility): The native real-cutoff carrier is empty below zero.

**Proof route.**

1. Bound each coordinate in the finite integer interval [−B,B]. The box is their Cartesian product. Apply the parent ofNat adapter; do not reuse weighted monic height.

**Acceptance checks.**

- A single integer has seven choices in the box of height 3.
- Only the zero vector has height 0.
- The native real-cutoff carrier is empty below zero.

**Consumers.** BSW II Theorems 1–2 — Select the coefficient box before the sieve.

<a id="st0-monic-weighted-height"></a>

### 0.39 Weighted height of monic polynomials

For a=(a₁,…,a_n) define f_a=x^n+Σ_{i=1}^n a_i x^(n−i) and H_w(a)=max_i |a_i|^(1/i), with the maximum of the empty vector 0. For X≥0, H_w≤X iff |a_i|≤X^i. Thus the inclusive count is ∏_{i=1}^n(2⌊X^i⌋+1), and the strict count for n≥1 is 2^n X^(n(n+1)/2)+O_n(X^(n(n+1)/2−1)). This ordering is not the coefficient maximum used by ABZ.

**Hypotheses.** Nonnegative X in the coordinate and floor formulas; n≥1 in the stated asymptotic.

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:Northcott`; `mathlib:Polynomial.discr`; [Integral coefficient boxes](#st0-coefficient-box) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/coefficient-box`)

**Sources.** [S0/bsw22](#source-s0-bsw22), §1 p.1, definition of H and first counting display. Weighted coordinate box for monic polynomials.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.weightedHeight` (data): The maximum of |a_i|^(1/(i+1)); empty maximum 0.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.weightedHeight_le` (characterisation): At X≥0, the height bound is equivalent to all weighted coefficient bounds.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.weightedHeight_northcott` (instance): The weighted height is Northcott.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.monicPolynomial_monic` (characterisation): The constructed polynomial is monic of degree n.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.weighted_test_quadratic` (computation): x²+4 has weighted height 2, though its coefficient maximum is 4.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.weighted_test_unit_box` (computation): At cutoff 1 the degree-two monic family has nine elements.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.weighted_test_degree_zero` (degenerate): The degree-zero polynomial is 1 and its coefficient height is 0.

**Proof route.**

1. Construct f_a from the finite coefficient tuple. Real roots of the nonnegative absolute values give the height. Monotonicity of powers converts sublevel sets to anisotropic integer boxes; multiply interval counts. The strict-cutoff asymptotic follows by expanding the product.

**Acceptance checks.**

- x²+4 has weighted height 2, though its coefficient maximum is 4.
- At cutoff 1 the degree-two monic family has nine elements.
- The degree-zero polynomial is 1 and its coefficient height is 0.

**Consumers.** BSW I Theorems 1.1–1.2 — Fix the anisotropic family and its denominator.

<a id="st0-binary-discriminant"></a>

### 0.40 Fixed-degree binary discriminant

For n≥2 the universal binary discriminant D_n∈Z[a₀,…,a_n] is the integral homogeneous polynomial of degree 2n−2 agreeing with Disc(Σ a_i x^(n−i)) when a₀ is invertible and the polynomial has degree n. Evaluation defines Δ_n over every commutative ring, including a₀=0. At n=0,1 use Δ_n=1. Its covariance under γ∈GL₂ is det(γ)^(n(n−1)), and Δ_{n+1}(xf)=Δ_n(f) f(0,1)². A leading-zero vector must never be evaluated with the discriminant of its lower-degree affine polynomial.

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:Polynomial.discr`

**Sources.** [S0/bsw25-published](#source-s0-bsw25-published), §1 pp.1–2 and Appendix A p.53. Binary discriminant and the root at infinity.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binaryDisc` (data): Evaluate the universal integral invariant in an arbitrary coefficient ring.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binaryDisc_monic` (compatibility): For leading coefficient 1, binary discriminant agrees with Mathlib polynomial discriminant.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binaryDisc_map` (functoriality): Evaluation commutes with every ring homomorphism.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binaryDisc_scale` (characterisation): Scalar multiplication contributes c^(2n−2) for n≥2.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binaryDisc_add_root` (characterisation): Multiplication by x adds the root (0:1) and contributes the square of f(0,1).

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binary_test_quadratic` (computation): The quadratic vector (a,b,c) has discriminant b²−4ac.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binary_test_infinity` (computation): The binary quadratic xy has discriminant 1 although its leading coefficient is zero.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binary_test_double_root` (non-example): The binary quadratic y² has a repeated projective root and discriminant zero.

**Proof route.**

1. Construct the universal polynomial through the resultant of the universal polynomial and its derivative, cancel the leading coefficient integrally, and prove base change. The root-product identity on the generic coefficient ring gives homogeneity, covariance and the added-root formula; injectivity into its fraction field extends them across the leading-zero locus.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The quadratic vector (a,b,c) has discriminant b²−4ac.
- The binary quadratic xy has discriminant 1 although its leading coefficient is zero.
- The binary quadratic y² has a repeated projective root and discriminant zero.

**Consumers.** BSW II Proposition A.1 — Retain degree when sorting roots at infinity.; BGW §2 — Use the fixed-degree invariant in the model family.

<a id="st0-binary-local-proportion"></a>

### 0.41 Finite binary squarefree-discriminant proportion

For n≥2 and prime p, α_n(p) is the fraction of all (n+1)-tuples modulo p² whose fixed-degree binary discriminant is nonzero modulo p². All tuples are included, including zero and leading-zero reductions. This finite count equals normalized Haar measure on Zp^(n+1).

**Dependencies.** [Fixed-degree binary discriminant](#st0-binary-discriminant) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/binary-discriminant`); `mathlib:ZMod`; `mathlib:Fintype.card`

**Sources.** [S0/bsw25-published](#source-s0-bsw25-published), Appendix A, Proposition A.1 pp.53–54. Coefficient-space local density for all binary forms.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binaryLocalProportion_nonneg` (characterisation): The proportion is nonnegative.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binaryLocalProportion_le_one` (characterisation): For p positive the proportion is at most one.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binaryLocalProportion_lift` (compatibility): The numerator agrees with integer representatives satisfying p²∤Δ.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.alpha_test_two_two` (computation): Binary quadratics at 2 have density 1/2.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.alpha_test_three_two` (computation): Binary cubics at 2 have density 3/8.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.alpha_test_four_three` (computation): Binary quartics at 3 have density 176/243.

**Proof route.**

1. Evaluate the universal discriminant directly in Z/p²Z. Count its nonzero locus and divide by p^(2n+2). Modulus invariance identifies this with the p-adic cylinder.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Binary quadratics at 2 have density 1/2.
- Binary cubics at 2 have density 3/8.
- Binary quartics at 3 have density 176/243.

**Consumers.** BSW II squarefree sieve — Supply the local factor; this definition does not prove an infinite-prime sieve.

<a id="st0-monic-local-proportions"></a>

### 0.42 Finite monic discriminant probabilities

For n≥0, prime p and j≥0, ν_j(n,p) is the fraction of monic coefficient vectors modulo p^(j+1) for which p^j divides the integral discriminant and p^(j+1) does not. Compute the discriminant using any integer lifts; congruence makes this independent of lifts. For j=0 reduction modulo p suffices, for j=1 use p². Degree zero and one have Δ=1.

**Dependencies.** [Weighted height of monic polynomials](#st0-monic-weighted-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/monic-weighted-height`); `mathlib:ZMod`; `mathlib:Fintype.card`

**Sources.** [S0/abz07](#source-s0-abz07), §2 p.368; §6 Propositions 6.4,6.7 and Theorem 6.8 pp.371–372. Finite residue proportions and modulus required to detect a valuation.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.monicProportion_nonneg` (characterisation): A finite discriminant proportion is nonnegative.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.monicProportion_le_one` (characterisation): At a positive modulus the proportion is at most one.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.monicDisc_lift` (compatibility): Discriminants of congruent monic coefficient tuples are congruent.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.nu_test_linear_unit` (computation): Every monic linear discriminant is a unit.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.nu_test_linear_one` (degenerate): No monic linear discriminant has valuation one.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.nu_test_two` (non-example): A quadratic discriminant at 2 has zero valuation-one probability.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.nu_test_quartic_three` (computation): The valuation-one probability for monic quartics at 3 is 8/81, not 80/729.

**Proof route.**

1. Choose canonical integer representatives, evaluate the integral polynomial discriminant, and filter the finite tuple space. Change of lifts alters the invariant by a multiple of the modulus. Uniform residue measure agrees with normalized p-adic Haar measure.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Every monic linear discriminant is a unit.
- No monic linear discriminant has valuation one.
- A quadratic discriminant at 2 has zero valuation-one probability.
- The valuation-one probability for monic quartics at 3 is 8/81, not 80/729.

**Consumers.** BSW II Appendix A — Separate unit and valuation-one strata before adding the infinity strata.

<a id="st0-strong-weak-discriminant"></a>

### 0.43 Strong and weak square divisibility

For an integral polynomial invariant D on a fixed coefficient vector, D(a) is strongly p²-divisible when every vector congruent to a modulo p still has p²|D. It is weakly p²-divisible when p²|D(a) but strong divisibility fails. For squarefree m, W_m^(i)=intersection over p|m of the corresponding strong or weak loci. These notions are coefficient-space notions; they are not defined by first factoring the affine polynomial.

**Hypotheses.** p is prime for the arithmetic interpretation; the predicates themselves make sense for every natural p.

**Dependencies.** [Fixed-degree binary discriminant](#st0-binary-discriminant) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/binary-discriminant`); [Families defined by local conditions, local densities and largeness](#st0-family-defined-by-local-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions`)

**Sources.** [S0/bsw22](#source-s0-bsw22), §1.1 pp.4–5. Strong perturbation condition and complementary weak locus. [S0/bsw25-published](#source-s0-bsw25-published), §1 pp.2–3. The same condition for binary coefficient vectors.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.WeakSquareDiv` (data): Square divisibility without strong divisibility.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.squareDiv_partition` (characterisation): Every square-divisible vector lies in exactly one of the two loci.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.strongSquareDiv_residue` (characterisation): Strong divisibility is unchanged by adding p times a vector.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.SquarefreeDivLocus` (data): The m-locus is the intersection of the selected prime loci.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.div_test_odd_weak` (computation): x²+9 is weakly 3²-divisible.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.div_test_triple_strong` (computation): x³ is strongly 3²-divisible.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.div_test_two_strong` (computation): x² is strongly 2²-divisible; adding 2 to its constant coefficient keeps 4|Δ.

**Proof route.**

1. Express all same-residue vectors as a+pb. Strong is residue-class stable. Weak is the difference between the full square-divisibility set and the strong locus. Form intersections for squarefree m.

**Acceptance checks.**

- x²+9 is weakly 3²-divisible.
- x³ is strongly 3²-divisible.
- x² is strongly 2²-divisible; adding 2 to its constant coefficient keeps 4|Δ.

**Consumers.** BSW I/II switching constructions — Identify the weak locus before changing representation.

<a id="st0-stickelberger-binary"></a>

### 0.44 Stickelberger congruence for binary forms

For every integral binary n-ic form with n≥2, Δ_n is congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 4. In particular 2|Δ_n implies 4|Δ_n, so weak square divisibility at 2 is empty. The theorem includes leading-zero forms.

**Dependencies.** [Fixed-degree binary discriminant](#st0-binary-discriminant) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/binary-discriminant`); [Orders and distinguished ideals of a binary form](#st1-refinement-binary-form-order) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/refinement-binary-form-order`); [Strong and weak square divisibility](#st0-strong-weak-discriminant) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/strong-weak-discriminant`)

**Sources.** [S0/bsw25-published](#source-s0-bsw25-published), §1 p.2 and Appendix A p.54. Prime-2 discriminant restriction, including nonmonic forms.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binary_no_weak_two` (characterisation): The binary weak 2²-locus is empty.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the ST.1 discriminant-preserving rank-n ring of a binary form. The integral trace Gram matrix of a based ring has determinant congruent to a square modulo 4 (Stickelberger); alternatively establish the universal binary polynomial congruence before specialization. Deduce invariance for all coefficient vectors congruent modulo 2.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Quadratic discriminants b²−4ac are 0 or 1 mod4; xy has Δ=1, and y² has Δ=0.

<a id="st0-monic-density-formulas"></a>

### 0.45 Correct monic local density formulas

For prime p, ν₀(0,p)=ν₀(1,p)=1 and ν₀(n,p)=1−1/p for n≥2. At p=2, ν₁(n,2)=0. For odd p, ν₁(0,p)=ν₁(1,p)=0, ν₁(2,p)=p^−1(1−p^−1), and for n≥3, ν₁(n,p)=(1−p^−1)²(1−(−p)^(2−n))/(p+1). Thus λ_n(p)=ν₀+ν₁ equals 1 for n≤1, 1/2 at p=2,n≥2, 1−1/p² for n=2, odd p, and 1−[3p^(n−1)−p^(n−2)+(−1)^n(p−1)²]/[p^n(p+1)] for n≥3, odd p. The exponent 2−n is essential.

**Dependencies.** [Finite monic discriminant probabilities](#st0-monic-local-proportions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/monic-local-proportions`); [Stickelberger congruence for binary forms](#st0-stickelberger-binary) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/stickelberger-binary`)

**Sources.** [S0/abz07](#source-s0-abz07), Proposition 6.4 p.371; Proposition 6.7 and Theorem 6.8 with proof pp.372–373. Correct the table using its generating function and the subsequent combined formula. [S0/bsw22](#source-s0-bsw22), §1 pp.1–2, formulas for λ_n(p). The correctly simplified squarefree-discriminant local factor.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.nuOneFormula` (data): The corrected valuation-one closed formula.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.monic_nu_one` (characterisation): The finite count equals the corrected formula.

**Proof route.**

1. Squarefree residue polynomials give generating series (1−t²/p)/(1−t). A single repeated linear factor, a squarefree complementary factor avoiding it, and a nonvanishing first-order lift give H(t)=(p−1)t²/p² · (1−t²/p)/((1−t)(1+t/p)). Extract coefficients; this yields exponent 2−n, also at n=3. Combine the two strata algebraically.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The monic quartic at p=3 has ν₀=2/3, ν₁=8/81 and λ=62/81; these counts disagree with exponent −n.

<a id="st0-local-maximality"></a>

### 0.46 Local monic maximality

A monic integral f is p-maximal exactly when it is not contained in the ideal (p², pu, u²) for any monic integral u whose reduction is irreducible over Fp. Equivalently use Dedekind’s gcd(f_corr,g,h)=1 criterion, where g,h lift the distinct-factor product and its complementary multiplicity product. The ideal condition is determined modulo p² and extends to separable products. Its finite coefficient proportion is 1−p^−2 for every n≥2, and 1 for n=0,1. Global independence in ABZ is a heuristic, whereas BSW’s global result uses its tail theorem.

**Dependencies.** [Weighted height of monic polynomials](#st0-monic-weighted-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/monic-weighted-height`); [Layer 1](#layer-1) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1`; required refinement)

**Sources.** [S0/abz07](#source-s0-abz07), Lemma 3.1, Corollary 3.2 pp.368–369; Proposition 3.5 pp.369–370. Ideal avoidance and its exact local counting proof.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pMaximal_modulus` (characterisation): The local predicate depends only on coefficients modulo p².
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pMaximal_unit_disc` (characterisation): A discriminant not divisible by p forces local maximality.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pMaximal_proportion` (characterisation): The exact degree-n local proportion is 1−1/p² for n≥2.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pMax_test_linear` (computation): Every linear monic polynomial is p-maximal.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pMax_test_nonmaximal` (non-example): x² is not p-maximal.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pMax_test_eisenstein` (computation): x²−3 is 3-maximal despite its discriminant being divisible by 3.

**Proof route.**

1. Define the explicit polynomial ideal obstruction. Count intersections indexed by distinct irreducible factors of total degree d: zero if 2d>n, otherwise p^−3d (Proposition 3.4). Inclusion–exclusion and the polynomial zeta Euler product give (1−t²/p²)/(1−t). Import the order-theoretic interpretation from ST.1.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Every linear monic polynomial is p-maximal.
- x² is not p-maximal.
- x²−3 is 3-maximal despite its discriminant being divisible by 3.

**Consumers.** BSW I Theorem 1.2 and BSW II Proposition A.2 — Use the locally maximal predicate without imposing squarefree discriminant.

<a id="st0-binary-density-formulas"></a>

### 0.47 Binary local density formulas

For n≥2, α₂(2)=1/2 and α_n(2)=3/8 for n≥3. For odd p, α₂(p)=(1−p^−1)(1+p^−1−p^−3), α₃(p)=(1−p^−1)²(1+p^−1)², and α_n(p)=(1−p^−1)²(1+p^−1)(1+p^−1−p^−2) for every n≥4. The density of p-maximal rank-n binary-form rings is β₂(p)=(1−p^−1)(1+p^−1−p^−3) and β_n(p)=(1−p^−2)(1−p^−3) for n≥3, at every prime. The special printed degree-four α formula is replaced by the n≥4 formula.

**Dependencies.** [Finite binary squarefree-discriminant proportion](#st0-binary-local-proportion) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/binary-local-proportion`); [Correct monic local density formulas](#st0-monic-density-formulas) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/monic-density-formulas`); [Local monic maximality](#st0-local-maximality) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/local-maximality`); [Orders and distinguished ideals of a binary form](#st1-refinement-binary-form-order) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/refinement-binary-form-order`)

**Sources.** [S0/bsw25-published](#source-s0-bsw25-published), Appendix A Propositions A.1–A.2 pp.53–55. Partition of coefficients by the root multiplicity at infinity, with corrected degree-four factor.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.binary_alpha_two` (characterisation): The prime-2 density has separate degree-two and degree≥3 cases.

**Proof route.**

1. Partition into a₀ unit; a₀∈p,a₁ unit; and a₀,a₁∈p. For odd p their contributions are (1−p^−1)λ_n, p^−1(1−p^−1)λ_{n−1}, and p^−2(1−p^−1)²ν₀(n−2,p). Substitute corrected ν₁; degree zero has ν₀=1. At 2 use the mod-4 restriction and squarefree projective root count. For β, the local order criterion at a root of infinity of multiplicity ≥2 is failure of p²|a₀; sum over its multiplicity.

**Acceptance checks.**

- At (n,p)=(4,3), α=176/243; at (4,2), α=3/8. The degree-four odd factor agrees with n≥5 after correction.

**Interface qualification.** The β_n(p) assertion additionally needs ST.1’s rank-n binary-form ring and p-maximal-order predicate; these are not replaced by monic maximality on a leading-zero affine polynomial.

<a id="st0-kappa-acceptable-specifications"></a>

### 0.48 Acceptable monic local specifications

Fix n≥1 and κ≥2. A finite-place specification assigns to each prime p a set of monic coefficient residues modulo p^κ. Its p-adic condition is the inverse image of that residue set. It is κ-acceptable when, for all sufficiently large primes, it contains every coefficient tuple with p²∤Δ. The integral finite-place family is their intersection. A separately supplied real root stratum may then be intersected with this family through the parent local-conditions interface; acceptability concerns only the finite places. Finite modification preserves acceptability. Existence of an Euler-product asymptotic requires the ST.2 tail estimate.

**Hypotheses.** κ≥2 so squarefree-discriminant safety is visible in the modulus. Real root strata are supplied by the polynomial root-count API.

**Dependencies.** [Weighted height of monic polynomials](#st0-monic-weighted-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/monic-weighted-height`); [Families defined by local conditions, local densities and largeness](#st0-family-defined-by-local-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions`)

**Sources.** [S0/bsw22](#source-s0-bsw22), §4 local specifications pp.20–21. Finite-modulus conditions and eventual containment of the squarefree-discriminant locus.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.localSpecificationFamily` (data): The integral family satisfying every local residue condition.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.kappaAcceptable_univ` (characterisation): The unconstrained specification is acceptable whenever κ≥2.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.kappaAcceptable_inter` (characterisation): Intersecting two acceptable specifications preserves acceptability.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.localSpecificationFamily_mono` (characterisation): Enlarging each local specification enlarges the global family.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.kappaAcceptable_finite_modification` (functoriality): Changing the residue sets at finitely many primes preserves κ-acceptability; no nonemptiness of the resulting global family is implied.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.kappa_test_all` (computation): The full degree-two residue family is 2-acceptable.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.kappa_test_empty` (non-example): An empty specification at every prime is not acceptable, even for linear polynomials.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.kappa_test_finite_exception` (computation): Imposing an empty condition only at 2 still gives an acceptable specification, although the resulting global family is empty.

**Proof route.**

1. Use actual residue subsets at each prime. Pull them back along coefficient reduction. The exceptional primes are finite; outside their union both specifications contain the safe locus.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The full degree-two residue family is 2-acceptable.
- An empty specification at every prime is not acceptable, even for linear polynomials.
- Imposing an empty condition only at 2 still gives an acceptable specification, although the resulting global family is empty.

**Consumers.** BSW I local-specification counting theorem — State local eligibility without embedding the tail theorem in the definition.

<a id="st0-primitive-hypersurface-family"></a>

### 0.49 Primitive projective coefficient family

Let M=binomial(n+d,d), with the monomial ordering of ST.5. Take nonzero primitive vectors in Z^M (the gcd of all coefficients is 1), modulo a∼−a, and order classes by the Euclidean norm (Σ a_i²)^(1/2). They parametrize equations of degree-d hypersurfaces in fixed P^n. There is no quotient by PGL_(n+1), and singular equations remain in the ambient family. Each class has precisely two primitive vectors; the Euclidean norm descends and is Northcott.

**Dependencies.** [Integral coefficient boxes](#st0-coefficient-box) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/coefficient-box`); [Coefficient-vector forms and the Veronese vector](#st5-coefficient-vector-form) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/coefficient-vector-form`); [Arithmetic families: objects up to equivalence, ordered by a Northcott height, with weighted and unweighted counting functions](#st0-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/arithmetic-family`)

**Sources.** [S0/bls23](#source-s0-bls23), §1 pp.1–3. Projective coefficient classes, primitive representatives and Euclidean height.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.coefficientSignSetoid` (data): Two primitive vectors are equivalent exactly when equal or opposite.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.HypersurfaceCoefficients` (constructor): The coefficient carrier is the sign quotient.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.euclideanHeightSq` (data): The squared Euclidean height on integer vectors.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.euclideanHeightSq_neg` (characterisation): The squared norm is invariant under the sign relation.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hypersurfaceHeightSq` (data): The squared height descends to the quotient.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hypersurfaceHeight_northcott` (instance): The squared height on classes is Northcott.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.primitiveSign_fiber` (characterisation): Every coefficient class has two primitive representatives.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hypersurfaceHeight` (data): The source real height is the square root of the descended natural-valued squared height.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hypersurfaceHeight_le` (characterisation): For X≥0, the real-height cutoff H≤X is exactly the squared-height cutoff H²≤X².
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hypersurfaceHeight_real_northcott` (instance): The real Euclidean height on coefficient classes is Northcott.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hypersurface_test_zero` (non-example): The zero vector is not primitive in any dimension.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hypersurface_test_norm` (computation): The vector (1,1) has squared Euclidean height 2 and box height 1.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hypersurface_test_sign` (computation): Primitive vectors (1,2) and (−1,−2) define one class; (1,2) and (2,1) need not.

**Proof route.**

1. Use primitive gcd and a nonzero condition, then the two-element sign action. The squared Euclidean norm is a natural Northcott height; taking square roots gives the specified real height. Coordinate bounds prove finiteness; a=−a over Z forces a=0, excluded by primitivity.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The zero vector is not primitive in any dimension.
- The vector (1,1) has squared Euclidean height 2 and box height 1.
- Primitive vectors (1,2) and (−1,−2) define one class; (1,2) and (2,1) need not.

**Consumers.** BLS Theorems 1.1–1.2 — Use the same projective coefficient denominator for both global and local ratios.

<a id="st0-finite-local-hypersurface-set"></a>

### 0.50 Finite local-solubility coefficient set

For Q≥1, let R_M(Q) be ST.5’s primitive coefficient residue vectors. F_loc(Q) consists of a∈R_M(Q) such that for each prime power p^r exactly dividing Q the homogeneous equation f_a has a primitive zero modulo p^r. By CRT this is equivalent to having a primitive zero modulo Q and to ST.5’s σ(a;Q)>0. It is a finite-level condition; it does not alone assert a Qp-point. At Q=1 the primitive condition is vacuous and F_loc is the singleton residue vector.

**Dependencies.** [The finite-level local density σ(a; Q)](#st5-local-density-of-a-form-modulo-q) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/local-density-of-a-form-modulo-q`); [Coefficient-vector forms and the Veronese vector](#st5-coefficient-vector-form) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/coefficient-vector-form`)

**Sources.** [S0/bls23](#source-s0-bls23), Local coefficient set and primitive residue conventions p.55. Finite local sieve uses a positive primitive-root count.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.finiteLocal_mem` (characterisation): Membership requires both a primitive coefficient vector and a primitive root.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.finiteLocal_finite` (characterisation): The finite-level family is a finite coefficient set.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.finiteLocal_positive_count` (characterisation): A primitive-root count is positive exactly on this coefficient set, for primitive a.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.finiteLocal_test_one` (degenerate): Modulo 1 every tuple is primitive and the equation has a primitive root.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.finiteLocal_test_no_root` (non-example): The constant polynomial 1 has no root modulo 2.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.finiteLocal_test_zero_coeff` (computation): The zero coefficient vector modulo 2 is excluded even for an identically zero evaluator.

**Proof route.**

1. Import the primitive residue vectors and coefficient-to-form evaluator. Apply CRT to both coefficient and root vectors and to the gcd conditions. Record Q=1 separately.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Modulo 1 every tuple is primitive and the equation has a primitive root.
- The constant polynomial 1 has no root modulo 2.
- The zero coefficient vector modulo 2 is excluded even for an identically zero evaluator.

**Consumers.** BLS local denominator — Approximate everywhere-local solubility by finite congruence conditions.

<a id="st0-hyperelliptic-model-family"></a>

### 0.51 Hyperelliptic equation models

For g≥1 let the carrier be integral coefficient vectors of degree 2g+2 with Δ≠0, representing z²=f(x,y), ordered by the coefficient maximum. They are models in fixed coordinates, each counted once; there is no quotient by GL₂(Z), rational curve isomorphism or scalar multiplication. Bounded-height finiteness is inherited from the coefficient box. Geometric smoothness and genus g are imported from the hyperelliptic owner.

**Dependencies.** [Integral coefficient boxes](#st0-coefficient-box) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/coefficient-box`); [Fixed-degree binary discriminant](#st0-binary-discriminant) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/binary-discriminant`); [Layer 1](#layer-1) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1`; required refinement)

**Sources.** [S0/bgw17](#source-s0-bgw17), §1 pp.1–2; §3 p.9. The statistics use integral equations ordered by coefficient maximum.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.modelHeight` (data): Height is the maximum of the model coefficients.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.modelHeight_northcott` (instance): Each fixed-genus model family has Northcott height.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.model_count_le_box` (characterisation): The model count is bounded by its ambient coefficient box.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.model_test_zero_excluded` (non-example): The zero coefficient vector is excluded.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.model_test_two_equations` (computation): x⁴+y⁴ and 4x⁴+4y⁴ are distinct integral models of isomorphic curves over Q (z↦2z).
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.model_test_height` (computation): The two models have heights 1 and 4.

**Proof route.**

1. Take the nonzero-discriminant subtype. Restrict the box Northcott proof. A coordinate transformation may preserve the curve without identifying elements of this carrier.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The zero coefficient vector is excluded.
- x⁴+y⁴ and 4x⁴+4y⁴ are distinct integral models of isomorphic curves over Q (z↦2z).
- The two models have heights 1 and 4.

**Consumers.** BGW Theorems 1–3 — Count models when transferring the orbit statistic to equations.

<a id="st0-odd-root-criterion"></a>

### 0.52 Odd-prime root criterion

For odd p and a monic degree-n integral polynomial, strong p²-divisibility is equivalent to its reduction having either at least two distinct repeated roots over Fp-bar or a root of multiplicity at least three. Among p²-divisible polynomials, weak divisibility means exactly one repeated root, which is an Fp-rational double root. For binary forms use projective roots, including infinity. The zero reduction is handled separately as strongly divisible for degree at least two. At p=2 this root criterion is not asserted.

**Hypotheses.** p odd; monic case has full degree. Nonzero binary reduction for the projective factorization statement.

**Dependencies.** [Strong and weak square divisibility](#st0-strong-weak-discriminant) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/strong-weak-discriminant`); [Layer 1](#layer-1) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1`; required refinement)

**Sources.** [S0/bsw22](#source-s0-bsw22), §1.1 p.4 and Proposition 2.2 p.5. Odd-prime factorization criterion and weak-locus coordinate shape. [S0/bsw25-published](#source-s0-bsw25-published), §1 pp.2–3. Binary analogue uses projective roots.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.odd_root_criterion`.

**Proof route.**

1. Factor over the residue algebraic closure and apply the discriminant-product formula. The codimension-two singular locus is the two-double-root/triple-root locus. The unique double root is Frobenius fixed. Translation to that root makes the last two coefficients divisible by p and p², respectively.

**Acceptance checks.**

- x²+9 is weak at 3, x³ is strong at 3, and x² is strong at 2 despite its single double root; this detects the odd-prime restriction.

**Interface qualification.** Requires the ST.1 fixed-degree projective root-multiplicity and representation API, absent from the pinned library. No affine substitute is proposed.

<a id="st0-density-denominator-comparisons"></a>

### 0.53 Source-specific density denominators

Skorobogatov–Sofos relative coefficient density is computed inside the stated degree-pattern ambient coefficient family, with both numerator and denominator intersected with that family and the same box cutoff. BLS global and everywhere-local ratios both divide by all projective coefficient classes, so the conditional ratio global/local is their quotient only when the local density is positive. A density-one statement inside a positive-density subfamily transfers by the parent density tower; no conclusion is justified from a zero-density denominator.

**Hypotheses.** No transfer across a zero-density denominator.

**Dependencies.** [Upper, lower and limiting relative densities of a subfamily in a height-ordered family](#st0-relative-density) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/relative-density`); [Relative densities multiply along a tower of subfamilies](#st0-relative-density-is-multiplicative-in-towers) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/relative-density-is-multiplicative-in-towers`); [A density-one subset stays of density one in every subfamily of positive lower density](#st0-density-one-restricts-to-subfamilies-of-positive-lower-density) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/density-one-restricts-to-subfamilies-of-positive-lower-density`); [Primitive projective coefficient family](#st0-primitive-hypersurface-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/primitive-hypersurface-family`)

**Sources.** [S0/ss23](#source-s0-ss23), Published §1, height conventions and Theorems 1.1–1.2 pp.674–675. Relative density uses the constrained coefficient family. [S0/bls23](#source-s0-bls23), §1 pp.1–3. Global and local fractions use the same full denominator.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.ratio_denominator_test`.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.density_test_relative` (computation): A numerator of 30 inside a constrained family of 40 has relative density 3/4, rather than 3/10 in a larger family of 100.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.density_test_local` (computation): If global and local counts are 3 and 4 among 10 ambient classes, the conditional global fraction is 3/4.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.density_test_empty` (degenerate): Finite ratios with an empty denominator are assigned zero, never one.

**Proof route.**

1. Identify both finite counting carriers with the parent family. Write the finite identity N(S∩T)/N(U)=[N(S∩T)/N(T)]·[N(T)/N(U)] when N(T)>0. Positivity of its limiting relative density makes this denominator eventually nonzero.

**Acceptance checks.**

- A numerator of 30 inside a constrained family of 40 has relative density 3/4, rather than 3/10 in a larger family of 100.
- If global and local counts are 3 and 4 among 10 ambient classes, the conditional global fraction is 3/4.
- Finite ratios with an empty denominator are assigned zero, never one.

<a id="st0-negative-pell-radicands"></a>

### 0.54 Stevenhagen radicand family

Let D be the positive squarefree integers all of whose prime factors are either 2 or 1 modulo 4. D(X) uses d≤X. The unit 1 belongs to this radicand carrier; a quadratic-field subfamily excludes it explicitly. The negative-Pell subset consists of d with integers x,y solving x²−dy²=−1. A radicand and its quadratic-field discriminant are not one constant multiple throughout D: disc=d for d≡1 mod4 and 4d otherwise.

**Dependencies.** [The positive squarefree integers ordered by n, and Burungale–Tian's subfamily n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8)](#st0-positive-squarefree-family-over-q) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/positive-squarefree-family-over-q`); [Changing a height by constant factors on finitely many pieces averages the piecewise densities](#st0-piecewise-rescaling-of-a-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/piecewise-rescaling-of-a-height`)

**Sources.** [S0/kp22](#source-s0-kp22), §1 pp.1–2. The radicand family, truncation and soluble negative-Pell subfamily.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.NegativePellSoluble` (data): The soluble subset uses an actual integral solution.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pellRadicand_finite` (characterisation): At every cutoff only finitely many radicands occur.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.quadraticRadicandDisc` (data): The positive fundamental discriminant on this squarefree family.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pell_no_three_mod_four` (characterisation): No prime 3 modulo 4 divides an admitted radicand.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pell_test_admitted` (computation): 1,2,5,10 all belong to the radicand family.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pell_test_rejected` (non-example): 3 and 6 are excluded.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pell_test_ordering` (computation): Radicands 2 and 5 have discriminants 8 and 5.

**Proof route.**

1. Restrict the squarefree Northcott carrier by the prime-factor condition. Define the soluble subset by the integral equation. Partition into odd and even radicands before converting to discriminant order; invoke the parent piecewise-rescaling theorem only with its sector-density hypotheses.

**Acceptance checks.**

- 1,2,5,10 all belong to the radicand family.
- 3 and 6 are excluded.
- Radicands 2 and 5 have discriminants 8 and 5.

**Consumers.** KP Theorem 1.1 — Choose the radicand denominator; prior bounds and the density theorem stay in ST.5.

<a id="st0-field-permutation-type"></a>

### 0.55 Number-field permutation-type adapter

For a degree-n number field K, the normal closure acts on Hom_Q(K,Qbar), an n-element set. Choose a labeling with Fin n and compare the image subgroup to Γ≤S_n up to conjugation. This predicate descends to Q-isomorphism classes and is independent of the labeling. It supplies the missing Galois restriction in the parent field-counting function. The restriction on a fixed resolvent F is an additional ST.3 predicate, not equality of abstract groups.

**Dependencies.** [Number fields ordered by |Disc|: embedded fields, isomorphism classes, degree and automorphism weights](#st0-number-fields-ordered-by-discriminant) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/number-fields-ordered-by-discriminant`); [The counting function of number fields of fixed degree by discriminant, with signature, Galois-group and local restrictions](#st3-number-field-counting-function) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/number-field-counting-function`); `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PolynomialGaloisGroups#layer-2-the-dictionary-between-galois-theory-and-permutations`

**Sources.** [S0/wood19](#source-s0-wood19), §2 pp.383–384. Normal-closure actions must retain the embedding and its image. [S0/bsw22](#source-s0-bsw22), §1 pp.2–3. S_n field families use the action on embeddings. [S0/bstttz20](#source-s0-bstttz20), §1 pp.1–3, N_n(G,X) and fixed-resolvent notation. The restriction uses the normal-closure permutation group.

**API.**
