- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.permutationType_self` (characterisation): Every representation has its own image type.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.permutationType_relabel` (characterisation): Conjugating a representation preserves its permutation type.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.permutationType_card` (characterisation): The conjugate image and target subgroup have the same cardinality.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.type_test_full_two` (computation): The identity permutation representation has full S₂ type.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.type_test_trivial_not_full` (non-example): The trivial permutation representation does not have full S₂ type.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.type_test_one` (degenerate): The trivial representation on one point has full permutation type S₁, so the predicate does not impose a spurious nontriviality condition.

**Proof route.**

1. Import the normal-closure permutation representation; compare its image under a labeling via subgroup conjugacy. Changing the labeling conjugates the image. An isomorphism of fields induces an equivariant bijection of embedding sets. Restrict the existing Hermite-finite carrier.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The identity permutation representation has full S₂ type.
- The trivial permutation representation does not have full S₂ type.
- The trivial representation on one point has full permutation type S₁, so the predicate does not impose a spurious nontriviality condition.

**Consumers.** BSTTTZ §1 N_n(G,X) and N_n(G,F,X) — Attach a conjugacy-invariant predicate to the existing discriminant family.

<a id="st0-twist-denominator-frontier"></a>

### 0.56 General number-field twist denominator

For a number field F, the parent squareclass height H(t)=product of norms of finite primes with odd valuation has finite fibers. For a nonempty admissible finite set of local conditions Σ, one needs #Σ(X)=c_(F,Σ) X+o(X), c_(F,Σ)>0, where each squareclass is counted once. Admissible means local conditions are compatible with global squareclasses, not merely that each local set is individually nonempty. Its ideal-counting proof must distinguish classes modulo Cl(F)² and the finite unit/Selmer fibers. This precise input is an open supplier frontier; it is not obtained from Northcott finiteness.

**Dependencies.** [The squareclass height H(t) = ∏_{ord_v(t) odd} N v on F×/F×²](#st0-squareclass-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/squareclass-height`); [Bounded-height finiteness for squareclasses of a number field](#st0-finiteness-of-squareclasses-of-bounded-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/finiteness-of-squareclasses-of-bounded-height`); `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4`

**Sources.** [S0/bklos19](#source-s0-bklos19), §2 p.2, squareclass height and Σ(X). General-number-field twist ordering and its denominator.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.twist_denominator_frontier`.

**Proof route.**

1. Expand squarefree ideals in each ray class and use finite-order Hecke characters to select compatible classes. Count unit/Selmer fibers and local squareclass conditions explicitly. Analytic continuation and a Tauberian/ideal equidistribution theorem must produce the residue and its strict positivity. These analytic statements are requested from AN.4, rather than asserted as already supplied.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Over Q with no local restriction the positive squarefree denominator is (6/π²)X+o(X). Compatibility and residue positivity, rather than mere local nonemptiness, must be established for general F.

**Interface qualification.** The global squareclass family and local-condition supplier types are not yet library declarations; the exact asymptotic is a recorded gap, not a dummy Lean proposition.

<a id="st0-unpolarized-abelian-count"></a>

### 0.57 Unweighted finite-field abelian-variety count

For a finite field k and g≥0, B(k,g) counts k-isomorphism classes of dimension-g abelian varieties, once per class. Use the native Tau Ceti category and dimension; do not count geometric classes, isogeny classes or 1/Aut stack mass. Finiteness is imported from the finite-field arithmetic-moduli classification.

**Dependencies.** `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety`; `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII:F3`

**Sources.** [S0/lt18](#source-s0-lt18), Introduction §0, Theorem 0.1, pp.1–2 (arXiv v1). B(p,g) is the unweighted class count.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.UnpolarizedClasses` (constructor): Native dimension-g abelian varieties modulo k-isomorphism.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.unpolarizedCount` (data): The unweighted number of classes, used only with the finite-field finiteness theorem.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.unpolarizedClasses_finite` (instance): Over a finite field the class carrier is finite.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.unpolarized_iso` (characterisation): Two representatives have the same class precisely when k-isomorphic.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.unpolarizedCountOn` (data): For a subfamily S of native class objects, its unweighted count is Set.ncard S; finiteness is required before treating ncard as a count.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.unpolarizedCountOn_univ` (compatibility): Counting the full class subfamily recovers unpolarizedCount.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.abelian_test_zero_dim` (degenerate): There is one dimension-zero abelian-variety class over a finite field.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.abelian_test_iso` (compatibility): Isomorphic representatives contribute one class.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.abelian_test_mass_distinction` (non-example): For an actual native dimension-g object A with #Aut(A)=2, the singleton class subfamily has unpolarizedCountOn=1, differing from its inverse-automorphism mass 1/2.

**Proof route.**

1. Restrict the native category by dimension and quotient by categorical isomorphism. Import finite-field classification to obtain finiteness before interpreting Nat.card as a counting function. The dimension-zero variety is the identity object.

**Acceptance checks.**

- There is one dimension-zero abelian-variety class over a finite field.
- Isomorphic representatives contribute one class.
- For an actual native dimension-g object A with #Aut(A)=2, the singleton class subfamily has unpolarizedCountOn=1, differing from its inverse-automorphism mass 1/2.

**Consumers.** LT Theorem 0.1; arithmetic-moduli Part II F.6 — Supply the unpolarized denominator without a mass weighting.

<a id="st0-principally-polarized-count"></a>

### 0.58 Principally polarized class count

A(k,g) is the number of k-isomorphism classes of pairs (A,λ), with A a dimension-g abelian variety and λ a principal polarization defined over k. An isomorphism f identifies the pairs when f∨ λ′ f=λ. Polarization means the ample line-bundle-induced symmetric isogeny, with the descent convention of AbelianSchemes; its native type is imported. This is an unweighted count, not the coarse moduli space k-point count or inverse-automorphism mass.

**Dependencies.** `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2`; `PELModuli:M6`; [Unweighted finite-field abelian-variety count](#st0-unpolarized-abelian-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/unpolarized-abelian-count`)

**Sources.** [S0/lt18](#source-s0-lt18), Introduction §0 pp.1–2; §4.4 Proposition 4.11 p.20 (arXiv v1). The statistic counts polarized pairs, not polarizations without the automorphism quotient.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.ppavClasses` (characterisation): The type of k-isomorphism classes of dimension-g principally polarized pairs.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.ppavCount` (characterisation): Nat.card of ppavClasses, after the finite-field finiteness input.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.ppav_forget` (characterisation): Forget λ to the unpolarized class.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.ppavCount_fiber_sum` (characterisation): A(k,g)=Σ_[A] # (principal polarizations of A modulo Aut_k(A)).

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.ppav_test_zero_dim` (degenerate): A(k,0)=1.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.ppav_test_elliptic` (compatibility): A(k,1)=B(k,1): elliptic curves have a canonical principal polarization.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.ppav_test_mass` (non-example): For a principally polarized elliptic curve with automorphism group of order 2, its class contributes 1 and its mass contributes 1/2.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the imported principal-polarization type and pair-isomorphism relation. Prove the forgetful fiber is the Aut(A)-orbit set of principal polarizations. Import finiteness from the arithmetic-moduli classification, then count.

**Acceptance checks.**

- A(k,0)=1.
- A(k,1)=B(k,1): elliptic curves have a canonical principal polarization.
- For a principally polarized elliptic curve with automorphism group of order 2, its class contributes 1 and its mass contributes 1/2.

**Consumers.** LT polarized-growth comparison — Compare A(k,g) with B(k,g) without changing weights.

**Interface qualification.** The pinned abelian-variety category has no native dual/principal-polarization type. Every name below is explicitly omitted until A.2/M.6 supplies that geometric type; no opaque Prop polarization predicate is declared.

<a id="st0-polarization-fiber-count"></a>

### 0.59 Principal-polarization fiber

For a fixed abelian variety A/k, the fiber of the forgetful class map consists of Aut_k(A)-orbits of principal polarizations, acting by λ↦u∨λu. The orbit set may be finite although Aut_k(A) is infinite. Given λ₀, Proposition 4.11 identifies it with Rosati-conjugacy orbits of integral symmetric ample automorphisms. The geometry belongs to AbelianSchemes/PELModuli; hermitian or integral-lattice classifications are imported from IntegralLattices, never redeveloped here.

**Dependencies.** [Principally polarized class count](#st0-principally-polarized-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/principally-polarized-count`); `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII:F5`; `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2`; `mathlib:MulAction.orbitRel`

**Sources.** [S0/lt18](#source-s0-lt18), Proposition 4.11, Examples 4.12–4.13 p.20. Polarization fiber is an orbit set, with automorphism action rather than raw polarization count.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.polarizationOrbitCount_empty` (characterisation): An empty polarization type has zero orbits.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.polarizationOrbitCount_single` (characterisation): A singleton polarization type has one orbit.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.polarizationOrbitCount_finite` (characterisation): For a finite polarization carrier, orbit count is at most its cardinality.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pol_test_empty` (degenerate): An abelian variety with no principal polarization has empty fiber.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pol_test_unique` (computation): A single canonical principal polarization gives one orbit.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pol_test_infinite_group` (non-example): The orbit-set count is meaningful for an infinite automorphism group with a singleton carrier; no inverse group cardinal is involved.

**Proof route.**

1. Use transport of λ along an isomorphism from a fixed representative. Two transports differ by Aut_k(A), giving the fiber-orbit bijection. The finite orbit-set cardinality is appropriate even if the acting group is infinite.

**Acceptance checks.**

- An abelian variety with no principal polarization has empty fiber.
- A single canonical principal polarization gives one orbit.
- The orbit-set count is meaningful for an infinite automorphism group with a singleton carrier; no inverse group cardinal is involved.

**Consumers.** LT comparison of polarizations on A — Make the fiber multiplicity explicit instead of using 1/Nat.card Aut(A).

<a id="st0-natural-bundle-law"></a>

### 0.60 Natural bundle probability law

Over F_q, q>1, normalized rank-two bundle classes on P¹ modulo tensoring by line bundles are indexed by ν=|a−b|. Their natural inverse-automorphism probability is μ_q(0)=(q−1)/(2q), and μ_q(n)=(q²−1)/(2q^(n+1)) for n≥1. Each parity has mass 1/2. The GL₂ automorphism orders are (q²−1)(q²−q) at n=0 and (q−1)²q^(n+1) at n>0; their inverse masses have total 2/((q−1)³(q+1)), while the PGL₂ weights have total 2/((q−1)²(q+1)). Scalar automorphisms cancel in the passage to PGL₂.

**Hypotheses.** q>1; the geometric interpretation requires q the order of a finite field.

**Dependencies.** [Stabilizer weights 1/#Stab and the weighted orbit count of a family of orbits](#st0-stabilizer-weighted-orbit-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/stabilizer-weighted-orbit-count`); [Weighted and unweighted orbit counts differ by at most the number of orbits with a nontrivial stabilizer](#st0-weighted-and-unweighted-orbit-counts) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/weighted-and-unweighted-orbit-counts`); `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-b-coherent-cohomology-over-k-genus-riemannroch-serre-duality`

**Sources.** [S0/st17](#source-s0-st17), §4, bundle measure display pp.29–30. Normalized bundle weights and automorphism convention.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundleLaw` (constructor): The mass function defines a probability mass function for q>1.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundleMass_nonneg` (characterisation): All masses are nonnegative.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundleMass_sum` (characterisation): The total mass is one.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundleMass_parity` (characterisation): Even and odd classes each carry half the mass.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundleAutOrder` (data): The natural automorphism order has a separate balanced-bundle case.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundleAutOrder_inverse_sum` (characterisation): For q>1, the GL₂ inverse-automorphism weights sum to 2/((q−1)³(q+1)); the PGL₂ sum has one fewer factor q−1.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundleMass_from_aut` (compatibility): Dividing the GL₂ inverse-automorphism weight by its total gives the stated probability.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundle_test_zero` (computation): At q=3 the balanced bundle has mass 1/3.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundle_test_one` (computation): At q=3 the next two masses are 4/9 and 4/27.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundle_test_aut` (computation): At q=3 the balanced and first unbalanced GL₂ automorphism orders are 48 and 36.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundle_test_normalization` (computation): At q=3, the total GL₂ inverse-automorphism weight is 1/16.

**Proof route.**

1. Import Grothendieck splitting of bundles on P¹ and compute upper-triangular bundle automorphisms: n+1 global sections in the off-diagonal entry for n>0. Sum the geometric series, retaining the exceptional balanced bundle. The scalar quotient rescales all inverse masses by one common factor.

**Acceptance checks.**

- At q=3 the balanced bundle has mass 1/3.
- At q=3 the next two masses are 4/9 and 4/27.
- At q=3 the balanced and first unbalanced GL₂ automorphism orders are 48 and 36.
- At q=3, the total GL₂ inverse-automorphism weight is 1/16.

**Consumers.** ST joint equidistribution formulation — Provide the marginal target law with its correct normalization.

<a id="st0-bundle-parity-tails"></a>

### 0.61 Exact bundle parity tails

For d≥1, μ_q({d,d+2,d+4,…})=1/(2q^(d−1)); the even tail starting at d=0 has mass 1/2. Consequently μ_q({a+1,a+3,…})=1/(2q^a) for a≥0. The d=0 exception is required by the balanced-bundle weight.

**Hypotheses.** q>1, as in the natural-bundle-law prerequisite; q is a prime power in the finite-field specialization.

**Dependencies.** [Natural bundle probability law](#st0-natural-bundle-law) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/natural-bundle-law`)

**Sources.** [S0/st17](#source-s0-st17), §4 tail display pp.29–30. Parity-tail geometric series, with the balanced term separated.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.bundle_parity_tail`.

**Proof route.**

1. Sum the unbalanced geometric series with common ratio q^−2. At d=0 add the exceptional n=0 term to the positive even tail.

**Acceptance checks.**

- At q=3 the tail {1,3,…} has mass 1/2, the tail {2,4,…} has mass 1/6, and the even tail starting at 0 has mass 1/2.

<a id="st0-finite-picard-quotient"></a>

### 0.62 Picard quotient by the hyperelliptic pencil

For a smooth geometrically connected hyperelliptic C/F_q, let κ be its degree-two pencil and P=Pic(C) of rational line bundles. Q=P/Zκ has two parity sectors. Over a finite field Pic¹(C)(F_q) is nonempty by Lang’s theorem on its Jacobian torsor and Brauer obstruction vanishing, even when C(F_q) is empty. Thus deg:P→Z is onto, Pic⁰(C)=J(F_q) is finite of size h, and Q is finite of size 2h. Uniform probability on Q assigns 1/(2h) per class; conditioning on either parity assigns 1/h.

**Dependencies.** `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/picard-brauer-sequence`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/degree-zero-class-comparison`; `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-d-the-relative-picard-functor-and-the-jacobian-scheme`; `mathlib:QuotientGroup.lift`; `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII:F5/finite-field-abelian-lang`

**Sources.** [S0/st17](#source-s0-st17), §4 Picard quotient and probability discussion pp.30–32. Finite quotient, parity and the Jacobian denominator.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.picClass` (constructor): The canonical class map into the quotient.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.picParity` (data): Degree modulo 2 descends to the quotient.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.picQuotient_finite` (instance): Surjective degree and finite degree-zero kernel make Q finite.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.picQuotient_card` (characterisation): The quotient has twice the degree-zero cardinality.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.picParity_class` (characterisation): The parity of a class is degree modulo 2.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pic_test_degree_two` (computation): For P=Z, degree=id and κ=2 the quotient has two elements.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pic_test_parity` (computation): Degree 0 and degree 1 remain distinct in the quotient.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pic_test_tensor` (compatibility): Tensoring by the pencil preserves a class.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the rational Picard-to-line-bundle comparison over a finite field. Apply Lang to Pic¹, not existence of a rational curve point. Abstractly, for an additive group P with onto degree map and deg κ=2, each parity sector is a Pic⁰ torsor, giving the cardinality 2h.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For P=Z, degree=id and κ=2 the quotient has two elements.
- Degree 0 and degree 1 remain distinct in the quotient.
- Tensoring by the pencil preserves a class.

**Consumers.** ST joint pushforward — The probability space for one or two bundle invariants is Q, with both parities.

<a id="st0-picard-representatives-and-carry"></a>

### 0.63 Picard parity representatives and carry

Each class of Q has a unique representative of degree r∈{0,1}: L−((deg L−r)/2)κ. Choosing D₀ of degree one identifies Q as a set with Pic⁰×{0,1}. If c=κ−2D₀, addition is (x,r)+(y,s)=(x+y−floor((r+s)/2)c,(r+s) mod2). This need not be a direct-product group decomposition; c must be divisible by 2 in Pic⁰ for such a split after changing D₀.

**Dependencies.** [Picard quotient by the hyperelliptic pencil](#st0-finite-picard-quotient) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/finite-picard-quotient`)

**Sources.** [S0/st17](#source-s0-st17), §4 pp.30–32, Picard quotient construction. Degree normalization supplies representatives; carry follows from the same quotient.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pic_carry` (characterisation): Two odd representatives create the carry −c.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.carry_test_nonsplit` (non-example): In P=Z×Z/2 with κ=(2,1), the parity-one class has order four: Q is not the direct product of its two order-two sectors.

**Proof route.**

1. Subtract an integer multiple of κ to normalize degree. Uniqueness follows by comparing degrees of two representatives differing by mκ. Express their sum in normalized coordinates: replace 2D₀ with κ−c. The resulting carry has a minus sign.

**Acceptance checks.**

- In P=Z×Z/2 with κ=(2,1), the parity-one class has order four: Q is not the direct product of its two order-two sectors.

<a id="st0-finite-joint-bundle-mass"></a>

### 0.64 Joint bundle pushforward from the Picard quotient

Given the two quotient-invariant bundle indices ν(L⊗M₁) and ν(L⊗M₂), push the uniform law on Q to N×N. Its mass at (i,j) is the fiber cardinality divided by 2h, not h. Uniform translation makes it depend on M₂−M₁. The ratio and inverse-line-bundle conventions used in theta intersections must be compared using the hyperelliptic involution identity σL=(deg L)κ−L and invariance of the pushforward under σ; replacing only the second factor by inversion is not a general property of joint measures.

**Dependencies.** [Picard quotient by the hyperelliptic pencil](#st0-finite-picard-quotient) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/finite-picard-quotient`); `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-b-coherent-cohomology-over-k-genus-riemannroch-serre-duality`

**Sources.** [S0/st17](#source-s0-st17), §4 joint distribution and theta intersection formulas pp.30–33. Joint pushforward, its parity support and normalization.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.jointFiberMass_nonneg` (characterisation): Joint masses are nonnegative.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.jointFiberMass_equiv` (functoriality): Relabeling the uniform source by a bijection preserves the joint law.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.jointFiberMass_no_fiber` (characterisation): An empty fiber has zero mass.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.jointFiberMass_total` (characterisation): For a nonempty finite source the sum of the masses is one.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.joint_test_diagonal` (computation): Uniform Fin 2 pushed forward diagonally gives mass 1/2 at (0,0).
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.joint_test_empty_cell` (non-example): The same diagonal law has zero mass at (0,1).
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.joint_test_not_half_changed` (computation): A constant pair pushed from two source classes has mass 1, not 2; the denominator includes both classes.

**Proof route.**

1. Use finite uniform counting on Q. Translate the common variable by M₁. Import the involution relation and bundle-index invariance for the ratio/inverse convention comparison. Each marginal is the corresponding uniform bundle pushforward.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Uniform Fin 2 pushed forward diagonally gives mass 1/2 at (0,0).
- The same diagonal law has zero mass at (0,1).
- A constant pair pushed from two source classes has mass 1, not 2; the denominator includes both classes.

**Consumers.** ST mixing conjecture — State the finite measure before its asymptotics.

<a id="st0-theta-tail-normalization"></a>

### 0.65 Theta tail event bijections

Let h=#J(F_q). For a≥0, the event ν(L)∈a+1+2N in uniform Q has probability #Θ_(g−a)(F_q)/(2h), with Θ_d empty for d<0. For a,b≥0, write d₁=g−a,d₂=g−b. If deg M and d₁+d₂ have different parity the joint event for ν(L),ν(M⊗L^−1) is empty. Otherwise set M′=M⊗κ^((d₁+d₂−deg M)/2); the event is in bijection with Θ_d₁ ∩ (M′−Θ_d₂), and its probability is that intersection count divided by 2h. Conditional on its parity sector the denominator is h.

**Dependencies.** [Joint bundle pushforward from the Picard quotient](#st0-finite-joint-bundle-mass) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/finite-joint-bundle-mass`); [Picard parity representatives and carry](#st0-picard-representatives-and-carry) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/picard-representatives-and-carry`); `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-b-coherent-cohomology-over-k-genus-riemannroch-serre-duality`

**Sources.** [S0/st17](#source-s0-st17), §4 pp.30–33, single and joint theta-tail displays. Tail events correspond to effective divisor classes of the required degrees; unconditional probability requires both parity sectors.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.theta_tail_normalization`.

**Proof route.**

1. For a split pushforward O(u)⊕O(v), use u+v=deg L−g−1 and h⁰(C,L)=h⁰(P¹,π_*L). Normalize the degree by κ to d=g−a. A nonzero section is equivalent to membership in Θ_d. Repeat for M⊗L^−1; degree parity determines whether simultaneous normalization is possible. Count distinct rational line-bundle classes, not individual divisors or sections.

**Acceptance checks.**

- In the pointless genus-two F₃ example, Θ₀ contributes 1/8 to the unconditional ν≥3 odd tail, while its conditional odd-sector probability is 1/4.

**Interface qualification.** The theta loci, geometric pushforward and splitting index are absent at the pin. Both event bijections remain typed geometric supplier work; the finite jointFiberMass denominator is already stated without any substitute cohomology predicates.

<a id="st0-parity-product-candidate"></a>

### 0.66 Parity-compatible product probability

Let δ be the parity of deg(M₂−M₁). Define μ_r(n)=2μ_q(n) when n≡r mod2 and 0 otherwise. The candidate joint law is 1/2[μ₀⊗μ_δ+μ₁⊗μ_(1+δ)]. Equivalently its mass is 2μ_q(i)μ_q(j) when i+j≡δ and zero otherwise. It has both marginals μ_q and total mass 1. This construction states the candidate only; equidistribution and its hypotheses are ST.5/geometry results, not part of its definition.

**Hypotheses.** q>1, as in the natural-bundle-law prerequisite; q is a prime power in the finite-field specialization.

**Dependencies.** [Natural bundle probability law](#st0-natural-bundle-law) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/natural-bundle-law`); [Exact bundle parity tails](#st0-bundle-parity-tails) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/bundle-parity-tails`)

**Sources.** [S0/st17](#source-s0-st17), §4 pp.31–33, parity-conditioned limit alternatives. Product law conditioned on the allowed parity pairs.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.parityProduct_support` (characterisation): Incompatible parity has zero mass.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.parityProduct_marginal` (characterisation): Each first-coordinate marginal is the natural bundle law.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.parityProduct_total` (characterisation): The joint mass sums to one.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.parity_test_same` (computation): At q=3 and δ=0 the (0,0) mass is 2/9.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.parity_test_opposite` (computation): At q=3 and δ=1 the (0,1) mass is 8/27.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.parity_test_forbidden` (non-example): The (0,0) mass vanishes for δ=1.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the half-mass parity sectors. Normalize each conditional marginal by 2, and average the two allowed sector products with coefficient 1/2.

**Acceptance checks.**

- At q=3 and δ=0 the (0,0) mass is 2/9.
- At q=3 and δ=1 the (0,1) mass is 8/27.
- The (0,0) mass vanishes for δ=1.

**Consumers.** ST mixing conjecture — Fix the proposed limiting measure before proving or assuming convergence.

<a id="st0-hecke-pushforward"></a>

### 0.67 Hecke probability as a weighted pushforward

For effective D on P¹ let g_D be the corresponding adelic diagonal translation. Push the normalized invariant finite-volume probability on X=PGL₂(F)\PGL₂(A) through x↦(xK,xg_DK). This is μ_D on the pair of bundle classes. Its marginals are the natural inverse-automorphism law. Uniformly choosing neighboring isomorphism classes does not generally give this law: multiplicities and stabilizers must remain in the pushforward.

**Dependencies.** [Natural bundle probability law](#st0-natural-bundle-law) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/natural-bundle-law`); [Stabilizer weights 1/#Stab and the weighted orbit count of a family of orbits](#st0-stabilizer-weighted-orbit-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/stabilizer-weighted-orbit-count`); `AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.2`; `mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.map`

**Sources.** [S0/st17](#source-s0-st17), Appendix A.4, Hecke Measures, p.38 (arXiv v1). The Hecke measure is induced by invariant adelic probability.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.heckePairPushforward_marginal` (characterisation): The first marginal of a measurable pair map is its first pushforward.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.heckePairPushforward_probability` (instance): A measurable pair pushforward of a probability is a probability.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.heckePairPushforward_dirac` (characterisation): A point mass maps to the corresponding pair point mass.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hecke_test_diagonal` (degenerate): Identity translation gives a diagonal measure.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hecke_test_one_point` (computation): A constant correspondence pushes every point to its constant pair.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.hecke_test_asymmetric` (non-example): For distinct b,c, the pair pushforward of a Dirac mass along constant maps b,c differs from the reversed Dirac mass at (c,b).

**Proof route.**

1. Use the actual adelic quotient and its normalized Haar-derived measure from the geometric/adelic supplier. Measurable quotient maps define the pushforward; right-translation invariance gives the second marginal.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Identity translation gives a diagonal measure.
- A constant correspondence pushes every point to its constant pair.
- For distinct b,c, the pair pushforward of a Dirac mass along constant maps b,c differs from the reversed Dirac mass at (c,b).

**Consumers.** ST special-correspondence alternative — Distinguish a correspondence law from a product law.

<a id="st0-pointless-curve-regression"></a>

### 0.68 Pointless genus-two bundle regression

For C/F₃ given by y²=2((x³−x)²+1), the smooth projective curve has genus 2, no F₃-points, fourteen F₉-points and #J(F₃)=4. Consequently Q has eight elements. Its exact bundle pushforward has μ_C(0)=1/2, μ_C(1)=3/8, μ_C(3)=1/8 and all other masses zero. This is a finite regression example, not the limiting natural μ₃. It detects both a spurious rational-point assumption on Pic¹ and a denominator h in place of 2h.

**Dependencies.** [Theta tail event bijections](#st0-theta-tail-normalization) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/theta-tail-normalization`); [Picard quotient by the hyperelliptic pencil](#st0-finite-picard-quotient) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/finite-picard-quotient`); `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-b-coherent-cohomology-over-k-genus-riemannroch-serre-duality`

**Sources.** [S0/st17](#source-s0-st17), §4 Picard and theta normalization pp.30–33. Finite test of the quotient and tail formulas; this example is derived here, rather than asserted in the paper.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.pointless_curve_regression`.

**Proof route.**

1. In characteristic 3 the defining sextic has derivative 2(x³−x), coprime to the sextic, so its smooth projective hyperelliptic model has genus 2. Enumerate x,y over F₃ and F₉=F₃[u]/(u²+1), including the infinity equation y²=2: N₁=0 and N₂=14.
2. Since N₁=0, the seven Frobenius pairs among C(F₉) are exactly the rational effective divisors of degree 2. Riemann–Roch and Serre duality give h⁰(L)=1 for every degree-two class except the canonical class κ, where h⁰(κ)=2. Thus the canonical Abel fiber has #P¹(F₃)=4 divisors and every other fiber has one. Hence #Pic²(F₃)=7−4+1=4; translation by κ identifies it with J(F₃). This proof needs no zeta-function theorem.
3. The degree-two Picard quotient has 2h=8 elements even though C(F₃) is empty. Θ₀ is a singleton, Θ₁ has no rational points, and the higher tails are empty. Applying the one-tail formula and the half-mass of each parity sector gives masses 1/2,3/8,1/8 at ν=0,1,3.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Finite F₃/F₉ enumeration gives N₁=0,N₂=14. The effective-divisor count and Riemann–Roch give h=4,Q=8; the exact bundle masses sum to one.

**Interface qualification.** The concrete smooth-projective curve, its Jacobian and bundle pushforward are not native at the pin. The finite-field enumeration and the Riemann–Roch fiber count are independently checked in the review; no geometric Lean signature is fabricated.

<a id="st0-wood-outside-involutions"></a>

### 0.69 Outside involutions in a wreath type

Use the already built Tau Ceti wreath product W=G≀S₂ with its coordinate-permutation action. For H≤W define c(H)={w∈H : w²=1 and its top permutation is nontrivial}. These elements have exact order two. The canonical swap is (1,swap). Conjugacy means conjugacy by H, not by the ambient W.

**Dependencies.** `tauceti:TauCeti.WreathProduct`; `tauceti:TauCeti.WreathProduct.map`

**Sources.** [S0/wood19](#source-s0-wood19), §1 p.378; §2 p.383. Outside order-two elements and the top projection.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.canonicalSwap` (constructor): The wreath element with trivial base and transposed coordinates.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.outside_ne_one` (characterisation): An outside involution is not the identity.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.outside_conjugate` (characterisation): Conjugating by H preserves the outside-involution set.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.outside_finite` (instance): For finite G the outside set is finite.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.outside_test_swap` (computation): The canonical swap is an outside involution in the full wreath group.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.outside_test_identity` (non-example): The identity is excluded even though its square is one.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.outside_test_trivial_G` (degenerate): When G is trivial, the full wreath group has one outside involution.

**Proof route.**

1. Reuse WreathProduct and its projections, multiplication and functorial map. Nontrivial top projection excludes the identity. The canonical swap has order two.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The canonical swap is an outside involution in the full wreath group.
- The identity is excluded even though its square is one.
- When G is trivial, the full wreath group has one outside involution.

**Consumers.** Wood admissibility and real twists — Select the possible quadratic inertia images without constructing another wreath product.

<a id="st0-wood-admissible-type"></a>

### 0.70 Admissible wreath subgroup

For a finite G, H≤G≀S₂ is admissible if it contains the canonical swap, is generated by its outside involutions, and the first-coordinate projection of ker(H→S₂) is onto G. All three conditions are required. Types are embedded subgroups, not abstract isomorphism classes.

**Dependencies.** [Outside involutions in a wreath type](#st0-wood-outside-involutions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-outside-involutions`)

**Sources.** [S0/wood19](#source-s0-wood19), §1 p.378; §2.2 Proposition 2.2 pp.386–387. The admissibility conditions forced by an unramified extension over a quadratic base.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.admissible_outside_nonempty` (characterisation): Admissibility guarantees at least one outside involution.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.admissible_coordinate_surjective` (characterisation): The top-kernel first coordinate is onto G.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.admissible_generated` (characterisation): The outside involutions generate exactly H.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.admissible_test_trivial` (computation): For trivial G, the full S₂ wreath group is admissible.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.admissible_test_bottom` (non-example): The identity subgroup is not admissible.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.admissible_test_swap_only` (non-example): For nontrivial G the subgroup generated only by the canonical swap fails the coordinate condition.

**Proof route.**

1. Express generation as subgroup closure of the outside set, and the coordinate condition by elements of the top kernel. This definition uses the existing wreath structure.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For trivial G, the full S₂ wreath group is admissible.
- The identity subgroup is not admissible.
- For nontrivial G the subgroup generated only by the canonical swap fails the coordinate condition.

**Consumers.** Wood Theorems 1.1–1.2 — Restrict the allowable embedded normal-closure types.

<a id="st0-wood-good-type"></a>

### 0.71 Good embedded type

An admissible H is good when c(H) is one H-conjugacy class. This permits the common rigidification multiplicity |c(H)|·|Aut_H(G)|. Ambient conjugacy is insufficient, and the condition on the outside class is additional to admissibility.

**Dependencies.** [Admissible wreath subgroup](#st0-wood-admissible-type) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-admissible-type`)

**Sources.** [S0/wood19](#source-s0-wood19), §1 p.378; Lemma 2.1 pp.385–386. Goodness is the single outside conjugacy-class hypothesis.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.good_admissible` (characterisation): Good types are admissible.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.good_conjugate` (characterisation): Any two outside involutions are conjugate inside H.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.good_single_outside` (characterisation): An admissible subgroup with at most one outside element is good.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.good_test_trivial` (computation): The full wreath group for trivial G is good.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.good_test_bottom` (non-example): The empty outside set in the identity subgroup is not good.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.good_test_diagonal_c2` (non-example): For G=C₂, the diagonal G times swap subgroup is admissible but not good: its two outside involutions are distinct central elements.

**Proof route.**

1. Use conjugation by elements of the subgroup itself. Admissibility supplies nonemptiness of the outside set, preventing a vacuous empty-class definition.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The full wreath group for trivial G is good.
- The empty outside set in the identity subgroup is not good.
- For G=C₂, the diagonal G times swap subgroup is admissible but not good: its two outside involutions are distinct central elements.

**Consumers.** Wood Lemma 2.1 — Make the real rigid/unrigid multiplicity uniform.

<a id="st0-wood-type-automorphisms"></a>

### 0.72 Type-preserving automorphisms

Aut_H(G) is the subgroup of Aut(G) whose diagonal functorial action on G≀S₂ fixes H as an embedded subgroup. It is not Aut(H). For an imaginary unrigid extension of type H, exactly |Aut_H(G)| rigid markings have the same embedded type.

**Dependencies.** [Admissible wreath subgroup](#st0-wood-admissible-type) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-admissible-type`); `tauceti:TauCeti.WreathProduct.map`

**Sources.** [S0/wood19](#source-s0-wood19), §2.1.1 printed pp.383–385. Setwise preservation of the actual wreath image defines the marking multiplicity.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.typeAutomorphisms_mem` (characterisation): Membership is setwise preservation under the induced wreath map.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.typeAutomorphisms_finite` (instance): The type-preserving automorphism group is finite for finite G.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.typeAutomorphisms_full` (characterisation): Every automorphism preserves the full wreath subgroup.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.typeAut_test_trivial` (computation): For G=1, the type automorphism count is one.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.typeAut_test_c2` (non-example): For G=C₂ the type automorphism count is one, although the full wreath group has eight elements.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.typeAut_test_identity` (degenerate): Identity always preserves the type.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the already built wreath map induced by α:G≃*G on both base coordinates and identity on the top permutation. Identity, composition and inverse preserve the setwise stabilizer.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For G=1, the type automorphism count is one.
- For G=C₂ the type automorphism count is one, although the full wreath group has eight elements.
- Identity always preserves the type.

**Consumers.** Wood imaginary rigid average — Convert marked surjections to unmarked field extensions.

<a id="st0-wood-continuous-surjections"></a>

### 0.73 Continuous marked surjections

For a profinite Γ and finite discrete G, Sur_c(Γ,G) is the type of continuous surjective group homomorphisms. A kernel specifies an unmarked finite G-extension; the identifications of its quotient with G form an Aut(G)-torsor. A type-preserving fiber has Aut_H(G)-torsor size. Finiteness in the arithmetic application is a separate Hermite/Hurwitz theorem, not a consequence of G being finite.

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:ContinuousMonoidHom`; [Type-preserving automorphisms](#st0-wood-type-automorphisms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-type-automorphisms`)

**Sources.** [S0/wood19](#source-s0-wood19), §2.1 printed pp.383–385. Rigid extensions are continuous surjections, including a quotient marking.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.continuousSurjectionKernel` (projection): The kernel is a subgroup; normality is inherited from the homomorphism.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.continuousSurjection_aut_action` (functoriality): Postcomposition by an automorphism preserves surjectivity, and continuity when G is discrete.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.continuousSurjection_same_kernel` (characterisation): Maps with the same kernel differ by a unique automorphism of G.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.continuousSurjectionPostcompose` (constructor): For discrete G, postcompose a continuous surjection with α∈Aut(G) to obtain another element of ContinuousSurjections Γ G.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.continuousSurjectionPostcompose_apply` (simp): The underlying map evaluates to α(ρ(x)).
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.continuousSurjectionPostcompose_kernel` (compatibility): Postcomposition by α leaves the kernel unchanged.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.sur_test_trivial_target` (computation): There is one continuous surjection to the trivial group.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.sur_test_trivial_source` (non-example): There is no surjection from the trivial group to a nontrivial finite group.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.sur_test_not_injective` (computation): The reduction C₄→C₂ is an element of ContinuousSurjections with nontrivial kernel; replacing the carrier by continuous embeddings fails this test.

**Proof route.**

1. Take the surjective subtype of Mathlib’s continuous monoid homomorphisms; group domains make these group homomorphisms. Two maps with equal kernels differ by exactly one automorphism of the finite quotient. Use the type automorphism subgroup when preserving the embedded image.

**Acceptance checks.**

- There is one continuous surjection to the trivial group.
- There is no surjection from the trivial group to a nontrivial finite group.
- The reduction C₄→C₂ is an element of ContinuousSurjections with nontrivial kernel; replacing the carrier by continuous embeddings fails this test.

**Consumers.** Wood rigid moments — Count markings rather than only extension fields.

<a id="st0-wood-infinity-and-type-adapter"></a>

### 0.74 Marked global extensions and infinity conventions

For Q or F_q(t), fix a separable closure and the specified infinity embedding. K^(un,∞) is the maximal extension unramified at every finite place and split at all places above infinity; it is the full extension, without a prime-to quotient. Imaginary number fields have nonsplit archimedean infinity; in the function-field case choose specifically the completion F_q((t^−1))(sqrt(t)), excluding the other nonsplit squareclass. Real means infinity splits. An imaginary marked surjection obtains a canonical outside involution from infinity and hence an actual embedded wreath image H. In the real case one instead chooses an outside order-two twist y; the rigid object is the pair (ρ,y).

**Dependencies.** [Continuous marked surjections](#st0-wood-continuous-surjections) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-continuous-surjections`); [Outside involutions in a wreath type](#st0-wood-outside-involutions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-outside-involutions`); `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4/marked-arithmetic-extensions`; `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4/unramified-gamma-groups`; `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4`

**Sources.** [S0/wood19](#source-s0-wood19), §2 printed pp.383–385. Full unramified/split-infinity group and the pointed imaginary/real embeddings.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.woodFullUnramifiedInfinityGroup` (characterisation): Full profinite Galois group of K^(un,∞)/K, with its finite-quotient classification.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.woodImaginaryType` (characterisation): Image of the infinity-marked normal-closure embedding in the built wreath product.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.woodRealTwistType` (characterisation): Image of the normal-closure embedding attached to a real pair (ρ,y).
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.woodType_admissible` (characterisation): Every resulting embedded type is admissible (Wood Proposition 2.2).

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.woodInfinity_test_full` (non-example): A quotient with order divisible by Δ must not be excluded merely by the prime-to-Δ group supplier.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.woodInfinity_test_function_field` (non-example): Only the chosen sqrt(t) completion is in the imaginary function-field family, not every nonsplit completion.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.woodInfinity_test_real` (compatibility): A split-infinity real field has no canonical outside inertia involution; its rigid data include a twist y.

**Proof route.**

1. Import the marked arithmetic extension and normal-closure embedding. Verify the full universal extension has the continuous finite-quotient classification. The existing prime-to-Δ unramified group in IG.4 does not supply this full object; request its extension. For an index-two kernel and chosen y²=1 outside it, the two base coordinates are restriction to L and its y-conjugate; y maps to the canonical swap.

**Acceptance checks.**

- A quotient with order divisible by Δ must not be excluded merely by the prime-to-Δ group supplier.
- Only the chosen sqrt(t) completion is in the imaginary function-field family, not every nonsplit completion.
- A split-infinity real field has no canonical outside inertia involution; its rigid data include a twist y.

**Consumers.** Wood §2 rigid family definitions — Retain the infinity marking and actual wreath image, avoiding abstract-group type counts.

**Interface qualification.** Native global-field places, the full split-infinity maximal extension and its marked normal-closure representation are not simultaneously available at the pin. This exact construction is a supplier request, not a structure of unspecified proposition fields.

<a id="st0-wood-average-normalizations"></a>

### 0.75 Rigid finite-height and exact-slice averages

Use the parent discriminant family, restricting its base to the prescribed imaginary or real infinity type. The imaginary rigid numerator sums type-H continuous surjections; the real numerator sums type-H pairs (ρ,y). Divide both by the number of quadratic base fields in the same carrier. Over Q use |Disc(K)|≤X for a height average; over F_q(t) use exact |Disc(K)|=q^(2n) slices when applying ST.5’s parametrizations. A genuinely empty slice is assigned zero at the finite level; a claimed limiting statement must specify a sequence of inhabited slices. For fixed unmarked extensions the imaginary multiplicity is |Aut_H(G)|; in the good real case it is |c(H)|·|Aut_H(G)|.

**Dependencies.** [Number fields ordered by |Disc|: embedded fields, isomorphism classes, degree and automorphism weights](#st0-number-fields-ordered-by-discriminant) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/number-fields-ordered-by-discriminant`); [Imaginary discriminant slices over F_q(t) are monic squarefree polynomials of odd degree](#st5-imaginary-exact-slice-parametrization) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/imaginary-exact-slice-parametrization`); [Real discriminant slices over F_q(t) are monic squarefree polynomials of even degree](#st5-real-exact-slice-parametrization) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/real-exact-slice-parametrization`); [Good embedded type](#st0-wood-good-type) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-good-type`); [Type-preserving automorphisms](#st0-wood-type-automorphisms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-type-automorphisms`); [Marked global extensions and infinity conventions](#st0-wood-infinity-and-type-adapter) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-infinity-and-type-adapter`); `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4`

**Sources.** [S0/wood19](#source-s0-wood19), §2.1.1–2.1.2 pp.383–386, Lemma 2.1. Different rigid numerators, common base-field denominators and real multiplicity.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.wood_finite_multiplicity_transfer`.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.wood_average_test_trivial` (degenerate): For G=1 on an inhabited imaginary slice each base contributes one surjection and the average is one.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.wood_average_test_empty` (computation): An empty finite slice has assigned average zero.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.wood_average_test_markings` (computation): Two markings per extension multiply the numerator but not the base denominator.

**Proof route.**

1. Restrict the base carrier, then use the parent weighted count with the exact rigid fiber count as weight. Kernel fibers give the imaginary torsor factor. For real good H, Wood Lemma 2.1 conjugates twists inside the top kernel and counts c(H) choices, each with the same type-preserving automorphism fiber. Do not identify exact and cumulative slices. The function-field imaginary monic family is one leading-coefficient squareclass, not all odd-degree squarefree equations.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For G=1 on an inhabited imaginary slice each base contributes one surjection and the average is one.
- An empty finite slice has assigned average zero.
- Two markings per extension multiply the numerator but not the base denominator.

<a id="st0-wood-root-unity-and-tame-comparison"></a>

### 0.76 Root-of-unity and tame refinement comparisons

Wood’s correction is the |μ_K|-torsion subgroup of the reduced multiplier H₂(H,c), where μ_K is the roots-of-unity group of the base global field K. Over Q use 2; over F_q(t) use q−1. The reduced multiplier and global lifting invariant are imported from InductionRestrictionPartII RS.1 and InverseGalois IG.4. Restricting the quadratic base to the tame subfamily changes the denominator too. Moment counts refined by invariant value partition the rigid numerator; summing them does not by itself prove the arithmetic distribution law.

**Hypotheses.** Tame ramification and the lifting invariant’s hypotheses remain those of its owner.

**Dependencies.** `InductionRestrictionPartII:RS.1/reduced-multiplier`; `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4/global-arithmetic-invariant`; [Rigid finite-height and exact-slice averages](#st0-wood-average-normalizations) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-average-normalizations`)

**Sources.** [S0/wood19](#source-s0-wood19), §1 p.378 and §3 arithmetic invariant pp.388–393. The correction is base-field root-of-unity torsion; tame marking is an additional arithmetic restriction.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.root_unity_test_torsion`.

**Proof route.**

1. Reuse the reduced multiplier and its torsion subgroup. Check root-of-unity orders for the two bases. Apply finite partition identities to the already defined rigid fibers and the same tame base slice.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For a reduced multiplier C₃, 2-torsion has size 1 while 6-torsion has size 3; the q−1 correction can depend on q.

<a id="st0-monic-euler-products"></a>

### 0.77 Monic squarefree Euler constants

For n≥2 set λ_n=product over all primes of λ_n(p), with λ_n(p)=ν₀(n,p)+ν₁(n,p). The product converges to a strictly positive real number because its factors are positive and 1−λ_n(p)=O_n(p^−2). As n→∞ it tends to (1/2) times the product over odd primes of [1−(3p−1)/(p²(p+1))]. For degree two λ₂=4/π². These are local Euler constants; identifying them with global family densities still requires the infinite-prime tail theorem in ST.2.

**Dependencies.** [Correct monic local density formulas](#st0-monic-density-formulas) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/monic-density-formulas`)

**Sources.** [S0/bsw22](#source-s0-bsw22), §1 pp.1–2, constants λ_n and limiting λ. Positive Euler products and the limit in degree.

**API.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.monicEulerProduct` (data): The product over prime local factors.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.monicEulerProduct_pos` (characterisation): The degree-n product is strictly positive.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.monicEulerProduct_limit` (characterisation): The products tend to the limiting odd-prime product.

**Checks.**

- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.lambda_test_two` (computation): At 2 every degree≥2 monic factor is 1/2.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.lambda_test_quartic` (computation): The corrected monic quartic factor at 3 is 62/81.
- `ArithmeticStatistics.ST0.lambda_test_quadratic_global` (compatibility): The quadratic global local-product constant is 4/π².

**Proof route.**

1. Separate the factor at 2. Bound the defect at odd p by a summable constant times p^−2 uniformly for n≥2. Establish nonzero convergence from positivity and the defect bound. Pointwise convergence plus the uniform product tail permits exchanging the degree limit and the product.

**Acceptance checks.**

- At 2 every degree≥2 monic factor is 1/2.
- The corrected monic quartic factor at 3 is 62/81.
- The quadratic global local-product constant is 4/π².

**Consumers.** BSW I global asymptotic — Supply the candidate product without replacing the sieve proof.
