Define bounded sets of real binary quartic forms: L^(0) := {x^3y − (1/3)xy^3 − (J/27)y^4 : −2 < J < 2}; L^(1) := {x^3y − (I/3)xy^3 ± (2/27)y^4 : −1 ≤ I < 1} ∪ {x^3y + (1/3)xy^3 − (J/27)y^4 : −2 < J < 2}; L^(2+) := {(1/16)x^4 − (√(2 − J)/(3√3))x^3y + (1/2)x^2y^2 + y^4 : −2 < J < 2}; L^(2−) := {−f : f ∈ L^(2+)}. Then for each i ∈ T: (a) L^(i) ⊆ V_ℝ^(i) and every f ∈ L^(i) has H(f) = max(|I(f)|^3, J(f)^2/4) = 1; (b) f ↦ (I(f), J(f)) is a bijection from L^(i) onto {(I, J) : H(I, J) = 1, 4I^3 − J^2 > 0} (i ∈ {0, 2±}) or onto {(I, J) : H(I, J) = 1, 4I^3 − J^2 < 0} (i = 1); (c) every GL_2(ℝ)-orbit in V_ℝ^(i) meets L^(i) in exactly one point, and the same holds for h·L^(i) for every h ∈ GL_2(ℝ); (d) all coefficients of all forms in L^(i) have absolute value at most 1. Put R^(i) := Λ·L^(i) = {λ·f : λ > 0, f ∈ L^(i)} (λ·f = f((x, y)λ) = λ^4 f); then f ↦ (I(f), J(f)) is a bijection from R^(i) onto {(I, J) : 4I^3 − J^2 > 0} (resp. < 0), with inverse (I, J) ↦ p^(i)_{I,J}.

**Hypotheses.** The ± in the first family of L^(1) gives J = ∓2; Scaling by λ ∈ Λ multiplies (I, J) by (λ^8, λ^12), i.e. by (μ^2, μ^3) with μ = λ^4

**Dependencies.** [The loci V_ℝ^(0), V_ℝ^(1), V_ℝ^(2±) of real binary quartic forms by number of real roots and definiteness](#st2-real-root-types-of-binary-quartic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-root-types-of-binary-quartic-forms`); [Real binary quartic forms with given invariants form one or three SL_2^±(ℝ)-orbits](#st2-real-orbits-of-binary-quartic-forms-with-fixed-invariants) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-of-binary-quartic-forms-with-fixed-invariants`); [The eligible invariant pairs ordered by H(I, J), with the curve normalisation 27·H_E = 4·H′ (the binary-quartic invariant and height interface)](#st0-invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.1, Table 1, printed p. 8 (checked on the page image). The construction; the invariants of every family were recomputed. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.1, after Table 1, printed p. 8. Part (d) and the translate property (c). [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.4, printed p. 13. The scaled sets R^(i) and the section p^(i)_{I,J}.

**API.**

- `quarticFundSet` (constructor): quarticFundSet i = L^(i) ⊆ V_ℝ, given by the explicit parametrisations of Table 1.
- `quarticFundSet_subset_locus` (relation): L^(i) ⊆ V_ℝ^(i).
- `height_eq_one_of_mem_quarticFundSet` (simp): f ∈ L^(i) → H(f) = 1.
- `invariants_bijOn_quarticFundSet` (equivalence): (I, J) is a bijection from L^(i) onto the height-one pairs with the sign condition of i.
- `existsUnique_smul_mem_quarticFundSet` (characterisation): For f ∈ V_ℝ^(i) and h ∈ GL_2(ℝ) there is a unique f′ ∈ h·L^(i) that is GL_2(ℝ)-equivalent to f.
- `abs_coeff_le_one_of_mem_quarticFundSet` (other): Every coefficient of every f ∈ L^(i) has absolute value ≤ 1 (boundedness).
- `quarticSection` (data): The section p^(i) : {(I, J) : sign condition} → R^(i) = Λ·L^(i) with invariants (I, J).
- `invariants_quarticSection` (simp): (I, J)(p^(i)_{I,J}) = (I, J).

**Checks.**

- `quarticFundSet.zero_example` (computation): x^3y − (1/3)xy^3 ∈ L^(0), with (I, J) = (1, 0).
- `quarticFundSet.one_boundary` (computation): x^3y + (1/3)xy^3 − (2/27)y^4 ∈ L^(1) with (I, J) = (−1, 2); it lies in the first family (I = −1, sign −) and not in the second (which has |J| < 2).
- `quarticFundSet.not_boundary` (non-example): No form in L^(0) ∪ L^(1) ∪ L^(2±) has invariants (1, 2): that pair has Δ = 0.
- `quarticFundSet.twoNeg` (degenerate): L^(2−) = −L^(2+), and f ↦ −f sends (I, J) to (I, −J).

**Proof route.**

1. Compute invariants: for x^3y − (1/3)xy^3 − (J/27)y^4, I = −3·1·(−1/3) = 1 and J(f) = −27·(−J/27) = J; for x^3y − (I/3)xy^3 ± (2/27)y^4, (I(f), J(f)) = (I, ∓2); for x^3y + (1/3)xy^3 − (J/27)y^4, (I(f), J(f)) = (−1, J); for the L^(2+) forms, I = 12/16 + 1/4 = 1 and J = 9/4 − 27·(2 − J)/27 − 1/4 = J. Hence H = 1 and the sign of 4I^3 − J^2 is as stated, and the pieces of the curve H = 1 are covered bijectively: for Δ < 0 the curve H(I, J) = 1 is {I = −1, |J| ≤ 2} ∪ {|J| = 2, −1 ≤ I < 1}, matching the two families with the overlap (−1, ±2) assigned to the first.
2. The root types: x^3 − x/3 − J/27 has discriminant (4 − J^2)/27 > 0 for |J| < 2, so the L^(0) forms (with the root [1 : 0]) have four real roots; the L^(1) forms have 4I^3 − J^2 < 0 and hence two real roots by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-of-binary-quartic-forms-with-fixed-invariants; the L^(2+) forms are positive definite (positive at J near 2 and Δ ≠ 0 on the connected parameter interval).
3. (c) from (b), H(λ^2 I, λ^3 J) = λ^6 H(I, J) (a unique λ > 0 normalises the height to 1) and part (c) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-of-binary-quartic-forms-with-fixed-invariants; h·L^(i) inherits the property since h permutes the GL_2(ℝ)-orbits trivially.
4. (d): |J| < 2 and −1 ≤ I < 1 bound the listed coefficients by 1 (the largest is |√(2 − J)/(3√3)| < 2/(3√3) < 1).

**Acceptance checks.**

- x^3y − (1/3)xy^3 ∈ L^(0) has invariants (1, 0); x^3y + (1/3)xy^3 − (2/27)y^4 ∈ L^(1) has invariants (−1, 2); the point (I, J) = (1, 2) with Δ = 0 is not attained.
- Coefficient bound constant: C^4 with C = 1 works for L^(i) itself; for G_0·L the constant C of Proposition 2.7 depends on G_0.

**Consumers.** Bhargava-Shankar, (10) and Theorem 2.5 — the multiset F h·L^(i) is the region whose lattice points are averaged over h ∈ G_0; Bhargava-Shankar, Proposition 2.7 — the constant C with C^4 bounding the coefficients of G_0·L controls the cusp cut-off Cλ < t; Bhargava-Shankar, Section 2.4 and Proposition 2.8 — R^(i) = Λ·L^(i) is the section of the invariant map used in the change of measure; Bhargava-Shankar, Section 2.6, Theorems 2.18 and 2.20 — F^(ε)·R^(i)(X) is the bounded, homogeneously expanding region to which the geometric sieve is applied

<a id="st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates"></a>

### 2.16 Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure

Every g ∈ GL_2(ℝ) with det g > 0 has a unique Iwasawa decomposition g = n(u)a(t)k(θ)λ with n(u) = [[1, 0], [u, 1]] (u ∈ ℝ), a(t) = diag(t^{−1}, t) (t > 0), k(θ) = [[cos θ, sin θ], [−sin θ, cos θ]] (θ ∈ ℝ/2πℤ) and λ = λ·1 (λ > 0). The measure dg = t^{−2} du d^×t dk d^×λ (d^×t = dt/t, d^×λ = dλ/λ, dk = dθ/2π of total mass 1 on SO_2(ℝ)) is a Haar measure on GL_2^+(ℝ). Let ν(t) := {u ∈ [−1/2, 1/2] : u^2 + t^4 ≥ 1}, N′(t) := {n(u) : u ∈ ν(t)}, A′ := {a(t) : t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2}, K_+ := {k(θ) : 0 ≤ θ < π} and Λ := {λ·1 : λ > 0}. Then F := N′(t)A′K_+Λ is a fundamental domain for the left action of GL_2(ℤ) on GL_2(ℝ) (GL_2(ℝ) = ⋃_{γ ∈ GL_2(ℤ)} γF up to a null set, the translates pairwise almost disjoint), and its image F_PGL2 in PGL_2(ℝ) is a fundamental domain for PGL_2(ℤ). Moreover g ↦ z(g) := −u + it^2 identifies N′(t)A′ with the standard domain fd of the upper half-plane, and t^{−2} du d^×t = (1/2)·dx dy/y^2 under z = x + iy.

**Hypotheses.** K_+ is a set of representatives of SO_2(ℝ)/{±1}; with the full SO_2(ℝ), as printed in the source, F would contain both g and −g ∈ GL_2(ℤ)g and would be a union of two fundamental domains (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E301); GL_2(ℤ) acts on the left; F ⊆ GL_2^+(ℝ), which suffices because GL_2(ℤ) contains matrices of determinant −1; ν(t) is a union of one or two intervals depending only on t, and ν(t) = [−1/2, 1/2] for t ≥ 1; The circular and vertical edges of the upper-half-plane region are included, so K_+ only removes the central ±1 ambiguity: this remains a measure-theoretic fundamental domain, not an exact transversal on its boundary. Exact pointwise orbit-multiplicity claims require a boundary selector, or the almost-everywhere-in-h formulation used below.

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:ModularGroup.fd`; `mathlib:ModularGroup.fdo`; `mathlib:ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd`; `mathlib:ModularGroup.eq_smul_self_of_mem_fdo_mem_fdo`; `tauceti:ModularGroup.isFundamentalDomain_fdo`; `mathlib:MeasureTheory.IsFundamentalDomain`; `mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.1, (7), printed p. 8 (checked on the page image). The construction; K is replaced by K_+ = SO_2(ℝ)/{±1} (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E301). [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.3, the Haar measure after (10), printed pp. 10-11. The Haar measure; its density was re-derived. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.1, (15), p. 10. The same domain in the cubic paper, with the fact about ν(t) used in the slicing and cusp estimates.

**API.**

- `iwasawaN` (constructor): n(u) = [[1, 0], [u, 1]].
- `iwasawaA` (constructor): a(t) = diag(t^{−1}, t) for t > 0.
- `iwasawaK` (constructor): k(θ) = [[cos θ, sin θ], [−sin θ, cos θ]].
- `iwasawa_existsUnique` (characterisation): det g > 0 → ∃! (u, t, θ mod 2π, λ) with t, λ > 0 and g = n(u)a(t)k(θ)λ.
- `gaussDomain` (constructor): F = {n(u)a(t)k(θ)λ : u ∈ ν(t), t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2, 0 ≤ θ < π, λ > 0}.
- `mem_gaussDomain_iff` (characterisation): For t,lambda>0 and the canonical representative 0≤theta<2pi, n(u)a(t)k(theta)lambda lies in F iff −u+it² lies in fd and theta<pi. The angular restriction is essential because k is periodic.
- `isFundamentalDomain_gaussDomain` (characterisation): F is a measure-theoretic fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ) acting on GL_2(ℝ) by left multiplication, for the Haar measure dg.
- `gaussDomain_haar` (data): The Haar measure dg = t^{−2} du d^×t dk d^×λ in Iwasawa coordinates, as a measure on GL_2^+(ℝ).
- `neg_mem_gaussDomain_iff` (relation): g ∈ F → −g ∉ F (the half circle K_+ removes the ±1 ambiguity).

**Checks.**

- `gaussDomain.one_mem` (computation): 1 ∈ F: its coordinates are u = 0, t = 1, θ = 0, λ = 1.
- `gaussDomain.neg_one_not_mem` (non-example): −1 ∉ F (θ = π), although −1 = (−1)·1 with −1 ∈ GL_2(ℤ): with the full SO_2(ℝ) both would lie in F.
- `gaussDomain.det_pos` (degenerate): Every g ∈ F has det g = λ^2 > 0; diag(1, −1) ∉ F.
- `gaussDomain.nu_full` (characterisation): For t ≥ 1, n(u)a(t)k(0) ∈ F ↔ |u| ≤ 1/2.

**Proof route.**

1. Iwasawa: Gram-Schmidt on the rows of g gives g = (lower unitriangular)(positive diagonal)(orthogonal); det g > 0 forces the orthogonal factor into SO_2(ℝ), and the diagonal factor is a(t)λ. Uniqueness from N ∩ AΛ ∩ SO_2 = {1}.
2. Haar density: the left-invariant form g^{−1}dg in these coordinates has density proportional to t^{−3}λ^{−1} (a direct computation), i.e. t^{−2} du d^×t dθ d^×λ.
3. Upper half-plane: the positive definite binary quadratic form (x, y)gg^T(x, y)^T equals λ^2 t^{−2}((x + uy)^2 + t^4y^2), whose root in the upper half-plane is z(g) = −u + it^2; left multiplication by γ ∈ SL_2(ℤ) acts on z(g) by the Möbius action of γ (up to the transpose-inverse convention), and k(θ), λ do not change z(g). The conditions u ∈ ν(t), t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2 say exactly |Re z| ≤ 1/2 and |z| ≥ 1, i.e. z(g) ∈ fd (ModularGroup.fd).
4. Covering and disjointness: a GL_2(ℤ)-coset meets GL_2^+(ℝ) in one SL_2(ℤ)-coset. By ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd every z is moved into fd, and by ModularGroup.eq_smul_self_of_mem_fdo_mem_fdo (or the measure form ModularGroup.isFundamentalDomain_fdo of Tau Ceti, a MeasureTheory.IsFundamentalDomain for PSL_2(ℤ)) two points of the open domain in one orbit coincide; the kernel {±1} of SL_2(ℤ) → PSL_2(ℤ) acts on the K-coordinate by θ ↦ θ + π, which K_+ resolves.
5. Measure: with y = t^2, dy = 2t dt, so dx dy/y^2 = 2t^{−3} du dt = 2t^{−2} du d^×t.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The identity 1 = n(0)a(1)k(0)·1 lies in F (z = i, on the boundary |z| = 1), and −1 = n(0)a(1)k(π)·1 does not, although −1 ∈ GL_2(ℤ)·1.
- For t ≥ 1 the slice N′(t) is the whole interval [−1/2, 1/2].
- F contains no matrix of negative determinant.

**Consumers.** Bhargava-Shankar, (10)-(17) and Theorem 2.5 — the multiset F h·L^(i) is n_i fundamental domains for GL_2(ℤ) on V_ℝ^(i), and the Iwasawa coordinates of F carry the t- and λ-integrals; Bhargava-Shankar, Section 2.4 — F_PGL2 has ω-volume 2ζ(2), the archimedean factor of the count; Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman, Section 5, (16)-(26) — the same domain acting on binary cubic forms, with the cusp t → ∞; ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4/average-size-of-the-2-selmer-group-is-three — Vol(PGL_2(ℤ)\PGL_2(ℝ)) = 2ζ(2) enters the Tamagawa number 2

<a id="st2-hyperbolic-area-of-the-modular-fundamental-domain"></a>

### 2.17 The standard fundamental domain of SL_2(ℤ) has hyperbolic area π/3

For the invariant measure on the upper half-plane (Mathlib's volume on ℍ, density 1/(Im z)^2 with respect to Lebesgue measure), volume(ModularGroup.fd) = π/3.

**Hypotheses.** The measure is Mathlib's MeasureSpace instance on ℍ

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:ModularGroup.fd`; `mathlib:UpperHalfPlane.volume_eq_lintegral`; `tauceti:ModularGroup.volume_fd_lt_top`; `mathlib:Real.hasDerivAt_arcsin`; `mathlib:intervalIntegral.integral_deriv_eq_sub`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.4, p. 14. The fundamental volume computed from Gauss's domain; the hyperbolic area π/3 is the input (see ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/covolume-of-pgl2-z for the normalisations).

**Proof route.**

1. By UpperHalfPlane.volume_eq_lintegral, volume(fd) = ∫∫ y^{−2} dy dx over {|x| ≤ 1/2, y ≥ √(1 − x^2)}.
2. The inner integral is ∫_{√(1−x^2)}^∞ y^{−2} dy = (1 − x^2)^{−1/2}.
3. ∫_{−1/2}^{1/2} (1 − x^2)^{−1/2} dx = arcsin(1/2) − arcsin(−1/2) = π/3 by the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_deriv_eq_sub with Real.hasDerivAt_arcsin; the integrand is continuous on [−1/2, 1/2]).

**Acceptance checks.**

- The value refines Tau Ceti's ModularGroup.volume_fd_lt_top (finiteness only).
- π/3 = 2ζ(2)/π, the form in which the value enters the volume computations.

<a id="st2-covolume-of-pgl2-z"></a>

### 2.18 Vol(PGL_2(ℤ)\PGL_2(ℝ)) = 2ζ(2) for the ℤ-form ω, and the Iwasawa-measure volume of Gauss's domain

(a) Let ω be the left-invariant top form on PGL_2(ℝ) whose value at the identity is the dual of the ℤ-basis E_11, E_12, E_21 of pgl_2(ℤ) = gl_2(ℤ)/ℤ·1 (well defined up to sign; |ω| is the associated Haar measure). In the coordinates [n(u)a(t)k(θ)] of PGL_2^+(ℝ), |ω| = 2t^{−3} du dt dθ, and Vol_ω(F_PGL2) = Vol_ω(PGL_2(ℤ)\PGL_2(ℝ)) = 2ζ(2) = π^2/3. (b) For the Haar measure dg = t^{−2} du d^×t dk d^×λ of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates, the domain N′(t)A′K_+ (λ omitted) has measure π/12 = ζ(2)/(2π); equivalently Vol(GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2^{±1}(ℝ)) = ζ(2)/(2π). (c) On PGL_2^+(ℝ), |ω| = 4π·t^{−2} du d^×t dk.

**Hypotheses.** F is the strict domain with K_+ (θ ∈ [0, π)); with the full circle both volumes double; ω is determined by the ℤ-structure of PGL_2 up to sign, as in the source

**Dependencies.** [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`); [The standard fundamental domain of SL_2(ℤ) has hyperbolic area π/3](#st2-hyperbolic-area-of-the-modular-fundamental-domain) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/hyperbolic-area-of-the-modular-fundamental-domain`); `mathlib:riemannZeta_two`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.4, (23), printed p. 13. Part (a); the source quotes Langlands [33], and the proof steps compute it directly. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.4, printed p. 13. The normalisation of ω. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.4, p. 14. Part (b), with the corrected value ζ(2)/(2π) (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E305).

**Proof route.**

1. (a) Compute g^{−1}dg for g = n(u)a(t)k(θ) and express it modulo scalars in the basis E_11, E_12, E_21 (the E_11-coordinate of X ∈ gl_2 modulo scalars is X_11 − X_22): the determinant of the resulting 3 × 3 matrix of one-forms is −2t^{−3} du dt dθ (a direct computation).
2. Integrate over F_PGL2: θ ranges over [0, π) and (u, t) over N′(t)A′; with y = t^2, 2t^{−3} du dt = du dy/y^2, so Vol_ω = π·volume(fd) = π·π/3 = π^2/3 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/hyperbolic-area-of-the-modular-fundamental-domain; and 2ζ(2) = π^2/3 by riemannZeta_two.
3. (b) ∫ t^{−2} du d^×t over N′(t)A′ equals (1/2)·volume(fd) = π/6, and K_+ has dk-mass 1/2; the product is π/12 = ζ(2)/(2π).
4. (c) Compare the densities: 2t^{−3} du dt dθ = 4π·t^{−2} du d^×t (dθ/2π).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Tamagawa check: 2ζ(2)·∏_p (1 − p^{−2}) = 2, the Tamagawa number of PGL_2 used by Bhargava-Shankar at the end of Section 3.6.
- Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman state Vol(GL_2^{±1}(ℤ)\GL_2^{±1}(ℝ)) = ζ(2)/π; the value here is ζ(2)/(2π), and the factor 2 is compensated by the Jacobian constant of their Proposition 23 (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E305).
- Independent check: the ω-volume π^2/3 was recomputed symbolically from the Maurer-Cartan form.

<a id="st2-orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets"></a>

### 2.19 The multiset F h·L^(i) is n_i fundamental domains: orbit multiplicities m(x) = #Stab_{GL_2(ℝ)}(x)/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x)

Let i∈T and let F be the Gauss region with K_+, retaining the boundary of the modular domain. For each fixed x∈V_R^(i), for Haar-almost every h∈GL2^+(R), the sum of multiplicities in Fh·L^(i) over the GL2(Z)-orbit of x equals m(x)=#Stab_GL2(R)(x)/#Stab_GL2(Z)(x), an integer between 1 and n_i. This ratio equals n_i whenever the integral stabilizer is {±1}, and for almost every real x. For the countable set of integral x, choose one common conull set of h. On that set the irreducible count of height<X, with multiplicity, is the sum over classes of n_i·2/#Stab_GL2(Z)(x). Consequently the averaged count has these class weights. The assertion for every h would require an exact boundary selector, which F as defined does not supply.

**Hypotheses.** F must be the strict domain (K_+); with the full SO_2(ℝ) every multiplicity doubles (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E301); N(S; X) is the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible elements of S of height < X

**Dependencies.** [Lemma 2.2: stabilisers in GL_2(ℝ) of real binary quartic forms, and the weights n_i](#st2-stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms`); [The fundamental sets L^(i) of Table 1 and their scalings R^(i) = Λ·L^(i)](#st2-fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.1, the claim (8) and its proof, printed p. 9. Part (a). [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.1, printed p. 9. Parts (b) and (c).

**Proof route.**

1. For fixed x choose the unique point x_L of L^(i) in its real orbit. The set of g taking x_L to x is a finite coset of its real stabilizer. For each gamma∈GL2(Z), the condition that one of the corresponding points of gamma g Stab(x_L) h^{-1} lies on the boundary of F defines a Haar-null set of h, by translation and inversion invariance of Haar measure. The countable union over gamma and the finite stabilizer remains null.
2. Outside this null set each relevant GL2(Z)-coset meets F exactly once. The double-coset calculation then gives #Stab_GL2(R)(x)/#Stab_GL2(Z)(x). Both stabilizers contain ±1, giving the bounds and the claimed class weight.
3. For each gamma outside {±1}, its fixed locus on binary quartics is a proper linear subspace. Countability of GL2(Z) makes their union null, so the generic ratio is n_i. For integral x use the countable union of the exceptional h-sets to obtain the common conull set needed to sum the counts.
4. Integrate over a compact averaging set of positive Haar measure. Boundary changes have no effect on this integral; a null set in the real coefficient space alone would not justify discarding integral points.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For x=x⁴+y⁴, m(x)=1. If h sends the chosen L^(2+) representative to x, both g=1 and g=k(pi/2) lie in F and fix x, so the point has multiplicity at least two for this exceptional h. This refutes the former assertion for every h and tests the boundary qualification.
- For x=x³y−xy³, the integral stabilizer contains the quarter-turn and has order at least four, so m(x)≤2<n_0. The ratio, rather than a pointwise boundary count, is what controls the averaged formula.

<a id="st2-averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits"></a>

### 2.20 The averaged orbit count N(S; X) of binary quartic forms and the regions B(n, t, λ, X)

Fix a compact semialgebraic set G_0 ⊂ GL_2(ℝ) that is left SO_2(ℝ)-invariant, is the closure of a nonempty open set, and has det h ≥ 1 for h ∈ G_0; let dh be the Haar measure of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates and F the strict Gauss domain. For i ∈ T, S ⊆ V_ℤ^(i) (not necessarily GL_2(ℤ)-invariant) and X > 0 define N(S; X) := (1/C_{G_0}^(i)) ∫_{h ∈ G_0} #{x ∈ F h·L^(i) ∩ S^irr : H(x) < X} dh, where C_{G_0}^(i) := n_i ∫_{G_0} dh, S^irr is the set of elements of S irreducible over ℚ, and the count is taken with the multiplicities of the multiset F h·L^(i). For a weight φ : V_ℤ → ℝ, N_φ(S; X) is defined in the same way with each x counted with weight φ(x). For n = n(u), t > 0, λ > 0 put B(n, t, λ, X) := n a(t) λ G_0·L^(i) ∩ {x ∈ V_ℝ^(i) : H(x) < X}, a bounded semialgebraic multiset.

**Hypotheses.** G_0, i and the fundamental set L^(i) are fixed; for GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S the value does not depend on G_0; Only irreducible elements are counted; H is the height max(|I|^3, J^2/4) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs; G_0 is a set of matrices with Haar measure. An arbitrary subset of Iwasawa coordinate space can cover the same matrix different numbers of times; invariance of its image alone does not give the invariant averaging measure. The prototype now integrates on the matrix carrier. The general semialgebraic predicate and multiset Davenport interface remain GN.4 supplier work.

**Dependencies.** [The fundamental sets L^(i) of Table 1 and their scalings R^(i) = Λ·L^(i)](#st2-fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`); [The multiset F h·L^(i) is n_i fundamental domains: orbit multiplicities m(x) = #Stab_{GL_2(ℝ)}(x)/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x)](#st2-orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets`); [Lemma 2.2: stabilisers in GL_2(ℝ) of real binary quartic forms, and the weights n_i](#st2-stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms`); [The eligible invariant pairs ordered by H(I, J), with the curve normalisation 27·H_E = 4·H′ (the binary-quartic invariant and height interface)](#st0-invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.3, (10), printed p. 10. The hypotheses on G_0. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.3, (11) and the sentence after it, printed p. 11. The definition for arbitrary S. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Theorem 2.5, (17), printed p. 11. The regions B(n, t, λ, X).

**API.**

- `quarticAveragedCount` (constructor): N(S; X) for S ⊆ V_ℤ, with G_0 and i as parameters, by the formula (11).
- `quarticAveragedCount_weighted` (constructor): N_φ(S; X), the same average with weights φ(x).
- `quarticRegionB` (data): B(n, t, λ, X) = n a(t) λ G_0·L^(i) ∩ {H < X} as a multiset in V_ℝ.
- `quarticAveragedCount_eq_sum_classes` (compatibility): For GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S: N(S; X) = Σ over irreducible classes [x] ⊆ S with H(x) < X of 2/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x).
- `quarticAveragedCount_union` (structure): N(S_1 ∪ S_2; X) = N(S_1; X) + N(S_2; X) for disjoint S_1, S_2.
- `quarticAveragedCount_mono` (relation): S_1 ⊆ S_2 → N(S_1; X) ≤ N(S_2; X), and X ↦ N(S; X) is monotone.
- `quarticAveragedCount_indep` (characterisation): For GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S, N(S; X) does not depend on G_0 or on the choice of the fundamental set L^(i).
- `quarticAveragedCount_reducible` (simp): N(S; X) = 0 when every element of S is reducible over ℚ (for example when every element has a = 0).

**Checks.**

- `quarticAveragedCount.empty` (degenerate): N(∅; X) = 0 for every X, and N(S; X) = 0 for every S when X ≤ 1: by Theorem 1.7 every integral binary quartic form with Δ ≠ 0 has height at least 49/4, attained at the eligible pairs (I, J) = (−2, ±7).
- `quarticAveragedCount.reducible_zero` (computation): For S = {f ∈ V_ℤ^(i) : a(f) = 0}, N(S; X) = 0: every such form has the linear factor y.
- `quarticAveragedCount.not_orbit_count` (non-example): For a single point S = {f} with f irreducible and trivial stabiliser, N(S; X) = (1/C) ∫_{G_0} mult_{F h·L}(f) dh, which is in general strictly between 0 and 1: on non-invariant sets N(·; X) is not a count of orbits.
- `quarticAveragedCount.invariant` (compatibility): For S = V_ℤ^(i), N(S; X) = Σ_{[x]} 2/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x) over the irreducible classes of height < X, independently of G_0.

**Proof route.**

1. On a compact averaging set the height bound and a≠0 for irreducible forms bound lambda and then the cusp parameter t by the leading-coefficient estimate. Thus the union of contributing integral irreducible points is bounded and finite. Their finite multiplicity functions are measurable (using the semialgebraic descriptions), so the count and each fixed weighted count are integrable.
2. For GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets gives, for Haar-almost every h (one common conull set for the countable integral lattice), #{x ∈ F h·L^(i) ∩ S^irr : H(x) < X} = Σ over irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-classes [x] ⊆ S of height < X of n_i·2/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x); averaging over h gives N(S; X) = Σ_{[x]} 2/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x), which is the number of classes counted with weight 1 except for the classes with a stabiliser larger than {±1}.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For S = V_ℤ^(i), N(S; X) differs from the number of irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-classes in V_ℤ^(i) of height < X by at most the number of classes with stabiliser larger than {±1}, which is O(X^{3/4+ε}) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbits-with-large-stabilizer-are-negligible).
- N(S_1 ⊔ S_2; X) = N(S_1; X) + N(S_2; X) for disjoint S_1, S_2, invariant or not: the definition (11) of the source extends N to all subsets.

**Consumers.** Bhargava-Shankar, Theorem 2.5 and (18)-(20) — N(V_ℤ^(i); X) is evaluated through the averaged count; Bhargava-Shankar, Section 2.5, (27) — N(L_j; X) for non-invariant lattice translates L_j is the averaged count; Bhargava-Shankar, Theorems 2.12, 2.13 and 2.21 — weighted averaged counts N_φ and the tail N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(V); X); ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4/average-size-of-the-2-selmer-group-is-three — the weighted count of locally soluble forms with weight 1/m(f) is an N_φ

<a id="st2-averaging-formula-for-binary-quartic-forms"></a>

### 2.21 Theorem 2.5: the averaging formula N(S; X) as an integral over N′A′Λ of lattice-point counts in B(n, t, λ, X)

For every i ∈ T, every S ⊆ V_ℤ^(i) and every X > 0, N(S; X) = (1/(2C_{G_0}^(i))) ∫_{n(u)a(t)λ ∈ N′(t)A′Λ} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ B(n, t, λ, X)} t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ, where the count in B is with multiplicity, dk has total mass 1 on SO_2(ℝ), and F is the strict domain N′(t)A′K_+Λ. (If, as printed in the source, the K-factor of F is all of SO_2(ℝ), the same computation gives the identity without the factor 1/2, but then the average (11) with C_{G_0}^(i) = n_i∫_{G_0} dh is twice the orbit count; normalising by 2n_i∫_{G_0} dh instead gives exactly the statement here.)

**Hypotheses.** S arbitrary; the proof uses only the definition of N(S; X), Fubini and the invariance of Haar measure; The factor 1/2 is ∫_{K_+} dk (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E301)

**Dependencies.** [The averaged orbit count N(S; X) of binary quartic forms and the regions B(n, t, λ, X)](#st2-averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`); [The multiset F h·L^(i) is n_i fundamental domains: orbit multiplicities m(x) = #Stab_{GL_2(ℝ)}(x)/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x)](#st2-orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.3, (12)-(15) and Theorem 2.5 with (16), printed p. 11. The theorem; the constant is adjusted to the strict fundamental domain (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E301).

**Proof route.**

1. Write the integrand of the definition as a sum over x ∈ S^irr with H(x) < X of #{g ∈ F : x = gh·x_L}, where x_L is the point of L^(i) in the GL_2(ℝ)-orbit of x (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits).
2. For fixed x with x = g_j·x_L (finitely many g_j, one for each element of the stabiliser), ∫_{G_0} #{g ∈ F : gh = g_j} dh = Σ_j vol(G_0 ∩ F^{−1}g_j) = Σ_j vol(G_0 g_j^{−1} ∩ F^{−1}) by invariance of dh (GL_2(ℝ) is unimodular), which equals ∫_{g ∈ F} #{h ∈ G_0 : x = gh·x_L} dg.
3. Exchange sum and integral: N(S; X) = (1/C) ∫_{g ∈ F} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ gG_0·L : H(x) < X} dg.
4. Write g = n(u)a(t)kλ with k ∈ K_+: since kG_0 = G_0 (left SO_2(ℝ)-invariance) the integrand does not depend on k, and ∫_{K_+} dk = 1/2, which gives the formula with B(n, t, λ, X) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits).
5. The Gauss region is only a transversal away from its boundary; use the almost-everywhere-in-h multiplicity statement. The Fubini change of variables is on GL2^+(R) with genuine Haar measure and G_0 as a matrix set, not a coordinate set with uncontrolled angular multiplicity.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Sanity check of the constant: inserting Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) for the count and unfolding the integral over the full SO_2(ℝ) gives ∫ Vol(B) t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ = 2∫_{G_0} Vol(F h·L ∩ {H < X}) dh, hence the main term Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/n_i of (20).
- For S invariant under GL_2(ℤ) the right side is independent of G_0, as is the left side.

<a id="st2-reducible-binary-quartic-forms-in-the-main-body"></a>

### 2.22 Lemma 2.3: reducible integral binary quartic forms with a ≠ 0 in R_X(h·L^(i)) number O(X^{2/3+ε})

Let G_0 ⊂ GL_2(ℝ) be compact and h ∈ G_0. For every ε > 0 the number of integral binary quartic forms f = ax^4 + bx^3y + cx^2y^2 + dxy^3 + ey^4 in the multiset R_X(h·L^(i)) := {w ∈ F h·L^(i) : H(w) < X} (counted with multiplicity) that are reducible over ℚ and have a ≠ 0 is O_ε(X^{2/3+ε}), the implied constant depending only on G_0 and ε.

**Hypotheses.** Only forms with a ≠ 0: the forms with a = 0 in the cusp are reducible and are excluded from the counts by other means (they are never irreducible); Multiplicities are at most n_i ≤ 4; When concluding that O(X^{3/4+epsilon}) is lower order than X^{5/6}, choose 0<epsilon<1/12; the bound itself is stated for every positive epsilon.

**Dependencies.** [The fundamental sets L^(i) of Table 1 and their scalings R^(i) = Λ·L^(i)](#st2-fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`); [The multiset F h·L^(i) is n_i fundamental domains: orbit multiplicities m(x) = #Stab_{GL_2(ℝ)}(x)/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x)](#st2-orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets`); `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.2, Lemma 2.3, printed p. 9. The lemma (the printed 'cy2' is a misprint for cx2y2; sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E306). [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Proof of Lemma 2.3, printed p. 10. The divisor-bound step.

**Proof route.**

1. Coefficient bounds: R_X(h·L) ⊆ N′A′KΛh·L with h·L in a fixed compact set and 0 < λ ≪_{G_0} X^{1/24} (H scales by λ^24 and det(h)^12, with |det(h)| bounded away from zero on the compact subset G_0 of GL2(R)). Hence a, b, c = O(X^{1/6}) and ad, bd, ae = O(X^{1/3}); in particular the forms with a ≠ 0 and e = 0 number O(X^{4/6+ε}).
2. Linear factor, a, e ≠ 0: the quadruple (a, b, d, e) has O(X^{4/6+ε}) possibilities; a linear factor px + qy (p, q coprime) has p | a and q | e, so O(X^ε) choices by the divisor bound d(n) = O_ε(n^ε) (requested from AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5); then f(−q, p) = 0 determines c.
3. Product of two irreducible quadratics (px^2 + qxy + ry^2)((a/p)x^2 + sxy + (e/r)y^2): O(X^{2/6+ε}) pairs (a, e) (ae = O(X^{1/3})), O(X^ε) pairs (p, r) by the divisor bound; if the linear system (a/p)q + ps = b, (e/r)q + rs = d is nonsingular, (b, d) determine (q, s) and then c, giving O(X^{4/6+ε}); if singular, d = (r/p)b is determined by b and there are O(X^{1/6}) choices each for b and c, again O(X^{4/6+ε}).
4. Multiply by the bounded multiplicity.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Order check: X^{2/3+ε} is smaller than the main term X^{5/6} and than the error X^{3/4+ε} of Theorem 2.1.
- The analogous cubic statement is ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body, with X^{3/4+ε}.

<a id="st2-reducible-monic-binary-cubic-forms"></a>

### 2.23 Lemma 2.22: reducible monic integral binary cubic forms of bounded height number O(X^{1/2+ε}) up to unipotent equivalence

For a monic integral binary cubic form g = x^3 + rx^2y + sxy^2 + ty^3 put I(g) := r^2 − 3s, J(g) := −2r^3 + 9rs − 27t and H(g) := max(|I(g)|^3, J(g)^2/4); these are invariant under the group F_{ℤ,1} of lower unitriangular integer matrices acting by g ↦ g((x, y)γ). For every ε > 0 the number of F_{ℤ,1}-orbits of monic integral binary cubic forms that are reducible over ℚ and have H(g) < X is O_ε(X^{1/2+ε}).

**Hypotheses.** Monic means g(1, 0) = 1; The invariants agree with those of the binary quartic whose monic cubic resolvent is g (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/embedding-into-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms)

**Dependencies.** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.8, Lemma 2.22 and its proof, printed p. 21. The lemma, with the invariants (46) and the normalisation r ∈ {−1, 0, 1} of the proof.

**Proof route.**

1. The substitution x ↦ x + ky changes r by 3k, so every F_{ℤ,1}-orbit has a representative with r ∈ {−1, 0, 1}.
2. Then |r^2 − 3s|^3 < X gives s = O(X^{1/3}) and J^2/4 < X gives t = O(X^{1/2}).
3. t = 0 (the factor x): O(X^{1/3}) forms. t ≠ 0: a linear factor x − my has m | t, so O(X^ε) choices of m for each t (divisor bound, requested from AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5); r, t, m then determine s through g(m, 1) = 0. Total O(X^{1/2+ε}).

**Acceptance checks.**

- The count of all monic forms with r ∈ {−1, 0, 1} and H < X is of order X^{1/3}·X^{1/2} = X^{5/6}, so reducibility saves X^{1/3}.
- F_{ℤ,1}-invariance: g(x + ky, y) has the same I and J (a direct computation).

<a id="st2-orbits-with-large-stabilizer-are-negligible"></a>

### 2.24 Lemma 2.4: GL_2(ℤ)-orbits of binary quartic forms with stabiliser in GL_2(ℚ) of order > 2 number O(X^{3/4+ε})

For every ε > 0 the number of GL_2(ℤ)-orbits of integral binary quartic forms f with Δ(f) ≠ 0, H(f) < X and #Stab_{GL_2(ℚ)}(f) > 2 is O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}). In particular the same bound holds for the orbits whose stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ) is larger than {±1}.

**Hypotheses.** The stabiliser is for the standard action; its image in PGL_2(ℚ) is nontrivial exactly when #Stab_{GL_2(ℚ)}(f) > 2; When concluding that O(X^{3/4+epsilon}) is lower order than X^{5/6}, choose 0<epsilon<1/12; the bound itself is stated for every positive epsilon.

**Dependencies.** [Bhargava-Shankar Theorem 3.2: Stab_{PGL2(K)}(f) is isomorphic to E(K)[2]](#st1-stabilizer-of-a-binary-quartic-is-two-torsion) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/stabilizer-of-a-binary-quartic-is-two-torsion`); [The embedding phi of binary quartic forms into pairs of ternary quadratic forms and the map psi on orbits](#st1-embedding-into-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/embedding-into-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms`); [Lemma 2.22: reducible monic integral binary cubic forms of bounded height number O(X^{1/2+ε}) up to unipotent equivalence](#st2-reducible-monic-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-monic-binary-cubic-forms`); [The eligible invariant pairs ordered by H(I, J), with the curve normalisation 27·H_E = 4·H′ (the binary-quartic invariant and height interface)](#st0-invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs`); [Bhargava-Shankar Proposition 2.16: the fibres of psi over nondegenerate classes are uniformly bounded](#st1-fibres-of-the-embedding-are-uniformly-bounded) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/fibres-of-the-embedding-are-uniformly-bounded`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.2, Lemma 2.4, printed p. 10. The lemma. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.8, proof of Lemma 2.4, printed p. 21. The imported bound, recorded as a gap.

**Proof route.**

1. A nontrivial element of Stab_{PGL_2(ℚ)}(f) gives, by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/stabilizer-of-a-binary-quartic-is-two-torsion (Stab_{PGL_2(ℚ)}(f) ≅ E(ℚ)[2] for E : y^2 = x^3 − (I/3)x − J/27), a rational 2-torsion point, i.e. a rational root of the monic cubic resolvent g = 4 Det(A_1x − B_f y) of f (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/embedding-into-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms), which has I(g) = I(f), J(g) = J(f); so g is reducible over ℚ.
2. The F_{ℤ,1}-orbit of g is an invariant of the PGL_2(ℤ)-orbit of f (the equivariance of φ in Theorem 2.14), and by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-monic-binary-cubic-forms there are O(X^{1/2+ε}) possibilities for it.
3. For a fixed reducible g, the number of GL_2(ℤ) × SL_3(ℤ)-orbits on pairs of integral ternary quadratic forms W_ℤ with cubic resolvent g is O(X^{1/4}) (Bhargava, 'The density of discriminants of quartic rings and fields', proof of Lemma 12; recorded as a gap), and each such orbit has at most 24 preimages in PGL_2(ℤ)\V_ℤ (Proposition 2.16, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/fibres-of-the-embedding-are-uniformly-bounded). So O(X^{1/4}) orbits of f per g.
4. Multiply: O(X^{1/2+ε}·X^{1/4}) = O(X^{3/4+ε}). The GL_2(ℤ)-stabiliser statement follows because a stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ) larger than {±1} has nontrivial image in PGL_2(ℚ).

**Acceptance checks.**

- The form x^3y − xy^3 has stabiliser containing the rotation (x, y) ↦ (−y, x), and its resolvent has the rational root corresponding to the 2-torsion point of y^2 = x^3 − x.
- Order check: X^{3/4+ε} is below the main term X^{5/6}.

<a id="st2-binary-quartic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp"></a>

### 2.25 Proposition 2.7: lattice points with a ≠ 0 in B(n, t, λ, X), and its version for translates of mV_ℤ

Let C > 0 be such that C^4 bounds the absolute values of all coefficients of all forms in G_0·L^(i). Let m ≥ 1 be an integer and L′ = v_0 + mV_ℤ a translate of the lattice mV_ℤ. For u ∈ [−1/2, 1/2], t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2, λ > 0 and X > 0, the number of points (a, b, c, d, e) ∈ L′ ∩ B(n(u), t, λ, X) with a ≠ 0 (counted with multiplicity) is 0 if Cλ < t, and is m^{−5}·Vol(B(n(u), t, λ, X)) + O(t^4λ^16) if Cλ ≥ t, where the implied constant depends only on G_0 and L^(i) (not on m, v_0, u, t, λ, X).

**Hypotheses.** C exists by the boundedness of L^(i) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits) and the compactness of G_0; m = 1, v_0 = 0 is Proposition 2.7 itself; the translate version is the one used in Section 2.5

**Dependencies.** `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4`; [The fundamental sets L^(i) of Table 1 and their scalings R^(i) = Λ·L^(i)](#st2-fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`); [The averaged orbit count N(S; X) of binary quartic forms and the regions B(n, t, λ, X)](#st2-averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.3, Proposition 2.7, printed p. 12 (checked on the page image). The case m = 1. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.5, printed p. 14. The translate version.

**Proof route.**

1. Coefficient ranges: a(t) multiplies the coefficient of x^{4−k}y^k by t^{2k−4}, n(u) with |u| ≤ 1/2 adds to each coefficient a bounded linear combination of the preceding ones (whose ranges are smaller), and λ multiplies all by λ^4; so in B(n, t, λ, X), |a|, |b|, |c|, |d|, |e| are respectively O(λ^4/t^4), O(λ^4/t²), O(λ^4), O(λ^4t²), O(λ^4t^4), with constants depending on G_0. The first coefficient is unchanged by n(u), so the precise bound |a|≤C^4λ^4/t^4 still holds; the later coefficients need enlarged constants.
2. If Cλ < t then |a| < 1, so a = 0 for every integral point.
3. If Cλ ≥ t then all five ranges are bounded below by a positive constant and the range of a is the smallest up to a constant; every projection of B onto a coordinate subspace has volume at most a constant times the product of the four largest ranges, O(λ^4/t^2·λ^4·λ^4t^2·λ^4t^4) = O(t^4λ^16), and scaling by 1/m (to pass to the lattice L′) only decreases the projection volumes.
4. B(n, t, λ, X) is a bounded semialgebraic multiset whose number of defining inequalities, their degrees and its maximum multiplicity are bounded in terms of G_0 and L^(i) (it is a linear image of G_0·L^(i) cut by H < X); apply Davenport's lemma (requested from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4) to the image of B under v ↦ (v − v_0)/m, whose volume is m^{−5}Vol(B).
5. Davenport first counts all lattice points with the multiset multiplicity. Subtract those on a=0: their number is bounded by the product of one plus the four remaining coefficient ranges, hence O(t^4 lambda^16) when t≤C lambda and t has its fixed positive lower bound. The same argument is uniform for translated sublattices mZ^5. The volume must also use the same multiset multiplicity, not the volume of its support.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Cusp mechanism: the region t > Cλ contains no integral point with a ≠ 0, so every integral point there has the factor y and is reducible.
- The projection bound drops the smallest range (that of a); for a = 0 slices there is no such saving, which is why the a = 0 points are removed as reducible.

<a id="st2-averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp"></a>

### 2.26 Averaging over the fundamental domain and cutting off the cusp: N(V_ℤ^(i); X) = Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/n_i + O(X^{3/4+ε})

(a) For i ∈ T and every ε > 0, N(V_ℤ^(i); X) = Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/n_i + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}), where N(V_ℤ^(i); X) is the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary quartic forms in V_ℤ^(i) of height < X and R_X(L^(i)) := {w ∈ F·L^(i) : H(w) < X} is the multiset over the strict domain F. (b) Cusp tail: there is c = c(G_0) such that for every S ⊆ V_ℤ^(i), every T ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2 and every X ≥ 1, (1/(2C_{G_0}^(i))) ∫_{t > T} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ B(n, t, λ, X)} t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ ≤ c·X^{5/6}/T^2 + O(X^{3/4}).

**Hypotheses.** The error term X^{3/4+ε} is smaller than the main term X^{5/6}; In (b) the bound is uniform in S; it is the form in which the cusp enters the uniformity estimate; When concluding that O(X^{3/4+epsilon}) is lower order than X^{5/6}, choose 0<epsilon<1/12; the bound itself is stated for every positive epsilon.

**Dependencies.** [Theorem 2.5: the averaging formula N(S; X) as an integral over N′A′Λ of lattice-point counts in B(n, t, λ, X)](#st2-averaging-formula-for-binary-quartic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-quartic-forms`); [Lemma 2.3: reducible integral binary quartic forms with a ≠ 0 in R_X(h·L^(i)) number O(X^{2/3+ε})](#st2-reducible-binary-quartic-forms-in-the-main-body) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-quartic-forms-in-the-main-body`); [Lemma 2.4: GL_2(ℤ)-orbits of binary quartic forms with stabiliser in GL_2(ℚ) of order > 2 number O(X^{3/4+ε})](#st2-orbits-with-large-stabilizer-are-negligible) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbits-with-large-stabilizer-are-negligible`); [Proposition 2.7: lattice points with a ≠ 0 in B(n, t, λ, X), and its version for translates of mV_ℤ](#st2-binary-quartic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-quartic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp`); [The multiset F h·L^(i) is n_i fundamental domains: orbit multiplicities m(x) = #Stab_{GL_2(ℝ)}(x)/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x)](#st2-orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets`); [The averaged orbit count N(S; X) of binary quartic forms and the regions B(n, t, λ, X)](#st2-averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.3, (18)-(20), printed p. 12 (checked on the page image). The cut-off and the evaluation (18)-(19). [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.3, (20), printed p. 12. Part (a).

**Proof route.**

1. By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-quartic-forms with S = V_ℤ^(i), and since L^(i) has height 1 and G_0 has determinant ≥ 1, the integrand vanishes unless t ≤ Cλ and λ < X^{1/24} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-quartic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp; points with a = 0 are reducible).
2. Irreducible points = points with a ≠ 0 minus reducible points with a ≠ 0: the latter contribute O(X^{2/3+ε}) after integration (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-quartic-forms-in-the-main-body, uniform in h ∈ G_0). The averaged count differs from the number of classes by the classes with stabiliser larger than {±1} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits), O(X^{3/4+ε}) of them (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbits-with-large-stabilizer-are-negligible).
3. Replace the count of points with a ≠ 0 by Vol(B) + O(t^4λ^16): the error integrates to ∫^{X^{1/24}}∫^{Cλ} t^4λ^16 t^{−2} d^×t d^×λ = O(X^{3/4}).
4. Main term: ∫ Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ over all of N′A′Λ equals 2∫_{G_0} Vol(R_X(h·L)) dh (unfold the integral over the full SO_2(ℝ) and use ∫_{K_+} dk = 1/2), and Vol(R_X(h·L)) = Vol(R_X(L)) for every h, because F h·L is n_i fundamental domains for every h (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets). Dividing by 2C_{G_0}^(i) = 2n_i∫_{G_0} dh gives Vol(R_X(L))/n_i.
5. Remove the cuspidal part t > Cλ from the main term: Vol(B) = O(λ^20), so ∫_{λ < X^{1/24}} ∫_{t > Cλ} λ^20 t^{−2} d^×t d^×λ = O(X^{3/4}).
6. (b) For t > T: the count is at most the number of points with a ≠ 0, i.e. Vol(B) + O(t^4λ^16) with Vol(B) = O(λ^20); ∫_{t > T} t^{−2} d^×t ≤ T^{−2}/2 and ∫^{X^{1/24}} λ^20 d^×λ = X^{5/6}/20, and the error term integrates to O(X^{3/4}).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Cusp check: in the region t > Cλ the leading coefficient vanishes, so the cusp contributes only reducible points.
- Error-term check: 3/4 < 5/6, so (a) is a genuine asymptotic once Vol(R_X(L^(i))) ≍ X^{5/6} is computed (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/volume-of-the-fundamental-region-for-binary-quartic-forms).
- Multiplicity check: the division by n_i reflects that F·L^(i) is n_i fundamental domains; with the source's F (full SO_2(ℝ)) both the count and the volume double.

<a id="st2-jacobian-change-of-measure-for-binary-quartic-forms"></a>

### 2.27 Proposition 2.8 (real case): dv = (1/27)·ω dI dJ under (g, I, J) ↦ g·p_{I,J}

Let PGL_2(ℝ) act on V_ℝ by the twisted action γ·f := (det γ)^{−2} f((x, y)γ), let ω be the ℤ-normalised invariant form of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/covolume-of-pgl2-z, dv = da db dc dd de, and for i ∈ T let p^(i) : (I, J) ↦ p^(i)_{I,J} ∈ R^(i) be the section of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits. Then for every measurable U ⊆ PGL_2(ℝ) and every measurable φ : V_ℝ → [0, ∞], ∫_{U·R^(i)} φ(v) dv = (1/27) ∫_{(I,J)} ∫_{g ∈ U} φ(g·p^(i)_{I,J}) ω(g) dI dJ, the left side over the multiset U·R^(i) (multiplicity #{(g, r) ∈ U × R^(i) : g·r = v}) and the outer integral over {4I^3 − J^2 > 0} (i ∈ {0, 2±}) or {4I^3 − J^2 < 0} (i = 1). In particular this holds for U = F_PGL2.

**Hypotheses.** The constant 1/27 is for the ℤ-basis E_11, E_12, E_21 of pgl_2(ℤ); a different normalisation of ω changes it; Only the real case is planned here; the p-adic analogue (Proposition 3.7, with |1/27|_p) belongs to ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4

**Dependencies.** [The eligible invariant pairs ordered by H(I, J), with the curve normalisation 27·H_E = 4·H′ (the binary-quartic invariant and height interface)](#st0-invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs`); [Bhargava-Shankar Theorem 3.2: E(K)/2E(K) and PGL2(K)-orbits of soluble quartics](#st1-binary-quartic-parametrization-of-e-mod-2e) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/binary-quartic-parametrization-of-e-mod-2e`); [The fundamental sets L^(i) of Table 1 and their scalings R^(i) = Λ·L^(i)](#st2-fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits`); [Vol(PGL_2(ℤ)\PGL_2(ℝ)) = 2ζ(2) for the ℤ-form ω, and the Iwasawa-measure volume of Gauss's domain](#st2-covolume-of-pgl2-z) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/covolume-of-pgl2-z`); [Lemma 2.2: stabilisers in GL_2(ℝ) of real binary quartic forms, and the weights n_i](#st2-stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms`); `mathlib:MeasureTheory.integral_image_eq_integral_abs_det_fderiv_smul`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.4, Proposition 2.8, printed p. 13. The proposition (the inner integral is over F_PGL2, as the left side requires). [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.4, after Proposition 2.8, printed p. 13. The route taken: a direct Jacobian computation, with the invariance argument of Section 3.4 (Steps 1-2 of Proposition 3.10) for the independence of the section.

**Proof route.**

1. Jacobian at the identity: for the polynomial section s_{I,J} = x^3y − (I/3)xy^3 − (J/27)y^4 (which has invariants (I, J), ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs), the 5 × 5 determinant of the vectors E_11·s, E_12·s, E_21·s, ∂s/∂I, ∂s/∂J (infinitesimal twisted action; E_11 acts by f ↦ x∂_x f − 2f) is −1/27 identically in (I, J) (a direct computation, rechecked by computer algebra).
2. Independence of the section and of the point: for f with Δ(f) ≠ 0, the orbit tangent vectors E·f span the kernel of (dI, dJ) at f, so det[E_11·f, E_12·f, E_21·f, w_1, w_2] with (dI, dJ)(w_j) = e_j depends only on f; it is invariant under PGL_2(ℂ) (the twisted action has determinant of absolute value 1 on V, and Λ^3 of the adjoint action is trivial). Forms with equal invariants and Δ ≠ 0 are PGL_2(ℂ)-equivalent (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/binary-quartic-parametrization-of-e-mod-2e over ℂ, where every form is soluble and E(ℂ)/2E(ℂ) = 0 (multiplication by 2 on a complex elliptic curve is surjective)), and s_{I,J} meets every such level set, so the determinant is −1/27 at every f with Δ(f) ≠ 0 and for every smooth section.
3. Left translation by g ∈ PGL_2(ℝ) preserves ω and changes dv by |det(g acting on V)| = 1, so the Jacobian of ψ(g, I, J) = g·p^(i)_{I,J} has absolute value 1/27 everywhere.
4. The explicit sections are smooth on finitely many pieces of the invariant region; along their joins a piecewise change of coordinates is required. On each smooth piece, the invertible Jacobian gives a local diffeomorphism. Cover by countably many open sets on which the map is injective, make them disjoint measurably, and apply MeasureTheory.integral_image_eq_integral_abs_det_fderiv_smul, then pass to nonnegative measurable functions by monotone approximation. The joins are lower-dimensional, hence null, and the finite fibres supply the stated multiplicity.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Checks of the constant: over each ℤ_p the analogous computation gives |1/27|_p (the source's Section 3.4), and the product formula ∏_v |1/27|_v = 1 is what makes the global Tamagawa computation of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4 consistent.
- The section of L^(i) differs from s_{I,J} by a PGL_2(ℂ)-valued function of (I, J); the determinant does not see the difference.

<a id="st2-volume-of-the-fundamental-region-for-binary-quartic-forms"></a>

### 2.28 The volumes Vol(R_X(L^(i))) = (16/135)ζ(2)X^{5/6} (i = 0, 2±) and (64/135)ζ(2)X^{5/6} (i = 1)

For i ∈ T let R^(i)(X) := {r ∈ R^(i) : H(r) < X}. Then R_X(L^(i)) = F_PGL2·R^(i)(X) as multisets, Vol(R_X(L^(i))) = (2ζ(2)/27)·∫_{R^(i)(X)} dI dJ, and ∫_{R^(i)(X)} dI dJ = (8/5)X^{5/6} for i ∈ {0, 2+, 2−} and (32/5)X^{5/6} for i = 1. Hence Vol(R_X(L^(i))) = (16/135)ζ(2)X^{5/6} for i ∈ {0, 2+, 2−} and (64/135)ζ(2)X^{5/6} for i = 1.

**Hypotheses.** F is the strict domain, whose image in PGL_2(ℝ) is F_PGL2; the Λ-coordinate of F is absorbed into R^(i) = Λ·L^(i)

**Dependencies.** [Proposition 2.8 (real case): dv = (1/27)·ω dI dJ under (g, I, J) ↦ g·p_{I,J}](#st2-jacobian-change-of-measure-for-binary-quartic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/jacobian-change-of-measure-for-binary-quartic-forms`); [Vol(PGL_2(ℤ)\PGL_2(ℝ)) = 2ζ(2) for the ℤ-form ω, and the Iwasawa-measure volume of Gauss's domain](#st2-covolume-of-pgl2-z) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/covolume-of-pgl2-z`); [The fundamental sets L^(i) of Table 1 and their scalings R^(i) = Λ·L^(i)](#st2-fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.4, (23)-(26), printed p. 13. The area computation; (25) and (26) follow as in the proof steps. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.4, (26), printed p. 13. The lemma.

**Proof route.**

1. F·L^(i) = N′A′K_+Λ·L^(i) = F_PGL2·(Λ·L^(i)) as multisets, since scalar matrices act on V_ℝ through Λ and the map F → F_PGL2 × Λ is a bijection for the strict domain.
2. Apply ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/jacobian-change-of-measure-for-binary-quartic-forms with U = F_PGL2 and φ the indicator of H < X, and Vol_ω(F_PGL2) = 2ζ(2) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/covolume-of-pgl2-z).
3. Areas: {(I, J) : H(I, J) < X, 4I^3 − J^2 > 0} = {0 < I < X^{1/3}, |J| < 2I^{3/2}}, of area ∫_0^{X^{1/3}} 4I^{3/2} dI = (8/5)X^{5/6}; the box {|I| < X^{1/3}, |J| < 2X^{1/2}} has area 8X^{5/6}, so the part with 4I^3 − J^2 < 0 has area 8X^{5/6} − (8/5)X^{5/6} = (32/5)X^{5/6}.
4. Multiply: (2ζ(2)/27)(8/5) = 16ζ(2)/135 and (2ζ(2)/27)(32/5) = 64ζ(2)/135.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Combined with (20): (16/135)ζ(2)/4 = (4/135)ζ(2) (i = 0), (64/135)ζ(2)/2 = (32/135)ζ(2) (i = 1), and (16/135)ζ(2)/4 = (4/135)ζ(2) for each of 2±, total (8/135)ζ(2) for i = 2.
- H(I, J) < X means |I| < X^{1/3} and |J| < 2X^{1/2}.

<a id="st2-count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height"></a>

### 2.29 Theorem 2.1 (Theorem 1.6): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary quartic forms of height < X

For every ε > 0: N(V_ℤ^(0); X) = (4/135)ζ(2)X^{5/6} + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}); N(V_ℤ^(1); X) = (32/135)ζ(2)X^{5/6} + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}); N(V_ℤ^(2); X) = (8/135)ζ(2)X^{5/6} + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}), where V_ℤ^(2) = V_ℤ^(2+) ⊔ V_ℤ^(2−) and each of the two definite parts contributes (4/135)ζ(2)X^{5/6}. Equivalently, with h^(i)(I, J) the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary quartic forms with 4 − 2i real roots and invariants (I, J), Σ_{H(I,J) < X} h^(i)(I, J) has the same asymptotics.

**Hypotheses.** Irreducible over ℚ; classes under GL_2(ℤ) (equivalently PGL_2(ℤ), as −1 acts trivially); Height H(f) = max(|I(f)|^3, J(f)^2/4); When concluding that O(X^{3/4+epsilon}) is lower order than X^{5/6}, choose 0<epsilon<1/12; the bound itself is stated for every positive epsilon.

**Dependencies.** [Averaging over the fundamental domain and cutting off the cusp: N(V_ℤ^(i); X) = Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/n_i + O(X^{3/4+ε})](#st2-averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp`); [The volumes Vol(R_X(L^(i))) = (16/135)ζ(2)X^{5/6} (i = 0, 2±) and (64/135)ζ(2)X^{5/6} (i = 1)](#st2-volume-of-the-fundamental-region-for-binary-quartic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/volume-of-the-fundamental-region-for-binary-quartic-forms`); [Lemma 2.2: stabilisers in GL_2(ℝ) of real binary quartic forms, and the weights n_i](#st2-stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2, Theorem 2.1, printed p. 7. The theorem. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 1.2, Theorem 1.6, printed p. 4. The equivalent formulation.

**Proof route.**

1. Combine ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp (a) with ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/volume-of-the-fundamental-region-for-binary-quartic-forms and n_0 = n_{2±} = 4, n_1 = 2 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms).
2. The reformulation: Σ_{H(I,J) < X} h^(i)(I, J) is N(V_ℤ^(i); X) by definition (every form of height < X has invariants of height < X).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Main-term constants: (4/135)ζ(2) ≈ 0.04874, (32/135)ζ(2) ≈ 0.38990, (8/135)ζ(2) ≈ 0.09748.
- The error term O(X^{3/4+ε}) is smaller than the main term X^{5/6}.
- Consistency with Theorem 1.8: dividing by the number of eligible invariant pairs gives ζ(2)/2, ζ(2), ζ(2) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/average-number-of-classes-per-eligible-invariant-pair).

<a id="st2-eligible-invariant-pairs-of-bounded-height"></a>

### 2.30 Lemma 2.9 and Proposition 2.10: eligible invariant pairs form 9 translates of 9ℤ × 27ℤ, and their number up to height X

(a) The set of eligible pairs (I, J) ∈ ℤ^2 (those occurring as the invariants of an integral binary quartic form) is the union of 9 distinct translates of the lattice 9ℤ × 27ℤ. (b) Let N^±_{I,J}(X) be the number of eligible (I, J) with H(I, J) < X and ±(4I^3 − J^2) > 0. Then N^+_{I,J}(X) = (8/135)X^{5/6} + O(X^{1/2}) and N^−_{I,J}(X) = (32/135)X^{5/6} + O(X^{1/2}).

**Hypotheses.** Eligibility is characterised by the congruences of Theorem 1.7, owned by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs

**Dependencies.** [The eligible invariant pairs ordered by H(I, J), with the curve normalisation 27·H_E = 4·H′ (the binary-quartic invariant and height interface)](#st0-invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs`); `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.4, Lemma 2.9 and Proposition 2.10 with proof, printed p. 14. Part (a). [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Proof of Proposition 2.10, printed p. 14. Part (b).

**Proof route.**

1. (a) By Theorem 1.7, (I, J) is eligible iff I ≡ 0 (mod 3) and J ≡ 0 (mod 27), or I ≡ 1, 4, 7 (mod 9) with J ≡ ±2, ±16, ±7 (mod 27) respectively. The first condition is 3 classes of I mod 9 times 1 class of J mod 27; the others are 3·2 = 6 classes; 9 classes of (I mod 9, J mod 27) in all.
2. (b) The region R^±_{I,J}(X) = {(i, j) : |i| < X^{1/3}, |j| < 2X^{1/2}, ±(4i^3 − j^2) > 0} is semialgebraic with bounded complexity and its coordinate projections have length O(X^{1/2}); Davenport's lemma (requested from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4) applied to each of the 9 translates of 9ℤ × 27ℤ (index 243) gives N^± = (9/243)Vol(R^±_{I,J}(X)) + O(X^{1/2}).
3. Vol(R^+_{I,J}(X)) = (8/5)X^{5/6} and Vol(R^−_{I,J}(X)) = (32/5)X^{5/6} (the areas of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/volume-of-the-fundamental-region-for-binary-quartic-forms, computed there by elementary integration); (1/27)(8/5) = 8/135 and (1/27)(32/5) = 32/135.

**Acceptance checks.**

- (I, J) = (−2, ±7) are eligible (I ≡ 7 mod 9, J ≡ ±7 mod 27) with Δ = −3, and they are the eligible pairs with Δ ≠ 0 of smallest height, 49/4; (1, 2) is eligible (realised by x^3y − x^2y^2) but has Δ = 0 and is excluded from both counts; (1, 1) is not eligible.
- The density of eligible pairs is 9/243 = 1/27, the factor that turns the areas 8/5 and 32/5 into 8/135 and 32/135.

<a id="st2-average-number-of-classes-per-eligible-invariant-pair"></a>

### 2.31 Theorem 1.8: the average number of classes of binary quartic forms per eligible invariant pair

For i = 0, 1, 2, lim_{X→∞} (Σ_{H(I,J) < X} h^(i)(I, J)) / #{eligible (I, J) : (−1)^i(4I^3 − J^2) > 0, H(I, J) < X} = 2ζ(2)/n_i, with n_0 = 4, n_1 = 2 and n_2 = 2 (the definite forms of both signs counted together).

**Hypotheses.** h^(i)(I, J) counts classes of irreducible integral forms with 4 − 2i real roots; for i = 2 both definite loci are included, so the effective n_2 is 2, not n_{2±} = 4

**Dependencies.** [Theorem 2.1 (Theorem 1.6): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary quartic forms of height < X](#st2-count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height`); [Lemma 2.9 and Proposition 2.10: eligible invariant pairs form 9 translates of 9ℤ × 27ℤ, and their number up to height X](#st2-eligible-invariant-pairs-of-bounded-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/eligible-invariant-pairs-of-bounded-height`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 1.2, Theorem 1.8, printed p. 5. The theorem, with the lumped n_2 = 2.

**Proof route.**

1. Divide the counts of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height by those of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/eligible-invariant-pairs-of-bounded-height: (4/135)ζ(2)/(8/135) = ζ(2)/2, (32/135)ζ(2)/(32/135) = ζ(2) and (8/135)ζ(2)/(8/135) = ζ(2).

**Acceptance checks.**

- The averages are ζ(2)/2 ≈ 0.822 (four real roots) and ζ(2) ≈ 1.645 (fewer than four).
- n_2 = 2 here is consistent with n_{2±} = 4: each eligible (I, J) with Δ > 0 carries one orbit of each definiteness.

<a id="st2-binary-quartic-counts-with-finitely-many-congruence-conditions"></a>

### 2.32 Theorem 2.11 and (27): counting binary quartic forms satisfying finitely many congruence conditions

(a) Let m ≥ 1 and let L_j = v_j + mV_ℤ be a translate of mV_ℤ. Then N(L_j ∩ V_ℤ^(i); X) = Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/(n_i m^5) + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}), the implied constant independent of m and v_j (N the averaged count). (b) If S ⊆ V_ℤ is defined by congruence conditions modulo m, i.e. a union of k translates of mV_ℤ, then N(S ∩ V_ℤ^(i); X) = k·Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/(n_i m^5) + O_{S,ε}(X^{3/4+ε}). (c) If the allowed residues of S form the CRT product of local allowed sets at finitely many distinct prime powers, then N(S ∩ V_ℤ^(i); X) = N(V_ℤ^(i); X)·∏_p μ_p(S) + O_{S,ε}(X^{3/4+ε}), where μ_p(S) is the p-adic density of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions.

**Hypotheses.** In (c) the implied constant depends on S (through k); For GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S the averaged count is the class count up to O(X^{3/4+ε})

**Dependencies.** [The averaged orbit count N(S; X) of binary quartic forms and the regions B(n, t, λ, X)](#st2-averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits`); [Theorem 2.5: the averaging formula N(S; X) as an integral over N′A′Λ of lattice-point counts in B(n, t, λ, X)](#st2-averaging-formula-for-binary-quartic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-quartic-forms`); [Proposition 2.7: lattice points with a ≠ 0 in B(n, t, λ, X), and its version for translates of mV_ℤ](#st2-binary-quartic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-quartic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp`); [Averaging over the fundamental domain and cutting off the cusp: N(V_ℤ^(i); X) = Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/n_i + O(X^{3/4+ε})](#st2-averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp`); [Theorem 2.1 (Theorem 1.6): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary quartic forms of height < X](#st2-count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height`); [Functions and sets defined by congruence conditions; acceptable functions](#st2-functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.5, (27), printed p. 14. Parts (a)-(b). [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.5, Theorem 2.11, printed p. 14. Part (c).

**Proof route.**

1. (a) Repeat the proof of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp with S = L_j: by the translate version of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-quartic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp the points with a ≠ 0 number 0 for Cλ < t and m^{−5}Vol(B) + O(t^4λ^16) otherwise, with the constant independent of m; the reducible points and the large-stabiliser classes contribute O(X^{3/4+ε}) as before (they are a subset of those of V_ℤ).
2. (b) Sum over the k translates.
3. (c) By the Chinese remainder theorem k·m^{−5} = ∏_p μ_p(S) because the allowed residue set is a Cartesian product under CRT, with m the product of the distinct prime powers involved; combine with ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height.

**Acceptance checks.**

- S = V_ℤ (m = 1, k = 1) recovers Theorem 2.1.
- For S = {f : p | a(f)} (m = p, k = p^4), μ_p(S) = 1/p and the count is N(V_ℤ^(i); X)/p + O(X^{3/4+ε}) for fixed p.
- For S defined by a(f) mod6 in {0,1,5}, the global density is 1/2 whereas its projections mod2 and mod3 are both full. Part (b) applies, but the product-of-local-closures formula does not. This tests the added product hypothesis in (c).

<a id="st2-weighted-binary-quartic-counts-with-finitely-many-congruence-conditions"></a>

### 2.33 Theorem 2.12: weighted counts of binary quartic forms with weights defined modulo finitely many prime powers

Let p_1, …, p_k be distinct primes and, for each j, let φ_{p_j} : V_ℤ → ℝ be GL_2(ℤ)-invariant and depend only on f mod p_j^{a_j}. Put φ := ∏_j φ_{p_j} and let N_φ(V_ℤ^(i); X) be the number of irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-orbits in V_ℤ^(i) of height < X, each orbit GL_2(ℤ)·f counted with weight φ(f). Then N_φ(V_ℤ^(i); X) = N(V_ℤ^(i); X)·∏_{j=1}^k ∫_{V_{ℤ_{p_j}}} φ̃_{p_j}(f) df + O(X^{3/4+ε}), where φ̃_{p_j} is the locally constant extension of φ_{p_j} to V_{ℤ_{p_j}}, df is the Haar probability measure, and the implied constant depends only on the φ_{p_j} and ε.

**Hypotheses.** Finitely many primes and finitely many residue conditions; The weights are GL_2(ℤ)-invariant so that N_φ counts orbits

**Dependencies.** [Theorem 2.11 and (27): counting binary quartic forms satisfying finitely many congruence conditions](#st2-binary-quartic-counts-with-finitely-many-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-quartic-counts-with-finitely-many-congruence-conditions`); [Functions and sets defined by congruence conditions; acceptable functions](#st2-functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.5, Theorem 2.12, printed p. 15. The theorem, whose proof the source says is identical to that of Theorem 2.11.

**Proof route.**

1. φ is a finite linear combination Σ_c φ(c)·1_{c} of indicator functions of residue classes c modulo m = ∏ p_j^{a_j}; each class is a translate of mV_ℤ.
2. Apply part (a) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-quartic-counts-with-finitely-many-congruence-conditions to each class and sum; Σ_c φ(c) m^{−5} = ∏_j ∫ φ̃_{p_j} df by the Chinese remainder theorem.
3. The averaged count of an invariant weighted set equals the weighted class count up to the O(X^{3/4+ε}) large-stabiliser classes.

**Acceptance checks.**

- φ ≡ 1 recovers Theorem 2.1; φ = 1_S recovers Theorem 2.11.

<a id="st2-uniformity-for-strongly-divisible-quartic-discriminants"></a>

### 2.34 Theorem 2.18: forms in a homogeneously expanding region reducing into V(Δ, ∂Δ/∂e) modulo some p > M

Let B_0 ⊂ V_ℝ be compact and let Y_4 = V(Δ, ∂Δ/∂e) ⊆ 𝔸^5_ℤ. There is C = C(B_0) such that for all X ≥ 1 and M ≥ 2, #{f ∈ X^{1/6}B_0 ∩ V_ℤ : f mod p ∈ Y_4(𝔽_p) for some prime p > M} ≤ C·(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{2/3}). In particular #(X^{1/6}B_0 ∩ ⋃_{p>M} W_p^(1)(V)) ≤ C·(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{2/3}). The source uses the bounded, generally nonclosed set B_src = F^(ε)_PGL2·R^(i)(1), where F^(ε)_PGL2 ⊂ F_PGL2 is cut off at a height t ≤ T_ε chosen so that Vol(F^(ε)_PGL2) = (1 − ε)Vol(F_PGL2); then X^{1/6}B_src = F^(ε)_PGL2·R^(i)(X). Apply the compact-set bound to the closure of B_src; B_src itself need not be compact.

**Hypotheses.** B_0 compact; the constant depends on B_0 (for the source's region, on ε); W_p^(1)(V) ⊆ {f : f mod p ∈ Y_4(𝔽_p)} is the inclusion of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus; the larger set is what is bounded

**Dependencies.** [The quantitative Ekedahl geometric sieve (Bhargava, Theorem 3.3; Bhargava-Shankar, Theorem 2.17)](#st2-quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve`); [Strong multiples of p^2 reduce into the codimension-two locus f = ∂f/∂x_n = 0](#st2-strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus`); [The discriminants of binary quartic and binary cubic forms are primitive and coprime to their derivatives in the last coefficient](#st2-discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two`); [The fundamental sets L^(i) of Table 1 and their scalings R^(i) = Λ·L^(i)](#st2-fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.6, Theorem 2.18, printed p. 17. The theorem, for the source's region. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.6, after Theorem 2.18, printed p. 18. The proof.

**Proof route.**

1. Y_4 has codimension 2 in 𝔸^5_ℤ (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two).
2. Apply ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve with n = 5, k = 2, B = B_0, r = X^{1/6}: r^n/(M^{k−1} log M) = X^{5/6}/(M log M) and r^{n−k+1} = X^{4/6} = X^{2/3}.
3. The second statement by part (a) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus.
4. F^(ε)_PGL2·R^(i)(X) = X^{1/6}·(F^(ε)_PGL2·R^(i)(1)) because H(c·f) = c^6 H(f) for scalars c > 0, and F^(ε)_PGL2·R^(i)(1) is bounded (t is bounded above on F^(ε) and the coefficients of R^(i)(1) are bounded).

**Acceptance checks.**

- The forms with f mod p of splitting type (1^3 1), (1^2 1^2), (2^2), (1^4) or f ∈ pV_ℤ (for p ≥ 3) are the strongly divisible ones; the larger set counted also contains weakly divisible forms whose double root mod p is at [1 : 0], such as 25x^4 + x^2y^2 + y^4 for p = 5.
- The bound is used with M fixed and X → ∞: the term X^{2/3} is then negligible against X^{5/6}.

<a id="st2-weakly-divisible-quartic-discriminants-via-ternary-pairs"></a>

### 2.35 (37): N(W_p^(2)(V); X) = O(X/p^2) uniformly in p, through pairs of ternary quadratic forms

There is an absolute constant C such that for every prime p and every X ≥ 1, the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary quartic forms f ∈ W_p^(2)(V) with H(f) < X is at most C·X/p^2.

**Hypotheses.** Rests on Theorem 2.19 (Bhargava, 'The density of discriminants of quartic rings and fields', Proposition 23), which is recorded as a gap; Uniform in both p and X

**Dependencies.** [The embedding phi of binary quartic forms into pairs of ternary quadratic forms and the map psi on orbits](#st1-embedding-into-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/embedding-into-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms`); [Strong and weak multiples of p^2: the sets W_p, W_p^(1), W_p^(2) of binary quartic and binary cubic forms](#st2-strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values`); [The eligible invariant pairs ordered by H(I, J), with the curve normalisation 27·H_E = 4·H′ (the binary-quartic invariant and height interface)](#st0-invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs`); [Bhargava-Shankar Proposition 2.16: the fibres of psi over nondegenerate classes are uniformly bounded](#st1-fibres-of-the-embedding-are-uniformly-bounded) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/fibres-of-the-embedding-are-uniformly-bounded`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.6, Theorem 2.19 and (37), printed p. 18. The imported estimate (a gap here) and its transport (37) through Proposition 2.16.

**Proof route.**

1. The map φ of (30) sends f to (A_1, B_f) ∈ W_ℤ, preserves the discriminant, and induces ψ : PGL_2(ℤ)\V_ℤ → (GL_2(ℤ) × SL_3(ℤ))\W_ℤ with fibres of size at most 24 over elements of nonzero discriminant (Theorem 2.14 and Proposition 2.16, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/fibres-of-the-embedding-are-uniformly-bounded).
2. φ is affine-linear in f with φ(f + pg) − φ(f) = (0, p·B_g), so if Δ(f + pg) is not divisible by p^2 for some g, the same perturbation shows Δ_W(φ(f)) is not strongly divisible: φ maps W_p^(2)(V) into W_p^(2)(W) (definitions of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values).
3. H(f) < X implies |Δ(f)| = |4I^3 − J^2|/27 ≤ (4|I|^3 + J^2)/27 ≤ 8H(f)/27 < X.
4. Theorem 2.19: the number of GL_2(ℤ) × SL_3(ℤ)-orbits on W_p^(2)(W) with |Δ| < X is O(X/p^2) with the constant independent of p (gap); multiply by 24.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For p>X^{1/2} the set is empty: irreducibility implies Δ(f)≠0, while p²|Δ(f) gives p²≤|Δ(f)|<X. This follows from the discriminant inequality, not by dropping the unspecified constant in O(X/p²).
- The transport uses only that φ preserves the discriminant and is affine in f; no information about the strongly divisible part of W_ℤ is needed, because W_p^(1)(V) is handled by the geometric sieve.

<a id="st2-uniformity-for-weakly-divisible-quartic-discriminants"></a>

### 2.36 Theorem 2.20, corrected: forms with p^2 | Δ and p ∤ ∂Δ/∂e in a homogeneously expanding region

Let W′_p := {f ∈ V_ℤ : p^2 | Δ(f), p ∤ ∂Δ/∂e(f)}, a subset of W_p^(2)(V). Let B_0 ⊂ V_ℝ be compact. (a) There is C = C(B_0) with #(X^{1/6}B_0 ∩ W′_p) ≤ C·(X^{5/6}/p^2 + X^{2/3}) for every prime p and X ≥ 1. (b) If moreover every irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-orbit meets X^{1/6}B_0 in at most c_0 points (counted with multiplicity), then #(X^{1/6}B_0 ∩ V_ℤ^irr ∩ ⋃_{p>M} W′_p) ≤ C′·(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{5/6}/log X) for all X ≥ 2 and M ≥ 2, with C′ depending on B_0 and c_0 only. Together with ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-for-strongly-divisible-quartic-discriminants this bounds the whole irreducible part X^{1/6}B_0 ∩ V_ℤ^irr ∩ ⋃_{p>M} W_p(V), since W_p(V) ⊆ W′_p ∪ {f : f mod p ∈ Y_4(𝔽_p)}.

**Hypotheses.** The source states the bound for W_p^(2)(V) and asserts p ∤ ∂Δ/∂e on it; that assertion is false (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E302), and the forms of W_p^(2)(V) with p | ∂Δ/∂e are covered by the geometric sieve instead; The orbit-multiplicity hypothesis in (b) holds for the source's region F^(ε)·R^(i)(X) and for the truncated regions used in the proof of Theorem 2.13

**Dependencies.** [(37): N(W_p^(2)(V); X) = O(X/p^2) uniformly in p, through pairs of ternary quadratic forms](#st2-weakly-divisible-quartic-discriminants-via-ternary-pairs) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/weakly-divisible-quartic-discriminants-via-ternary-pairs`); [Chebyshev-type bounds for the prime-counting function and for tails of prime sums](#st2-chebyshev-bounds-for-prime-sums) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/chebyshev-bounds-for-prime-sums`); [Strong and weak multiples of p^2: the sets W_p, W_p^(1), W_p^(2) of binary quartic and binary cubic forms](#st2-strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values`); [The discriminants of binary quartic and binary cubic forms are primitive and coprime to their derivatives in the last coefficient](#st2-discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.6, Theorem 2.20, printed p. 18 (checked on the page image). The theorem, restated for W′_p and a general compact region. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Proof of Theorem 2.20, printed p. 18. The step that fails (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E302); the count (39) itself is correct for W′_p.

**Proof route.**

1. W′_p ⊆ W_p^(2)(V): p ∤ ∂Δ/∂e(f) excludes strong divisibility (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values, gradient characterisation).
2. (a) X^{1/6}B_0 has sides of length O(X^{1/6}), so there are O(X^{4/6}) quadruples (a_0, b_0, c_0, d_0). For fixed ones, Δ(a_0, b_0, c_0, d_0, e) mod p is a polynomial in e of degree ≤ 3 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two); the residues e mod p with p | Δ and p ∤ ∂Δ/∂e are simple roots of a nonzero polynomial, at most 3 of them, and each lifts to exactly one class e mod p^2 with p^2 | Δ (Hensel's lemma for a simple root). An interval of length O(X^{1/6}) contains at most O(X^{1/6}/p^2 + 1) integers in a class mod p^2.
3. (b) For M < p < X^{1/6} use (a): Σ_{p>M} X^{5/6}/p^2 = O(X^{5/6}/(M log M)) and Σ_{p<X^{1/6}} X^{2/3} = O(X^{5/6}/log X) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/chebyshev-bounds-for-prime-sums.
