For p ≥ X^{1/6} use ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/weakly-divisible-quartic-discriminants-via-ternary-pairs: the irreducible points of W′_p ⊆ W_p^(2)(V) in the region lie in at most C X/p^2 classes (the region has height ≤ c·X), each contributing at most c_0 points, and Σ_{p ≥ X^{1/6}} X/p^2 = O(X^{5/6}/log X).

**Acceptance checks.**

- The source's bound O(X^{5/6}/log M) follows from (b) when M ≤ X^{1/6}, because then 1/log X ≤ 1/(6 log M); for M > X^{1/6} only the second step applies and gives O(X/(M log M)), which is O(X^{5/6}/log M).
- The form 25x^4 + x^2y^2 + y^4 lies in W_5^(2)(V) but not in W′_5; it lies in Y_4(𝔽_5) modulo 5.

### 2.37 Theorem 2.13: a uniform tail estimate for binary quartic forms whose discriminant is divisible by p^2 for some p > M

For a prime p let W_p(V) := {f ∈ V_ℤ : p^2 | Δ(f)}. There are constants c (absolute, given G_0) and C_T (for each T ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2, independent of M) such that for every M ≥ 2 and every T, lim sup_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(V); X)/X^{5/6} ≤ C_T/(M log M) + c/T^2. Consequently lim_{M→∞} lim sup_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(V); X)/X^{5/6} = 0: for every δ > 0 there is M_δ with lim sup_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(V); X)/X^{5/6} < δ for all M ≥ M_δ. Here N is the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible forms of height < X (equivalently the averaged count, up to O(X^{3/4+ε})), summed over i ∈ T.

**Hypotheses.** The source states lim_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(V); X)/X^{5/6} = O(1/log M) with an implied constant independent of M; its proof does not track how the constants of Theorems 2.18 and 2.20 depend on the cut-off ε, which the rate needs, while the sieve (Theorem 2.21) uses only the limit statement proved here (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E304); The statement is about orbit counts, not lattice-point counts; the limits are in X first, then M

**Proof route.**

1. Apply ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-quartic-forms to S := V_ℤ^(i) ∩ ⋃_{p>M} W_p(V) and split the integral at t = T.
2. t > T: at most c·X^{5/6}/T^2 + O(X^{3/4}) by part (b) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp.
3. t ≤ T: every B(n, t, λ, X) with t ≤ T lies in Ω_T(X) := X^{1/6}·Ω_T, where Ω_T := ⋃_{|u| ≤ 1/2, t_0 ≤ t ≤ T, λ ≤ 1} n(u)a(t)λG_0·L^(i) is bounded (take its compact closure for the lattice-point estimates) (H(λ·f) = λ^24 H(f)). For each x the set {(u, t, λ) : x ∈ B(n(u), t, λ, X)} has measure at most a constant depending on G_0 (it is contained in finitely many translates g_x Stab(x_L)G_0^{−1} of G_0^{−1}, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms), so the t ≤ T part is at most c′·#(S^irr ∩ Ω_T(X)); every GL_2(ℤ)-orbit meets Ω_T(X) in boundedly many points (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets). To justify the orbit bound, project the truncated matrix set N_{|u|≤1/2} A_{t_0≤t≤T} G_0 to PGL2(R); it is compact. The modular tessellation is locally finite, so it is covered by finitely many GL2(Z)-translates of the Gauss region, with a uniform finite boundary multiplicity. Absorb positive scalar factors into R^(i). Each orbit therefore contributes at most a constant depending on T,G_0, including on the boundary. One cannot infer this merely by taking an uncountable union of the fixed-h multiplicity assertions.
4. Split S ⊆ {f mod p ∈ Y_4(𝔽_p) for some p > M} ∪ ⋃_{p>M} W′_p (for f ∈ W_p(V) either p | ∂Δ/∂e(f), and then f mod p ∈ Y_4(𝔽_p), or f ∈ W′_p). The first part is O_T(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{2/3}) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-for-strongly-divisible-quartic-discriminants with B_0 = Ω_T; the second is O_T(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{5/6}/log X) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-for-weakly-divisible-quartic-discriminants.
5. Divide by X^{5/6}, let X → ∞, sum over the four values of i; then let T → ∞ after M → ∞ (choose T with c/T^2 < δ/2, then M with C_T/(M log M) < δ/2).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Interchange check: the acceptance condition of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2 (an interchange of the sieve limit and the height limit needs a uniform tail theorem) is met by this statement: the bound on lim sup_X is uniform in the set of congruence conditions imposed at primes ≤ M.
- Order check: the tail is o(1)·X^{5/6} as M → ∞; for fixed M it is of the same order X^{5/6} as the main term, so it cannot be dropped.
- Squarefree-discriminant application: excluding ⋃_p W_p(V) leaves the forms of squarefree discriminant, counted by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/squarefree-sieve-for-binary-quartic-forms.

<a id="st2-squarefree-sieve-for-binary-quartic-forms"></a>

### 2.38 Theorem 2.21: counting binary quartic forms weighted by an acceptable function defined by infinitely many congruence conditions

Let φ : V_ℤ → [0, 1] be acceptable (for Δ) and defined by congruence conditions via local functions φ_p : V_{ℤ_p} → [0, 1] (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions), with each φ_p invariant under GL_2(ℤ). For i ∈ T let N_φ(V_ℤ^(i); X) be the number of irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-orbits in V_ℤ^(i) of height < X, each orbit GL_2(ℤ)·f counted with weight φ(f). Then N_φ(V_ℤ^(i); X) = N(V_ℤ^(i); X)·∏_p ∫_{V_{ℤ_p}} φ_p(f) df + o(X^{5/6}), and the Euler product converges.

**Hypotheses.** Acceptability: φ_p = 1 on {p^2 ∤ Δ} for all large p; GL_2(ℤ)-invariance of the φ_p makes N_φ an orbit count; the source uses it implicitly ('with notation as in Theorem 2.12')

**Dependencies.** [Theorem 2.12: weighted counts of binary quartic forms with weights defined modulo finitely many prime powers](#st2-weighted-binary-quartic-counts-with-finitely-many-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/weighted-binary-quartic-counts-with-finitely-many-congruence-conditions`); [Theorem 2.13: a uniform tail estimate for binary quartic forms whose discriminant is divisible by p^2 for some p > M](#st2-uniformity-estimate-for-infinitely-many-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-infinitely-many-congruence-conditions`); [Functions and sets defined by congruence conditions; acceptable functions](#st2-functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions`); [The p-adic density of {p^2 | f} is O(p^{-2})](#st2-local-density-of-values-divisible-by-p-squared) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/local-density-of-values-divisible-by-p-squared`); [The discriminants of binary quartic and binary cubic forms are primitive and coprime to their derivatives in the last coefficient](#st2-discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two`); [Theorem 2.1 (Theorem 1.6): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary quartic forms of height < X](#st2-count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 2.7, Theorem 2.21, printed p. 19. The theorem. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Proof of Theorem 2.21, (44)-(45), printed pp. 19-20. The lower-bound step, which uses the tail estimate.

**Proof route.**

1. For n≥1, define psi_{p,n} and psiPrime_{p,n} as the infimum and supremum of phi_p on each residue cylinder modulo p^n. These are actual pointwise lower and upper bounds, including on the exceptional null set, and they converge to phi_p at every point where phi_p is locally constant. They inherit GL2(Z)-invariance because that action permutes the cylinders. Bounded convergence gives convergence of their integrals. Do not assert a lower bound psi_{p,0}=1≤phi_p.
2. For sufficiently large p and n≥2, a residue cylinder not meeting {p²|Δ} lies entirely in the region phi_p=1, so both approximants equal one there. Level n=1 is insufficient for a condition modulo p². In particular acceptability and the local O(p^{-2}) density bound imply convergence of product_p integral(phi_p).
3. Fix M above the acceptability threshold. For the finitely many primes p≤M, take cylinder approximants of level n and use the weighted finite-congruence count. The global product phi is at most the product of the upper approximants. The product of the lower approximants is at most phi outside the tail union_{p>M} W_p, so subtract that tail count for the lower bound.
4. First take limsup or liminf as X→∞, next n→∞ with M fixed. This gives upper and lower bounds involving the finite product of the actual local masses and an error bounded by the uniform tail delta(M). Finally let M→∞: the finite products converge and delta(M)→0. This order of limits avoids the false assertion that level floor(Y/p) always resolves a p² condition.
5. The unweighted leading constant exists by count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height. The stabilizer correction is negligible since the weights lie in [0,1].

**Acceptance checks.**

- Squarefree discriminants: φ = 1_{Δ squarefree}, φ_p = 1_{p^2 ∤ Δ}; the proportion of irreducible classes with squarefree discriminant is ∏_p μ_p{p^2 ∤ Δ}.
- For φ defined by finitely many congruence conditions the theorem reduces to Theorem 2.12 with error O(X^{3/4+ε}); for infinitely many conditions only o(X^{5/6}) is claimed.
- ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4 applies it with the weight 1/m(f) times local solubility, which is acceptable by Bhargava-Shankar Proposition 3.18.
- At a null exceptional point the cylinder infimum/supremum still bound the actual value, even if convergence there fails. At p∈(Y/2,Y], floor(Y/p)=1 does not resolve p² divisibility; the proof uses fixed finite primes followed by n→∞ instead.

**Interface qualification.**  The suggested signature explicitly assumes invariance of each p-adic factor under the integral GL₂ action, matching the cylinder-approximation proof. Invariance of only the infinite global product does not provide invariance of its finite truncations.

<a id="st2-real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms"></a>

### 2.39 Real binary cubic forms: the two open GL_2(ℝ)-orbits and their stabilisers (n_0 = 6, n_1 = 2)

Let U_ℝ be the space of real binary cubic forms f = ax^3 + bx^2y + cxy^2 + dy^3 with the twisted action γ·f := (det γ)^{−1} f((x, y)γ) of GL_2(ℝ) (the action (9) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings), and Disc(f) = b^2c^2 − 4ac^3 − 4b^3d − 27a^2d^2 + 18abcd. (a) Disc(γ·f) = (det γ)^2 Disc(f), and the scalar matrix λ·1 acts by f ↦ λf. (b) U_ℝ^(0) := {Disc > 0}, the forms with three distinct real roots in ℙ^1(ℝ), and U_ℝ^(1) := {Disc < 0}, the forms with one real root and a pair of complex conjugate roots, are each a single GL_2(ℝ)-orbit. (c) The stabiliser in GL_2(ℝ) of f ∈ U_ℝ^(0) has order n_0 := 6 and acts on the three roots as the full symmetric group; the stabiliser of f ∈ U_ℝ^(1) has order n_1 := 2. Put U_ℤ^(i) := U_ℝ^(i) ∩ U_ℤ.

**Hypotheses.** The twisted action (det gamma)^{-1} is the Delone–Faddeev action; the untwisted scalar action would be lambda³ instead of lambda, although over R the stabilizer orders are still 6 and 2 because every nonzero real scalar has a unique real cube root.; Only forms with Disc ≠ 0 are in U_ℝ^(0) ∪ U_ℝ^(1)

**Dependencies.** [Delone-Faddeev: GL2(R)-classes of binary cubic forms parametrize cubic rings](#st1-delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings`); `mathlib:Cubic.discr_eq_prod_three_roots`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5, opening, p. 9. Part (b). [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.1, p. 10. Part (c); the printed indices n_1, n_2 stand for n_0, n_1 (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E307), and the proof steps avoid the ring-theoretic detour.

**Proof route.**

1. (a) Disc is homogeneous of degree 4 and relatively invariant of weight 6 under substitution, Disc(f((x, y)γ)) = (det γ)^6 Disc(f); the factor (det γ)^{−1} multiplies Disc by (det γ)^{−4}. For λ·1: f((x, y)λ)/λ^2 = λf.
2. (b) Roots: by Cubic.discr_eq_prod_three_roots (after moving a root away from [1 : 0] if a = 0), Disc > 0 iff the three roots are real and distinct, and Disc < 0 iff one is real and two are complex conjugate. PGL_2(ℝ) is simply 3-transitive on ℙ^1(ℝ), and transitive on pairs (real point, conjugate pair) (move the pair to ±i, then rotate by the stabiliser SO_2(ℝ) of i, which is transitive on ℙ^1(ℝ)). A form is determined by its roots up to a nonzero scalar, and the scalars λ·1 realise every scalar factor by (a).
3. (c) An element of the stabiliser permutes the roots; the map to permutations is injective (an element fixing three points of ℙ^1 is a scalar λ·1, which fixes f only for λ = 1). Every permutation of three real roots is induced by a unique class in PGL_2(ℝ), and exactly one scalar multiple of a representative fixes f; for one real root and a conjugate pair, only the identity and the swap of the pair preserve the real structure, and the swap is realised by a reflection.

**Acceptance checks.**

- x^3 − 3xy^2 ∈ U_ℝ^(0) with Disc = 108 and x^3 + xy^2 ∈ U_ℝ^(1) with Disc = −4; the stabiliser of x^3 + xy^2 is {1, diag(−1, 1)} (diag(1, −1) sends it to its negative).
- The scalar −1 ∈ GL_2(ℤ) sends f to −f: unlike binary quartic forms, the centre does not act trivially, which is why n_i is the full stabiliser order here and half of it for quartics.

<a id="st2-stabilizers-of-irreducible-integral-binary-cubic-forms"></a>

### 2.40 The GL_2(ℤ)-stabiliser of an irreducible integral binary cubic form is trivial or cyclic of order 3

Let f ∈ U_ℤ be irreducible over ℚ. Then Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(f) (twisted action) is trivial or cyclic of order 3, and if it has order 3 then Disc(f) is a positive square.

**Hypotheses.** Irreducibility over ℚ is essential: xy(x − y) has a stabiliser of order 6 in GL_2(ℤ)

**Dependencies.** [Real binary cubic forms: the two open GL_2(ℝ)-orbits and their stabilisers (n_0 = 6, n_1 = 2)](#st2-real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms`); [Delone-Faddeev: GL2(R)-classes of binary cubic forms parametrize cubic rings](#st1-delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings`); `mathlib:Cubic.discr_eq_prod_three_roots`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.1, p. 10. The statement; the proof steps give a direct Galois-theoretic argument instead of the Delone-Faddeev detour. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.2, before Lemma 22, p. 11. The sign statement.

**Proof route.**

1. As in part (c) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms, Stab_{GL_2(ℚ)}(f) embeds into the permutations of the three roots of f in ℙ^1(ℚ̄), and the image commutes with the action of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) because the elements are rational.
2. f irreducible: Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) acts transitively on the roots, through A_3 or S_3. The centraliser of A_3 in S_3 is A_3 and that of S_3 is trivial.
3. If the stabiliser is A_3 ≅ C_3, the Galois image is A_3, so √Disc(f) = a^2(r_1 − r_2)(r_1 − r_3)(r_2 − r_3) (Cubic.discr_eq_prod_three_roots) is fixed by Galois and rational; a cyclic cubic splits over ℝ as soon as one root is real, so Disc(f) > 0.

**Acceptance checks.**

- f = x^3 + x^2y − 2xy^2 − y^3 (the cyclic cubic of conductor 7, Disc = 49) is fixed by the order-3 element γ = [[0, −1], [1, −1]] of SL_2(ℤ), i.e. (x, y) ↦ (y, −x − y); its stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ) is exactly {1, γ, γ^2} (checked by enumeration).
- A form with Disc < 0 always has trivial stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ).

<a id="st2-reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body"></a>

### 2.41 Lemma 21: reducible integral binary cubic forms with a ≠ 0 in R_X(v) number O(X^{3/4+ε})

Let B ⊂ U_ℝ be compact with |Disc(v)| ≥ 1 for v ∈ B. For v ∈ B with Disc(v) ≠ 0 let R_X(v) := {w ∈ F·v : |Disc(w)| < X} (multiset over the strict Gauss domain F). For every ε > 0 the number of integral forms ax^3 + bx^2y + cxy^2 + dy^3 in R_X(v) that are reducible over ℚ with a ≠ 0 is O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}), the implied constant depending only on B and ε.

**Hypotheses.** Only a ≠ 0; the forms with a = 0 have the factor y; When concluding that O(X^{3/4+epsilon}) is lower order than X^{5/6}, choose 0<epsilon<1/12; the bound itself is stated for every positive epsilon.

**Dependencies.** [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`); [Real binary cubic forms: the two open GL_2(ℝ)-orbits and their stabilisers (n_0 = 6, n_1 = 2)](#st2-real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms`); `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.2, Lemma 21 and proof, pp. 10-11. The lemma; the source attributes it to Davenport [15, Lem. 3], [16, Lem. 2] and gives the proof followed here.

**Proof route.**

1. Coefficient bounds: f ∈ N′A′KΛv with λ < X^{1/4} (Disc(λ·v) = λ^4 Disc(v)); the twisted action of a(t) multiplies the coefficients by t^{−3}, t^{−1}, t, t^3, so a = O(λ/t^3) = O(X^{1/4}), ab = O(λ^2/t^4), ac, ad = O(λ^2) = O(X^{1/2}), abc = O(λ^3/t^3) and abd = O(λ^3/t) = O(X^{3/4}).
2. d = 0 with a ≠ 0: O(X^{3/4+ε}) forms from the bounds on (a, b, c). a, d ≠ 0: O(X^{3/4+ε}) triples (a, b, d); a linear factor rx + sy has r | a and s | d, O(X^ε) choices by the divisor bound (requested from AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5), and then f(−s, r) = 0 determines c.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Order check: X^{3/4+ε} is below the error term X^{5/6} of Theorem 20.
- Quartic analogue: ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-quartic-forms-in-the-main-body (O(X^{2/3+ε})).

<a id="st2-binary-cubic-forms-with-cyclic-stabilizer"></a>

### 2.42 Lemma 22: points with stabiliser C_3 are O(X^{3/4+ε})

The number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of integral binary cubic forms with 0 < Disc < X whose stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ) is cyclic of order 3 is O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}). Consequently, for every v ∈ U_ℝ^(0), the number of points of U_ℤ ∩ R_X(v) (with multiplicity) with stabiliser C_3 is O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}), with the implied constant independent of v.

**Hypotheses.** Positive discriminant: by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-irreducible-integral-binary-cubic-forms no irreducible form of negative discriminant has stabiliser C_3; When concluding that O(X^{3/4+epsilon}) is lower order than X^{5/6}, choose 0<epsilon<1/12; the bound itself is stated for every positive epsilon.

**Dependencies.** [The GL_2(ℤ)-stabiliser of an irreducible integral binary cubic form is trivial or cyclic of order 3](#st2-stabilizers-of-irreducible-integral-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-irreducible-integral-binary-cubic-forms`); [Lemma 21: reducible integral binary cubic forms with a ≠ 0 in R_X(v) number O(X^{3/4+ε})](#st2-reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.2, Lemma 22 and proof, p. 11. The lemma and the Hessian argument of its proof.

**Proof route.**

1. The orbit-multiplicity ratio is 6/3=2 away from the modular boundary. On the closed boundary the count can be larger, but local finiteness of the tessellation gives a universal finite bound on the overlap. Thus the point count for every v is bounded by a universal constant times the class count; equality to twice the count is not needed.
2. Take v = x^3 − 3xy^2, whose Hessian covariant H_f = (b^2 − 3ac)x^2 + (bc − 9ad)xy + (c^2 − 3bd)y^2 is 9(x^2 + y^2). The Hessian is SL_2-equivariant, so for g ∈ F the Hessian of g·v is 9 times the positive definite quadratic form attached to g, which is reduced (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates): F·v consists of forms with |bc − 9ad| ≤ b^2 − 3ac ≤ c^2 − 3bd.
3. An order-three stabilizer has determinant one and preserves the Hessian. A reduced positive definite binary quadratic form with such an automorphism has coefficients A=C=|B|: both x²+xy+y² and x²−xy+y² occur on the two boundary edges. Treat these two signs separately; A=C=±B determines at most O(1) choices of c from each triple (a,b,d).
4. The triples (a, b, d) of forms in R_X(v) number O(X^{3/4+ε}) by the coefficient bounds of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body (the case a = 0 forces f = b·xy(x + y) up to the constraint and contributes O(X^{1/4})).

**Acceptance checks.**

- The source notes that the count is asymptotic to (π√3/18)X^{1/2}; only the upper bound X^{3/4+ε} is needed.
- C_3-points are absorbed into the error term O(X^{5/6}) of Theorem 20.

<a id="st2-invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms"></a>

### 2.43 Proposition 23, corrected: |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv is GL_2(ℝ)-invariant, with the Jacobian constant 4π

Let dg = t^{−2} du d^×t dk d^×λ be the Haar measure on GL_2(ℝ), with dk the invariant probability measure on SO_2(ℝ) extended to the other coset of O_2(ℝ), and dv = da db dc dd on U_ℝ. For i ∈ {0, 1}, v_i ∈ U_ℝ^(i) and every f ∈ C_c(U_ℝ^(i)): ∫_{GL_2(ℝ)} f(g·v_i) dg = (1/4π) ∫_{GL_2(ℝ)·v_i} f(v) |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv = (n_i/4π) ∫_{U_ℝ^(i)} f(v) |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv, where GL_2(ℝ)·v_i is the multiset image (each point covered n_i times). Equivalently, on GL_2^+(ℝ) the map g ↦ g·v_i satisfies dv = 4π|Disc(g·v_i)| dg.

**Hypotheses.** The constant depends on the normalisation of dk; the source's 1/(2π) is off by a factor 2 for its stated normalisation (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E305)

**Dependencies.** [Real binary cubic forms: the two open GL_2(ℝ)-orbits and their stabilisers (n_0 = 6, n_1 = 2)](#st2-real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`); `mathlib:MeasureTheory.integral_image_eq_integral_abs_det_fderiv_smul`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.3, Proposition 23, p. 12. The proposition, with the constant corrected from 1/(2π) to 1/(4π) (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E305).

**Proof route.**

1. At g = n(u)a(t)k(θ)λ the Jacobian determinant of (u, t, θ, λ) ↦ g·v with respect to da db dc dd equals ±2|Disc(g·v)|·t^{−3}λ^{−1} (checked symbolically at the forms xy(x − y), x^3 + xy^2, x^3 − 3xy^2 and 2x^3 + x^2y − 5xy^2 + 7y^3); since t^{−3}λ^{−1} du dt dθ dλ = 2π·dg, dv = 4π|Disc(g·v)| dg on GL_2^+(ℝ).
2. |Disc|^{−1}dv is then GL_2(ℝ)-invariant (Disc(γ·v) = (det γ)^2 Disc(v) and the twisted action has determinant (det γ)^2 on U_ℝ).
3. The orbit map is n_i-to-one onto U_ℝ^(i) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms); decompose into injective pieces and apply the change-of-variables formula (MeasureTheory.integral_image_eq_integral_abs_det_fderiv_smul). The component of determinant −1 contributes the same as GL_2^+(ℝ) by right translation.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Check against Davenport: with this constant and the strict Gauss domain (covolume π/12), Vol(R_X(v))/n_0 = 4π·(X/4)·(π/12)/6 = π^2X/72, Davenport's constant.
- In the source's normalisation the product of the Jacobian constant 2π with the stated covolume ζ(2)/π is 2ζ(2), equal to the product 4π·ζ(2)/(2π) here, so Theorem 20 is unaffected.

<a id="st2-averaged-count-of-binary-cubic-orbits"></a>

### 2.44 The averaged orbit count N(S; X) of binary cubic forms and the regions B(n, t, λ, X)

Fix C ≥ 2 and the compact SO_2(ℝ)-invariant set B = B(C) := {w ∈ U_ℝ : 3a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 3d^2 ≤ C, |Disc(w)| ≥ 1}. For i ∈ {0, 1}, S ⊆ U_ℤ^(i) and X > 0 define N(S; X) := ∫_{v ∈ B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)} #{x ∈ F·v ∩ S^irr : |Disc(x)| < X} |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv / (n_i ∫_{B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)} |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv), where F is the strict Gauss domain, F·v is a multiset and S^irr is the set of elements of S irreducible over ℚ. For n = n(u), t > 0, λ > 0 put B(n, t, λ, X) := n a(t) λ (B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)) ∩ {|Disc| < X}, and M_i := (n_i/4π) ∫_{B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)} |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv.

**Hypotheses.** 3a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 3d^2 is three times the Bombieri norm, invariant under SO_2(ℝ) for the twisted action; Only irreducible elements are counted

**Dependencies.** [Real binary cubic forms: the two open GL_2(ℝ)-orbits and their stabilisers (n_0 = 6, n_1 = 2)](#st2-real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms`); [The GL_2(ℤ)-stabiliser of an irreducible integral binary cubic form is trivial or cyclic of order 3](#st2-stabilizers-of-irreducible-integral-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-irreducible-integral-binary-cubic-forms`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.3, (17), p. 12. The definition (the source's instruction to weight C_3-points by 1/3 is replaced by the exact class weights; sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E312). [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.3, p. 12. The averaging set B.

**API.**

- `cubicAveragedCount` (constructor): N(S; X) by the formula (17), with C and i as parameters.
- `cubicRegionB` (data): B(n, t, λ, X) = n a(t) λ (B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)) ∩ {|Disc| < X}.
- `cubicAveragingConstant` (data): M_i = (n_i/4π) ∫_{B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)} |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv.
- `cubicAveragedCount_eq_sum_classes` (compatibility): For GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S: N(S; X) = Σ over irreducible classes [x] ⊆ S with |Disc(x)| < X of 1/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x).
- `cubicAveragedCount_union` (structure): Additivity over disjoint subsets.
- `cubicAveragedCount_mono` (relation): Monotone in S and in X.
- `cubicAveragedCount_indep` (characterisation): For invariant S the value does not depend on C in the range C≥2.
- `bombieri_smul_rotation` (other): 3a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 3d^2 is invariant under the twisted action of SO_2(ℝ), so B is SO_2(ℝ)-invariant.

**Checks.**

- `cubicAveragedCount.empty` (degenerate): N(∅; X) = 0 for every X, and N(S; X) = 0 for X ≤ 1 (a nonzero integral discriminant has absolute value ≥ 1).
- `cubicAveragedCount.reducible_zero` (computation): For S = {f ∈ U_ℤ^(i) : a(f) = 0}, N(S; X) = 0: every such form has the factor y.
- `cubicAveragedCount.cyclic_weight` (non-example): The class of the cyclic form x^3 + x^2y − 2xy^2 − y^3 contributes 1/3, not 1, to N(U_ℤ^(0); X) for X > 49.
- `cubicAveragedCount.invariant` (compatibility): For S = U_ℤ^(i), N(S; X) = Σ_{[x]} 1/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x), independent of C.
- `cubicAveragingSet.positive_denominators` (computation): At C=2, (1/3,0,−1,0) has norm expression 4/3 and discriminant 4/3; (1/2,0,0,1/2) has expression 3/2 and discriminant −27/16. Both strict inequalities persist on open neighborhoods, so both averaging denominators are positive.

**Proof route.**

1. The denominator is positive and finite for C≥2: the positive-discriminant form (a,b,c,d)=(1/3,0,−1,0) has Bombieri expression 4/3<2 and discriminant 4/3>1; the negative form (1/2,0,0,1/2) has expression 3/2<2 and |Disc|=27/16>1. Thus both loci contain an open subset of B(C); compactness and |Disc|≥1 give finiteness.
2. For GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S the integrand is, for almost every v, with respect to |Disc(v)|^{-1}dv (the boundary exceptions are null under the orbit-map change of variables), Σ over irreducible classes [x] ⊆ S with |Disc(x)| < X of n_i/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x) (F·v is n_i fundamental domains), so N(S; X) = Σ_{[x]} 1/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x): classes are counted with weight 1, and the classes with stabiliser C_3 with weight 1/3.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For S = U_ℤ^(i) the averaged count differs from the number of classes by at most the O(X^{3/4+ε}) classes with stabiliser C_3.
- N is additive over disjoint subsets, invariant or not.

**Consumers.** Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman, (20)-(26) — N(U_ℤ^(i); X) is computed through the averaged count; Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman, Section 5.5, (28)-(31) — N(L_j; X) for non-invariant lattice translates; Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman, Section 8 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3) — N of the sets of maximal forms and of forms maximal and not totally ramified at every p, via the sieve

<a id="st2-averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms"></a>

### 2.45 The averaging formula for binary cubic forms, (20)-(23), with the corrected constants

For i ∈ {0, 1}, S ⊆ U_ℤ^(i) and X > 0: N(S; X) = (1/M_i) ∫_{g ∈ F} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ g(B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)) : |Disc(x)| < X} dg = (1/(2M_i)) ∫_{n(u)a(t)λ ∈ N′(t)A′Λ} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ B(n, t, λ, X)} t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ, with M_i = (n_i/4π) ∫_{B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)} |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv.

**Hypotheses.** The factor 1/2 is ∫_{K_+} dk; the constant 4π is that of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms (the source has M_i with 2π and no 1/2; see sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E305 and E301)

**Dependencies.** [The averaged orbit count N(S; X) of binary cubic forms and the regions B(n, t, λ, X)](#st2-averaged-count-of-binary-cubic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-cubic-orbits`); [Proposition 23, corrected: |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv is GL_2(ℝ)-invariant, with the Jacobian constant 4π](#st2-invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.3, (18)-(23), pp. 12-13. The formula, with M_i and the factor 1/2 adjusted to the strict domain and the corrected Jacobian constant.

**Proof route.**

1. Choose H^(i) ⊆ GL_2(ℝ) maximal with H^(i)·v_i = B ∩ U_ℝ^(i) as an n_i-fold multiset. By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms, ∫_{B ∩ U^(i)} Φ(v)|Disc(v)|^{−1} dv = (4π/n_i) ∫_{H^(i)} Φ(h·v_i) dh.
2. Apply this to Φ(v) = #{g ∈ F : x = g·v}, sum over x, exchange the order (unimodularity of GL_2(ℝ)) as in (18)-(19), and use that the multiset H^(i)·v_i covers B ∩ U^(i) n_i times: the numerator of N(S; X) equals 4π ∫_F #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ gB : |Disc(x)| < X} dg.
3. Divide by n_i ∫ |Disc|^{−1}: this is the first formula. For the second, write g = n(u)a(t)kλ with k ∈ K_+, use kB = B and ∫_{K_+} dk = 1/2 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-cubic-orbits).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Inserting Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) for the count gives Vol(R_X(v))/n_i, independent of v (the computation in the proof of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms).
- For invariant S both sides are independent of C.

<a id="st2-binary-cubic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp"></a>

### 2.46 Lemma 25 and (28): lattice points with a ≠ 0 in B(n, t, λ, X), for translates of mU_ℤ

Let C bound the absolute values of all coefficients of all forms in B. Let m ≥ 1 and let L′ = v_0 + mU_ℤ, and let a′ ≥ 1 be the smallest nonzero |a|-coordinate of a point of L′. For u ∈ [−1/2, 1/2], t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2, λ > 0 and X > 0, the number of points (a, b, c, d) ∈ L′ ∩ B(n(u), t, λ, X) with a ≠ 0 is 0 if Cλ/t^3 < a′, and otherwise m^{−4}Vol(B(n(u), t, λ, X)) + O(C^3t^3λ^3/m^3 + C^2t^4λ^2/m^2 + Ct^3λ/m + 1), the implied constant absolute. For m = 1 the error is O(max(C^3t^3λ^3, 1)).

**Hypotheses.** The x^3-coefficient of a form in B(n, t, λ, X) is at most Cλ/t^3 in absolute value; Davenport's lemma is the input (a request)

**Dependencies.** `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4`; [The averaged orbit count N(S; X) of binary cubic forms and the regions B(n, t, λ, X)](#st2-averaged-count-of-binary-cubic-orbits) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-cubic-orbits`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.3, Lemma 25 and proof, p. 13. The case m = 1. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.5, (28), p. 14. The translate version.

**Proof route.**

1. Under the twisted action, n(u) with |u| ≤ 1/2 adds to each coefficient a bounded combination of the preceding ones, a(t) multiplies them by t^{−3}, t^{−1}, t, t^3 and λ·1 by λ; so the ranges of (a, b, c, d) are O(Cλ/t^3, Cλ/t, Cλt, Cλt^3).
2. If Cλ/t^3 < a′ no point of L′ with a ≠ 0 fits.
3. Otherwise apply Davenport's lemma (requested from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4) to the image of B(n, t, λ, X) under v ↦ (v − v_0)/m: the projection onto a = 0 has volume O(C^3t^3λ^3/m^3), the 2-dimensional projections O(C^2t^4λ^2/m^2) (the two largest ranges), the 1-dimensional ones O(Ct^3λ/m).
4. Remove the a=0 slice after Davenport: its count is bounded by the product of one plus the three remaining coefficient ranges divided by m. Expanding that product gives exactly terms of the same orders as the displayed error; the slice has zero four-dimensional volume.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Unlike the quartic cusp, the cubic cusp t^3 > Cλ still contains integral points with a = 0 only, but in the range t^3 ≤ Cλ the error C^3t^3λ^3 integrates to X^{5/6}, the size of the error term (and of the second main term of Shintani, which this fragment does not plan).
- For m = 1 the terms t^4λ^2 and t^3λ are dominated by t^3λ^3 in the range t^3 ≤ Cλ, t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2.

<a id="st2-davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms"></a>

### 2.47 Theorem 20 (Davenport): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms of bounded discriminant

(a) N(U_ℤ^(0); X) = (π^2/72)X + O(X^{5/6}) and N(U_ℤ^(1); X) = (π^2/24)X + O(X^{5/6}), where N(U_ℤ^(i); X) is the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms f with 0 < (−1)^i Disc(f) < X. (b) For every v ∈ U_ℝ^(i), Vol(R_X(v)) = π^2X/12, where R_X(v) = {w ∈ F·v : |Disc(w)| < X} is the multiset over the strict Gauss domain; so Vol(R_X(v))/n_i = π^2X/(12n_i). (c) Cusp tail: there is c = c(C) such that for every S ⊆ U_ℤ^(i), T ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2 and X ≥ 1, (1/(2M_i)) ∫_{t > T} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ B(n, t, λ, X)} t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ ≤ c·X/T^2 + O(X^{5/6}).

**Hypotheses.** Classes under GL_2(ℤ) with the twisted action; the classes with stabiliser C_3 are counted with weight 1 (their number is O(X^{3/4+ε})); Davenport's original error was O(X^{15/16}); When concluding that O(X^{3/4+epsilon}) is lower order than X^{5/6}, choose 0<epsilon<1/12; the bound itself is stated for every positive epsilon.

**Dependencies.** [The averaging formula for binary cubic forms, (20)-(23), with the corrected constants](#st2-averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms`); [Lemma 25 and (28): lattice points with a ≠ 0 in B(n, t, λ, X), for translates of mU_ℤ](#st2-binary-cubic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp`); [Lemma 21: reducible integral binary cubic forms with a ≠ 0 in R_X(v) number O(X^{3/4+ε})](#st2-reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body`); [Lemma 22: points with stabiliser C_3 are O(X^{3/4+ε})](#st2-binary-cubic-forms-with-cyclic-stabilizer) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-forms-with-cyclic-stabilizer`); [Proposition 23, corrected: |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv is GL_2(ℝ)-invariant, with the Jacobian constant 4π](#st2-invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms`); [Vol(PGL_2(ℤ)\PGL_2(ℝ)) = 2ζ(2) for the ℤ-form ω, and the Iwasawa-measure volume of Gauss's domain](#st2-covolume-of-pgl2-z) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/covolume-of-pgl2-z`); [Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure](#st2-gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5, Theorem 20, p. 9. Part (a). [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.4, p. 14. Part (b), recomputed with the corrected constants 4π and ζ(2)/(2π), whose product is the same (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E305). [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Section 1.2, Theorem 1.5, printed p. 3. The classical statement, which part (a) proves with an error term.

**Proof route.**

1. By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms with S = U_ℤ^(i), the integrand vanishes unless t^3 ≤ Cλ and λ ≤ X^{1/4} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp; B has |Disc| ≥ 1 and points with a = 0 are reducible).
2. Irreducible points = points with a ≠ 0 minus reducible ones: O(X^{3/4+ε}) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body; the C_3-classes change the count by O(X^{3/4+ε}) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-forms-with-cyclic-stabilizer).
3. The error O(max(C^3t^3λ^3, 1)) integrates over t^3 ≤ Cλ, λ ≤ X^{1/4} to O(X^{5/6}); the part of the main term with t^3 > Cλ is O(X^{5/6}) since Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) ≪ λ^4.
4. Main term: ∫ Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) over all of N′A′Λ is 2∫_F Vol(gB ∩ {|Disc| < X}) dg; writing Vol(gB ∩ …) = ∫_{w ∈ B} 1[|Disc(gw)| < X]·|Disc(gw)|/|Disc(w)| dw and applying ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms gives (1/4π) Vol(R_X(v)) ∫_B |Disc|^{−1}, so the main term is Vol(R_X(v))/n_i (Vol(R_X(w)) does not depend on w ∈ U_ℝ^(i), as F·w is n_i fundamental domains).
5. (b) For |Disc(v)| = 1, Vol(R_X(v)) = ∫_{g ∈ F} 1[λ^4 < X]·4π|Disc(g·v)| dg = 4π ∫_0^{X^{1/4}} λ^4 d^×λ · ∫_{N′A′K_+} t^{−2} du d^×t dk = 4π·(X/4)·(π/12) = π^2X/12 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/covolume-of-pgl2-z (b); for general v rescale by λ·1.
6. (a) follows with n_0 = 6, n_1 = 2. (c) Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) ≪ λ^4, ∫_{t > T} t^{−2} d^×t ≤ T^{−2}/2 and ∫^{X^{1/4}} λ^4 d^×λ = X/4; the error terms integrate to O(X^{5/6}).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Davenport's constants: π^2/72 ≈ 0.1371 and π^2/24 ≈ 0.4112.
- Delone-Faddeev reading (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3): these count isomorphism classes of orders in cubic fields of bounded discriminant.
- The error O(X^{5/6}) is of the same order as Shintani's second main term, which requires the slicing argument of BST Section 6.

<a id="st2-binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions"></a>

### 2.48 Theorem 26 with (29)-(31): binary cubic forms in lattice translates, uniformly in the modulus

(a) Let 1 ≤ m ≤ X^{1/6} and L = v_0 + mU_ℤ. Then N(L ∩ U_ℤ^(i); X) = m^{−4}·(π^2/(12n_i))X + O(m^{−3}X^{5/6}) − R_L(X), where the implied constant is independent of m, v_0 and X, and R_L(X) ≥ 0 is the averaged contribution of reducible points with nonzero leading coefficient in L, so that Σ_L R_L(X) = O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}) over any finite family of disjoint translates. (b) If S ⊆ U_ℤ is a union of k translates of mU_ℤ with m ≤ X^{1/6}, then N(S ∩ U_ℤ^(i); X) = (k/m^4)(π^2/(12n_i))X + O(k m^{−3}X^{5/6}) + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}). (c) If S ⊆ U_ℤ^(i) is defined by a product of finitely many independently imposed local congruence conditions modulo prime powers, then lim_{X→∞} N(S ∩ U_ℤ^(i); X)/X = (π^2/(12n_i))·∏_p μ_p(S).

**Hypotheses.** N is the averaged count. For invariant S its class weight is 1/#Stab_GL2(Z)(f), not exactly one: cyclic cubic classes have weight 1/3. Their O(X^{1/2}) contribution can be absorbed when converting to the unweighted asymptotic.; m ≤ X^{1/6} makes the lower-dimensional projection terms of (29) smaller than m^{−3}X^{5/6}; Use the positive averaging denominators with C≥2. For (c), the allowed residue set modulo m must be the CRT product of its local projections; an arbitrary coupled residue set does not satisfy the displayed product formula.

**Dependencies.** [The averaging formula for binary cubic forms, (20)-(23), with the corrected constants](#st2-averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms`); [Lemma 25 and (28): lattice points with a ≠ 0 in B(n, t, λ, X), for translates of mU_ℤ](#st2-binary-cubic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp`); [Theorem 20 (Davenport): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms of bounded discriminant](#st2-davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms`); [Lemma 21: reducible integral binary cubic forms with a ≠ 0 in R_X(v) number O(X^{3/4+ε})](#st2-reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body`); [Lemma 22: points with stabiliser C_3 are O(X^{3/4+ε})](#st2-binary-cubic-forms-with-cyclic-stabilizer) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-forms-with-cyclic-stabilizer`); [Functions and sets defined by congruence conditions; acceptable functions](#st2-functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.5, Theorem 26, p. 14. Part (c). [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 5.5, (30)-(31), p. 15. Parts (a)-(b).

**Proof route.**

1. (a) Repeat the proof of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms with ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp for L: integrating its error terms gives (29), O(C^{10/3}X^{5/6}/(a′^{1/3}m^3) + C^{8/3}X^{2/3}/(a′^{2/3}m^2) + C^{4/3}X^{1/3}/(a′^{1/3}m) + log X), which is O(m^{−3}X^{5/6}) for a′ ≥ 1 and m ≤ X^{1/6}.
2. The reducible remainder is nonnegative and additive over finite disjoint sets before averaging, so its total is O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}) by the reducible bound. Cyclic-stabilizer corrections are needed only when converting the weighted class count to the unweighted count; they are not part of this remainder.
3. (b) Sum (a) over the k translates. (c) Fix S, let X → ∞ in (b), and use k m^{−4} = ∏_p μ_p(S) (under the CRT-product hypothesis; Chinese remainder theorem; ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions).

**Acceptance checks.**

- S = U_ℤ recovers Theorem 20 (m = 1).
- Uniformity check: for S_p = {f : p | a(f)} (m = p, k = p^3) the error is O(X^{5/6}) + O(X^{3/4+ε}) uniformly for p ≤ X^{1/6}.

<a id="st2-index-p-switching-for-binary-cubic-forms"></a>

### 2.49 Index-p switching: forms with p^2 | a, p | b come from forms of discriminant Disc/p^2 with a marked root modulo p

Let p be a prime and use the twisted action on U_ℚ. (a) If f = (a, b, c, d) ∈ U_ℤ has p^2 | a and p | b, then f′ := diag(p^{−1}, 1)·f = (a/p^2, b/p, c, pd) ∈ U_ℤ, Disc(f′) = p^{−2}Disc(f), f′(0, 1) ≡ 0 (mod p), and f = diag(p, 1)·f′. (b) Conversely, if g ∈ U_ℤ and α ∈ ℙ^1(𝔽_p) is a root of g mod p, choose γ_α ∈ GL_2(ℤ) whose bottom row reduces to a representative of α; then f_{g,α} := diag(p, 1)·(γ_α·g) ∈ U_ℤ has p^2 | a and p | b, and its GL_2(ℤ)-class depends only on the GL_2(ℤ)-class of g and on α modulo the action of Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(g). (c) Consequently every GL_2(ℤ)-class of forms f with Disc(f) ≠ 0 having a translate with p^2 | a and p | b is the class of some f_{g,α} with |Disc(g)| = |Disc(f)|/p^2, and the number of such classes attached to one class [g] is at most the number of roots of g mod p in ℙ^1(𝔽_p): at most 3 if g ≢ 0 (mod p), at most p + 1 otherwise.

**Hypotheses.** This is the form-theoretic content of BST Lemma 13 and Propositions 15-16 (index-p overrings and subrings of cubic rings); no ring theory is used; The twisted action is the one of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings

**Dependencies.** [Delone-Faddeev: GL2(R)-classes of binary cubic forms parametrize cubic rings](#st1-delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings`); [Real binary cubic forms: the two open GL_2(ℝ)-orbits and their stabilisers (n_0 = 6, n_1 = 2)](#st2-real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms`); `mathlib:Polynomial.card_roots'`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 3, Lemma 13 and the sentence after it, pp. 6-7. The form conditions (i) and (ii) whose classes are counted here. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Proof of Propositions 15 and 16, pp. 7-8. The switching f ↦ f′ and the root parametrisation, stated here for forms.

**Proof route.**

1. (a) diag(p^{−1}, 1)·f = f(x/p, y)/det(diag(p^{−1}, 1)) = p·f(x/p, y) = (a/p^2)x^3 + (b/p)x^2y + cxy^2 + pdy^3, and Disc(γ·f) = (det γ)^2 Disc(f) with det γ = 1/p (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms (a)).
2. (b) γ_α·g vanishes at [0 : 1] mod p, i.e. its y^3-coefficient d′ is divisible by p; then diag(p, 1)·(γ_α·g) = (p^2a′, pb′, c′, d′/p) is integral. Two choices γ_α, γ′_α differ by δ ∈ GL_2(ℤ) with p | δ_21, and diag(p, 1)δ diag(p, 1)^{−1} = [[δ_11, pδ_12], [δ_21/p, δ_22]] ∈ GL_2(ℤ); replacing g by ε·g (ε ∈ GL_2(ℤ)) moves α accordingly.
3. (c) Given f, move it so that p^2 | a and p | b, and take g = f′ from (a), α = [0 : 1]; then f = f_{g,α}. A nonzero binary cubic form over 𝔽_p has at most 3 roots in ℙ^1(𝔽_p) (Polynomial.card_roots' for its dehomogenisation, plus possibly [1 : 0]); the zero form has p + 1.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For p = 5 and g = x^3 + xy^2 (which vanishes at [0 : 1]), f_{g,[0:1]} = diag(5, 1)·g = g(5x, y)/5 = 25x^3 + xy^2, and Disc(f) = −100 = 25·Disc(g).
- The bound 3 (not p + 1) for g ≢ 0 mod p is what makes the switching estimate O(X/p^2) rather than O(X/p).

<a id="st2-uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms"></a>

### 2.50 Proposition 29 (non-maximal part), for forms: the classes in W_p^DH have O(X/p^2) elements of discriminant < X, uniformly in p

For a prime p let W_p^DH := {f ∈ U_ℤ : f ∈ pU_ℤ, or some γ ∈ GL_2(ℤ) has γ·f = (a, b, c, d) with p^2 | a and p | b}. There is an absolute constant C such that for every prime p and every X ≥ 1 the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible f ∈ W_p^DH with 0 < |Disc(f)| < X is at most C·X/p^2.

**Hypotheses.** W_p^DH is the complement of the Davenport-Heilbronn set U_p; by BST Theorem 14 (owned with the Delone-Faddeev correspondence) it is the set of forms whose cubic ring is not maximal at p, but only the form definition is used here

**Dependencies.** [Index-p switching: forms with p^2 | a, p | b come from forms of discriminant Disc/p^2 with a marked root modulo p](#st2-index-p-switching-for-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/index-p-switching-for-binary-cubic-forms`); [Theorem 20 (Davenport): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms of bounded discriminant](#st2-davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.2, Proposition 29 and proof, pp. 23-24. The statement for the non-maximal part W_p; the proof via overrings of index p is transcribed into forms. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Proof of Proposition 29, case (i), p. 23. The counting step, with Lemma 30 replaced by the root bound of the switching lemma.

**Proof route.**

1. Let N(Y) be the number of classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms with 0 < |Disc| < Y; by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms, N(Y) ≤ C_0·Y for Y ≥ 1, and N(Y) = 0 for Y ≤ 1.
2. f ∈ pU_ℤ: f = pf_0 with f_0 irreducible and Disc(f) = p^4 Disc(f_0), at most N(X/p^4) classes.
3. Otherwise, by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/index-p-switching-for-binary-cubic-forms, the classes are among the f_{g,α} with |Disc(g)| < X/p^2 and g irreducible (g is GL_2(ℚ)-equivalent to f): at most 3N(X/p^2) from g ≢ 0 (mod p), and at most (p + 1)N(X/p^6) from g = pg_0.
4. Total ≤ C_0(X/p^4 + 3X/p^2 + (p + 1)X/p^6) ≤ 5C_0·X/p^2.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The bound is uniform in p; for p^2 > X the set is empty.
- The totally ramified maximal forms (Y_p of BST) are not in W_p^DH; BST bound them by class field theory, while here they are covered by the geometric sieve in ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-binary-cubic-discriminants.

<a id="st2-uniformity-estimate-for-binary-cubic-discriminants"></a>

### 2.51 A uniform tail estimate for binary cubic forms whose discriminant is divisible by p^2 for some p > M

For a prime p let W_p(U) := {f ∈ U_ℤ : p^2 | Disc(f)}. There are constants c and C_T (for each T ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2, independent of M) such that for every M ≥ 3, lim sup_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(U); X)/X ≤ C_T/(M log M) + c/T^2, where N counts GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible forms with 0 < |Disc| < X. Consequently lim_{M→∞} lim sup_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(U); X)/X = 0.

**Hypotheses.** Both signs of the discriminant are included; The strongly divisible part (triple root modulo p, which contains the maximal totally ramified forms) is handled by the geometric sieve; BST use class field theory for the totally ramified part

**Dependencies.** [Proposition 29 (non-maximal part), for forms: the classes in W_p^DH have O(X/p^2) elements of discriminant < X, uniformly in p](#st2-uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms`); [The quantitative Ekedahl geometric sieve (Bhargava, Theorem 3.3; Bhargava-Shankar, Theorem 2.17)](#st2-quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve`); [Strong multiples of p^2 reduce into the codimension-two locus f = ∂f/∂x_n = 0](#st2-strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus`); [The discriminants of binary quartic and binary cubic forms are primitive and coprime to their derivatives in the last coefficient](#st2-discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two`); [Strong and weak multiples of p^2: the sets W_p, W_p^(1), W_p^(2) of binary quartic and binary cubic forms](#st2-strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values`); [Chebyshev-type bounds for the prime-counting function and for tails of prime sums](#st2-chebyshev-bounds-for-prime-sums) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/chebyshev-bounds-for-prime-sums`); [The averaging formula for binary cubic forms, (20)-(23), with the corrected constants](#st2-averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms`); [Theorem 20 (Davenport): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms of bounded discriminant](#st2-davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.2, p. 23. The role of the estimate; the node proves the tail form needed by the sieve, covering the totally ramified part by the geometric sieve instead of class field theory. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Proof of Proposition 29, last paragraph, p. 24. The step replaced by the geometric sieve (Datskovsky-Wright [13] was not read).

**Proof route.**

1. Decomposition for p ≥ 3: if f ∈ W_p(U) and f mod p ∉ Y_3(𝔽_p), where Y_3 = V(Disc, ∂Disc/∂d), then f ∈ W_p^DH. Indeed p ∤ ∂Disc/∂d(f) makes f weakly divisible (gradient characterisation in ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values), so f ≢ 0 (mod p) and f mod p has no triple root (a triple root moved to [1 : 0] gives p | a, b, c, hence p^2 | Disc(f + pg) for all g); as p | Disc(f), f mod p has a double root α ∈ ℙ^1(𝔽_p) (a repeated root of a cubic is rational). Move α to [1 : 0] by γ ∈ GL_2(ℤ): γ·f = (a, b, c, d) with p | a, p | b and p ∤ c, and Disc(γ·f) ≡ −4ac^3 (mod p^2), so p^2 | Disc forces p^2 | a (p odd).
2. The W_p^DH part: Σ_{p>M} N(W_p^DH; X) ≤ C X Σ_{p>M} p^{−2} = O(X/(M log M)) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/chebyshev-bounds-for-prime-sums.
3. The Y_3 part: by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms split the integral at t = T. For t > T use part (c) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms: ≤ cX/T^2 + O(X^{5/6}). For t ≤ T all regions lie in X^{1/4}·Ω_T using the compact closure of the bounded region Ω_T. The multiplicity bound is uniform: the truncated compact matrix set is covered by finitely many translates of a fixed Gauss region (local finiteness of the modular tessellation), and each such region has uniformly bounded multiplicity, including its boundary. Thus each integral point is counted with bounded weight, and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve with n = 4, k = 2, r = X^{1/4} (Y_3 of codimension 2 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two; strongly divisible forms reduce into Y_3 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus) gives O_T(X/(M log M) + X^{3/4}).
4. Divide by X, let X → ∞, then choose T and M as in the quartic case.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3: every acceptable collection of local specifications in the sense of BST (Σ_p contains the maximal, not totally ramified cubic rings over ℤ_p for large p) corresponds to an acceptable set of forms for Disc, and this theorem is the tail estimate the sieve needs, for Theorems 1, 2 and 8 of BST alike.
- The rate C_T/(M log M) + c/T^2 is uniform in the congruence conditions imposed at primes ≤ M.

<a id="st2-sieve-to-acceptable-functions-for-binary-cubic-forms"></a>

### 2.52 Counting binary cubic forms weighted by an acceptable function defined by infinitely many congruence conditions

Let φ : U_ℤ → [0, 1] be acceptable for Disc and defined by congruence conditions via GL_2(ℤ)-invariant local functions φ_p : U_{ℤ_p} → [0, 1] (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions). For i ∈ {0, 1} let N_φ(U_ℤ^(i); X) be the number of irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-classes in U_ℤ^(i) with |Disc| < X, each class counted with weight φ. Then N_φ(U_ℤ^(i); X) = (π^2/(12n_i))·∏_p ∫_{U_{ℤ_p}} φ_p(f) df · X + o(X), and the Euler product converges. In particular, for an acceptable set S = ⋂_p S_p, lim_{X→∞} N(S ∩ U_ℤ^(i); X)/X = (π^2/(12n_i))∏_p μ_p(S_p).

**Hypotheses.** Acceptability: φ_p = 1 on {p^2 ∤ Disc} for large p; The cubic-ring translation (maximality, splitting types, local masses Σ 1/(Disc_p(R)|Aut(R)|)) belongs to ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3 and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1

**Dependencies.** [Theorem 26 with (29)-(31): binary cubic forms in lattice translates, uniformly in the modulus](#st2-binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions`); [A uniform tail estimate for binary cubic forms whose discriminant is divisible by p^2 for some p > M](#st2-uniformity-estimate-for-binary-cubic-discriminants) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-binary-cubic-discriminants`); [Functions and sets defined by congruence conditions; acceptable functions](#st2-functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions`); [The p-adic density of {p^2 | f} is O(p^{-2})](#st2-local-density-of-values-divisible-by-p-squared) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/local-density-of-values-divisible-by-p-squared`); [The discriminants of binary quartic and binary cubic forms are primitive and coprime to their derivatives in the last coefficient](#st2-discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.3, proof of Theorem 1, p. 24. The upper-bound half of the sieve, for the set of maximal forms. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.4, p. 25. The general acceptable case, stated here for weighted counts of forms.

**Proof route.**

1. Approximate φ_p from above and below by functions defined modulo p^n, as in ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/squarefree-sieve-for-binary-quartic-forms; convergence of the Euler product from 1 − ∫φ_p ≤ μ_p{p^2 | Disc} ≤ Cp^{−2} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/local-density-of-values-divisible-by-p-squared, Disc being primitive and coprime to ∂Disc/∂d by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two).
2. Upper bound: a weight defined modulo finitely many prime powers is a finite linear combination of indicators of translates of mU_ℤ; ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions gives its limit; let the truncation grow.
3. Lower bound: fix M above the acceptability threshold and approximate each of the finitely many factors p≤M by its actual infimum on residue cylinders modulo p^n, with n≥2. The finite approximation has the required lattice-count limit as X→∞. Its difference from the full weight has two contributions: the finite-prime approximation error, whose integral tends to zero as n→∞, and the tail union over p>M, bounded by the uniformity estimate. Take X→∞, then n→∞ at fixed M, then M→∞. The finite approximation error is not supported only on the tail union.

**Acceptance checks.**

- φ ≡ 1 recovers Theorem 20; φ = 1_{U_p} for all p gives Davenport-Heilbronn's count of maximal cubic orders through the Delone-Faddeev and Davenport-Heilbronn correspondences (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields), with ∏_p μ_p(U_p) = ∏_p (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−3}) and limit 1/(2n_iζ(3)).
- With φ_p the indicator of forms maximal and not totally ramified at p, the local densities are (1 − p^{−2})^2 (BST Lemma 19), the input for BST Theorem 2.

**Interface qualification.**  The suggested signature explicitly assumes invariance of each p-adic factor under the integral GL₂ action, matching the cylinder-approximation proof. Invariance of only the infinite global product does not provide invariance of its finite truncations.

<a id="st2-refinement-quartic-finite-congruence-count"></a>

### 2.53 Quartic pair counts with finite local conditions

For integral pairs of ternary quadratic forms in a G_Z-invariant union S of finitely many residue classes, count absolutely irreducible orbits with 0<|Disc|<X in real signature i=0,1,2. Then N_i(S;X)=C_i X nu(S)+o_S(X), with normalized coefficient Haar measures, C_i=zeta(2)^2 zeta(3)/(2 n_i) and (n_0,n_1,n_2)=(24,4,8). Absolutely irreducible means the quartic field has S4 closure. This is not an all-etale-orbit count. Here nu(S) is the actual proportion of allowed coefficient residues modulo a defining modulus m, with denominator m^dim(V). It equals the product of normalized prime-power densities only when the conditions are imposed independently at those primes; coupled CRT conditions use nu(S).

**Hypotheses.** Conventions and all parameter restrictions in the statement are part of the target.

**Dependencies.** [Pairs of ternary quadratic forms, the GL3 x GL2 action and the cubic resolvent form](#st1-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms`); [Bhargava: pairs of ternary quadratic forms parametrize quartic rings with cubic resolvents](#st1-bhargava-parametrization-of-quartic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/bhargava-parametrization-of-quartic-rings`); `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4/davenport-semialgebraic-count`

**Sources.** [S2/quartic](#source-s2-quartic), Theorem 22 and (32), pp.1054–1055. Independent review REV-ArithmeticStatistics--ST.2: Quartic Theorem 22/(32) gives the stated signature constants and S4 locus; corrected the finite coefficient to actual CRT density.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticCountingRefinement.quartic_finite_congruence_count`.

**Proof route.**

1. Average the finite-cover fundamental domain with its stabilizer multiplicities. Use GN.4 on each congruence translate in the main body.
2. Use the source cusp/reducibility estimate, including Lemma 12; integrate the explicitly normalized discriminant volume. Finite congruence conditions do not change the discarded error.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Check the stated exponent and constant dependence; establish finiteness before using a natural cardinal.
- Do not replace a uniform estimate by separate fixed-prime asymptotics.
- Test coupled CRT conditions: the two residues (0 mod 3,0 mod 5) and (1 mod 3,1 mod 5) have density 2/15, whereas the product of their marginal densities is 4/15. Finite disjoint residue sums must retain this coupling.

<a id="st2-refinement-quartic-fixed-reducible-resolvent"></a>

### 2.54 Quartic pairs above a reducible cubic resolvent

For every epsilon>0 and every reducible cubic ring R with nonzero discriminant d, the number of quartic-pair orbits with resolvent R is O_epsilon(|d|^(1/4+epsilon)). The constant is independent of R. This is the corrected loss-bearing input for the parent large-stabilizer estimate, not an O(|d|^1/4) assertion.

**Hypotheses.** Conventions and all parameter restrictions in the statement are part of the target.

**Dependencies.** [Quartic rings and their cubic resolvent rings](#st1-quartic-ring-and-cubic-resolvent) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/quartic-ring-and-cubic-resolvent`); [Every quartic ring has a cubic resolvent; primitive (in particular maximal) quartic rings have exactly one](#st1-existence-and-number-of-cubic-resolvents) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/existence-and-number-of-cubic-resolvents`); `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5`

**Sources.** [S2/quartic](#source-s2-quartic), Lemma 12 and proof, pp.1044–1046. Independent review REV-ArithmeticStatistics--ST.2: Lemma 12 supplies the fixed-resolvent route; the epsilon loss and unread Nakagawa/Baily/genus inputs remain explicit G-quartic obligations.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticCountingRefinement.quartic_fixed_reducible_resolvent`.

**Proof route.**

1. The fixed-resolvent field count uses the squareclass/quadratic genus bound with an epsilon loss.
2. Sum quartic suborder counts by index and include cubic-resolvent multiplicity at nonprimitive content. Nakagawa/Baily inputs remain the explicitly named source gap.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Retain epsilon in both the fixed-resolvent and induced X^(3/4+epsilon) bound.
- The zero-discriminant resolvent is excluded.

<a id="st2-refinement-quartic-nonmaximal-overramified-tail"></a>

### 2.55 Quartic nonmaximal and overramified prime bound

Let W_p be quartic pairs whose quartic ring is nonmaximal at p, or maximal with one of the overramified splitting types P^4, P^2, P1^2 P2^2 of §3.2. For absolutely irreducible S4 orbits, N_i(W_p;X)<=C X/p^2 uniformly in primes p and X>=1. Restricting to nonmaximal pairs also satisfies this bound.

**Hypotheses.** Conventions and all parameter restrictions in the statement are part of the target.

**Dependencies.** [Quartic pair counts with finite local conditions](#st2-refinement-quartic-finite-congruence-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-quartic-finite-congruence-count`); [Maximality of Q(A,B) at p in terms of the lambda-invariants](#st1-maximality-of-quartic-rings-at-p) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/maximality-of-quartic-rings-at-p`); [Every quartic ring has a cubic resolvent; primitive (in particular maximal) quartic rings have exactly one](#st1-existence-and-number-of-cubic-resolvents) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/existence-and-number-of-cubic-resolvents`)

**Sources.** [S2/quartic](#source-s2-quartic), Proposition 23, pp.1056–1058. Independent review REV-ArithmeticStatistics--ST.2: Proposition 23 bounds nonmaximal/overramified S4 orbits uniformly by X/p^2. The non-S4 transport and acyclic class-mass inputs remain G-quartic.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticCountingRefinement.quartic_nonmaximal_overramified_tail`.

**Proof route.**

1. For nonmaximal orders use the suborder index bound and sum the content factor sigma(n)/n^6.
2. For overramification use acceptable quadratic extensions of noncyclic cubic fields, square conductor norms, and the O(X) sum of their 2-class-group masses. The absolute convergence of sum 3^omega(m)/m^2 gives a p-independent constant.

**Acceptance checks.**

- State the S4 restriction and the exact W_p set.
- Do not infer the parent binary-quartic weak-discriminant bound for all irreducible resolvents without the separate transport and exceptional-orbit comparison.

For G_Z-invariant finite congruence conditions S on integral quadruples of quinary alternating forms, count irreducible quintic-field orbits of signature i=0,1,2 and 0<|Disc|<X. Then N_i(S;X)=C_i X nu(S)+o_S(X), where C_i=zeta(2)^2 zeta(3)^2 zeta(4)^2 zeta(5)/(2 n_i), (n_i)=(120,12,8). The same main term holds for S5 orbits. Here nu(S) is the actual proportion of allowed coefficient residues modulo a defining modulus m, with denominator m^dim(V). It equals the product of normalized prime-power densities only when the conditions are imposed independently at those primes; coupled CRT conditions use nu(S).

**Hypotheses.** Conventions and all parameter restrictions in the statement are part of the target.

- Check the stated exponent and constant dependence; establish finiteness before using a natural cardinal.
- Do not replace a uniform estimate by separate fixed-prime asymptotics.

<a id="st2-refinement-quintic-nonmaximal-tail"></a>

### 2.57 Uniform quintic nonmaximality estimate

Let W_p be quadruples whose quintic ring is nonmaximal at p. For irreducible quintic-field orbits N_i(W_p;X)<=C X/p^2, with C independent of p and X>=1.

**Hypotheses.** Conventions and all parameter restrictions in the statement are part of the target.

<a id="st2-refinement-global-field-generic-finite-count"></a>

### 2.58 Global-field finite-condition orbit count

Fix a global field F, a nonempty finite S containing the archimedean places, and n in {2,3,4,5}. For n=3,4,5 use the representation G_n,V_n in Global Fields I Table 1. For n=2 use §9's affine representation V={x^2+a xy+b y^2}, with G={[[1,t],[0,lambda]]:lambda invertible} acting by change of variables; this model works also in characteristic two and at places above 2. Fix an S-local type sigma. Let Gamma be commensurable with G(O_S), let L be commensurable with V(O_S), and require Gamma to preserve L. Let F_G be a fundamental domain for Gamma in G(F_S). The generic Gamma-orbit count, weighted by 1/|Stab_Gamma(v)|, is vol_L(F_G(X)v_sigma)/|Aut(sigma)|+o(X). Number-field height regions have 0<|Delta|_S<X; function-field regions have |Delta|_S=X, with X tending to infinity through admissible norm values. Additive volume is normalized by the coefficient lattice. An invariant finite congruence subset of L multiplies this main term by its actual finite residue density; independently imposed prime-power conditions factor that density. Generic means the S_n-field condition, not just nonzero Delta.

**Hypotheses.** Conventions and all parameter restrictions in the statement are part of the target.

**Dependencies.** [Bhargava: pairs of ternary quadratic forms parametrize quartic rings with cubic resolvents](#st1-bhargava-parametrization-of-quartic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/bhargava-parametrization-of-quartic-rings`); [Bhargava: quadruples of quinary alternating forms parametrize quintic rings with sextic resolvents](#st1-bhargava-parametrization-of-quintic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/bhargava-parametrization-of-quintic-rings`); `GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4/davenport-semialgebraic-count`

**Sources.** [S2/global](#source-s2-global), Theorem 4.7, §4.6, p.18; count convention §4.1; quadratic replacement §§9.1–9.4, pp.25–28. Independent review REV-ArithmeticStatistics--ST.2: Read global count conventions, Theorem 4.7 and §9. Corrected Gamma-stability, stabilizer weights, function-field norm shells, actual CRT density and the native all-characteristic quadratic model.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticCountingRefinement.global_field_generic_finite_count`.

**Proof route.**

1. Choose the S-arithmetic Siegel set and invariant bounded-height slice. Generic means the field/Galois-group condition in this representation, not merely nonzero discriminant.
2. Use the lattice estimate on a compact truncation, the coordinate cusp estimate and finite splitting-type sieve to discard nongeneric points. S-adic measure and reduction-theory interfaces are gap G-global.
3. Keep weighted counts and the source function-field norm shells. For n=2 the bounded fundamental region and nonreductive Haar/Jacobian computation are §9.2 and §9.4 inputs; Table 1's G_m model cannot parametrize characteristic-two quadratic extensions.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Check the stated exponent and constant dependence; establish finiteness before using a natural cardinal.
- Do not replace a uniform estimate by separate fixed-prime asymptotics.

<a id="st2-refinement-global-field-large-prime-tail"></a>

### 2.59 Global-field uniform tail estimate

For the fixed global field, S and native representation of the preceding count, first take the standard arithmetic lattice V(O_S) and group G(O_S). At each prime p outside S let W_p be the union of rings nonmaximal at p and rings with extra ramification there, in the intrinsic ring-theoretic sense of Global Fields I §5. Then sum_{N(p)>M} N(W_p;X)=O(X/(M log M))+o(X), for M>=2, using stabilizer-weighted generic orbit counts and the same number-field regions or function-field norm shells. The O constant is independent of M and the negligible term is uniform for the sieve limit. Extension to a fixed Gamma-stable commensurable lattice requires a finite-index/denominator comparison; it is recorded in G-global. For quadratic rings use the §9 model; there is no extra-ramification locus in that case. In characteristic two this is a maximality sieve, not an ordinary-discriminant squarefree sieve.

**Hypotheses.** Conventions and all parameter restrictions in the statement are part of the target.

**Dependencies.** [Global-field finite-condition orbit count](#st2-refinement-global-field-generic-finite-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-global-field-generic-finite-count`); [The quantitative Ekedahl geometric sieve (Bhargava, Theorem 3.3; Bhargava-Shankar, Theorem 2.17)](#st2-quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve`); [Strong and weak multiples of p^2: the sets W_p, W_p^(1), W_p^(2) of binary quartic and binary cubic forms](#st2-strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values`)

**Sources.** [S2/global](#source-s2-global), Theorems 5.2–5.3 and proof, pp.19–21; quadratic maximal sieve §9.3, p.27. Independent review REV-ArithmeticStatistics--ST.2: Read the full Theorems 5.2–5.3 proof and §9.3. Corrected the intrinsic nonmaximal/extra-ramification partition, standard-lattice scope and separate commensurable comparison; polynomial squarefreeness is not used in characteristic two.

**Intended theorem name.** `ArithmeticCountingRefinement.global_field_large_prime_tail`.

**Proof route.**

1. The extra-ramification locus W_p^(2) reduces into a fixed codimension-two scheme; apply the S-arithmetic geometric sieve outside finitely many exceptional primes.
2. The nonmaximal but not extra-ramified locus W_p^(1) admits local maximalization, a discriminant decrease by N(p)^2, and at most 10 orbit preimages. Use the finite ideal-class lattices and sum prime-ideal reciprocal squares. These intrinsic loci are not the polynomial strong/weak partition in characteristic two.
3. For n=2 use the change-of-generator argument of §9.3: nonmaximality yields a in p and b in p^2 after a local group move. Record the separate group and fixed-lattice comparison adapters in G-global.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Check the stated exponent and constant dependence; establish finiteness before using a natural cardinal.
- Do not replace a uniform estimate by separate fixed-prime asymptotics.

<a id="st2-refinement-global-field-large-local-count"></a>

### 2.60 Global-field infinitely many local conditions

In the Gamma-stable commensurable lattice setting above, write L_p for each local coefficient-lattice closure and normalize vol(L_p)=1. Let Z=L intersection intersection_{p outside S} Z_p, where the local compact Z_p are invariant under the local closure of Gamma, have null boundary, and contain every maximal minimally ramified ring for all sufficiently large p. With stabilizer-weighted generic orbits and the same function-field norm-shell convention, N(Z;X)=vol_L(F_G(X)v_sigma)/|Aut(sigma)| times product_{p outside S} vol(Z_p)+o(X). The factors are imposed independently; an arbitrary subset with these marginal closures is insufficient. The commensurable-lattice tail comparison and §9 quadratic model are explicit G-global obligations.

**Hypotheses.** Conventions and all parameter restrictions in the statement are part of the target.

**Dependencies.** [Global-field finite-condition orbit count](#st2-refinement-global-field-generic-finite-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-global-field-generic-finite-count`); [Global-field uniform tail estimate](#st2-refinement-global-field-large-prime-tail) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-global-field-large-prime-tail`); [Functions and sets defined by congruence conditions; acceptable functions](#st2-functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions`)

**Proof route.**

2. The difference from all local conditions is bounded by the uniform tail; take X to infinity before M. Deduce convergence and the stated normalization, with zero products allowed.

### 2.61 Cubic secondary term on a lattice

For a sublattice L of integral binary cubic forms of index T, containing m V_Z, write T=T1 T2 where the first coefficient projection has image T1 Z and T2 is the index in each remaining-coordinate fibre. If m^4<=X, then N_i(L;X/2,X)=c1_i X/(2T)+(1−2^(−5/6))c2_i X^(5/6)/(T1^(1/3) T2)+O(m X^(3/4)/T). Here c1=(pi^2/72,pi^2/24); c2 is the signed secondary coefficient of BST Theorem 6. The translated-lattice result has a separately computed c2(L+a), not this same coefficient.
