<a id="st3-splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms"></a>

### 3.3 The splitting symbol (f, p) of an integral binary cubic form and the local sets T_p(σ), V_p, Y_p, Z_p

Let V_Z be the space of integral binary cubic forms f(x, y) = a x³ + b x² y + c x y² + d y³ (coefficients (a, b, c, d) ∈ Z⁴, the carrier of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) and p a prime. If f ≢ 0 (mod p), f mod p has exactly three zeros in P¹(F̄_p) counted with multiplicity; the splitting symbol (f, p) = (f₁^{e₁} f₂^{e₂} …) lists the degrees f_i over F_p of the fields of definition of the distinct zeros and their multiplicities e_i, and takes one of the five values (111), (12), (3), (1²1), (1³). For each symbol σ, T_p(σ) := {f ∈ V_Z : f ≢ 0 (mod p), (f, p) = σ}. With U_p ⊆ V_Z the set of forms f such that the cubic ring R(f) is maximal at p (the Davenport-Heilbronn set of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1: f ∉ U_p iff f ≡ 0 (mod p), or some GL₂(Z)-translate of f has a ≡ 0 (mod p²) and b ≡ 0 (mod p)), put U_p(σ) := U_p ∩ T_p(σ), V_p := U_p \ T_p(1³) (maximal at p and not totally ramified at p), Y_p := U_p ∩ T_p(1³) (maximal and totally ramified at p), W_p := V_Z \ U_p and Z_p := V_Z \ V_p = W_p ⊔ Y_p. Over Z_p use the corresponding coefficient conditions in Z_p⁴. Only the splitting-symbol sets T_p descend to F_p⁴; U_p and the maximality-dependent sets require coefficients modulo p² and cannot be defined from a residue in F_p⁴ alone.

**Hypotheses.** p is prime; the symbol is undefined for f ≡ 0 (mod p), and such f lie in W_p; All the sets depend only on f mod p² (T_p(σ) only on f mod p), so they are finite unions of translates of p²V_Z and have well-defined p-adic densities; The symbol is invariant under the twisted GL₂(Z)-action (γf)(x, y) = det(γ)^{-1} f((x, y)γ) of ST.1, since GL₂ permutes the zeros in P¹ preserving degrees and multiplicities; Z_p is BST's set of forms 'whose discriminants are not fundamental'; W_p and Y_p are its two parts

**Dependencies.** [Delone-Faddeev: GL2(R)-classes of binary cubic forms parametrize cubic rings](#st1-delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings`); [Binary cubic forms, their discriminant and the twisted GL2-action](#st1-binary-cubic-forms-and-the-twisted-action) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/binary-cubic-forms-and-the-twisted-action`); [The Davenport-Heilbronn sets U_p of binary cubic forms](#st1-davenport-heilbronn-sets) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/davenport-heilbronn-sets`); [Davenport-Heilbronn: R(f) is maximal at p if and only if f is in U_p](#st1-davenport-heilbronn-maximality-criterion) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/davenport-heilbronn-maximality-criterion`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 4, p. 8. The splitting symbol and the five values, verbatim. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 4, p. 9 and Section 8.2, p. 23. The sets V_p and Z_p; W_p and Y_p are the two parts named in the proof of Proposition 29.

**API.**

- `cubicSplittingSymbol` (constructor): (f, p) as a multiset of pairs (degree, multiplicity), defined for f ≢ 0 (mod p).
- `splittingTypeSet` (constructor): T_p(σ) = {f ∈ V_Z : f ≢ 0 mod p, (f, p) = σ}.
- `maximalNotTotallyRamifiedSet` (constructor): V_p = U_p \ T_p(1³).
- `maximalTotallyRamifiedSet` (constructor): Y_p = U_p ∩ T_p(1³).
- `notFundamentalSet` (constructor): Z_p = V_Z \ V_p.
- `cubicSplittingSymbol_mem_five` (characterisation): For f ≢ 0 (mod p), (f, p) ∈ {(111), (12), (3), (1²1), (1³)}.
- `cubicSplittingSymbol_smul` (compatibility): (γf, p) = (f, p) for γ ∈ GL₂(Z) (twisted action of ST.1).
- `splittingTypeSet_mod` (other): Membership in T_p(σ) depends only on f mod p; membership in U_p, V_p, Y_p, Z_p only on f mod p².
- `notFundamentalSet_eq_union` (relation): Z_p = W_p ⊔ Y_p, a disjoint union.

**Checks.**

- `cubicSplittingSymbol_xy_xsuby` (computation): (x y (x − y), p) = (111) for every prime p.
- `cubicSplittingSymbol_triple` (computation): (y³ + 2x³, 2) = (1³), and y³ + 2x³ ∈ Y₂.
- `splittingTypeSet_zero` (degenerate): The zero form lies in no T_p(σ) and in W_p for every p.
- `notFundamentalSet_mem_pSq` (non-example): y³ + 4x³ has symbol (1³) at 2 but is not in Y₂ (it lies in W₂, since a ≡ 0 mod 4 and b ≡ 0 mod 2): the symbol alone does not decide maximality.
- `cubicSplittingSymbol_smul_example` (compatibility): For γ = [[0, 1], [1, 0]], γ(x²y) = −xy² and both have symbol (1²1).

**Proof route.**

1. Factor f mod p over F_p into irreducible binary forms (homogeneous factorisation in F_p[x, y]); the pairs (degree, multiplicity) of the distinct irreducible factors, as a multiset, is the symbol; the five values are the multisets with Σ f_i e_i = 3.
2. GL₂(F_p) acts on binary forms over F_p by linear substitution and scaling by det^{-1}, which maps irreducible factors to irreducible factors of the same degree with the same multiplicities; reduction mod p commutes with the action, so T_p(σ), U_p and hence V_p, Y_p, W_p, Z_p are GL₂(Z)-invariant.
3. U_p is imported from ST.1 (Davenport-Heilbronn's maximality criterion, BST Theorem 14); the remaining sets are Boolean combinations.

**Acceptance checks.**

- x y (x − y) has symbol (111) at every p, x (x² + y²) has symbol (12) at p = 3, and x²y has symbol (1²1) at every p.
- y³ + p x³ has symbol (1³), lies in U_p (a ≢ 0 mod p²) and hence in Y_p; y³ + p² x³ has symbol (1³) but lies in W_p.
- V_Z = W_p ⊔ V_p ⊔ Y_p as a disjoint union.

**Consumers.** Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman, Lemmas 17-19 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-splitting-types and the two following nodes) — the densities of T_p(σ), U_p(σ), U_p and V_p; Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman, Section 8.2, Proposition 29 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse) — the uniformity estimate for Z_p = W_p ⊔ Y_p; Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman, Section 8.5 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/davenport-heilbronn-mean-of-three-torsion) — V = ∩_p V_p parametrises nowhere totally ramified cubic fields

<a id="st3-splitting-symbol-determines-the-reduction-mod-p"></a>

### 3.4 The splitting symbol determines R(f)/(p), and for f ∈ U_p it is the splitting type of p in R(f)

For an integral binary cubic form f with f ≢ 0 (mod p) and cubic ring R(f) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings): (f, p) = (f₁^{e₁} f₂^{e₂} …) iff R(f)/pR(f) ≅ F_{p^{f₁}}[t₁]/(t₁^{e₁}) ⊕ F_{p^{f₂}}[t₂]/(t₂^{e₂}) ⊕ …. Consequently, if f ∈ U_p (R(f) maximal at p) and f is irreducible with R(f) ⊗ Q = K a cubic field, then (f, p) is the splitting type of p in K: (111) split, (12) one degree-1 and one degree-2 prime, (3) inert, (1²1) partially ramified, (1³) totally ramified.

**Hypotheses.** f ≢ 0 (mod p); The comparison with the splitting of p in K needs R(f) ⊗ Z_p maximal, i.e. f ∈ U_p

**Dependencies.** [Delone-Faddeev: GL2(R)-classes of binary cubic forms parametrize cubic rings](#st1-delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings`); [The splitting symbol (f, p) of an integral binary cubic form and the local sets T_p(σ), V_p, Y_p, Z_p](#st3-splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic#layer-1-the-splitting-dictionary

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 4, p. 8. The equivalence verbatim; the proof step checks the five orbit representatives. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 4, p. 8. The consequence for maximal rings.

**Proof route.**

1. R(f)/pR(f) = R(f mod p), the cubic F_p-algebra of the reduction (the Delone-Faddeev construction commutes with base change Z → F_p, BST Section 2, last paragraph).
2. Both sides depend only on the GL₂(F_p)-orbit of f mod p; check the five orbits on representatives: xy(x − y) gives F_p³, x·q(x, y) with q irreducible gives F_p ⊕ F_{p²}, an irreducible cubic gives F_{p³}, x²y gives F_p[t]/(t²) ⊕ F_p, x³ gives F_p[t]/(t³); these are pairwise non-isomorphic algebras.
3. If R(f) ⊗ Z_p is the maximal order of K ⊗ Q_p, then R(f)/pR(f) = O_K/pO_K ≅ ⊕_{𝔭 | p} O_K/𝔭^{e(𝔭)}, and O_K/𝔭^{e} ≅ F_{p^{f(𝔭)}}[t]/(t^e) (Dedekind–Kummer; NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 1 splitting dictionary), so the symbol records (f(𝔭), e(𝔭)).

**Acceptance checks.**

- x²y: R/pR ≅ F_p[t]/(t²) ⊕ F_p, symbol (1²1).
- For f = x³ − x y² − y³ (the form of the discriminant −23 field) and p = 23, (f, 23) = (1²1): 23 is partially ramified, consistent with 23 ∥ Disc.
- The comparison with the maximal order needs f∈U_p. For g=x³+x²y+xy²+2y³, Disc(g)=−83 is squarefree and g is irreducible, so R(g)=O_K. At p=2, g has symbol (12). Its index-2 subring corresponds to f=4x³+2x²y+xy²+y³, of discriminant −332 and symbol (1²1). Thus R(f)/2R(f)≅F₂[t]/(t²)×F₂ whereas O_K/2O_K≅F₂×F₄. The former example y³+4x³ was non-maximal, but both algebras there are abstractly F₂[t]/(t³), so it did not establish the claimed non-isomorphism.

<a id="st3-densities-of-splitting-types"></a>

### 3.5 Lemma 17: the p-adic densities of the sets T_p(σ)

Let μ_p be the p-adic density on V_Z (the Haar measure of the p-adic closure in V_{Z_p} = Z_p⁴, total mass 1; for a set defined modulo p it is (number of residue classes mod p)/p⁴). Then μ_p(T_p(111)) = (1/6)(p − 1)² p (p + 1)/p⁴, μ_p(T_p(12)) = (1/2)(p − 1)² p (p + 1)/p⁴, μ_p(T_p(3)) = (1/3)(p − 1)² p (p + 1)/p⁴, μ_p(T_p(1²1)) = (p − 1) p (p + 1)/p⁴ and μ_p(T_p(1³)) = (p − 1)(p + 1)/p⁴.

**Hypotheses.** p prime; μ_p is the normalised additive Haar measure on Z_p⁴ (the density used in BST Theorem 26, supplied with that theorem by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2)

**Dependencies.** [The splitting symbol (f, p) of an integral binary cubic form and the local sets T_p(σ), V_p, Y_p, Z_p](#st3-splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms`); `mathlib:Matrix.card_GL_field`; [Functions and sets defined by congruence conditions; acceptable functions](#st2-functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Lemma 17 and its proof, pp. 8-9. The counting method of the proof; the five formulas of the lemma are those stated in the node.

**Proof route.**

1. Membership in T_p(σ) depends only on f mod p, so μ_p(T_p(σ)) = #{f ∈ F_p⁴ : (f, p) = σ}/p⁴.
2. A nonzero binary cubic form over F_p is determined up to the p − 1 nonzero scalars by its zero divisor in P¹(F̄_p), a Frobenius-stable effective divisor of degree 3.
3. Count the divisors of each shape: unordered triples of distinct points of P¹(F_p): (p + 1)p(p − 1)/6; a point of P¹(F_p) plus a conjugate pair from P¹(F_{p²}) \ P¹(F_p): (p + 1)(p² − p)/2; a conjugate triple from P¹(F_{p³}) \ P¹(F_p): (p³ − p)/3; a double point and a different single point, both rational: (p + 1)p; a rational triple point: p + 1.
4. Multiply each count by p − 1 and divide by p⁴.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The five densities sum to (p⁴ − 1)/p⁴, the density of forms not ≡ 0 mod p: (p − 1)(p + 1)[(p − 1)p + p + 1] = (p² − 1)(p² + 1).
- At p = 2 the counts of forms are 1, 3, 2, 6, 3 (sum 15 = 2⁴ − 1).

<a id="st3-densities-of-splitting-types-of-maximal-forms"></a>

### 3.6 Lemma 18: the p-adic densities of the sets U_p(σ)

U_p(111) = T_p(111), U_p(12) = T_p(12), U_p(3) = T_p(3); and μ_p(U_p(1²1)) = (p − 1)²(p + 1)/p⁴, μ_p(U_p(1³)) = (p − 1)²(p + 1)/p⁵. Equivalently, a proportion (p − 1)/p of the forms in T_p(1²1) and in T_p(1³) lie in U_p.

**Hypotheses.** p prime; U_p is the Davenport-Heilbronn set of ST.1 (R(f) maximal at p iff f ∈ U_p)

**Dependencies.** [Lemma 17: the p-adic densities of the sets T_p(σ)](#st3-densities-of-splitting-types) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-splitting-types`); [The splitting symbol (f, p) of an integral binary cubic form and the local sets T_p(σ), V_p, Y_p, Z_p](#st3-splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms`); [The Davenport-Heilbronn sets U_p of binary cubic forms](#st1-davenport-heilbronn-sets) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/davenport-heilbronn-sets`); [Davenport-Heilbronn: R(f) is maximal at p if and only if f is in U_p](#st1-davenport-heilbronn-maximality-criterion) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/davenport-heilbronn-maximality-criterion`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Lemma 18 and the paragraph before it, p. 9. The proof of the two nontrivial densities, verbatim.

**Proof route.**

1. For σ ∈ {(111), (12), (3)} the discriminant is prime to p (f mod p is squarefree), so R(f) is maximal at p (an overring of index divisible by p would force p² | Disc); hence U_p(σ) = T_p(σ).
2. For σ ∈ {(1²1), (1³)} move the unique multiple zero of f mod p to (1 : 0) by an element of GL₂(Z); then a ≡ b ≡ 0 (mod p), and by the criterion of ST.1 the form fails to be maximal exactly when additionally a ≡ 0 (mod p²).
3. Among the forms of T_p(σ) put in this position, the condition a ≡ 0 (mod p²) cuts out a proportion 1/p (a mod p² is uniformly distributed among the p residues ≡ 0 mod p), and the normalisation is GL₂(Z)-equivariant, so μ_p(U_p(σ)) = ((p − 1)/p) μ_p(T_p(σ)); insert Lemma 17.

**Acceptance checks.**

- μ_p(U_p(1²1)) = ((p − 1)/p) · (p − 1)p(p + 1)/p⁴ = (p − 1)²(p + 1)/p⁴.
- μ_p(U_p(1³)) = ((p − 1)/p) · (p − 1)(p + 1)/p⁴.

<a id="st3-densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms"></a>

### 3.7 Lemma 19: μ_p(U_p) = (p³ − 1)(p² − 1)/p⁵ and μ_p(V_p) = (p² − 1)²/p⁴

μ_p(U_p) = (p³ − 1)(p² − 1)/p⁵ = (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−3}) and μ_p(V_p) = (p² − 1)²/p⁴ = (1 − p^{−2})².

**Hypotheses.** p prime

**Dependencies.** [Lemma 18: the p-adic densities of the sets U_p(σ)](#st3-densities-of-splitting-types-of-maximal-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-splitting-types-of-maximal-forms`); [The splitting symbol (f, p) of an integral binary cubic form and the local sets T_p(σ), V_p, Y_p, Z_p](#st3-splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Lemma 19, p. 9. The lemma verbatim with its one-line proof.

**Proof route.**

1. U_p is the disjoint union of the U_p(σ) over the five symbols (a form ≡ 0 mod p is not in U_p) and V_p is the union over σ ≠ (1³).
2. Sum the densities of Lemma 18: (p − 1)²(p + 1)[p² + p + 1]/p⁵ = (p² − 1)(p³ − 1)/p⁵, and without the (1³) term (p − 1)²(p + 1)(p² + p)/p⁵ = (p² − 1)²/p⁴.

**Acceptance checks.**

- ∏_p μ_p(U_p) = ∏_p (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−3}) = 1/(ζ(2)ζ(3)) and ∏_p μ_p(V_p) = 1/ζ(2)² = 36/π⁴ (Euler products).
- At p = 2: μ₂(U₂) = 21/32 and μ₂(V₂) = 9/16.

<a id="st3-maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields"></a>

### 3.8 Maximal cubic domains are the rings of integers of cubic fields; the orbits in ∩_p U_p count cubic fields

Let f be an irreducible integral binary cubic form, so that R(f) is an order in the cubic field K = R(f) ⊗ Q (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings). (a) R(f) is maximal (contained in no strictly larger cubic ring inside K) iff R(f) = O_K, iff R(f) is maximal at every prime p, iff f ∈ U := ∩_p U_p. (b) The map f ↦ R(f) ⊗ Q induces a bijection between GL₂(Z)-orbits of irreducible forms in U and Q-isomorphism classes of cubic fields, with Disc(f) = Disc(R(f)) = Disc(K); hence for every interval, N(U ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X) (the number of irreducible GL₂(Z)-orbits in U with 0 < (−1)^i Disc < X) equals N₃(⊤; 0, X) for i = 0 and N₃(⊤; −X, 0) for i = 1. (c) For f ∈ U, p is totally ramified in K iff f ∈ T_p(1³); hence the irreducible orbits in V := ∩_p V_p correspond to the cubic fields in which no prime is totally ramified.

**Hypotheses.** f irreducible over Q (equivalently R(f) is a domain, ST.1); V_Z^{(0)} and V_Z^{(1)} are the forms of positive and negative discriminant

**Dependencies.** [Delone-Faddeev: GL2(R)-classes of binary cubic forms parametrize cubic rings](#st1-delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings`); [Cubic rings, their discriminant, and maximality at a prime](#st1-cubic-ring) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/cubic-ring`); [Reducible forms correspond to cubic rings with zero divisors](#st1-reducible-forms-and-zero-divisors) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/reducible-forms-and-zero-divisors`); [Davenport-Heilbronn: R(f) is maximal at p if and only if f is in U_p](#st1-davenport-heilbronn-maximality-criterion) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/davenport-heilbronn-maximality-criterion`); [The splitting symbol (f, p) of an integral binary cubic form and the local sets T_p(σ), V_p, Y_p, Z_p](#st3-splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms`); [The splitting symbol determines R(f)/(p), and for f ∈ U_p it is the splitting type of p in R(f)](#st3-splitting-symbol-determines-the-reduction-mod-p) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/splitting-symbol-determines-the-reduction-mod-p`); [The counting function of number fields of fixed degree by discriminant, with signature, Galois-group and local restrictions](#st3-number-field-counting-function) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/number-field-counting-function`); `mathlib:NumberField.RingOfIntegers`; `mathlib:NumberField.discr`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 3, first paragraph, p. 6. Parts (a) and (b); the domain case is the ring of integers of the cubic field. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.3, p. 24. The identification of U used in the proof of Theorem 1.

**Proof route.**

1. Every element of an order R ⊆ K is integral over Z (R is a finitely generated Z-module), so R ⊆ O_K; O_K is itself a cubic ring (free of rank 3), so a maximal order equals O_K, and conversely O_K is contained in no larger order.
2. R ⊆ O_K has finite index, and R = O_K iff no prime p divides [O_K : R], iff R ⊗ Z_p = O_K ⊗ Z_p for all p, i.e. R is maximal at every p; by the Davenport-Heilbronn criterion of ST.1 this holds iff f ∈ U_p for all p.
3. By Delone-Faddeev (ST.1), GL₂(Z)-orbits of forms correspond to isomorphism classes of cubic rings with Disc(f) = Disc(R(f)); restricting to orbits with R(f) ≅ O_K for a cubic field K gives a bijection with isomorphism classes of cubic fields (K ≅ K' iff O_K ≅ O_{K'}), and Disc(O_K) = NumberField.discr K.
4. Part (c) is ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/splitting-symbol-determines-the-reduction-mod-p applied to f ∈ U_p.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The form x³ − x y² − y³ lies in U (its discriminant −23 is squarefree) and corresponds to the cubic field of discriminant −23.
- The form 4x³ + y³ lies in W₂ (a ≡ 0 mod 4, b ≡ 0 mod 2): R(f) = Z[∛4], of index 2 in O_{Q(∛2)} = Z[∛2], with Disc −432 = 2²·(−108); its orbit is not counted by N(U; X).
- The irreducible orbits in U with |Disc| < 50 are exactly four, of discriminants −23, −31, −44 and 49, matching the four cubic fields with |Disc| < 50.

<a id="st3-davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields"></a>

### 3.9 The Davenport-Heilbronn theorem: N₃(0, X) ~ X/(12ζ(3)) and N₃(−X, 0) ~ X/(4ζ(3))

Let N₃(ξ, η) = N₃(⊤; ξ, η) be the number of cubic fields K up to isomorphism with ξ < Disc(K) < η (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/number-field-counting-function, n = 3, no Galois-group restriction: cyclic cubic fields are included). Then N₃(0, X) = X/(12ζ(3)) + o(X) and N₃(−X, 0) = X/(4ζ(3)) + o(X) as X → ∞. More precisely, for i ∈ {0, 1} with n₀ = 6 = #Aut_R(R³) and n₁ = 2 = #Aut_R(R ⊕ C), lim_{X→∞} N(U ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X)/X = (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_p (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−3}) = 1/(2 n_i ζ(3)). The same method gives, for any finite set of primes and prescribed splitting types at them, the count multiplied by the product of the corresponding relative local densities (the finite-condition case of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/density-of-cubic-orders-with-local-specifications).

**Hypotheses.** The count is by isomorphism classes of fields, ordered by the signed discriminant; the total is N₃(X) ~ X/(3ζ(3)); Cyclic cubic fields are included but number O(X^{1/2}) (every ramified prime is totally ramified, so Disc = f² with f the conductor), so the same asymptotic holds for S₃-cubic fields; The error term is only o(X); power savings are in the second-order node ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/roberts-second-order-term-for-cubic-fields

**Dependencies.** [Maximal cubic domains are the rings of integers of cubic fields; the orbits in ∩_p U_p count cubic fields](#st3-maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields`); [Lemma 19: μ_p(U_p) = (p³ − 1)(p² − 1)/p⁵ and μ_p(V_p) = (p² − 1)²/p⁴](#st3-densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms`); [The counting function of number fields of fixed degree by discriminant, with signature, Galois-group and local restrictions](#st3-number-field-counting-function) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/number-field-counting-function`); [Theorem 26 with (29)-(31): binary cubic forms in lattice translates, uniformly in the modulus](#st2-binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions`); [Proposition 29 (non-maximal part), for forms: the classes in W_p^DH have O(X/p^2) elements of discriminant < X, uniformly in p](#st2-uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms`); [Real binary cubic forms: the two open GL_2(ℝ)-orbits and their stabilisers (n_0 = 6, n_1 = 2)](#st2-real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms`); `mathlib:riemannZeta_two`; `mathlib:riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Theorem 1, p. 1. The theorem verbatim. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.3, proof of Theorem 1, p. 24. The upper-bound half of the sieve; the lower bound uses Proposition 29 as in the proof steps. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.3, last paragraph, p. 24. The finitely-many-local-conditions variant stated in the node.

**Proof route.**

1. By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields, N₃(0, X) = N(U ∩ V_Z^{(0)}; X) and N₃(−X, 0) = N(U ∩ V_Z^{(1)}; X), where N(S; X) counts irreducible GL₂(Z)-orbits in S with |Disc| < X and U = ∩_p U_p.
2. Upper bound: for every Y, ∩_{p<Y} U_p is defined by congruence conditions modulo ∏_{p<Y} p², so the congruence-condition count of binary cubic forms (BST Theorem 26, supplied by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2) gives lim_{X} N(∩_{p<Y} U_p ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X)/X = (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_{p<Y} μ_p(U_p); since U ⊆ ∩_{p<Y} U_p, limsup_X N(U ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X)/X ≤ (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_{p<Y} (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−3}) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms); let Y → ∞.
3. Lower bound: ∩_{p<Y} U_p ⊆ U ∪ ∪_{p≥Y} W_p with W_p = V_Z \ U_p, so N(U ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X) ≥ N(∩_{p<Y} U_p ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X) − Σ_{p≥Y} N(W_p; X); the uniformity estimate N(W_p; X) = O(X/p²) with a constant independent of p (BST Proposition 29, nonmaximal part, supplied by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2) bounds the tail by O(X Σ_{p≥Y} p^{−2}) = O(X/Y). Hence liminf ≥ (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_{p<Y} (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−3}) − O(1/Y); let Y → ∞.
4. Evaluate the constant: ∏_p (1 − p^{−2}) = 1/ζ(2) = 6/π² and ∏_p (1 − p^{−3}) = 1/ζ(3) (Euler product, riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod; ζ(2) = π²/6, riemannZeta_two), so (π²/(12 n_i)) · (6/π²)/ζ(3) = 1/(2 n_i ζ(3)); with n₀ = 6, n₁ = 2 this is 1/(12ζ(3)) and 1/(4ζ(3)). The values n₀, n₁ are the orders of the GL₂(R)-stabilizers of forms of positive and negative discriminant (Aut_R(R³) = S₃ and Aut_R(R ⊕ C) = Z/2), supplied with the count of ST.2.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Total: N₃(X) = N₃(0, X) + N₃(−X, 0) ~ (1/(12ζ(3)) + 1/(4ζ(3))) X = X/(3ζ(3)) ≈ 0.2773 X.
- Ratio: asymptotically three times as many complex cubic fields as totally real ones (n₀/n₁ = 3).
- The count is by fields, not orders: the order count of BST Theorem 6 has the larger constants π²/72 and π²/24; the ratio (π²/(12 n_i))/(1/(2n_i ζ(3))) = ζ(2)ζ(3) = ∏_p μ_p(U_p)^{−1}.

<a id="st3-nowhere-totally-ramified-cubic-fields-and-unramified-cubic-extensions-of-the-resolvent"></a>

### 3.10 A cubic field is nowhere totally ramified iff its Galois closure is unramified over the quadratic resolvent field; then Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂)

Let K₃ be a cubic field. (a) If K₃ is nowhere totally ramified (no prime p has p O_{K₃} = 𝔭³), then K₃ is not Galois (an S₃-cubic field). (b) For an S₃-cubic field K₃ with Galois closure K₆ and quadratic resolvent K₂ ⊆ K₆ (the fixed field of A₃ = Gal(K₆/K₂); K₂ = Q(√Disc(K₃))), the extension K₆/K₂ is unramified at all finite primes iff K₃ is nowhere totally ramified, and in that case Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂). (c) Conversely, if K₂ is a quadratic field and L/K₂ is an unramified cyclic cubic extension that is Galois over Q with Gal(L/Q) ≅ S₃, then each of the three conjugate cubic subfields of L is nowhere totally ramified and has discriminant Disc(K₂). (The archimedean places impose no condition: a Galois extension of odd degree is unramified at infinity.)

**Hypotheses.** 'Unramified' is at finite primes; K₆/K₂ is Galois of odd degree, so its real-place inertia groups, of order at most two, are trivial. Odd degree alone would not suffice for an arbitrary non-Galois extension.; K₂ is Q(√Disc(K₃)): √Disc(K₃) generates the fixed field of A₃ in K₆; Disc(K₃) ∈ Disc(K₂)·(Q^×)² always; equality needs the nowhere-totally-ramified hypothesis

**Dependencies.** [Maximal cubic domains are the rings of integers of cubic fields; the orbits in ∩_p U_p count cubic fields](#st3-maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields`); `mathlib:NumberField.discr`; `mathlib:NumberField.abs_discr_gt_two`; `mathlib:Ideal.inertia`; `mathlib:Ideal.ramificationIdx`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic#layer-6-global-ramification-consequences; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-3-ramification-the-tame-and-wild-cases-and-the-filtration

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.1, p. 23. Parts (b) and (c); the source says 'one checks', and the proof steps supply the inertia-group argument. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.5, p. 26. The discriminant equality of (b).

**Proof route.**

1. (a) A cyclic cubic field has Disc = f² with f its conductor and every ramified prime totally ramified (inertia groups are subgroups of Z/3Z); a field with no ramified prime would be an unramified extension of Q, which does not exist (Minkowski, |Disc| > 1: NumberField.abs_discr_gt_two); so a nowhere totally ramified cubic field is S₃.
2. (b) For a prime 𝔓 of K₆ over p with inertia group I ≤ S₃ acting on the three embeddings of K₃: the ramification indices of the primes of K₃ above p are the orbit lengths of I on {1, 2, 3} (Galois correspondence for inertia groups; NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 6 and LocalFieldsRamification Layer 3). p is totally ramified in K₃ iff I acts transitively iff 3 divides #I iff I ∩ A₃ ≠ 1 iff 𝔓 ∩ K₂ ramifies in K₆/K₂ (the inertia group of K₆/K₂ at 𝔓 is I ∩ A₃).
3. Discriminant equality: at a prime p not totally ramified in K₃, K₃ ⊗ Q_p is either unramified (both discriminants prime to p; in the case (12) p is inert in K₂ but unramified) or Q_p × F with F/Q_p a ramified quadratic extension, and then K₂ ⊗ Q_p ≅ F (the discriminant algebra of Q_p × F is F), so v_p(Disc K₃) = v_p(disc F) = v_p(Disc K₂); the signs agree because Disc(K₃)/Disc(K₂) is a square. Hence Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂).
4. (c) The three cubic subfields of L are the fixed fields of the three transpositions; they are conjugate, and by (b) applied to L = K₆ they are nowhere totally ramified with discriminant Disc(K₂).

**Acceptance checks.**

- For K₃ the field of x³ − x − 1 (Disc −23): K₂ = Q(√−23), and K₆ is the Hilbert class field of Q(√−23) (class number 3); 23 is partially ramified in K₃.
- The cyclic cubic field of discriminant 49 is totally ramified at 7 and is excluded, consistent with (a).
- Q(∛2) (Disc −108 = −2²·3³) is totally ramified at 2 and 3, K₂ = Q(√−3) with Disc −3 ≠ −108.

<a id="st3-three-torsion-of-quadratic-class-groups-counts-cubic-fields"></a>

### 3.11 Hasse's correspondence: the nowhere totally ramified cubic fields with resolvent K₂ number (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2

For every quadratic field K₂, the number of isomorphism classes of cubic fields K₃ that are nowhere totally ramified and whose quadratic resolvent is K₂ (equivalently, by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/nowhere-totally-ramified-cubic-fields-and-unramified-cubic-extensions-of-the-resolvent, with Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂)) equals (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2, where h₃(K₂) = #Cl(K₂)[3]. Consequently, for i ∈ {0, 1}, Σ_{0<(−1)^i Disc(K₂)<X} (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2 = N(V ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X), the number of irreducible GL₂(Z)-orbits in V = ∩_p V_p with 0 < (−1)^i Disc < X.

**Hypotheses.** The count is of fields up to isomorphism; each such field has three conjugate embeddings, all with the same resolvent; h₃ is the wide class group's 3-torsion (Mathlib ClassGroup); for p = 3 wide and narrow class groups have the same 3-part; The sign condition matches: Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂), so real quadratic resolvents correspond to totally real cubic fields (positive discriminant)

**Dependencies.** [A cubic field is nowhere totally ramified iff its Galois closure is unramified over the quadratic resolvent field; then Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂)](#st3-nowhere-totally-ramified-cubic-fields-and-unramified-cubic-extensions-of-the-resolvent) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/nowhere-totally-ramified-cubic-fields-and-unramified-cubic-extensions-of-the-resolvent`); [Maximal cubic domains are the rings of integers of cubic fields; the orbits in ∩_p U_p count cubic fields](#st3-maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields`); [The number h_m(K) of m-torsion elements of the class group of a number field](#st3-torsion-count-of-class-groups) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/torsion-count-of-class-groups`); `mathlib:ClassGroup`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-13-norm-theorems-and-class-fields

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.5, (59), p. 26. The count and the summed identity (59); the source cites class field theory without further proof. [P/wood-asymptotics-2016](#source-p-wood-asymptotics-2016), Section 3, p. 7. The class-field-theoretic steps (stated for imaginary K there; the argument is the same for real K).

**Proof route.**

1. Class field theory (ClassFieldTheory Layer 13, gal_hilbertClassField_equiv_classGroup): unramified abelian extensions of K₂ inside a fixed algebraic closure correspond to subgroups of Cl(K₂), and unramified cyclic cubic extensions L/K₂ to subgroups of index 3; a finite abelian group A has (#A[3] − 1)/2 subgroups of index 3 (they correspond to the lines of the F₃-vector space Hom(A, Z/3Z), which has #A[3] elements).
2. Each such L is Galois over Q (its norm subgroup is stable under Gal(K₂/Q), whose generator σ acts on Cl(K₂) by c ↦ c^{−1}, because c·σ(c) is the class of the ideal norm to Q, which is principal), and Gal(L/Q) ≅ Z/3Z ⋊ Z/2Z with σ acting by inversion, i.e. S₃.
3. By the resolvent lemma, the three cubic subfields of such an L form one isomorphism class of nowhere totally ramified cubic fields with resolvent K₂, and conversely the Galois closure of such a K₃ is such an L; distinct L give non-isomorphic cubic fields (L is the Galois closure). Hence the count is (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2.
4. Summing over K₂ with 0 < (−1)^i Disc(K₂) < X and using ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields (c) (irreducible orbits in V ↔ nowhere totally ramified cubic fields, Disc preserved) gives the displayed identity (BST (59)).

**Acceptance checks.**

- K₂ = Q(√−23): h₃ = 3, so exactly one nowhere totally ramified cubic field has discriminant −23 (the field of x³ − x − 1).
- K₂ = Q(√−3), Q(i): h₃ = 1, so no cubic field has discriminant −3 or −4.
- K₂ = Q(√229) (class number 3): exactly one cubic field of discriminant 229, the totally real field of x³ − 4x + 1.

<a id="st3-cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse"></a>

### 3.12 Uniformity for totally ramified primes: the cubic fields with |Disc| < X totally ramified at p number O(X/p²), uniformly in p

There is an absolute constant C such that for every prime p and every X ≥ 1, the number of cubic fields K (up to isomorphism) with |Disc(K)| < X in which p is totally ramified is at most C X/p². Equivalently N(Y_p ∩ U; X) ≤ C X/p², where U = ∩_q U_q. This is the part of BST Proposition 29 (N(Z_p; X) = O(X/p²)) concerning totally ramified primes, restricted to maximal forms, which is all the sieve for the mean of 3-torsion uses: ∩_{p<Y} V_p ⊆ V ∪ ∪_{q≥Y} W_q ∪ ∪_{p≥Y} (Y_p ∩ U).

**Hypotheses.** The constant is uniform in p; this is what licenses the sieve over infinitely many primes in the proof of the mean of 3-torsion; Only the maximal (field) part of Y_p is bounded here; a form in Y_p that is not maximal at another prime q lies in W_q and is covered by the nonmaximal estimate of ST.2

**Dependencies.** [A cubic field is nowhere totally ramified iff its Galois closure is unramified over the quadratic resolvent field; then Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂)](#st3-nowhere-totally-ramified-cubic-fields-and-unramified-cubic-extensions-of-the-resolvent) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/nowhere-totally-ramified-cubic-fields-and-unramified-cubic-extensions-of-the-resolvent`); [Hasse's correspondence: the nowhere totally ramified cubic fields with resolvent K₂ number (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2](#st3-three-torsion-of-quadratic-class-groups-counts-cubic-fields) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/three-torsion-of-quadratic-class-groups-counts-cubic-fields`); [The number h_m(K) of m-torsion elements of the class group of a number field](#st3-torsion-count-of-class-groups) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/torsion-count-of-class-groups`); [The splitting symbol (f, p) of an integral binary cubic form and the local sets T_p(σ), V_p, Y_p, Z_p](#st3-splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms`); [Maximal cubic domains are the rings of integers of cubic fields; the orbits in ∩_p U_p count cubic fields](#st3-maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields`); [Theorem 20 (Davenport): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms of bounded discriminant](#st2-davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-13-norm-theorems-and-class-fields; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields#layer-11-orders-and-picard-groups

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.2, Proposition 29 and the last sentence of its proof, pp. 23-24. The statement for Y_p; the source gives no proof and cites Datskovsky-Wright [13], which is not public. The proof steps reconstruct the standard ring-class-field argument for the maximal part, which is recorded as a gap.

**Proof route.**

1. Cyclic cubic fields have Disc=f², and total ramification at p forces p|f. There are at most C·2^{ω(f)} fields of conductor f, with an absolute constant (including the exceptional conductor factor at 3). Bound each indicator f²<X by X/f². The count is at most C X Σ_{p|f}2^{ω(f)}/f² ≤ 2C X/p² · Σ_{g≥1}2^{ω(g)}/g² = O(X/p²), since the last Euler product converges. This directly gives uniformity; the former bound O(X^{1/2+ε}/p) does not imply O(X/p²) uniformly up to p=√X.
2. S₃-cubic fields: for K with quadratic resolvent K₂ of discriminant D₂, the Galois closure K₆ is a cyclic cubic extension of K₂ on whose group Gal(K₂/Q) acts by inversion, hence K₆ lies in the ring class field of an order O_f of K₂ (ClassFieldTheory Layer 13, ringClassField and gal_ringClassField_equiv_pic), and Disc(K) = D₂ f² with f the conductor; by the inertia argument of the resolvent lemma a prime p ≥ 5 is totally ramified in K iff p | f.
3. For fixed K₂ and f, the cubic fields with resolvent K₂ and conductor f correspond to some of the index-3 subgroups of Pic(O_f) (quadratic orders and their Picard groups: GlobalNumberFields Layer 11), so there are at most #Pic(O_f)[3]; from the exact sequence 1 → (O_{K₂}/fO_{K₂})^×/((Z/fZ)^×·image(O_{K₂}^×)) → Pic(O_f) → Cl(K₂) → 1, whose kernel has 3-rank at most ω(f) + 2, #Pic(O_f)[3] ≤ 3^{ω(f)+2} h₃(K₂).
4. Σ_{0<|D₂|<Y} h₃(K₂) = O(Y): by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/three-torsion-of-quadratic-class-groups-counts-cubic-fields, Σ (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2 counts nowhere totally ramified cubic fields with |Disc| < Y, which is at most the number M₃(Y) = O(Y) of orders in cubic fields (BST Theorem 6, from ST.2), and the number of K₂ is O(Y).
5. Summing over f divisible by p and K₂ with |D₂| < X/f²: the count is O(X Σ_{p|f} 3^{ω(f)} f^{−2}) ≤ O(3X p^{−2} Σ_{g≥1} 3^{ω(g)} g^{−2}) = O(X/p²), the series converging. The primes p = 2, 3 are covered by the trivial bound N₃(X) = O(X) with a fixed constant.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Summed over p ≥ Y the bound is O(X/Y), the tail estimate used in the sieve for V = ∩_p V_p.
- For p = 5 the fields counted include Q(∛5) (Disc −675 = −3³·5², O = Z[∛5]) in which 5 is totally ramified.
- The bound is sharp in order: by the congruence count of ST.2 and Lemma 18, a proportion μ_p(U_p(1³))/μ_p(U_p) ≍ p^{−2} of cubic fields is totally ramified at p.

<a id="st3-squarefree-integers-in-residue-classes-modulo-four"></a>

### 3.13 Squarefree integers in each nonzero residue class modulo 4 have density 2/π²

For a ∈ {1, 2, 3} and x ≥ 1, #{1 ≤ n ≤ x : n squarefree, n ≡ a (mod 4)} = (2/π²) x + O(√x), with an absolute implied constant.

**Hypotheses.** The residue class a = 0 contains no squarefree integers; The error O(√x) is not optimised

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:Nat.sq_mul_squarefree_of_pos`; `mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius`; `mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.coe_zeta_mul_coe_moebius`; `mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.LSeries_zeta_mul_Lseries_moebius`; `mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.LSeries_zeta_eq_riemannZeta`; `mathlib:riemannZeta_two`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.5, (60), p. 26. The source quotes (60) as known; this lemma is the elementary input from which the next node derives it. [P/wood-asymptotics-2016](#source-p-wood-asymptotics-2016), Section 8, p. 13. The total density 6/π² of quadratic fields (both signs), the sum of the three residue-class densities used here.

**Proof route.**

1. Squarefree detection: for n ≥ 1, write n = b² m with m squarefree (Nat.sq_mul_squarefree_of_pos); then d² | n iff d | b, so Σ_{d² | n} μ(d) = Σ_{d | b} μ(d) = [b = 1] = [n squarefree] (ArithmeticFunction.coe_zeta_mul_coe_moebius).
2. For odd a: an n ≡ a (mod 4) is odd, so only odd d contribute, and #{n ≤ x : n ≡ a (4), d² | n} = x/(4d²) + O(1) for odd d (CRT, d² and 4 coprime). Summing over odd d ≤ √x: (x/4) Σ_{d odd} μ(d)/d² + O(√x) + O(x Σ_{d>√x} d^{−2}) = (x/4) ∏_{p>2} (1 − p^{−2}) + O(√x).
3. ∏_{p>2} (1 − p^{−2}) = (1/ζ(2))/(1 − 1/4) = (6/π²)(4/3) = 8/π² (ArithmeticFunction.LSeries_zeta_mul_Lseries_moebius and ArithmeticFunction.LSeries_zeta_eq_riemannZeta at s = 2, riemannZeta_two, and the Euler factor at 2), so the count is (2/π²) x + O(√x).
4. For a = 2: n = 2m with m ≤ x/2 odd squarefree; the odd squarefree m ≤ y number (4/π²) y + O(√y) (sum of the two odd classes), giving (2/π²) x + O(√x).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Sum over a = 1, 2, 3: (6/π²) x + O(√x), the classical density of squarefree integers.
- Numerical check: there are 608 squarefree n ≤ 1000 (200, 204 and 204 in the classes 1, 2 and 3 mod 4), and 6000/π² ≈ 607.9, 2000/π² ≈ 202.6.

<a id="st3-count-of-quadratic-fields"></a>

### 3.14 The number of quadratic fields with 0 < ±Disc < X is 3X/π² + O(√X)

N₂(⊤; 0, X) = (3/π²) X + O(√X) and N₂(⊤; −X, 0) = (3/π²) X + O(√X). Equivalently, the number of fundamental discriminants D ≠ 1 (Int.IsFundamentalDiscr) with 0 < D < X, respectively −X < D < 0, is (3/π²) X + O(√X).

**Hypotheses.** Quadratic fields are counted up to isomorphism (each has one subfield of Q̄ and #Aut = 2); the weighted count of BSW is half of this; D = 1 (the discriminant of Q) is excluded

**Dependencies.** [Squarefree integers in each nonzero residue class modulo 4 have density 2/π²](#st3-squarefree-integers-in-residue-classes-modulo-four) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/squarefree-integers-in-residue-classes-modulo-four`); [The counting function of number fields of fixed degree by discriminant, with signature, Galois-group and local restrictions](#st3-number-field-counting-function) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/number-field-counting-function`); `mathlib:Int.IsFundamentalDiscr`; `mathlib:Int.isFundamentalDiscr_iff_squarefree`; `tauceti:NumberField.discr_eq_of_squarefree_of_mod_four_eq_one`; `tauceti:NumberField.discr_eq_four_mul_of_mod_four_ne_one`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic#layer-0-the-multiquadratic-field

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.5, (60), p. 26. The statement (60), which the source quotes as known. [P/wood-asymptotics-2016](#source-p-wood-asymptotics-2016), Section 8, p. 13. The two-sign total, obtained there by a Tauberian argument; the elementary squarefree count is used here instead.

**Proof route.**

1. Quadratic fields up to isomorphism correspond bijectively to fundamental discriminants D ≠ 1 via K ↦ Disc(K): every quadratic field is Q(√d) with d ≠ 1 squarefree, Disc(Q(√d)) = d if d ≡ 1 (mod 4) and 4d otherwise (Tau Ceti NumberField.discr_eq_of_squarefree_of_mod_four_eq_one and NumberField.discr_eq_four_mul_of_mod_four_ne_one), these values are exactly the fundamental discriminants ≠ 1 (Int.isFundamentalDiscr_iff_squarefree), and Q(√d) ≅ Q(√d') iff d = d' for squarefree d, d'.
2. Count positive fundamental discriminants: D = n ≡ 1 (mod 4) squarefree, n < X (n ≠ 1): (2/π²) X + O(√X); D = 4m with m ≡ 2, 3 (mod 4) squarefree, m < X/4: (4/π²)(X/4) + O(√X). Total (3/π²) X + O(√X) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/squarefree-integers-in-residue-classes-modulo-four).
3. Negative: D = −n with n ≡ 3 (mod 4) squarefree, n < X: (2/π²) X; D = −4m with m ≡ 1, 2 (mod 4) squarefree (so −m ≡ 3, 2), m < X/4: (4/π²)(X/4). Total (3/π²) X + O(√X).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Small values: the negative fundamental discriminants in (−25, 0) are −3, −4, −7, −8, −11, −15, −19, −20, −23, −24, i.e. N₂(⊤; −25, 0) = 10, against 3·25/π² ≈ 7.6.
- Both signs together: (6/π²) X, agreeing with Wood's Tauberian count N_{S₂}(X) ~ (6/π²) X.
- This is the denominator of the Davenport-Heilbronn mean of 3-torsion; it is 3/π², not 6/π², per sign (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E402).

<a id="st3-davenport-heilbronn-mean-of-three-torsion"></a>

### 3.15 The Davenport-Heilbronn theorem on 3-torsion: the mean of #Cl(K)[3] is 4/3 over real and 2 over imaginary quadratic fields

Σ_{0<Disc(K)<X} h₃(K) = (4/3) Σ_{0<Disc(K)<X} 1 + o(X) and Σ_{−X<Disc(K)<0} h₃(K) = 2 Σ_{−X<Disc(K)<0} 1 + o(X), the sums over quadratic fields K up to isomorphism ordered by discriminant, h₃(K) = #Cl(K)[3]. Equivalently lim_{X→∞} (Σ_{0<±Disc(K)<X} h₃(K)) / N₂(⊤; 0 < ±Disc < X) = 4/3 (real) and 2 (imaginary).

**Hypotheses.** Quadratic fields are ordered by |Disc| and weighted equally; the averages are over all quadratic fields of the given sign; The proof sieves to V = ∩_p V_p, defined by infinitely many congruence conditions, and needs the uniform tail bound for Z_p = W_p ⊔ Y_p; No Cohen-Lenstra hypothesis is used; the theorem is the case p = 3, α = 1 of the moment prediction ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/cohen-lenstra-moment-prediction, which it confirms

**Dependencies.** [Hasse's correspondence: the nowhere totally ramified cubic fields with resolvent K₂ number (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2](#st3-three-torsion-of-quadratic-class-groups-counts-cubic-fields) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/three-torsion-of-quadratic-class-groups-counts-cubic-fields`); [The Davenport-Heilbronn theorem: N₃(0, X) ~ X/(12ζ(3)) and N₃(−X, 0) ~ X/(4ζ(3))](#st3-davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields`); [Lemma 19: μ_p(U_p) = (p³ − 1)(p² − 1)/p⁵ and μ_p(V_p) = (p² − 1)²/p⁴](#st3-densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms`); [Uniformity for totally ramified primes: the cubic fields with |Disc| < X totally ramified at p number O(X/p²), uniformly in p](#st3-cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse`); [The number of quadratic fields with 0 < ±Disc < X is 3X/π² + O(√X)](#st3-count-of-quadratic-fields) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/count-of-quadratic-fields`); [The number h_m(K) of m-torsion elements of the class group of a number field](#st3-torsion-count-of-class-groups) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/torsion-count-of-class-groups`); [Theorem 26 with (29)-(31): binary cubic forms in lattice translates, uniformly in the modulus](#st2-binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions`); [Proposition 29 (non-maximal part), for forms: the classes in W_p^DH have O(X/p^2) elements of discriminant < X, uniformly in p](#st2-uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms`); `mathlib:riemannZeta_two`; `mathlib:riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Theorem 2, p. 1. The theorem verbatim. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 8.5, proof of Theorem 2, p. 26. The sieve step; the final evaluation 1 + 2·(3/(n_iπ²))/(3/π²) is on the same page.

**Proof route.**

1. By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/three-torsion-of-quadratic-class-groups-counts-cubic-fields, Σ_{0<(−1)^i Disc(K)<X} (h₃(K) − 1)/2 = N(V ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X).
2. The sieve of the proof of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields with V_p in place of U_p: the upper bound from the congruence count over ∩_{p<Y} V_p (ST.2) and μ_p(V_p) = (1 − p^{−2})² (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms); the lower bound from ∩_{p<Y} V_p ⊆ V ∪ ∪_{p≥Y} (W_p ∪ Y_p), the nonmaximal bound N(W_p; X) = O(X/p²) (ST.2) and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse. Hence lim N(V ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X)/X = (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_p (1 − p^{−2})² = (π²/(12 n_i))(36/π⁴) = 3/(n_i π²).
3. By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/count-of-quadratic-fields, Σ_{0<±Disc<X} 1 ~ 3X/π².
4. Therefore the mean of h₃ is 1 + 2 · (3/(n_i π²))/(3/π²) = 1 + 2/n_i: 1 + 2/6 = 4/3 for i = 0 (positive discriminant, real quadratic) and 1 + 2/2 = 2 for i = 1 (imaginary).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Imaginary: mean h₃ = 2, i.e. the mean number of surjections Cl(K) → Z/3Z (which is h₃ − 1) is 1; real: mean 4/3, i.e. 1/3 surjections on average — the Cohen-Lenstra predictions |A|^0 and |A|^{−1} for A = Z/3Z.
- Small-range sanity check (not a test of the limit): among the 10 imaginary quadratic fields with |Disc| < 25 only Q(√−23) has h₃ = 3, giving an average 6/5.
- The sieve cannot be run with a pointwise density at each prime alone: without the uniform bound for Y_p (totally ramified primes, via class field theory) only the upper bound follows.

<a id="st3-acceptable-local-specifications-for-cubic-orders"></a>

### 3.16 Local specifications Σ = (Σ_p) ∪ Σ_∞ for cubic orders, acceptable and strongly acceptable collections, and local masses

A local specification for cubic orders is a collection Σ = (Σ_p)_p ∪ Σ_∞ where, for each prime p, Σ_p is a set of isomorphism classes of nondegenerate cubic rings over Z_p (orders in étale cubic Q_p-algebras; by Delone-Faddeev over Z_p, equivalently a GL₂(Z_p)-invariant set of binary cubic forms over Z_p of nonzero discriminant), and Σ_∞ ⊆ {R³, R ⊕ C}. An order R in a cubic field is a Σ-order if R ⊗ Z_p ∈ Σ_p for all p and R ⊗ R ∈ Σ_∞. Σ is acceptable if for all sufficiently large p, Σ_p contains every maximal cubic Z_p-order that is not totally ramified; it is strongly acceptable if for all sufficiently large p, Σ_p is one of: all nondegenerate cubic Z_p-orders, all maximal ones, or all maximal ones not totally ramified. The local mass of Σ_p is m_p(Σ_p) := Σ_{R ∈ Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) · #Aut(R)), where Disc_p(R) = p^{v_p(Disc R)}; the archimedean mass is m_∞(Σ_∞) := Σ_{R ∈ Σ_∞} 1/#Aut(R) with #Aut(R³) = 6 and #Aut(R ⊕ C) = 2.

**Hypotheses.** Isomorphism classes over Z_p, not over Q_p: several orders can lie in the same étale algebra; Nondegenerate means nonzero discriminant; degenerate rings never occur as R ⊗ Z_p for an order R in a cubic field; The infinite sum m_p over all nondegenerate orders converges (BST (57))

**Dependencies.** [Delone-Faddeev: GL2(R)-classes of binary cubic forms parametrize cubic rings](#st1-delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings`); [The splitting symbol (f, p) of an integral binary cubic form and the local sets T_p(σ), V_p, Y_p, Z_p](#st3-splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/splitting-symbol-and-local-sets-of-binary-cubic-forms`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Section 1, before Theorem 7, p. 3. The two definitions, verbatim. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Remark 4, (57)-(58), p. 25. The local mass identities used as tests.

**API.**

- `CubicLocalSpecification` (structure): A family Σ_p (p prime) of GL₂(Z_p)-invariant sets of binary cubic forms over Z_p of nonzero discriminant, and a subset Σ_∞ of {R³, R ⊕ C}.
- `CubicLocalSpecification.IsAcceptable` (other): For all sufficiently large p, the forms of V_p ⊗ Z_p (maximal, not totally ramified) lie in Σ_p.
- `CubicLocalSpecification.IsStronglyAcceptable` (other): For all sufficiently large p, Σ_p is all nondegenerate forms, the maximal ones, or the maximal not totally ramified ones.
- `CubicLocalSpecification.IsStronglyAcceptable.isAcceptable` (relation): Strongly acceptable implies acceptable.
- `CubicLocalSpecification.maximal` (constructor): The specification of maximal orders (all real types at ∞).
- `CubicLocalSpecification.nowhereTotallyRamified` (constructor): The specification of maximal orders not totally ramified at any p.
- `CubicLocalSpecification.localMass` (data): m_p(Σ_p) = Σ_{R ∈ Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) #Aut(R)), as an element of [0, ∞].
- `CubicLocalSpecification.archimedeanMass` (data): m_∞(Σ_∞) = Σ_{R ∈ Σ_∞} 1/#Aut(R) ∈ {0, 1/6, 1/2, 2/3}.

**Checks.**

- `CubicLocalSpecification.maximal_isStronglyAcceptable` (characterisation): The maximal specification is strongly acceptable, hence acceptable.
- `CubicLocalSpecification.localMass_maximal` (computation): m_p(all maximal cubic Z_p-orders) = 1 + 1/p + 1/p².
- `CubicLocalSpecification.archimedeanMass_both` (computation): m_∞({R³, R ⊕ C}) = 1/6 + 1/2 = 2/3.
- `CubicLocalSpecification.archimedeanMass_empty` (degenerate): m_∞(∅) = 0, and then there are no Σ-orders.
- `CubicLocalSpecification.not_isAcceptable_totallyRamified` (non-example): The specification with Σ_p = {maximal totally ramified orders} for every p is not acceptable.
- `CubicLocalSpecification.localMaximal_contains_padic_orbit` (compatibility): For every prime p and γ∈GL₂(Z_p), γ·xy(x−y) lies in localMaximal p. This includes nonintegral p-adic coefficients and detects replacing the full p-adic set by the image of integral forms.

**Proof route.**

1. Represent Σ_p as a GL₂(Z_p)-invariant subset of V_{Z_p} of forms of nonzero discriminant (Delone-Faddeev over Z_p, ST.1) and Σ_∞ as a subset of the two real orbits; the predicates are statements about all but finitely many p.
2. The three standard specifications: 'all orders' (Σ_p = everything, Σ_∞ = both), 'maximal' (Σ_p = the p-adic closure of U_p, equivalently its residue preimage modulo p²) and 'maximal and not totally ramified' (Σ_p = the p-adic closure of V_p, equivalently its residue preimage modulo p²); each is strongly acceptable, and strongly acceptable implies acceptable.
3. The prototype must use the full residue preimage modulo p². Requiring one integral g congruent to a p-adic f modulo p^k for every k would restrict f to the countable integral image and would not even be GL₂(Z_p)-invariant. Equivalently one may use ∀k∃g, not ∃g∀k.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The maximal specification recovers Theorem 1 and the nowhere-totally-ramified one Theorem 2 in the density theorem.
- m_p(all maximal) = 1 + 1/p + 1/p² (BST (58)) and m_p(all nondegenerate) = (1 − 1/p)^{−1}(1 − 1/p²)^{−1} (BST (57)).
- A specification with Σ_p = {totally ramified maximal orders} for infinitely many p is not acceptable.

**Consumers.** Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman, Theorem 8 and Theorem 31 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/density-of-cubic-orders-with-local-specifications) — the density of Σ-orders is (1/2) m_∞(Σ_∞) ∏_p (1 − 1/p) m_p(Σ_p); Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman, Theorem 7 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/second-order-term-for-cubic-orders-with-local-specifications) — strongly acceptable collections admit a second main term; Bhargava-Shankar-Wang, Theorem 2 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/bhargava-shankar-wang-counts-over-number-fields) — the degree-n analogue of acceptable local specifications

<a id="st3-p-adic-density-of-a-local-specification"></a>

### 3.17 Lemma 32: the p-adic density of the forms whose ring lies in Σ_p is #GL₂(F_p)/p⁴ · Σ_{R ∈ Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) #Aut(R))

For a prime p and a set Σ_p of isomorphism classes of nondegenerate cubic rings over Z_p, the set S_p(Σ_p) := {x ∈ V_{Z_p} : R(x) ∈ Σ_p} has Haar measure μ_p(S_p(Σ_p)) = (#GL₂(F_p)/p⁴) Σ_{R ∈ Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) · #Aut_{Z_p}(R)) = (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−1}) m_p(Σ_p), with μ_p normalised to give V_{Z_p} measure 1.

**Hypotheses.** p prime; Σ_p consists of nondegenerate rings (each GL₂(Z_p)-orbit then has positive measure); Aut is the automorphism group of R as a Z_p-algebra, equal to the GL₂(Z_p)-stabilizer of a corresponding form (Delone-Faddeev over Z_p, ST.1)

**Dependencies.** [Delone-Faddeev: GL2(R)-classes of binary cubic forms parametrize cubic rings](#st1-delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings`); [Local specifications Σ = (Σ_p) ∪ Σ_∞ for cubic orders, acceptable and strongly acceptable collections, and local masses](#st3-acceptable-local-specifications-for-cubic-orders) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/acceptable-local-specifications-for-cubic-orders`); [Lemma 19: μ_p(U_p) = (p³ − 1)(p² − 1)/p⁵ and μ_p(V_p) = (p² − 1)²/p⁴](#st3-densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms`); `mathlib:Matrix.card_GL_field`; `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.8`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Lemma 32 and its proof, p. 25. The measure-theoretic step; the constant c = p^{−4} is obtained there 'by a Jacobian calculation using an indeterminate v0'.

**Proof route.**

1. By Delone-Faddeev over Z_p, S_p(Σ_p) is the disjoint union over R ∈ Σ_p of the GL₂(Z_p)-orbits GL₂(Z_p)·v_R, with Stab(v_R) ≅ Aut(R).
2. |Disc(x)|_p^{−1} dx is a GL₂(Q_p)-invariant measure on the nondegenerate locus of V_{Q_p}; with Haar measure dg on GL₂(Z_p) normalised to total mass #GL₂(F_p), the orbit map g ↦ g·v_R is #Aut(R)-to-1 and the Jacobian identity ∫_{GL₂(Z_p)·v_R} dx = c · |Disc(v_R)|_p · #GL₂(F_p)/#Aut(R) holds with c = p^{−4} independent of v_R (an explicit Jacobian computation: in coefficient coordinates (a,b,c,d) and Lie coordinates (A,B,C,D), the derivative matrix is [[2a,b,0,−a],[b,2c,3a,0],[0,3d,2b,c],[−d,0,c,2d]] with columns (A,B,C,D), whose determinant is Disc(a,b,c,d); use the exact determinant check retained with this review). This p-adic change of variables is requested from AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.8.
3. Every nondegenerate GL₂(Z_p)-orbit is open by the invertible derivative over Q_p. In the second-countable coefficient space there are at most countably many disjoint open orbits. Thus the sum over any Σ_p is a countable sum of measurable disjoint sets; apply countable additivity and #GL₂(F_p)=(p²−1)(p²−p). This also proves local mass convergence by the total coefficient mass bound.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Σ_p = all maximal orders: (p² − 1)(p² − p)p^{−4}(1 + 1/p + 1/p²) = (p³ − 1)(p² − 1)/p⁵ = μ_p(U_p), agreeing with Lemma 19.
- Σ_p = all nondegenerate orders: the density is 1, which gives BST (57).
- Σ_p = {Z_p³}: #Aut = 6, Disc_p = 1, density (p² − 1)(p² − p)/(6p⁴) = μ_p(T_p(111)) (Lemma 17).

<a id="st3-density-of-cubic-orders-with-local-specifications"></a>

### 3.18 BST Theorem 8: the number of Σ-orders of bounded discriminant for an acceptable Σ

Let Σ = (Σ_p) ∪ Σ_∞ be an acceptable collection of local specifications (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/acceptable-local-specifications-for-cubic-orders) and N₃(Σ; X) the number of isomorphism classes of orders R in cubic fields with R ⊗ Z_p ∈ Σ_p for all p, R ⊗ R ∈ Σ_∞ and |Disc(R)| < X. Then N₃(Σ; X) = (1/2)(Σ_{R∈Σ_∞} 1/#Aut(R)) · ∏_p ((p − 1)/p · Σ_{R∈Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) #Aut(R))) · X + o(X). Equivalently (BST Theorem 31), for S(Σ, i) the irreducible forms of V_Z^{(i)} whose ring is a Σ-order, lim_X N(S(Σ, i); X)/X = (1/(2 n_i)) ∏_p (p − 1)/p · m_p(Σ_p).

**Hypotheses.** Σ must be acceptable; the condition at p is on R ⊗ Z_p (the printed Theorem 8 says R ⊗ Q_p, a misprint: sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E406); The count is of orders, not fields; fields are the case Σ_p = maximal for all p; The Euler product converges because Σ is acceptable (the p-factor is 1 + O(p^{−2}) for large p)

**Dependencies.** [Local specifications Σ = (Σ_p) ∪ Σ_∞ for cubic orders, acceptable and strongly acceptable collections, and local masses](#st3-acceptable-local-specifications-for-cubic-orders) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/acceptable-local-specifications-for-cubic-orders`); [Lemma 32: the p-adic density of the forms whose ring lies in Σ_p is #GL₂(F_p)/p⁴ · Σ_{R ∈ Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) #Aut(R))](#st3-p-adic-density-of-a-local-specification) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/p-adic-density-of-a-local-specification`); [Lemma 19: μ_p(U_p) = (p³ − 1)(p² − 1)/p⁵ and μ_p(V_p) = (p² − 1)²/p⁴](#st3-densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms`); [Uniformity for totally ramified primes: the cubic fields with |Disc| < X totally ramified at p number O(X/p²), uniformly in p](#st3-cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse`); [Maximal cubic domains are the rings of integers of cubic fields; the orbits in ∩_p U_p count cubic fields](#st3-maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields`); [Proposition 29 (non-maximal part), for forms: the classes in W_p^DH have O(X/p^2) elements of discriminant < X, uniformly in p](#st2-uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms`); [A uniform tail estimate for binary cubic forms whose discriminant is divisible by p^2 for some p > M](#st2-uniformity-estimate-for-binary-cubic-discriminants) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-binary-cubic-discriminants`); `mathlib:riemannZeta_two`; `mathlib:riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Theorem 8, p. 3. The hypotheses of Theorem 8 (with the misprint R ⊗ Q_p recorded as E406); the displayed formula (8) is the one in the node. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Theorem 31 and the paragraph after it, p. 25. The sieve step of the proof.

**Proof route.**

1. Each nondegenerate GL₂(Z_p)-orbit is open, and the complement of a union of such orbits is open within Disc≠0. Hence the indicator of any local specification is locally constant off the Haar-null hypersurface Disc=0. It need not be determined by one fixed modulus p^n. Approximate at each of the finitely many small primes by cylinder infima and suprema; their integrals converge. Use the corrected weighted sieve of ST.2 with X→∞, then n→∞ for the finite local approximations, then the prime cutoff→∞.
2. For all large p, violation of Σ_p implies nonmaximality or total ramification, hence p²|Disc. The ST.2 uniform tail estimate for binary cubic discriminants therefore controls the entire tail of orders directly. This avoids asserting a per-prime O(X/p²) bound for nonmaximal-at-other-primes forms from the field-only lemma. Cyclic cubic stabilizers contribute o(X), so the weighted and unweighted main terms agree.
3. Insert Lemma 32: π²/(12 n_i) ∏_p μ_p(S_p(Σ_p)) = π²/(12 n_i) ∏_p (1 − p^{−2})((p − 1)/p) m_p(Σ_p) = (1/(2 n_i)) ∏_p ((p − 1)/p) m_p(Σ_p), using ∏_p (1 − p^{−2}) = 6/π².
4. Sum over i ∈ Σ_∞ with 1/n_i = 1/#Aut(R) for R = R³ (i = 0) or R ⊕ C (i = 1).

**Acceptance checks.**

- Σ_p = all maximal, Σ_∞ = {R³}: (1/12) ∏_p (1 − 1/p)(1 + 1/p + 1/p²) = 1/(12ζ(3)), Theorem 1.
- Σ_p = all nondegenerate orders: (1/(2n_i)) ∏_p (1 − p^{−2})^{−1} = ζ(2)/(2 n_i) = π²/(12 n_i), i.e. π²/72 and π²/24 (BST Theorem 6 main term).
- Σ_p = maximal not totally ramified: (1/(2n_i)) ∏_p (1 − 1/p)(1 + 1/p) = 3/(n_i π²), the count used for Theorem 2.

### 3.19 BST Theorem 3 (Roberts' conjecture): the second main term in the count of cubic fields

N₃(0, X) = X/(12ζ(3)) + (4ζ(1/3)/(5Γ(2/3)³ζ(5/3))) X^{5/6} + O_ε(X^{5/6−1/48+ε}) and N₃(−X, 0) = X/(4ζ(3)) + (√3 · 4ζ(1/3)/(5Γ(2/3)³ζ(5/3))) X^{5/6} + O_ε(X^{5/6−1/48+ε}), for every ε > 0.

**Hypotheses.** The second main term has order X^{5/6}; the error O_ε(X^{5/6−1/48+ε}) is a power saving over it when ε<1/48; The proof uses the secondary lattice-count and sieve interfaces of Layer 2 and the local-factor and refined-sieve assembly of this layer, with the exact restrictions in those targets

**Dependencies.** [The Davenport-Heilbronn theorem: N₃(0, X) ~ X/(12ζ(3)) and N₃(−X, 0) ~ X/(4ζ(3))](#st3-davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields`); [The counting function of number fields of fixed degree by discriminant, with signature, Galois-group and local restrictions](#st3-number-field-counting-function) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/number-field-counting-function`); [Theorem 26 with (29)-(31): binary cubic forms in lattice translates, uniformly in the modulus](#st2-binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions`); [Cubic secondary term on a lattice](#st2-refinement-cubic-secondary-congruence-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-cubic-secondary-congruence-count`); [Cubic secondary-term sieve input](#st2-refinement-cubic-secondary-sieve-error) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-cubic-secondary-sieve-error`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Theorem 3, (3), p. 2. The statement verbatim; the constants are copied from the rendered page.

**Proof route.**

1. Count forms in dyadic ranges of the discriminant with the second-order count of binary cubic forms satisfying finitely many congruence conditions (BST Theorem 27, the congruence version of the Davenport-Shintani count; uniform lattice counts of ST.2).
2. Compute the second-order p-adic densities μ₂(σ, p), μ₂(p), μ₂'(p) (BST Section 7) and the second-order local masses (BST Lemma 37).
3. Sieve with the Möbius identities (61)-(62) over squarefree n, splitting n into three ranges: Theorem 27 with the identities of BST Proposition 33 for small n, the uniformity estimates of Belabas-Bhargava-Pomerance for large n, and an equidistribution argument (BST Section 9.4) for n near X^{1/6}.
4. These steps are recorded as the gap 'Second-order terms (BST Sections 6, 7 and 9) are not decomposed'.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The second-term constant is negative (ζ(1/3) < 0), explaining the poor early numerical agreement with Theorem 1 noted in BST Section 1.
- The ratio of the X^{5/6} coefficients (negative : positive discriminant) is √3, while the ratio of main terms is 3.

### 3.21 BST Theorem 7: two main terms for Σ-orders with a strongly acceptable Σ

Let Σ = (Σ_p) ∪ Σ_∞ be strongly acceptable. For a free Z_p-module M put M^{Prim} := M \ pM. Then N₃(Σ; X) = (1/2)(Σ_{R∈Σ_∞} 1/#Aut(R)) ∏_p ((p − 1)/p · Σ_{R∈Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) #Aut(R))) X + (1/ζ(2))(Σ_{R∈Σ_∞} c₂(R)) ∏_p ((1 − p^{−1/3}) Σ_{R∈Σ_p} (1/(Disc_p(R) #Aut(R))) ∫_{(R/Z_p)^{Prim}} i(x)^{2/3} dx) X^{5/6} + O_ε(X^{5/6−1/48+ε}), where i(x) is the index of Z_p[x] in R, dx gives (R/Z_p)^{Prim} measure 1, and c₂(R³) = √3 ζ(2/3)Γ(1/3)(2π)^{1/3}/(30Γ(2/3)), c₂(R ⊕ C) = ζ(2/3)Γ(1/3)(2π)^{1/3}/(10Γ(2/3)).

**Hypotheses.** Σ strongly acceptable (not merely acceptable); The proof is BST Sections 6, 7 and 9 with Lemma 37; not decomposed here (gap on second-order terms); A primitive class x modulo Z_p need not generate the cubic algebra. On the null set where its index form vanishes, i(x) is infinite; use an extended nonnegative integrand, or assign any finite value on that null set. Near a simple projective root the singularity is |t|_p^{-2/3}, which is locally integrable. This qualification is needed for the integral, and the source Lemma37 finite-partition proof must pass to the limit.

**Dependencies.** [BST Theorem 8: the number of Σ-orders of bounded discriminant for an acceptable Σ](#st3-density-of-cubic-orders-with-local-specifications) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/density-of-cubic-orders-with-local-specifications`); [Local specifications Σ = (Σ_p) ∪ Σ_∞ for cubic orders, acceptable and strongly acceptable collections, and local masses](#st3-acceptable-local-specifications-for-cubic-orders) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/acceptable-local-specifications-for-cubic-orders`); [Lemma 32: the p-adic density of the forms whose ring lies in Σ_p is #GL₂(F_p)/p⁴ · Σ_{R ∈ Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) #Aut(R))](#st3-p-adic-density-of-a-local-specification) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/p-adic-density-of-a-local-specification`); [Cubic secondary term on a lattice](#st2-refinement-cubic-secondary-congruence-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-cubic-secondary-congruence-count`); [Cubic secondary-term sieve input](#st2-refinement-cubic-secondary-sieve-error) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-cubic-secondary-sieve-error`)

1. Theorem 31 for the first term (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/density-of-cubic-orders-with-local-specifications).
2. Lemma 37 expresses the second-order local density μ₂(R, p) = (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−1/3}) (1/(Disc_p(R) #Aut(R))) ∫_{(R/Z_p)^{Prim}} i(x)^{2/3} dx, via the slicing count of Section 6 and the change of variables of Lemma 32.
3. The refined sieve of Section 9 (as in the second-order nodes) gives the error term.

<a id="st3-mertens-count-of-positive-definite-binary-quadratic-forms"></a>

### 3.22 Mertens: the number of SL₂(Z)-classes of positive definite binary quadratic forms with 0 < −D < X is (π/18) X^{3/2} + O(X log X)

For D < 0 let h⁺(D) be the number of SL₂(Z)-equivalence classes of positive definite integral binary quadratic forms a x² + b x y + c y² (a > 0) of discriminant b² − 4ac = D, all forms counted (primitive or not). Then Σ_{−X<D<0} h⁺(D) = (π/18) X^{3/2} + O(X log X).

**Hypotheses.** Positive definite forms only: counting the negative definite classes as well doubles the sum (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E401 on the printed statement); Non-primitive forms are included (they are irreducible over Q); the primitive count has constant (π/18)/ζ(3); Classes, not weighted classes: the forms x² + y² and x² + xy + y² and their multiples are counted with weight 1 (Hurwitz's weights 1/2, 1/3 change only lower-order terms)

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:ModularGroup.fd`; `mathlib:ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd`; `mathlib:ModularGroup.eq_smul_self_of_mem_fdo_mem_fdo`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-11-the-eichlerselberg-trace-formula-level-one

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Theorem 1.4(a) and footnote 1, p. 3. The statement, with h_D read as the number of positive definite classes (E401); the proof steps are the classical reduced-form count, not given in the source.

**Proof route.**

1. Reduction: every positive definite form is SL₂(Z)-equivalent to exactly one reduced form (|b| ≤ a ≤ c, with b ≥ 0 if |b| = a or a = c). Write f = a(x − τy)(x − τ̄y) with τ in the upper half plane; SL₂(Z) acts on τ by Möbius transformations, and f is reduced iff τ lies in the closed fundamental domain ModularGroup.fd with the boundary identified (ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd, ModularGroup.eq_smul_self_of_mem_fdo_mem_fdo). The canonical representatives are those pinned in ModularForms Layer 11.
2. Counting: h⁺ summed over −X < D < 0 is the number of integer triples (a, b, c) with |b| ≤ a ≤ c, 4ac − b² < X and the boundary convention. Slice by a: a ≤ √(X/3), and for each (a, b) the number of c is max(0, (X + b²)/(4a) − a) + O(1); summing over |b| ≤ a and a ≤ √(X/3) gives the integral V(X) over the actual nonempty slices plus O(X log X) (the O(1) terms contribute O(X), the Riemann-sum error in b and a contributes O(X log X)).
3. Volume: in coordinates (a, τ = x + iy), b = −2ax, c = a|τ|², the Jacobian is 4a²y and the discriminant condition is 4a²y² < X, so V(X) = ∫_{fd} ∫_0^{√X/(2y)} 4a²y da dx dy = (X^{3/2}/6) ∫_{fd} dx dy / y² = (X^{3/2}/6)(π/3) = (π/18) X^{3/2}, using the hyperbolic area ∫_{−1/2}^{1/2} ∫_{√(1−x²)}^∞ dy dx / y² = 2 arcsin(1/2) = π/3.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Numerical check: the number of reduced positive definite forms with 4ac − b² < X is 172131, 5494441, 44054144 for X = 10⁴, 10⁵, 4·10⁵, i.e. 0.17213, 0.17375, 0.17414 times X^{3/2}, against π/18 ≈ 0.17453.
- Small values: h⁺(−3) = h⁺(−4) = 1, h⁺(−12) = 2 (x² + 3y² and 2x² + 2xy + 2y²), h⁺(−16) = 2 (x² + 4y² and 2x² + 2y²).
- The constant is (1/6) × area(SL₂(Z)\H) = (1/6)(π/3).

**Interface qualification.**  Independent review removed Wood §11.3 Lemma 11.11 as a citation for Mertens: it states Davenport’s lattice estimate. The Bhargava–Shankar theorem reference remains.

<a id="st3-siegel-count-of-indefinite-binary-quadratic-forms"></a>

### 3.23 Siegel: the primitive indefinite quadratic class-number–regulator sum is asymptotic to π² X^{3/2}/(18ζ(3))

For positive nonsquare discriminants D≡0 or 1 (mod4), let h_D^prim be the number of SL₂(Z)-classes of primitive integral binary quadratic forms of discriminant D, and ε_D=(t+u√D)/2 for the least positive solution of t²−Du²=4. Then Σ_{0<D<X} h_D^prim log ε_D = π² X^{3/2}/(18ζ(3)) + O(X log X). Equivalently, counting all forms with each class weighted by the regulator of its primitive part gives Σ_{g≥1,D>0,g²D<X} h_D^prim log ε_D ~ (π²/18)X^{3/2}. The all-form class number at D multiplied by a single log ε_D is not this stabilizer-weighted count.

**Hypotheses.** Primitive means gcd(a,b,c)=1. The regulator attached to an imprimitive form of content g is log ε_{D/g²}, not log ε_D.; The class number is the strict class number of the quadratic order of discriminant D. The positive norm-one unit convention is fixed.; The public published source states the primitive/order theorem. Its analytic proof is not decomposed here; the existing proof gap remains.

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:NumberField.dedekindZeta_residue`; `mathlib:NumberField.tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT`; `mathlib:NumberField.Units.regulator`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Theorem 1.4(b), p. 3. Historical motivation only: its all-forms wording cannot be used with the uniform Pell weight as a stabilizer formula. The corrected primitive statement uses the published order-class theorem below. [P/andrade-jung-classnumber-2018](#source-p-andrade-jung-classnumber-2018), Section1.1, printed578–579, Theorem1.2(2). The displayed (1.4) gives π²/(18ζ(3)) and O(N logN) for the order/primitive count with the norm-one regulator.

**Proof route.**

1. For a primitive form, the positive generator of the stabilizer modulo {±I} is the Pell automorphism with eigenvalue ε_D. The full SL₂(Z)-stabilizer contains −I and is {±I} times an infinite cyclic group; it is not itself infinite cyclic.
2. The primitive/order version is Siegel’s mean theorem as stated in Andrade–Jung, Theorem1.2(2), with constant π²/(18ζ(3)) and error O(X log X). For fundamental D, the class-number formula identifies h_D^prim log ε_D with √D times the Dedekind zeta residue; extending the average to all orders requires the corresponding imprimitive Dirichlet characters. This analytic mean is still a quoted input, not a proved consequence of the library class-number formula.
3. For the all-form stabilizer-weighted corollary, write each form uniquely as g times a primitive form. Its discriminant is g²D and its stabilizer is unchanged. Sum the primitive asymptotic at X/g²; the leading constants multiply by Σg^{-3}=ζ(3). Dominate by O(X^{3/2}/g³) to justify the limit and the tail. This does not weight an imprimitive form by the Pell regulator of its larger discriminant.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For fundamental D > 0 and primitive forms: h⁺(D) log ε⁺_D = 2 h(D) R(D) = √D · dedekindZeta_residue(Q(√D)), since the residue is 2² h R/(2√D).
- D = 5: one class (x² + xy − y²), ε₅ = (3 + √5)/2, log ε₅ ≈ 0.9624.
- For q=x²+xy−y² and 2q, the matrix [[1,1],[1,2]] stabilizes both. Their discriminants are5 and20, but ε20=9+4√5=ε5³. Thus assigning log ε20 to the class of2q overstates its actual primitive stabilizer period by3.

### 3.24 The quadratic and cubic predecessors (Mertens/Siegel and Davenport), with the imaginary quadratic count corrected

(Theorem 1.4, Mertens 1874 / Siegel 1944, corrected) With h⁺(D) the number of SL₂(Z)-classes of positive definite integral binary quadratic forms of discriminant D < 0 and h_D^prim the number of SL₂(Z)-classes of primitive integral binary quadratic forms of non-square discriminant D > 0: Σ_{−X<D<0} h⁺(D) ~ (π/18) X^{3/2}, and Σ_{0<D<X} h_D^prim log ε_D ~ (π²/(18ζ(3))) X^{3/2}, where ε_D = (t + u√D)/2 with t, u the smallest positive integral solutions of t² − D u² = 4. (Theorem 1.5, Davenport 1951) With h(D) the number of GL₂(Z)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms of discriminant D: Σ_{−X<D<0} h(D) ~ (π²/24) X and Σ_{0<D<X} h(D) ~ (π²/72) X. Via Delone-Faddeev, classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms correspond to orders in cubic fields, so Theorem 1.5 counts cubic orders by discriminant.

**Hypotheses.** h⁺(D) counts positive definite classes only: the printed h_D ('irreducible forms of discriminant D') would include the negative definite classes and give (π/9) X^{3/2} (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E401); The indefinite count uses primitive forms and their norm-one regulators; the all-form version instead weights each class by the regulator of its primitive part and has constant π²/18. These two valid conventions must not be mixed.; The cubic statement is about GL₂(Z)-classes, and irreducibility is required; reducible forms are excluded; The Delone-Faddeev correspondence is with ORDERS in cubic fields (including non-maximal ones), not with cubic fields

**Dependencies.** [Mertens: the number of SL₂(Z)-classes of positive definite binary quadratic forms with 0 < −D < X is (π/18) X^{3/2} + O(X log X)](#st3-mertens-count-of-positive-definite-binary-quadratic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/mertens-count-of-positive-definite-binary-quadratic-forms`); [Siegel: the primitive indefinite quadratic class-number–regulator sum is asymptotic to π² X^{3/2}/(18ζ(3))](#st3-siegel-count-of-indefinite-binary-quadratic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/siegel-count-of-indefinite-binary-quadratic-forms`); [Theorem 20 (Davenport): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms of bounded discriminant](#st2-davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms`); [Delone-Faddeev: GL2(R)-classes of binary cubic forms parametrize cubic rings](#st1-delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), Theorem 1.4 and Theorem 1.5 with the surrounding interpretation, printed pp. 3-4. Verbatim Theorem 1.5; Theorem 1.4 is quoted in the Mertens and Siegel nodes, with the positive-definite correction E401 and the regulator/primitive qualification established in the Siegel node. [P/bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013](#source-p-bhargava-davenport-heilbronn-2013), Theorem 20, p. 9. The public proof of Davenport's theorem with error term, whose decomposition is supplied by ST.2.

**Proof route.**

1. Imaginary quadratic part: ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/mertens-count-of-positive-definite-binary-quadratic-forms, with error O(X log X).
2. Real quadratic part: ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/siegel-count-of-indefinite-binary-quadratic-forms (recorded with a gap: no public proof in the sources read).
3. Cubic part: Davenport's theorem is the main term of BST Theorem 20 / Theorem 5, N(V_Z^{(0)}; X) = (π²/72) X + O(X^{5/6}) and N(V_Z^{(1)}; X) = (π²/24) X + O(X^{5/6}), proved by the averaging method of BST Section 5 and supplied by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2 (uniform arithmetic lattice/orbit counts); the order interpretation is Delone-Faddeev (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) with irreducible forms ↔ domains (BST Proposition 11).
