**Dependencies.** [Families defined by local conditions, local densities and largeness](#st0-family-defined-by-local-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions`); [The eligible invariant pairs ordered by H(I, J), with the curve normalisation 27·H_E = 4·H′ (the binary-quartic invariant and height interface)](#st0-invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs`); [Higher height moments in an arithmetic family](#st5-height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family`); [Genus-one model stabilizer schemes in degrees2–5](#st1-refinement-genus-one-stabilizer-schemes) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/refinement-genus-one-stabilizer-schemes`); [Quaternary-pair acceptable-weight count](#st2-refinement-quaternary-acceptable-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-quaternary-acceptable-count`); [Theorem 3.1: the average size of S_2(E) over a large family is 3](#st4-average-size-of-the-2-selmer-group-is-three) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4/average-size-of-the-2-selmer-group-is-three`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-4selmer-2013](#source-p-bhargava-4selmer-2013), §1, Theorem 2, p. 1 (arXiv v1). Statement. [P/bhargava-4selmer-2013](#source-p-bhargava-4selmer-2013), §1, p. 2 (arXiv v1). Pairs of quadrics.

**Proof route.**

1. Parametrisation: locally soluble 4-coverings of E embed in ℙ³ as intersections of two quadrics (Cassels), so 4-Selmer elements correspond to locally soluble G(ℚ)-orbits on pairs of quaternary quadratic forms 2 ⊗ Sym²(4), G = {(g_2, g_4) : det g_2 det g_4 = 1}/{(λ^{−2}I_2, λI_4)}, whose invariants correspond to (A, B) (gap 'Orbit parametrisations of 3-, 4- and 5-Selmer elements'; scope of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1).
2. Counting integral orbits of bounded height in a fundamental domain and sieving to local solubility and to F (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2 methods, GN.4 Davenport input).
3. Mass computation with τ(G) and local masses gives σ(4) = 7 on average, the elements of Sel_4 of order dividing 2 being counted through Sel_2 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4/average-size-of-the-2-selmer-group-is-three).

**Acceptance checks.**

- 7 = 1 + 2 + 4 = σ(4): BS(4) holds (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/bhargava-shankar-selmer-average-conjecture).
- Not a moment of Sel_2: the second moment of #Sel_2 is predicted to be 15, not 7.

Averages are first moments in the sense of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family; Sel_n(E) is the n-Selmer group of EllipticCurves Layer 7.

**Hypotheses.** F a family of E_{A,B}/ℚ defined by finitely many congruence conditions on (A, B); F is nonempty and its height counting function tends to infinity; finite congruence conditions must admit minimal nonsingular models. Empty congruence families are excluded.

**Dependencies.** [Families defined by local conditions, local densities and largeness](#st0-family-defined-by-local-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions`); [The eligible invariant pairs ordered by H(I, J), with the curve normalisation 27·H_E = 4·H′ (the binary-quartic invariant and height interface)](#st0-invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs`); [Higher height moments in an arithmetic family](#st5-height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family`); [Genus-one model stabilizer schemes in degrees2–5](#st1-refinement-genus-one-stabilizer-schemes) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/refinement-genus-one-stabilizer-schemes`); [Degree-five genus-one acceptable-weight count](#st2-refinement-quinary-acceptable-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-quinary-acceptable-count`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-5selmer-2013](#source-p-bhargava-5selmer-2013), §1, Theorem 2, p. 1 (arXiv v1). Statement. [P/bhargava-5selmer-2013](#source-p-bhargava-5selmer-2013), §1, p. 2 (arXiv v1). The parametrisation of 5-Selmer elements.

**Proof route.**

1. Parametrisation: locally soluble 5-coverings embed in ℙ⁴ as genus-one normal curves of degree 5, cut out by the 4 × 4 Pfaffians of a 5 × 5 alternating matrix of linear forms; 5-Selmer elements correspond to locally soluble G(ℚ)-orbits on quintuples of 5 × 5 alternating matrices, where G={(g₁,g₂)∈GL₅×GL₅:(det g₁)²det g₂=1}/{(λI₅,λ⁻²I₅)}. The simply connected group SL₅×SL₅ has the same invariant polynomials, but its rational orbits are not the required parametrization (gap 'Orbit parametrisations of 3-, 4- and 5-Selmer elements'; scope of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1).
2. Counting and sieving as for n = 3, 4 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2 methods).
3. Mass computation: 5 nontrivial elements on average plus the identity.

**Acceptance checks.**

- 6 = 5 + 1 is the Poonen–Rains prediction p + 1 at p = 5.
- Combined with ST.4's rank inequality the average rank is at most (6 + 15)/20 = 1.05 using 20r − 15 ≤ 5^r; the source's sharper bound 0.885 uses root-number equidistribution (coverage remaining).

<a id="st5-second-moment-of-the-2-selmer-group"></a>

### 5.83 Bhargava–Shankar–Swaminathan: the second moment of #Sel_2 is at most 15

When elliptic curves over ℚ, or those of any nonempty subfamily defined by finitely many congruence conditions, are ordered by height, the upper second moment M⁺_2(#Sel_2(E)) is at most 15. (15 = (2 + 1)(4 + 1) is the Poonen–Rains prediction for the second moment; equality is not proved.) Bhargava–Shankar–Swaminathan use the model E_{I,J} : y² = x³ − (I/3)x − J/27 with height (4/27)max(|I|³, J²/4); its comparison with (E_{A,B}, max(4|A|³, 27B²)) is the normalisation comparison owned by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs and changes no average. Family: elliptic curves E_{A,B} : y² = x³ + Ax + B with A, B ∈ ℤ, 4A³ + 27B² ≠ 0 and no prime ℓ with ℓ⁴ | A and ℓ⁶ | B (one representative of each ℚ-isomorphism class), ordered by H(E_{A,B}) = max(4|A|³, 27B²) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0 and Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 8); a subfamily defined by finitely many congruence conditions is the set of E_{A,B} with (A, B) in a finite union of residue classes modulo some N (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions). Averages are first moments in the sense of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family; Sel_n(E) is the n-Selmer group of EllipticCurves Layer 7.

**Hypotheses.** F a family of elliptic curves over ℚ defined by finitely many congruence conditions; F is nonempty and its height counting function tends to infinity; finite congruence conditions must admit minimal nonsingular models. Empty congruence families are excluded.

**Dependencies.** [Families defined by local conditions, local densities and largeness](#st0-family-defined-by-local-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions`); [The eligible invariant pairs ordered by H(I, J), with the curve normalisation 27·H_E = 4·H′ (the binary-quartic invariant and height interface)](#st0-invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs`); [Higher height moments in an arithmetic family](#st5-height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family`); [Theorem 3.1: the average size of S_2(E) over a large family is 3](#st4-average-size-of-the-2-selmer-group-is-three) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4/average-size-of-the-2-selmer-group-is-three`); [Bhargava-Shankar Theorem 3.5: 2-Selmer elements are PGL2(Q)-classes of locally soluble integral quartics with invariants 2^4 I, 2^6 J](#st1-binary-quartic-parametrization-of-two-selmer) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/binary-quartic-parametrization-of-two-selmer`); [Layer 1](#layer-1) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1`; required refinement); [Smoothed special quaternary count](#st2-refinement-smoothed-quaternary-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-smoothed-quaternary-count`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-secondmoment-2021](#source-p-bhargava-secondmoment-2021), §1.1, Theorem 1.1, p. 2 (arXiv v1). Statement. [P/bhargava-secondmoment-2021](#source-p-bhargava-secondmoment-2021), §1.1, p. 2 (arXiv v1). Congruence families; tightness conditional on a tail estimate.

**Proof route.**

1. Separate the trivial first 2-Selmer element, whose contribution is the first-moment average 3. For a nontrivial first element choose its locally soluble integral binary quartic f with leading coefficient a≠0. The second element belongs to Sel₂(J_f), with J_f≅E. Its distribution over these marked quartics is weighted by the first element; one cannot multiply two unconditioned averages.
2. Replace f by f^mon=a⁻¹f(x,ay). The curve C_{f^mon} has a rational point and is a quadratic twist of C_f; its Jacobian has invariants (a²I,a³J). The canonical identification of the 2-torsion schemes gives an isomorphism on H¹, but does not identify the two Selmer groups. BSS Theorem 1.4 injects the original Sel₂(J_f) into (SL₄/μ₂)(Q)-orbits with determinant f^mon and supplies integral representatives after a fixed scaling κ.
3. Count the special integral orbits with their actual height and leading-coefficient conditions. For squarefree a the specialness condition is rank≤1 modulo every p|a; it has density about a⁻⁶. The source controls errors uniformly in a using twisted Poisson summation, and treats small a and large powerful parts by unskewing into the full SL₄ representation and separate upper bounds. A fixed-a Davenport estimate does not suffice.
4. The weighted global count, uniform errors and local mass evaluations in BSS §§5–7 bound the nontrivial-first-element contribution by 12, giving 3+12=15. The heuristic 3+2·6 on p.3 is a consistency guide, not the proof of that weighted bound. The parametrisation, sparse-orbit estimates and assembly remain explicit ST.1/ST.2/ST.5 planning gaps; this node records the theorem with partial proof coverage.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Consistency: M_1(#Sel_2) = 3 and M⁺_2(#Sel_2) ≤ 15 give, by Cauchy–Schwarz, no contradiction (9 ≤ 15).
- The Poonen–Rains moment formula at p = 2, m = 2 equals 15 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/poonen-rains-moments).

<a id="st5-two-selmer-distribution-in-full-two-torsion-twist-families"></a>

### 5.84 Heath-Brown, Swinnerton-Dyer, Kane: the 2-Selmer rank distribution in quadratic twist families

Let E : y² = (x − c_1)(x − c_2)(x − c_3) with c_i ∈ ℚ distinct and none of (c_i − c_j)(c_i − c_k) a rational square (equivalently E(ℚ)[2] = E[2] and E has no ℚ-rational cyclic subgroup of order 4), and for b ∈ ℤ \ {0} let E_b : y² = (x − bc_1)(x − bc_2)(x − bc_3) be the quadratic twist by ℚ(√b). Then for every d ≥ 0, lim_{N→∞} #{b ∈ ℤ : 0 < |b| ≤ N, dim_{𝔽_2} Sel_2(E_b) = d + 2}/(2N) = a_d, the Poonen–Rains weight at p = 2 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/poonen-rains-distribution); the same holds among positive b, and among squarefree b prime to any fixed D divisible by 8 and the bad primes (relative density). For E : y² = x³ − x this is Heath-Brown's theorem.

**Hypotheses.** c_1, c_2, c_3 ∈ ℚ distinct; (c_i − c_j)(c_i − c_k) ∉ ℚ^{×2} for {i, j, k} = {1, 2, 3}

**Dependencies.** [The Poonen–Rains distribution X_{Sel_p}](#st5-poonen-rains-distribution) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/poonen-rains-distribution`); [Moments of p^{X}: the Poonen–Rains moment formula](#st5-poonen-rains-moments) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/poonen-rains-moments`); [Random alternating kernels have the Poonen–Rains law in the parity-averaged limit](#st5-alternating-kernel-law-limit-is-poonen-rains) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/alternating-kernel-law-limit-is-poonen-rains`); [Higher height moments in an arithmetic family](#st5-height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family`); [The unweighted squareclass-height family of quadratic twists E^(t), t ∈ F×/F×²](#st0-quadratic-twist-squareclass-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family`); `SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4

**Sources.** [P/kane-2selmer-2013](#source-p-kane-2selmer-2013), §1, setting, p. 1 (arXiv v4). The curve and the twist family. [P/kane-2selmer-2013](#source-p-kane-2selmer-2013), §1, Theorem 3 and Corollaries 4–5, p. 2 (arXiv v4). The natural-density theorem. [P/kane-2selmer-2013](#source-p-kane-2selmer-2013), §1, Theorem 2, p. 2 (arXiv v4). The limiting law α_{n+2} = 2^n/(∏(2^j − 1)∏(1 + 2^{−j})) = a_n.

**Proof route.**

1. Swinnerton-Dyer's algebraic step: for b = p_1 ⋯ p_n squarefree prime to D, Sel_2(E_b) is the intersection of two Lagrangian subspaces of a symplectic 𝔽_2-space determined by the classes of p_i in (ℤ/D)^×/(ℤ/D)^{×2} and the Legendre symbols (p_i/p_j); the proportion π_d(n) of such data with dim Sel_2 = d tends to α_d = a_{d−2} as n → ∞ (a Markov chain whose stationary law is the Poonen–Rains law; ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/alternating-kernel-law-limit-is-poonen-rains identifies that law).
2. Kane's analytic step: the moments of #Sel_2(E_b)/4 over squarefree b ≤ N prime to D converge to the Poonen–Rains moments (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/poonen-rains-moments), using |U ∩ W| = |V|^{−1/2}Σ_{u,w}(−1)^{u·w} and bounds for character sums in Legendre symbols of the prime factors (large sieve, SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2). Thus the unnormalised m-th moments of #Sel₂ are 4^m∏_{i=1}^m(2^i+1), accounting for the fixed rational 2-torsion.
3. Moments determine the law here (parity is fixed by the class of b mod D, Kane Lemma 1, and the moments grow like 2^{m(m+1)/2}); pass from squarefree b prime to D to all b by twisting by divisors of D and noting that twists by squares do not change Sel_2. The analytic estimates are not decomposed (gap 'Kane's character-sum estimates').

**Acceptance checks.**

- d = 0 (Sel_2 = E[2] only): density a_0 ≈ 0.2097.
- The parity of dim Sel_2(E_b) depends only on the class of b in ∏_{v∈S}ℚ_v^×/ℚ_v^{×2}, and is even for exactly half of the classes (Kane, Lemma 1).

<a id="st5-function-field-3-selmer-average-bound"></a>

### 5.85 de Jong: the average size of the 3-Selmer group over 𝔽_q(t) is at most 4 + O(1/q)

Let 𝔽_q be a finite field with 3 ∤ q. When the elliptic curves over 𝔽_q(t) are ordered by height (isomorphism classes of height d, d → ∞), the upper average of #Sel_3(E/𝔽_q(t)) is at most 4 + ε(q), where ε(q) is an explicit rational function of q with ε(q) → 0 as q → ∞. This is the function-field analogue, as an upper bound, of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/average-size-of-the-3-selmer-group; de Jong speculated that the truth is 4.

**Hypotheses.** q a prime power with 3 ∤ q; elliptic curves over 𝔽_q(t) ordered by height

**Dependencies.** [Higher height moments in an arithmetic family](#st5-height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family`); [The Poonen–Rains conjecture for p-Selmer groups over ℚ (as a stated proposition)](#st5-poonen-rains-selmer-conjecture) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/poonen-rains-selmer-conjecture`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4

**Sources.** [P/poonen-isotropic-2012](#source-p-poonen-isotropic-2012), §1.2, list after Conjecture 1.1, p. 2. The statement of de Jong's bound. [P/bhargava-shankar-2013](#source-p-bhargava-shankar-2013), §1, p. 2 (arXiv v3). The same result as the function-field precursor.

**Proof route.**

1. de Jong counts isomorphism classes of elliptic curves of height d over 𝔽_q(t) and bounds the number of elliptic surfaces over ℙ¹ carrying a relative polarisation of degree 3 (plane cubic models of 3-coverings), then compares the two counts.
2. The de Jong primary paper was not obtained in readable full text in this review. The author lists a DVI, while MathNet links a full-text PDF; attempts through the AMS endpoint encountered access/login barriers. The theorem is supported here by the explicitly cited summaries of Poonen–Rains §1.2 and Bhargava–Shankar §1, with direct proof verification left in the recorded gap. This does not assert that DVI is its only available format.

**Acceptance checks.**

- As q → ∞ the bound tends to 4 = σ(3), the Poonen–Rains prediction p + 1 at p = 3.

<a id="st5-p-infinity-selmer-corank-distribution-in-twist-families"></a>

### 5.86 Distribution of p^∞-Selmer coranks in a quadratic twist family

Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field F and p a prime; write c_p(E/F) := corank_{ℤ_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/F) (the ℚ_p-dimension of the Pontryagin dual of Sel_{p^∞} tensored with ℚ_p; SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2). For a squareclass s ∈ F^×/F^{×2} let E^s be the quadratic twist of E by F(√s)/F (E^s ≅ E when s is a square; Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 5). (i) Signed-integer ordering over ℚ (Smith): for r ≥ 0 and an integer H ≥ 1, N_r(H) := #{d ∈ ℤ : 0 < |d| ≤ H, c_p(E^d/ℚ) = r} and the proportion N_r(H)/(2H); every nonzero integer d is counted, squares and non-squarefree d included, and E^d depends only on the squareclass of d. (ii) Squareclass ordering (Bhargava–Klagsbrun–Lemke Oliver–Shnidman, Burungale–Tian): for Σ ⊆ F^×/F^{×2} and X > 0, Σ(X) := {s ∈ Σ : H(s) < X} with H(s) := ∏_{𝔭 : v_𝔭(s) odd} N𝔭, each squareclass counted once (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family), and the proportion #{s ∈ Σ(X) : c_p(E^s/F) = r}/#Σ(X). (iii) For a probability vector π = (π_r)_{r≥0}, E has twist-corank law π at p (in ordering (i) or (ii)) if every proportion converges to π_r; lower bounds are stated with liminf. For F = ℚ the squareclass height of the class of a squarefree d is |d|.

**Hypotheses.** E elliptic over a number field F; p prime

**Dependencies.** [The unweighted squareclass-height family of quadratic twists E^(t), t ∈ F×/F×²](#st0-quadratic-twist-squareclass-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family`); [Higher height moments in an arithmetic family](#st5-height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family`); `SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2`

**Sources.** [P/smith-selmer-2026](#source-p-smith-selmer-2026), §1.1, pp. 2–3 (arXiv v2). The twist A^d by F(√d)/F. [P/smith-selmer-2026](#source-p-smith-selmer-2026), §1.1, Theorem 1.2, p. 3 (arXiv v2). The signed-integer ordering with denominator 2H. [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), §3.2.2, Theorem 3.5, p. 7. The squareclass family over K.

**API.**

- `signedTwistCorankCount` (constructor): N_r(H) = #{d : 0 < |d| ≤ H, c(d) = r} for a corank function c : ℤ → ℕ. Here H∈ℕ; for real H≥0 the total count is 2⌊H⌋.
- `HasSignedTwistCorankLaw` (data): ∀ r, N_r(H)/(2H) → π_r as H → ∞.
- `squareclassTwistCorankCount` (data): #{s ∈ Σ(X) : c(s) = r} for the squareclass family Σ(X).
- `LowerSquareclassCorankDensity` (data): liminf_{X→∞} #{s ∈ Σ(X) : c(s) = r}/#Σ(X).
- `sum_signedTwistCorankCount` (characterisation): Σ_r N_r(H) = 2H: the counts over r partition the nonzero d with |d| ≤ H. Here H∈ℕ; for real H≥0 the total count is 2⌊H⌋.
- `signedTwistCorankCount_mono` (other): N_r(H) ≤ N_r(H') for H ≤ H'.
- `hasSignedTwistCorankLaw_tail` (relation): If E has signed law π with π_0 + π_1 = 1 then #{0 < |d| ≤ H : c(d) ≥ 2}/(2H) → 0 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/two-point-corank-law-forces-zero-density-of-high-corank).

**Checks.**

- `signedTwistCorankCount.test_constant_zero` (degenerate): For c ≡ 0, signedTwistCorankCount c 0 H = 2H and HasSignedTwistCorankLaw c (point mass at 0). The exact identity uses H∈ℕ.
- `signedTwistCorankCount.test_parity` (computation): For c(d) = (1 if d > 0 else 0), HasSignedTwistCorankLaw c π with π_0 = π_1 = 1/2.
- `HasSignedTwistCorankLaw.test_pointwise_not_tight` (non-example): For c(d) = |d|, every proportion N_r(H)/(2H) tends to 0, so c has limiting proportions 0 for every r, which is not a probability vector: pointwise limits do not imply tightness.
- `squareclassTwistCorankCount.test_rational_squarefree` (compatibility): Over F = ℚ with Σ = ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2}, Σ(X) is in bijection with the squarefree d with |d| < X.

**Proof route.**

1. Import c_p(E/F) (request SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2) and the twist E^s (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 5, WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwist; request).
2. Define the counting functions as finite counts: {d : 0 < |d| ≤ H} is finite; Σ(X) is finite by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family (units modulo squares and finiteness of the class group).
3. Define the law predicates as limits (resp. liminf) of the proportions; the densities are the ones of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family specialised to these families.

**Acceptance checks.**

- If c_p(E^d/ℚ) = 0 for all d then the law is the point mass at 0.
- Signed ordering (i) versus squarefree ordering: the non-squarefree d have positive density (1 − 6/π²) in (i) but E^d = E^{d'} for the squarefree part d'; the two orderings are different families and need a comparison.

**Consumers.** Smith I, Theorem 1.2 — the 2^∞-corank law (1/2, 1/2, 0, …) of twists of A/ℚ under Assumption 1.1 in ordering (i); Burungale–Tian, Theorem 3.3 — density-one corank 0 among positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 mod 8; Burungale–Tian, Theorem 3.5; BKLOS Theorem 2.7 — lower density ≥ 1/2 of corank 0 in ordering (ii) over K; ArithmeticStatisticsPartIISmithMethod — states and proves Smith's theorems with this carrier

<a id="st5-smith-twist-family-hypothesis"></a>

### 5.87 Smith's Assumption 1.1 on an elliptic curve over ℚ

An elliptic curve A/ℚ satisfies Smith's Assumption 1.1 if one of the following holds: (1) A(ℚ)[2] = 0; (2) A(ℚ)[2] ≅ ℤ/2 and, for the unique ℚ-isogeny φ : A → A_0 of degree 2, ℚ(A_0[2]) ≠ ℚ and ℚ(A_0[2]) ≠ ℚ(A[2]); (3) A(ℚ)[2] ≅ (ℤ/2)² and A has no cyclic ℚ-isogeny of degree 4. For a model y² = f(x) with f ∈ ℚ[x] monic separable cubic this is equivalent to: (1) f has no rational root; or (2) f has exactly one rational root e and, writing f(x + e) = x(x² + ax + b), neither b nor b(a² − 4b) is a rational square; or (3) f = (x − e_1)(x − e_2)(x − e_3) with e_i ∈ ℚ and none of (e_i − e_j)(e_i − e_k) ({i, j, k} = {1, 2, 3}) is a rational square. The cubic form is the one used in Lean.

**Hypotheses.** A/ℚ given by y² = f(x), f monic separable cubic

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve`; `mathlib:Polynomial.coeff`

**Sources.** [P/smith-selmer-2026](#source-p-smith-selmer-2026), §1.1, Assumption 1.1, p. 3 (arXiv v2). The three cases. [P/kane-2selmer-2013](#source-p-kane-2selmer-2013), §1, p. 1 (arXiv v4). Case (3) in terms of the roots.

**API.**

- `SmithTwistHypothesis` (constructor): The disjunction of the three cubic-root conditions for a monic separable cubic f ∈ ℚ[x].
- `SmithTwistHypothesis.caseThree` (data): Case (3): three rational roots with no (e_i − e_j)(e_i − e_k) a square.
- `smithTwistHypothesis_of_irreducible` (other): If f is irreducible over ℚ (no rational root) then case (1) holds.
- `smithTwistHypothesis_caseThree_iff` (characterisation): For f = (x − e_1)(x − e_2)(x − e_3): case (3) ↔ ¬IsSquare((e_1 − e_2)(e_1 − e_3)) ∧ ¬IsSquare((e_2 − e_1)(e_2 − e_3)) ∧ ¬IsSquare((e_3 − e_1)(e_3 − e_2)).
- `smithTwistHypothesis_twist` (relation): The hypothesis holds for f(x) iff it holds for d³f(x/d) (the twist by d ≠ 0).

**Checks.**

- `SmithTwistHypothesis.test_congruent` (computation): SmithTwistHypothesis (X³ − X) holds by case (3).
- `SmithTwistHypothesis.test_case_three_fails` (non-example): For f = X(X − 1)(X − 4) the product (0 − 1)(0 − 4) = 4 is a square, so case (3) fails and SmithTwistHypothesis f is false (y² = x(x − 1)(x − 4) has a rational cyclic subgroup of order 4).
- `SmithTwistHypothesis.test_irreducible` (degenerate): SmithTwistHypothesis (X³ − 2) holds by case (1).
- `SmithTwistHypothesis.test_case_two_fails` (non-example): For f = X(X² + 4) (a = 0, b = 4 a square) case (2) fails and cases (1), (3) do not apply.

**Proof route.**

1. A(ℚ)[2] \ {O} = {(e, 0) : f(e) = 0, e ∈ ℚ} (2-torsion of a Weierstrass curve; Mathlib WeierstrassCurve points).
2. Case (2): for A : y² = x(x² + ax + b) the 2-isogenous curve is A_0 : y² = x(x² − 2ax + a² − 4b) (Vélu; Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 1), so ℚ(A[2]) = ℚ(√(a² − 4b)) and ℚ(A_0[2]) = ℚ(√b); two quadratic fields coincide iff the product of the radicands is a square.
3. Case (3): a cyclic subgroup of order 4 is ⟨P⟩ with 2P = (e_i, 0) and x(P) = e_i ± √((e_i − e_j)(e_i − e_k)); ⟨P⟩ is Galois-stable iff x(P) ∈ ℚ; so no cyclic ℚ-isogeny of degree 4 iff no (e_i − e_j)(e_i − e_k) is a square (equivalence stated by Kane, §1).

**Acceptance checks.**

- y² = x³ − x satisfies (3) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/congruent-number-curve-satisfies-smith-hypothesis).
- y² = x³ + 4x (Cremona 32a1) has a rational 4-torsion point (2, 4), so it fails (2): b = 4 is a square.

**Consumers.** Smith I, Theorems 1.2 and 1.5 — hypothesis of the 2^∞-Selmer distribution theorem (owned by ArithmeticStatisticsPartIISmithMethod); Burungale–Tian, Theorem 3.3 via Smith [21, Thm. 1.2] — y² = x³ − x satisfies case (3); Kane, §1 — the same case (3) condition for the 2-Selmer distribution

<a id="st5-congruent-number-curve-satisfies-smith-hypothesis"></a>

### 5.88 The congruent number curve satisfies Smith's Assumption 1.1 (case 3)

E : y² = x³ − x satisfies Smith's Assumption 1.1, case (3): E(ℚ)[2] = {O, (0, 0), (1, 0), (−1, 0)} ≅ (ℤ/2)² and E has no cyclic ℚ-isogeny of degree 4.

**Hypotheses.** E : y² = x³ − x over ℚ

**Dependencies.** [Smith's Assumption 1.1 on an elliptic curve over ℚ](#st5-smith-twist-family-hypothesis) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/smith-twist-family-hypothesis`)

**Sources.** [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), §3.2.1, Theorem 3.3, p. 6. Theorem 3.3 applies Smith's theorem to this curve. [P/kane-2selmer-2013](#source-p-kane-2selmer-2013), §1, p. 3 (arXiv v4). Heath-Brown's case y² = x³ − x of the same family condition.

**Proof route.**

1. The roots of x³ − x are 0, 1, −1; the products (e_i − e_j)(e_i − e_k) are (0 − 1)(0 + 1) = −1, (1 − 0)(1 + 1) = 2 and (−1 − 0)(−1 − 1) = 2, none a rational square; apply the cubic criterion of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/smith-twist-family-hypothesis (API smithTwistHypothesis_caseThree_iff).

**Acceptance checks.**

- The twists E^(n) : y² = x³ − n²x have roots 0, ±n and products −n², 2n², 2n², again non-squares.

<a id="st5-smith-selmer-rank-limit-equals-corank"></a>

### 5.89 Smith's ℓ^∞-Selmer corank equals the ℤ_ℓ-corank of Sel_{ℓ^∞}

Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field F and ℓ a prime. For k ≥ 1 let r_{ℓ^k}(E/F) be the largest r such that (ℤ/ℓ^k)^r injects into Sel_{ℓ^k}(E/F)/im(E(F)_tors). Then r_ℓ ≥ r_{ℓ²} ≥ …, the sequence is eventually constant, and its limit r_{ℓ^∞}(E/F) equals corank_{ℤ_ℓ} Sel_{ℓ^∞}(E/F).

**Hypotheses.** E elliptic over a number field F; ℓ prime

**Dependencies.** `SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4

**Sources.** [P/smith-selmer-2026](#source-p-smith-selmer-2026), §1.1, p. 2 (arXiv v2). Definition of r_{ℓ^k} and r_{ℓ^∞}. [P/dokchitser-parity-2013](#source-p-dokchitser-parity-2013), §2, Definition and Remark 2.1, p. 7 (arXiv v2). rk_p = rank + δ_p is the ℚ_p-dimension of the dual Selmer group.

**Proof route.**

1. Kummer: the sequence 0 → E(F)[ℓ^∞]/ℓ^k → Sel_{ℓ^k}(E/F) → Sel_{ℓ^∞}(E/F)[ℓ^k] → 0 is exact (surjectivity of H¹(F, E[ℓ^k]) → H¹(F, E[ℓ^∞])[ℓ^k] with kernel E(F)[ℓ^∞]/ℓ^k, compatible with local conditions; requests Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 7 and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2).
2. The image of E(F)_tors in Sel_{ℓ^k} is the image of E(F)[ℓ^∞]/ℓ^k (the prime-to-ℓ torsion is ℓ^k-divisible), so Sel_{ℓ^k}/im(E(F)_tors) ≅ Sel_{ℓ^∞}[ℓ^k].
3. Sel_{ℓ^∞} ≅ (ℚ_ℓ/ℤ_ℓ)^c ⊕ G with G finite (co-finite type; L2), c the corank; so Sel_{ℓ^∞}[ℓ^k] ≅ (ℤ/ℓ^k)^c ⊕ G[ℓ^k] and the largest free ℤ/ℓ^k-rank is c + #{cyclic factors of G of order ≥ ℓ^k}, which equals c once ℓ^k exceeds the exponent of G.

**Acceptance checks.**

- If Ш(E/F)[ℓ^∞] is finite then r_{ℓ^∞}(E/F) = rank E(F).
- Finite 2-Selmer rank r_2 can exceed the corank: for y² = x³ − x twisted by n = 5 (a congruent number with rank 1) r_2 = 1 = corank, but twists with Ш[2] ≠ 0 have r_2 > r_{2^∞}.

<a id="st5-two-point-corank-law-forces-zero-density-of-high-corank"></a>

### 5.90 A two-point limiting corank law forces density zero for corank at least 2

Let c : ℤ \ {0} → ℤ_{≥0} be any function and suppose that #{0 < |d| ≤ H : c(d) = 0}/(2H) → π_0 and #{0 < |d| ≤ H : c(d) = 1}/(2H) → π_1 with π_0 + π_1 = 1. Then #{0 < |d| ≤ H : c(d) ≥ 2}/(2H) → 0. In particular this holds when E has signed twist-corank law (1/2, 1/2, 0, 0, …), the conclusion of Smith I Theorem 1.2.

**Hypotheses.** c : ℤ \ {0} → ℤ_{≥0}; π_0 + π_1 = 1

**Dependencies.** [Distribution of p^∞-Selmer coranks in a quadratic twist family](#st5-p-infinity-selmer-corank-distribution-in-twist-families) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/p-infinity-selmer-corank-distribution-in-twist-families`)

**Sources.** [P/smith-selmer-2026](#source-p-smith-selmer-2026), §1.1, Theorem 1.2 and Remark 1.3, p. 3 (arXiv v2). The zero-density portion of Theorem 1.2.

**Proof route.**

1. #{0 < |d| ≤ H : c(d) ≥ 2} = 2⌊H⌋ − N_0(H) − N_1(H) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/p-infinity-selmer-corank-distribution-in-twist-families, API sum_signedTwistCorankCount); divide by 2H and take limits. For natural cutoffs the floor is H, as in the Lean API; for real H, ⌊H⌋/H→1 gives the same limit.
2. Note that the convergence of each N_r(H)/(2H) with r ≥ 2 to 0 would not suffice without π_0 + π_1 = 1 (tightness).

**Acceptance checks.**

- For Smith's law: the proportion of |d| ≤ H with corank ≥ 2 tends to 0; Smith's Remark 1.3 gives the rate exp(−c(log log log H)^{1/2}).

<a id="st5-even-congruent-twists-have-corank-zero-given-smith-law"></a>

### 5.91 Burungale–Tian Theorem 3.3 from Smith's 2^∞-Selmer law: corank zero for 100% of even congruent twists

Let E : y² = x³ − x and, for n ∈ ℤ \ {0}, E^(n) : ny² = x³ − x (≅ y² = x³ − n²x, the twist of E by ℚ(√n)). Stated input (Smith I, Theorem 1.2, for A = E, which satisfies Assumption 1.1 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/congruent-number-curve-satisfies-smith-hypothesis): for every r ≥ 0, lim_{H→∞} #{d ∈ ℤ : 0 < |d| ≤ H, r_{2^∞}(E^d/ℚ) = r}/(2H) = 1/2, 1/2, 0 for r = 0, r = 1, r ≥ 2. Conclusion: for a density-one subset of the positive squarefree integers n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8), corank_{ℤ_2} Sel_{2^∞}(E^(n)/ℚ) = 0; that is, with S(X) := {0 < n ≤ X : n squarefree, n mod 8 ∈ {1, 2, 3}}, #{n ∈ S(X) : corank = 0}/#S(X) → 1. ST.5 proves the implication; the stated input is Smith's theorem, whose proof belongs to ArithmeticStatisticsPartIISmithMethod (gap 'Smith's 2^∞-Selmer distribution theorem'), which applies this node to obtain Burungale–Tian's Theorem 3.3 unconditionally.

**Hypotheses.** E : y² = x³ − x over ℚ; Smith's law: the signed-integer 2^∞-Selmer corank law of the twists of E is (1/2, 1/2, 0, …)

**Dependencies.** [The congruent number curve satisfies Smith's Assumption 1.1 (case 3)](#st5-congruent-number-curve-satisfies-smith-hypothesis) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/congruent-number-curve-satisfies-smith-hypothesis`); [Smith's ℓ^∞-Selmer corank equals the ℤ_ℓ-corank of Sel_{ℓ^∞}](#st5-smith-selmer-rank-limit-equals-corank) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/smith-selmer-rank-limit-equals-corank`); [A two-point limiting corank law forces density zero for corank at least 2](#st5-two-point-corank-law-forces-zero-density-of-high-corank) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/two-point-corank-law-forces-zero-density-of-high-corank`); [Distribution of p^∞-Selmer coranks in a quadratic twist family](#st5-p-infinity-selmer-corank-distribution-in-twist-families) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/p-infinity-selmer-corank-distribution-in-twist-families`); `SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4`; [The classes n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8) have relative density 1/2 among positive squarefree integers](#st0-even-parity-classes-have-half-density) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/even-parity-classes-have-half-density`); [The positive squarefree integers ordered by n, and Burungale–Tian's subfamily n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8)](#st0-positive-squarefree-family-over-q) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/positive-squarefree-family-over-q`); [A density-one subset stays of density one in every subfamily of positive lower density](#st0-density-one-restricts-to-subfamilies-of-positive-lower-density) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/density-one-restricts-to-subfamilies-of-positive-lower-density`); [The unweighted squareclass-height family of quadratic twists E^(t), t ∈ F×/F×²](#st0-quadratic-twist-squareclass-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-5-twists-aec-x2-x5; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4

**Sources.** [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), §3.2.1, Theorem 3.3, p. 6. The statement proved here from Smith's law. [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), §1.0.2, footnote 2, p. 2. Root number +1 exactly for n ≡ 1, 2, 3 mod 8, which with 2-parity gives even corank. [P/smith-selmer-2026](#source-p-smith-selmer-2026), §1.1, Theorem 1.2, p. 3 (arXiv v2). The stated input, over all nonzero d with |d| ≤ H. [P/dokchitser-parity-2013](#source-p-dokchitser-parity-2013), §5, Theorem 5.1, p. 27 (arXiv v2). 2-parity for curves with a rational 2-torsion point, one public source for the L4 input.

**Proof route.**

1. Translate Smith's r_{2^∞} into corank_{ℤ_2} Sel_{2^∞} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/smith-selmer-rank-limit-equals-corank) and E^(n) into Smith's A^n (the model y² = x³ − n²x of A^d: y² = x³ + d²ax + d³b with a = −1, b = 0; isomorphism (x, y) ↦ (nx, n²y), Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 5).
2. Zero density of high corank: #{0 < |d| ≤ H : corank_{ℤ_2} Sel_{2^∞}(E^d) ≥ 2} = o(H) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/two-point-corank-law-forces-zero-density-of-high-corank).
3. Parity: for positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8), corank_{ℤ_2} Sel_{2^∞}(E^(n)/ℚ) is even (request SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4: 2-parity (−1)^{corank} = w(E^(n)/ℚ) together with w(E^(n)/ℚ) = +1 exactly for n ≡ 1, 2, 3 mod 8). Hence corank ≠ 0 implies corank ≥ 2 on S.
4. Positive density of S: S has relative density 1/2 in the positive squarefree integers (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/even-parity-classes-have-half-density), hence #S(X) ~ (3/π²)X (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/positive-squarefree-family-over-q).
5. Conclude: #{n ∈ S(X) : corank ≠ 0} ≤ #{0 < |d| ≤ X : corank ≥ 2} = o(X) = o(#S(X)); equivalently, the density-one set of all nonzero d with corank ≤ 1 restricts to relative density one in S (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/density-one-restricts-to-subfamilies-of-positive-lower-density), and on S corank ≤ 1 with even corank means corank 0.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The conclusion concerns 2^∞-Selmer coranks, not finite 2-Selmer ranks: dim Sel_2(E^(n)) − 2 is not 0 for a density-one subset (its law is Poonen–Rains, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/two-selmer-distribution-in-full-two-torsion-twist-families).
- Burungale–Tian Theorem 1.2 (analytic rank 0 for the same density-one set) follows by combining this conclusion with the rank-zero 2-converse; that consumer belongs to CMRankZeroConverse and is not part of ST.5.

<a id="st5-selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny"></a>

### 5.92 Local and global Selmer ratios of an isogeny and the classes T_m(φ)

Let φ : E → E' be an isogeny of elliptic curves over a number field F. For a place v of F put c_v(φ) := #coker(φ : E(F_v) → E'(F_v)) / #ker(φ : E(F_v) → E'(F_v)) ∈ ℚ_{>0} (finite: the kernel is finite and the cokernel is finite since E'(F_v)/φE(F_v) injects into H¹(F_v, E[φ])). The global Selmer ratio is c(φ) := ∏_v c_v(φ), a finite product because c_v(φ) = 1 for all finite v ∤ deg φ at which E has good reduction; c_v is multiplicative under composition of isogenies (index multiplicativity). For s ∈ F^×/F^{×2} let φ_s : E^s → E'^s be the quadratic twist of φ (twisting by the same cocycle, Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 5). For deg φ = 3, c(φ_s) ∈ 3^ℤ and t(φ_s) := ord_3 c(φ_s); for m ∈ ℤ, T_m(φ) := {s ∈ F^×/F^{×2} : c(φ_s) = 3^m} (signed; BKLOS §9 notation), and |T|_m := T_m ∪ T_{−m} is BKLOS §2's T_m.

**Hypotheses.** E, E' elliptic over a number field F; φ : E → E' an F-isogeny

**Dependencies.** [The unweighted squareclass-height family of quadratic twists E^(t), t ∈ F×/F×²](#st0-quadratic-twist-squareclass-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family`); `mathlib:WeierstrassCurve`

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §2, p. 2 (arXiv v2). Local φ-Selmer ratio c_p(φ_s) (displayed just before) and its average over s. [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §2, p. 2 (arXiv v2). The global Selmer ratio. [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §2, p. 4 (arXiv v2). T_m(φ) with |t(φ_s)| = m (§9 uses the signed version).

**API.**

- `localSelmerRatio` (constructor): c_v(φ) = #coker/#ker of φ on F_v-points, as a positive rational.
- `globalSelmerRatio` (data): c(φ) = ∏_v c_v(φ) (finite support).
- `logSelmerRatio` (data): t(φ) = ord_3 c(φ) for a 3-isogeny.
- `selmerRatioClass` (data): T_m(φ) = {s : c(φ_s) = 3^m}.
- `localSelmerRatio_of_good` (simp): If the finite kernel and cokernel have the same cardinality, their ratio is 1. The local Tamagawa formula proves this at good finite places away from deg φ; it does not assert that the map on local points is bijective.
- `localSelmerRatio_complex` (simp): If φ is surjective on points with kernel of order 3 (a 3-isogeny at a complex place) then c(φ) = 1/3.
- `localSelmerRatio_comp` (relation): c(ψ ∘ φ) = c(φ)·c(ψ) for homomorphisms with finite kernels and cokernels (snake lemma); the global identity c(φ)c(φ̂) = 1 is ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula.
- `globalSelmerRatio_twist_local` (characterisation): c(φ_s) depends only on the images of s in F_v^×/F_v^{×2} for v in a finite set S.

**Checks.**

- `localSelmerRatio.test_complex_place` (computation): A homomorphism surjective on points with kernel of order 3 (a 3-isogeny at a complex place) has localSelmerRatio = 1/3.
- `localSelmerRatio.test_real_kernel` (computation): For φ surjective on points (a 3-isogeny over ℝ): c = 1 when the kernel is trivial (E[φ](ℝ) = 0), and c = 1/3 when it has order 3.
- `globalSelmerRatio.test_identity_isogeny` (degenerate): For φ an isomorphism, c_v(φ) = 1 for all v and c(φ) = 1.
- `selmerRatioClass.test_not_selmer_size` (non-example): The Selmer ratio is a quotient of indices, not a group order: it is 1 for the identity of ℤ/3 and 1/3 for the zero map ℤ/3 → 0; so c(φ) is not #Sel_φ, which Cassels' formula relates to c(φ) only through the ratio #Sel_φ/#Sel_φ̂.

**Proof route.**

1. Define c_v(φ) from the local Kummer map (finite groups) and the product over all places; finiteness of the product support from ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers (c_v = 1 at good v ∤ deg φ).
2. Define the twisted isogeny φ_s and the classes T_m(φ) as subsets of the squareclass group (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family).
3. c(φ_s) depends on s only through its images in F_v^×/F_v^{×2} for v in the finite set S = {v | 3∞} ∪ {bad v} ∪ {v | 2}, so T_m(φ) ∩ Σ is defined by finitely many local conditions when Σ is (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined).

**Acceptance checks.**

- For F = ℂ-type places: c_v(φ) = 1/3 at every complex place (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers).
- For the curve 19a3 over ℚ with its 3-isogeny, every s lies in T_0 ∪ T_{±1} (BKLOS §2).

**Consumers.** BKLOS, Theorem 2.1 — the average of #Sel_{φ_s} over Σ is 1 + avg_Σ c(φ_s); BKLOS, §9.2 (Theorem 2.5) — s ∈ T_m forces dim Sel_3(E_s) ≡ m mod 2; BKLOS, §11 (Theorems 11.2, 2.7) — c(φ) = 1 for the CM 3-isogeny, so every s lies in T_0; Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner, Corollary 5.2.3 — positive proportions in local subfamilies meeting T_0 and T_{±1}

<a id="st5-local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers"></a>

### 5.93 Local Selmer ratios via Tamagawa numbers and the formal group (Schaefer)

Let φ : E → E' be an isogeny of elliptic curves over a local field F. (a) If F is a finite extension of ℚ_p, then c(φ) = (c(E')/c(E)) · |φ'(0)|_F^{−1}, where c(·) = #E(F)/E_0(F) is the Tamagawa number and |φ'(0)|_F is the normalised absolute value of the derivative at the origin of the map of formal groups induced by φ on minimal models; in particular c(φ) = c(E')/c(E) if p ∤ deg φ, and c(φ) = 1 if moreover E has good reduction. (b) For deg φ = 3: if F = ℂ then c(φ) = 1/3; if F = ℝ then c(φ) = 1/3 when E[φ](ℝ) ≅ ℤ/3 and c(φ) = 1 when E[φ](ℝ) = 0.

**Hypotheses.** F a local field; φ an isogeny over F; deg φ = 3 in (b)

**Dependencies.** [Local and global Selmer ratios of an isogeny and the classes T_m(φ)](#st5-selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-1-isogenies-the-dual-the-invariant-differential-and-formal-groups-aec-ii2-iii46-iv; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-4-elliptic-curves-over-local-fields--reduction-tates-algorithm-the-tate-curve-aec-vii-ataec-ivv

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §10.2, Proposition 10.2 and Corollary 10.3, p. 15 (arXiv v2), citing Schaefer [34, Lem. 3.8]. Part (a). [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §10.1, Proposition 10.1, p. 14 (arXiv v2). Part (b).

**Proof route.**

1. (a) Filter E(F) ⊇ E_0(F) ⊇ E_1(F) = Ê(𝔪) (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4: reduction, component group; Layer 1: formal groups). The index of φ on each graded piece multiplies: #coker/#ker is multiplicative in short exact sequences of finite-index maps (snake lemma).
2. On E(F)/E_0(F) the ratio is c(E')/c(E) after accounting for E_0/E_1, where φ induces an isogeny of the reduction (finite groups of the same order for an isogeny of connected algebraic groups over a finite field: ratio 1).
3. On Ê(𝔪): for a homomorphism of one-dimensional formal groups with φ'(0) ≠ 0, #coker/#ker on 𝔪-points equals |φ'(0)|^{−1} (compare with the filtration Ê(𝔪^r) ≅ 𝔪^r for r large, where φ acts as multiplication by φ'(0)).
4. (b) Over ℝ or ℂ the identity component of E'(F) is divisible and its component group is a 2-group, so φ(E(F)) = E'(F) when deg φ is odd and c(φ) = 1/#E[φ](F), which is 1/3 over ℂ and 1/3 or 1 over ℝ.

**Acceptance checks.**

- p ≠ 3, good reduction: c(φ) = 1.
- F = ℂ: c(φ) = 1/3 for every 3-isogeny.

<a id="st5-tamagawa-ratio-under-potentially-good-reduction"></a>

### 5.94 Isogenous curves with a quadratic twist of good reduction have equal Tamagawa numbers (BKLOS Lemma 11.1)

Let L be a finite extension of ℚ_p and φ : E → E' a 3-isogeny over L. If some quadratic twist of E has good reduction, then c(E) = c(E'). Consequently, for p ≠ 3, c(φ) = 1 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers).

**Hypotheses.** L/ℚ_p finite; φ a 3-isogeny over L; a quadratic twist of E has good reduction

**Dependencies.** [Local Selmer ratios via Tamagawa numbers and the formal group (Schaefer)](#st5-local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-4-elliptic-curves-over-local-fields--reduction-tates-algorithm-the-tate-curve-aec-vii-ataec-ivv

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §11, Lemma 11.1 and proof, p. 18 (arXiv v2). Statement and the case split p > 3, p = 2, p = 3.

**Proof route.**

1. Reduce to additive potentially good reduction (good reduction is immediate: both Tamagawa numbers are 1).
2. p > 3: E is a ramified quadratic twist of a curve with good reduction, so E has Kodaira type I_0^*; its Tamagawa number is 1 + #{roots in the residue field of the reduced cubic}, determined by the Galois module E[2]; a 3-isogeny induces E[2] ≅ E'[2] and E' is the twist of the corresponding good-reduction isogenous curve, so c(E) = c(E') (Tate's algorithm, Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4; BKLOS derive the same from their Theorem 6.2).
3. p = 2: c(E')/c(E) equals the ratio of norm indices [E'(L) : N E'(M)]/[E(L) : N E(M)] for the quadratic extension M trivialising the twist (Dokchitser–Dokchitser, 'Local invariants of isogenous elliptic curves', Lemma 4.6), a power of 2; c(E')/c(E) is a power of 3, because φ and φ̂ induce maps between the component groups E(L)/E_0(L) and E'(L)/E'_0(L) whose composites are multiplication by 3, so the kernel and cokernel of the induced map are 3-groups; hence the ratio is 1.
4. p = 3: the analogous argument with Dokchitser–Dokchitser Lemma 4.7. The two Dokchitser–Dokchitser lemmas are the gap 'Local invariants of isogenous elliptic curves at 2 and 3'.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Good reduction: c(E) = c(E') = 1.
- For p > 3 and type I_0^*, c(E) ∈ {1, 2, 4}.

<a id="st5-selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined"></a>

### 5.95 The classes T_m(φ) are cut out by finitely many local conditions

Let φ : E → E' be a 3-isogeny over a number field F and Σ ⊆ F^×/F^{×2} a set defined by finitely many local conditions. Then for every m ∈ ℤ, Σ ∩ T_m(φ) is a finite disjoint union of families defined by finitely many local conditions; T_m(φ) is empty for all but finitely many m; and each Σ ∩ T_m(φ) has a density in the squareclass ordering, which is positive when the set is nonempty.

**Hypotheses.** F number field; φ a 3-isogeny over F; Σ defined by finitely many local conditions

**Dependencies.** [Local and global Selmer ratios of an isogeny and the classes T_m(φ)](#st5-selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny`); [Isogenous curves with a quadratic twist of good reduction have equal Tamagawa numbers (BKLOS Lemma 11.1)](#st5-tamagawa-ratio-under-potentially-good-reduction) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/tamagawa-ratio-under-potentially-good-reduction`); [Local Selmer ratios via Tamagawa numbers and the formal group (Schaefer)](#st5-local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers`); [Families defined by local conditions, local densities and largeness](#st0-family-defined-by-local-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions`); [The unweighted squareclass-height family of quadratic twists E^(t), t ∈ F×/F×²](#st0-quadratic-twist-squareclass-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §9.1, proof of Theorem 2.4, p. 14 (arXiv v2). T_m is empty or cut out by finitely many local conditions. [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §2, p. 2 (arXiv v2). Sets defined by (finitely many) local conditions.

**Proof route.**

1. Let S be the finite set of places dividing 3·∞, the places of bad reduction of E and the places above 2. For v ∉ S, E^s has either good reduction (v(s) even) or is a ramified quadratic twist of a good-reduction curve (v(s) odd), and in both cases c_v(φ_s) = 1 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/tamagawa-ratio-under-potentially-good-reduction with ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers).
2. For v ∈ S, c_v(φ_s) depends only on the class of s in F_v^×/F_v^{×2}, a finite set; so c(φ_s) = ∏_{v∈S} c_v(φ_s) takes finitely many values and each level set is a finite union of sets defined by local conditions at S.
3. Decompose the finite set of allowed local squareclass tuples into single tuples. Each nonempty rectangle has a positive density by the number-field squareclass counting input used in BKLOS §8; sum the finitely many disjoint densities. A level set of the product of local ratios need not itself be a rectangle, and its density is a sum of products, not one product. ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions supplies only the definition; the required arithmetic equidistribution remains part of the BKLOS number-field counting gap.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Over ℚ with φ the 3-isogeny of 19a3 (conductor 19): S = {2, 3, 19, ∞}.

<a id="st5-bklos-average-size-of-three-isogeny-selmer-groups"></a>

### 5.96 BKLOS: the average size of 3-isogeny Selmer groups in quadratic twist families

Let φ : E → E' be a 3-isogeny of elliptic curves over a number field F and Σ ⊆ F^×/F^{×2} a nonempty set defined by finitely many local conditions. When the twists E^s, s ∈ Σ, are ordered by the height H(s) = ∏_{v_𝔭(s) odd} N𝔭, the average of #Sel_{φ_s}(E^s) exists and equals 1 + avg_Σ c(φ_s), where avg_Σ c(φ_s) := lim_{X→∞} (1/#Σ(X)) Σ_{s∈Σ(X)} c(φ_s) = ∏_{v | 3 f_E ∞} avg_{Σ_v} c_v(φ_s), a rational number. (BKLOS prove this for 3-isogenies of abelian varieties; the elliptic case is the one planned here, Sel_φ being the Selmer group of the Selmer structure of Kummer images on E[φ], Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 7.)

**Hypotheses.** φ : E → E' a 3-isogeny over F; Σ nonempty, defined by finitely many local conditions

**Dependencies.** [Local and global Selmer ratios of an isogeny and the classes T_m(φ)](#st5-selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny`); [The classes T_m(φ) are cut out by finitely many local conditions](#st5-selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined`); [Higher height moments in an arithmetic family](#st5-height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family`); [The unweighted squareclass-height family of quadratic twists E^(t), t ∈ F×/F×²](#st0-quadratic-twist-squareclass-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family`); [Families defined by local conditions, local densities and largeness](#st0-family-defined-by-local-conditions) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions`); [Binary cubic forms, their discriminant and the twisted GL2-action](#st1-binary-cubic-forms-and-the-twisted-action) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/binary-cubic-forms-and-the-twisted-action`); [Layer 1](#layer-1) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1`; required refinement); [Number-field three-isogeny orbit-count input](#st2-refinement-number-field-twist-orbit-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/refinement-number-field-twist-orbit-count`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §2, Theorem 2.1, p. 3 (arXiv v2). Statement. [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §8, proof of Theorem 8.1, p. 13 (arXiv v2). The counting input from BSW.

**Proof route.**

1. Parametrisation (BKLOS §§3–7): φ-coverings, in particular φ-Selmer elements, of E^s correspond to SL_2(F)-orbits of binary cubic forms with discriminant in a fixed class related to s; locally soluble orbits have integral representatives, and their discriminants are squarefree away from a fixed finite set of primes (Theorems 4.2, 5.3, 6.2, Proposition 6.1, Corollary 7.1). This is an orbit parametrisation over a Dedekind domain in the scope of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1.
2. Counting (BKLOS §8): count irreducible locally φ-soluble SL_2(O_F)-orbits of bounded height with discriminant in κ·Σ, by the general geometry-of-numbers theorem over number fields of Bhargava–Shankar–Wang [BKLOS ref. 7, Thm. 13] and the uniformity estimate [ref. 8, Thm. 17]; this is the ST.2 counting machinery over a number field.
3. Mass computation: the Tamagawa number τ(SL_2) = 1 and the local masses give avg_Σ c(φ_s); add the identity element.
4. These steps are not decomposed here (gap 'BKLOS binary-cubic parametrisation and counting over number fields').

**Acceptance checks.**

- For the CM 3-isogeny of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cm-three-isogeny-has-selmer-ratio-one, the average of #Sel_{φ_s} is 2.
- Unlike the Bhargava–Shankar averages over all curves, the answer depends on the family Σ through the local averages at v | 3 f_E ∞.

<a id="st5-cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula"></a>

### 5.97 Cassels' formula relating φ- and φ̂-Selmer groups to the Selmer ratio

Let φ : E → E' be an isogeny of elliptic curves over a number field F with dual φ̂. Then #Sel_φ(E)/#Sel_φ̂(E') = c(φ) · #E(F)[φ]/#E'(F)[φ̂]; in particular c(φ)·c(φ̂) = 1.

**Hypotheses.** φ an F-isogeny of elliptic curves over a number field F

**Dependencies.** [Local and global Selmer ratios of an isogeny and the classes T_m(φ)](#st5-selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny`); `SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1`; `ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §9.1, equation (9.2), p. 14 (arXiv v2), citing Cassels 1965. Cassels' formula and c(φ)c(φ̂) = 1. [P/dokchitser-parity-2013](#source-p-dokchitser-parity-2013), §2.2, p. 11 (arXiv v2). The same formula of Cassels (Birch, Fisher) in the parity literature.

**Proof route.**

1. Local conditions: the images of the local Kummer maps E'(F_v)/φE(F_v) ↪ H¹(F_v, E[φ]) and E(F_v)/φ̂E'(F_v) ↪ H¹(F_v, E'[φ̂]) are exact annihilators under local Tate duality for the Weil pairing E[φ] × E'[φ̂] → μ_{deg φ} (request SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1 for the annihilator property of these Kummer conditions; local duality from ClassFieldTheory via L1).
2. Greenberg–Wiles/Poitou–Tate Euler characteristic formula for dual Selmer structures on finite modules (request ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4): #Sel/#Sel^* = (#H⁰(F, E[φ])/#H⁰(F, E'[φ̂])) ∏_v #L_v/#H⁰(F_v, E[φ]).
3. #L_v/#H⁰(F_v, E[φ]) = #coker(φ_v)/#ker(φ_v) = c_v(φ) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny); take the product.
4. c(φ)c(φ̂) = 1: apply the formula to φ and to φ̂ (whose dual is φ) and multiply.

**Acceptance checks.**

- φ = [n] on E (not of prime degree) recovers no information: both sides are 1.
- For a 3-isogeny with c(φ) = 1 and trivial torsion, #Sel_φ(E) = #Sel_φ̂(E').

<a id="st5-isogeny-factorisation-selmer-exact-sequence"></a>

### 5.98 The Selmer exact sequence of a composite isogeny

Let φ_1 : A_1 → A_2 and φ_2 : A_2 → A_3 be isogenies of elliptic curves over a number field F and ψ = φ_2 ∘ φ_1. There is an exact sequence 0 → A_2(F)[φ_2]/φ_1(A_1(F)[ψ]) → Sel_{φ_1}(A_1) → Sel_ψ(A_1) → Sel_{φ_2}(A_2) → Ш(A_2)[φ_2]/φ_1(Ш(A_1)[ψ]) → 0. For a 3-isogeny φ : E → E' with ψ = φ̂ ∘ φ = [3] this gives dim_{𝔽_3} Sel_3(E) ≤ dim Sel_φ(E) + dim Sel_φ̂(E').

**Hypotheses.** φ_1, φ_2 isogenies over F

**Dependencies.** [Local and global Selmer ratios of an isogeny and the classes T_m(φ)](#st5-selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §9, Lemma 9.1 and (9.1), p. 13 (arXiv v2). The exact sequence. [P/bhargava-isogeny-2016](#source-p-bhargava-isogeny-2016), §8.1, Proposition 42(i) and (22), p. 21 (arXiv v1), citing Schaefer–Stoll. The inequality r_3 ≤ r_φ + r_φ̂.

**Proof route.**

1. The short exact sequence of Galois modules 0 → A_1[φ_1] → A_1[ψ] → A_2[φ_2] → 0 gives a long exact cohomology sequence compatible with the Kummer sequences of φ_1, ψ, φ_2 globally and locally (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 7, Selmer structures).
2. Diagram chase with the local conditions (the images of local points) gives exactness at the Selmer terms and identifies the kernel and cokernel with the displayed torsion and Ш quotients (Schaefer–Stoll, Corollary 1).
3. The inequality: exactness at Sel_ψ(A_1) bounds its dimension by the dimensions of its neighbours.

**Acceptance checks.**

- φ_1 = φ_2 = id: all terms vanish except Sel_id = 0.
- For [3] = φ̂φ and E(F)[3] = 0: dim Sel_3(E) ≤ dim Sel_φ(E) + dim Sel_φ̂(E').

<a id="st5-three-isogeny-selmer-parity"></a>

### 5.99 Parity of the 3-Selmer rank from the Selmer ratio (Cassels; BES Proposition 42(ii))

Let φ : E → E' be a 3-isogeny of elliptic curves over a number field F with c(φ) = 3^m. Then dim_{𝔽_3} Sel_3(E) − dim_{𝔽_3} E(F)[3] ≡ m (mod 2).

**Hypotheses.** φ a 3-isogeny over a number field F; c(φ) = 3^m

**Dependencies.** [The Selmer exact sequence of a composite isogeny](#st5-isogeny-factorisation-selmer-exact-sequence) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/isogeny-factorisation-selmer-exact-sequence`); [Cassels' formula relating φ- and φ̂-Selmer groups to the Selmer ratio](#st5-cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-isogeny-2016](#source-p-bhargava-isogeny-2016), §8.1, Proposition 42(ii) and proof, p. 21 (arXiv v1). Parity via the Cassels–Tate pairing. [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §9.2, p. 14 (arXiv v2). BKLOS use it over number fields.

**Proof route.**

1. Apply ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/isogeny-factorisation-selmer-exact-sequence to [3] = φ̂ ∘ φ: dim Sel_3(E) = dim Sel_φ(E) + dim Sel_φ̂(E') − dim(E'(F)[φ̂]/φ(E(F)[3])) − dim(Ш(E')[φ̂]/φ(Ш(E)[3])).
2. The last group has even 𝔽_3-dimension: φ is adjoint for the Cassels–Tate pairing, which induces a nondegenerate alternating pairing on Ш(E')[φ̂]/φ(Ш(E)[3]) (gap 'Cassels–Tate pairing and its isogeny adjointness'; no atlas owner).
3. By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula, dim Sel_φ(E) − dim Sel_φ̂(E') = m + dim E(F)[φ] − dim E'(F)[φ̂].
4. Combine and reduce modulo 2 using dim E(F)[3] = dim E(F)[φ] + dim(E'(F)[φ̂] ∩ φ(E(F)[3])) (routine torsion bookkeeping).

**Acceptance checks.**

- m = 0 and E(F)[3] = 0: dim Sel_3(E) is even.

<a id="st5-finitely-many-twists-with-rational-p-torsion"></a>

### 5.100 Only finitely many quadratic twists have rational odd p-torsion

Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field F and p an odd prime. Then {s ∈ F^×/F^{×2} : E^s(F)[p] ≠ 0} has at most p² − 1 elements; in particular it has density zero in the squareclass ordering.

**Hypotheses.** p odd prime

**Dependencies.** [Higher height moments in an arithmetic family](#st5-height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family`); [The unweighted squareclass-height family of quadratic twists E^(t), t ∈ F×/F×²](#st0-quadratic-twist-squareclass-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-5-twists-aec-x2-x5

**Sources.** [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), §3.2.2, Theorem 3.5, p. 7. The corank statement is about all squareclasses; torsion exceptions must be removed before counting Selmer ranks.

**Proof route.**

1. E^s(F)[p] ≅ {P ∈ E(F̄)[p] : σP = χ_s(σ)P for all σ} with χ_s the quadratic character of F(√s)/F (twist of E by −1 along χ_s, Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 5).
2. A nonzero P determines χ_s: if σP = χ(σ)P = χ'(σ)P then χ(σ) = χ'(σ) because P ≠ 0 and ±1 are distinct mod p (p odd).
3. So distinct squareclasses with nonzero p-torsion use disjoint sets of nonzero points of E[p], giving at most p² − 1 classes; a finite set has density zero (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family, test familyUpperDensity.test_finite_set).

**Acceptance checks.**

- p = 3 and E with E(F)[3] ≠ 0: s = 1 is one of the at most 8 exceptional classes.

<a id="st5-reduced-p-selmer-rank-bounds-the-corank"></a>

### 5.101 The p-Selmer rank modulo torsion bounds the p^∞-Selmer corank

For an elliptic curve E over a number field F and a prime p: corank_{ℤ_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/F) ≤ dim_{𝔽_p} Sel_p(E/F) − dim_{𝔽_p} E(F)[p]. In particular, if dim Sel_p(E/F) = dim E(F)[p] then corank_{ℤ_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/F) = 0.

**Hypotheses.** E elliptic over a number field F; p prime

**Dependencies.** [Smith's ℓ^∞-Selmer corank equals the ℤ_ℓ-corank of Sel_{ℓ^∞}](#st5-smith-selmer-rank-limit-equals-corank) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/smith-selmer-rank-limit-equals-corank`); `SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-modeling-2015](#source-p-bhargava-modeling-2015), §5.5, Proposition 5.9, p. 19. Sel_{p^e} versus Sel_{p^∞}[p^e]. [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), §1.0.1, p. 1. The p^∞-Selmer group and its corank.

**Proof route.**

1. Kummer sequence at level p: 0 → E(F)[p^∞]/p → Sel_p(E/F) → Sel_{p^∞}(E/F)[p] → 0 (as in ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/smith-selmer-rank-limit-equals-corank, with k = 1).
2. dim_{𝔽_p} E(F)[p^∞]/p = dim E(F)[p] (a finite abelian p-group A has #A/pA = #A[p]).
3. Sel_{p^∞} ≅ (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^c ⊕ G gives dim Sel_{p^∞}[p] = c + dim G[p] ≥ c.

**Acceptance checks.**

- E with E(F)[p] = 0 and Sel_p(E/F) = 0: corank 0.
- The inequality can be strict when Ш[p^∞] has nontrivial finite part.

<a id="st5-three-selmer-rank-zero-in-selmer-ratio-one-twists"></a>

### 5.102 At least half of the twists with Selmer ratio one have 3-Selmer rank zero (BKLOS Theorem 2.5(a), Selmer form)

Let φ : E → E' be a 3-isogeny over a number field F and Σ ⊆ F^×/F^{×2} a set defined by finitely many local conditions with Σ ∩ T_0(φ) ≠ ∅. Put r_3(E^s) := dim_{𝔽_3} Sel_3(E^s) − dim_{𝔽_3} E^s(F)[3]. Then liminf_{X→∞} #{s ∈ Σ(X) ∩ T_0(φ) : r_3(E^s) = 0}/#(Σ(X) ∩ T_0(φ)) ≥ 1/2; hence the lower density of {s ∈ Σ : r_3(E^s) = 0} within Σ is at least (1/2)μ(Σ ∩ T_0)/μ(Σ). BKLOS state the conclusion for Mordell–Weil rank 0; their proof gives this 3-Selmer statement, which implies it.

**Hypotheses.** φ a 3-isogeny over F; Σ defined by finitely many local conditions; Σ ∩ T_0(φ) ≠ ∅

**Dependencies.** [The classes T_m(φ) are cut out by finitely many local conditions](#st5-selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined`); [BKLOS: the average size of 3-isogeny Selmer groups in quadratic twist families](#st5-bklos-average-size-of-three-isogeny-selmer-groups) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/bklos-average-size-of-three-isogeny-selmer-groups`); [Cassels' formula relating φ- and φ̂-Selmer groups to the Selmer ratio](#st5-cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula`); [The Selmer exact sequence of a composite isogeny](#st5-isogeny-factorisation-selmer-exact-sequence) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/isogeny-factorisation-selmer-exact-sequence`); [Parity of the 3-Selmer rank from the Selmer ratio (Cassels; BES Proposition 42(ii))](#st5-three-isogeny-selmer-parity) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/three-isogeny-selmer-parity`); [Higher height moments in an arithmetic family](#st5-height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §2, Theorem 2.5, p. 4 (arXiv v2). Statement (Mordell–Weil form). [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §9.2, proof of Theorem 2.5, p. 14 (arXiv v2). The average of the 3-Selmer rank over T_0 is at most 1.

**Proof route.**

1. Σ' := Σ ∩ T_0(φ) is a finite disjoint union of nonempty rectangles of local squareclasses, each with positive density (selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined).
2. Averages: by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/bklos-average-size-of-three-isogeny-selmer-groups for φ and for φ̂ on Σ', and c(φ_s) = c(φ̂_s) = 1 on T_0 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula), the averages of #Sel_{φ_s} and #Sel_{φ̂_s} over Σ' are both 2. Apply the cited average theorem to each rectangle and combine using their limiting relative densities; this extends it to Σ′.
3. Convexity: k ≤ (3^k − 1)/2 for integers k ≥ 0, so the upper averages of dim Sel_{φ_s} and dim Sel_{φ̂_s} are at most 1/2 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family, monotonicity and subadditivity).
4. dim Sel_3(E^s) ≤ dim Sel_{φ_s} + dim Sel_{φ̂_s} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/isogeny-factorisation-selmer-exact-sequence), so the upper average of r_3 over Σ' is at most 1; r_3 ≥ 0 because E^s(F)[3^∞]/3 injects by Kummer and has the same F₃-dimension as E^s(F)[3].
5. Parity: r_3(E^s) is even for s ∈ T_0 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/three-isogeny-selmer-parity).
6. If P_X is the proportion of s ∈ Σ'(X) with r_3 = 0, the average of r_3 over Σ'(X) is at least 2(1 − P_X); taking limsup, 1 ≥ 2(1 − liminf P_X).

**Acceptance checks.**

- If Σ ⊆ T_0 then at least half of Σ has r_3 = 0.
- The bound 1/2 is attained by the model in which r_3 ∈ {0, 2} with probability 1/2 each.

<a id="st5-three-selmer-rank-one-in-odd-selmer-ratio-twists"></a>

### 5.103 At least five sixths of the twists with |t| = 1 have 3-Selmer rank one (BKLOS Theorem 2.5(b))

Let φ : E → E' be a 3-isogeny over F and Σ a set defined by finitely many local conditions with Σ ∩ (T_1(φ) ∪ T_{−1}(φ)) ≠ ∅. Then liminf_{X→∞} of the proportion of s ∈ Σ(X) ∩ (T_1 ∪ T_{−1}) with r_3(E^s) = 1 is at least 5/6.

**Hypotheses.** φ a 3-isogeny over F; Σ defined by finitely many local conditions; Σ ∩ (T_1 ∪ T_{−1}) ≠ ∅

**Dependencies.** [The classes T_m(φ) are cut out by finitely many local conditions](#st5-selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined`); [BKLOS: the average size of 3-isogeny Selmer groups in quadratic twist families](#st5-bklos-average-size-of-three-isogeny-selmer-groups) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/bklos-average-size-of-three-isogeny-selmer-groups`); [Cassels' formula relating φ- and φ̂-Selmer groups to the Selmer ratio](#st5-cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula`); [The Selmer exact sequence of a composite isogeny](#st5-isogeny-factorisation-selmer-exact-sequence) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/isogeny-factorisation-selmer-exact-sequence`); [Parity of the 3-Selmer rank from the Selmer ratio (Cassels; BES Proposition 42(ii))](#st5-three-isogeny-selmer-parity) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/three-isogeny-selmer-parity`); [Higher height moments in an arithmetic family](#st5-height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/height-moments-in-an-arithmetic-family`)

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §9.2, p. 14 (arXiv v2). Odd 3-Selmer rank on T_{±1}, average 4/3, 5/6.

**Proof route.**

1. On Σ ∩ T_1 the averages of #Sel_φ and #Sel_φ̂ are 4 and 4/3 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/bklos-average-size-of-three-isogeny-selmer-groups, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cassels-isogeny-selmer-ratio-formula); on T_{−1} the roles are exchanged. Decompose each nonempty intersection into finitely many disjoint local-squareclass rectangles and combine their averages using the positive density weights.
2. Convexity 2k + 1 − 2m ≤ 3^{k−m}: the upper averages of dim Sel_φ and dim Sel_φ̂ are at most 1/2 + 4/6 and −1/2 + 2/3, so the upper average of r_3 is at most 4/3. For T₁ use m=1 for the φ-dimension and m=0 for the dual dimension; reverse these choices on T₋₁. Combine the two strata by their limiting relative densities. The inequality holds for every integer k−m, including negative values.
3. Parity: r_3 is odd on T_{±1} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/three-isogeny-selmer-parity), so r_3 ∈ {1, 3, 5, …} and 2·Prob(r_3 ≥ 3) ≤ 4/3 − 1; hence Prob(r_3 = 1) ≥ 5/6 in the liminf sense.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For 19a3 over ℚ, half the squareclasses lie in T_{±1}, giving at least 41.6% of twists with 3-Selmer rank 1 (BKLOS §2).

<a id="st5-positive-proportions-of-three-selmer-ranks-in-local-subfamilies"></a>

### 5.104 Positive proportions of 3-Selmer ranks zero and one in local subfamilies of twists

Let E/F have a 3-isogeny φ and let nonempty Σ ⊆ F^×/F^{×2} be defined by finitely many local conditions. Then, in the squareclass ordering, the lower density within Σ of {s : r_3(E^s) = 0} is at least (1/2)μ(Σ ∩ T_0(φ))/μ(Σ), and that of {s : r_3(E^s) = 1} is at least (5/6)μ(Σ ∩ (T_1 ∪ T_{−1}))/μ(Σ). In particular, if Σ meets both T_0(φ) and T_1(φ) ∪ T_{−1}(φ), positive proportions of the twists in Σ have 3-Selmer rank 0 and 1. This is the input used by Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner (Corollary 5.2.3) for F = ℚ and a local condition at 3; it is not BKLOS Theorem 2.6 itself.

**Hypotheses.** E/F with a 3-isogeny φ; Σ is nonempty and defined by finitely many local conditions; its density μ(Σ) is therefore positive.

**Dependencies.** [At least half of the twists with Selmer ratio one have 3-Selmer rank zero (BKLOS Theorem 2.5(a), Selmer form)](#st5-three-selmer-rank-zero-in-selmer-ratio-one-twists) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/three-selmer-rank-zero-in-selmer-ratio-one-twists`); [At least five sixths of the twists with |t| = 1 have 3-Selmer rank one (BKLOS Theorem 2.5(b))](#st5-three-selmer-rank-one-in-odd-selmer-ratio-twists) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/three-selmer-rank-one-in-odd-selmer-ratio-twists`); [The classes T_m(φ) are cut out by finitely many local conditions](#st5-selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined`); [Only finitely many quadratic twists have rational odd p-torsion](#st5-finitely-many-twists-with-rational-p-torsion) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/finitely-many-twists-with-rational-p-torsion`)

**Sources.** [P/castella-anticyclotomic-2022](#source-p-castella-anticyclotomic-2022), §5.2, Corollary 5.2.3 and proof, p. 32 (arXiv v2). The consumer of the local-subfamily version. [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §2, Theorem 2.5, p. 4 (arXiv v2). The proportions ½μ(T_0) and (5/6)μ(T_1).

**Proof route.**

1. Apply ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/three-selmer-rank-zero-in-selmer-ratio-one-twists and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/three-selmer-rank-one-in-odd-selmer-ratio-twists to Σ ∩ T_0 and Σ ∩ (T_1 ∪ T_{−1}); these have densities (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-classes-are-locally-defined), positive when nonempty.
2. Remove the finitely many s with E^s(F)[3] ≠ 0 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/finitely-many-twists-with-rational-p-torsion), so the torsion correction in r_3 changes only finitely many s and no lower density.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For F = ℚ and 19a3 with Σ all squareclasses: at least 25% have r_3 = 0 and at least 41.6% have r_3 = 1.

<a id="st5-cm-curves-have-a-twist-with-good-reduction"></a>

### 5.105 A CM elliptic curve with maximal endomorphism order has a twist with good reduction at each finite place

Let E/F be an elliptic curve over a number field with End_F(E)=O_K for an imaginary quadratic field K⊆F. At each finite place v there is a twist of E by an O_K^×-valued character having good reduction; for j(E)∉{0,1728} the twist is quadratic. This is the maximal-order setting of Rubin Corollary 5.22, fixed at the start of §5.1; it is the case needed by cm-three-isogeny-has-selmer-ratio-one.

**Hypotheses.** E/F has End_F(E)=O_K, with all CM endomorphisms defined over F and K⊆F.

**Dependencies.** `ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.1`; `ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.3`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-4-elliptic-curves-over-local-fields--reduction-tates-algorithm-the-tate-curve-aec-vii-ataec-ivv; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-5-twists-aec-x2-x5; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-7-the-absolute-local-artin-map-its-normalizations-and-conductors

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §11, proof of Theorem 11.2, p. 18 (arXiv v2), citing Rubin [32, 5.22]. The input and its use. [P/rubin-cm-1999](#source-p-rubin-cm-1999), §5.1 p.16; Theorem 5.15 pp.19–20; Corollary 5.22 pp.21–22. The maximal-order scope and Hecke-character proof of the good-reduction twist.

**Proof route.**

1. Use the Hecke character ψ_E of Rubin Theorem 5.15, supplied by the main theorem of CM (CM.1). On local units U_v, part (i) places ψ_E(U_v) in O_K^×; part (ii) identifies it with the inertia action on prime-to-v Tate modules. This conclusion requires the Hecke-character theorem: finite order in (K⊗Q_ℓ)^× alone does not imply membership in K.
2. For the local assertion, extend ψ_E|U_v to F_v^× by assigning 1 to a uniformizer. Local class field theory gives an O_K^×-valued Galois character χ with that inertia restriction. Twist by χ⁻¹: inertia acts trivially, so Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich gives good reduction. Rubin Corollary 5.22 constructs even a global twist using the corresponding character-extension statement.
3. If j is neither 0 nor 1728, Aut(E)=O_K^×={±1}, so this twist is quadratic. The non-maximal-order case of the final corank theorem uses the separate isogeny to maximal order, not this lemma.
4. The public SWC copy of Rubin was read in this review: §3.2 Proposition 3.14, §5.1 Proposition 5.3 and §§5.1–5.2 through Corollary 5.22. The CM and character-theory inputs remain requested formal prerequisites.

**Acceptance checks.**

- j(E) ∉ {0, 1728}: a quadratic twist has good reduction at v.
- E : y² = x³ + 1 (j = 0, CM by ℤ[ζ_3]) over ℚ(ζ_3): a sextic twist may be needed at v | 2 or 3.

<a id="st5-cm-three-isogeny-has-selmer-ratio-one"></a>

### 5.106 BKLOS: a 3-isogeny between curves with CM by the maximal order has Selmer ratio one

Let φ : E → E' be a 3-isogeny of elliptic curves over a number field F with End_F(E) ≅ End_F(E') ≅ O_K for an imaginary quadratic field K (all CM endomorphisms are defined over F, hence K ⊆ F). Then c(φ) = 1.

**Hypotheses.** φ a 3-isogeny over F; End_F(E)≅End_F(E′)≅O_K; the hypothesis is not merely geometric CM.

**Dependencies.** [A CM elliptic curve with maximal endomorphism order has a twist with good reduction at each finite place](#st5-cm-curves-have-a-twist-with-good-reduction) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cm-curves-have-a-twist-with-good-reduction`); [Isogenous curves with a quadratic twist of good reduction have equal Tamagawa numbers (BKLOS Lemma 11.1)](#st5-tamagawa-ratio-under-potentially-good-reduction) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/tamagawa-ratio-under-potentially-good-reduction`); [Local Selmer ratios via Tamagawa numbers and the formal group (Schaefer)](#st5-local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers`); [Local and global Selmer ratios of an isogeny and the classes T_m(φ)](#st5-selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/selmer-ratio-of-an-isogeny`); `ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.1`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-1-isogenies-the-dual-the-invariant-differential-and-formal-groups-aec-ii2-iii46-iv

**Sources.** [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §11, Theorem 11.2, p. 18 (arXiv v2). Statement. [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §11, proof of Theorem 11.2, p. 19 (arXiv v2). The computation at the places above 3. [P/rubin-cm-1999](#source-p-rubin-cm-1999), Proposition 3.14, p.11. Action on invariant differentials identifies the formal-group derivative.

**Proof route.**

1. Every finite v: c_v(E) = c_v(E') — by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cm-curves-have-a-twist-with-good-reduction some twist of E has good reduction at v; if it is quadratic, apply ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/tamagawa-ratio-under-potentially-good-reduction; otherwise j(E) ∈ {0, 1728}: j = 1728 is impossible here: a 3-isogeny preserving the maximal CM order would give an ideal of norm 3 in ℤ[i], whereas 3 is inert, and for j = 0 also j(E') = 0, and its O_K-stable degree-3 kernel is the unique ideal kernel E[(√−3)]; quotienting by this kernel identifies E′ with E over F, with φ corresponding to √−3 up to automorphism. Consequently, for v∤3, c_v(φ) = 1 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/local-selmer-ratio-via-tamagawa-numbers.
2. Infinite places are complex (K ⊆ F): c_v(φ) = 1/3 at each of the [F : ℚ]/2 complex places.
3. Places above 3: c_v(φ) = |φ'(0)|_v^{−1} (Tamagawa numbers equal by the first step). Choose a prime ℓ ≠ 3 and an ℓ-isogeny λ : E' → E (exists since End(E') ≅ O_K and ideal classes have prime representatives; ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.1); λ ∘ φ = a ∈ O_K, |λ'(0)|_v = 1, and |a'(0)|_v = |a|_v (the normalised action of O_K on the invariant differential, CM.1; Rubin Prop. 3.14). So ∏_{v|3} c_v(φ) = ∏_{v|3} |a|_v^{−1} = (3-part of N_{K/ℚ}(a))^{[F:K]} = 3^{[F:K]}, because deg a = N(a) = 3ℓ.
4. Product: c(φ) = 3^{[F:K]} · 3^{−[F:ℚ]/2} = 1.

**Acceptance checks.**

- K = ℚ(√−3), E : y² = x³ + 1 over F = K, φ = √−3: c(φ) = 1.
- Non-maximal orders can give c(φ) ≠ 1 (BKLOS Remark 11.3).

<a id="st5-cm-twists-have-corank-zero-at-least-half"></a>

### 5.107 At least half of the quadratic twists of a CM curve have 3^∞-Selmer corank zero (Burungale–Tian Theorem 3.5)

Let K be an imaginary quadratic field in which 3 is not inert, and E/K an elliptic curve with CM by an order O of K. Then, ordering t ∈ K^×/K^{×2} by H(t) = ∏_{v_𝔭(t) odd} N𝔭 (each squareclass once), liminf_{X→∞} #{t : H(t) < X, corank_{ℤ_3} Sel_{3^∞}(E^t/K) = 0}/#{t : H(t) < X} ≥ 1/2. This is BKLOS Theorem 2.7 for F = K in its Selmer form (BKLOS state the Mordell–Weil consequence; the Selmer statement is what their proof gives). No finiteness of Ш is assumed.

**Hypotheses.** K imaginary quadratic, 3 split or ramified in K; E/K with End_K(E) an order O ⊆ O_K

**Dependencies.** [BKLOS: a 3-isogeny between curves with CM by the maximal order has Selmer ratio one](#st5-cm-three-isogeny-has-selmer-ratio-one) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cm-three-isogeny-has-selmer-ratio-one`); [At least half of the twists with Selmer ratio one have 3-Selmer rank zero (BKLOS Theorem 2.5(a), Selmer form)](#st5-three-selmer-rank-zero-in-selmer-ratio-one-twists) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/three-selmer-rank-zero-in-selmer-ratio-one-twists`); [The p-Selmer rank modulo torsion bounds the p^∞-Selmer corank](#st5-reduced-p-selmer-rank-bounds-the-corank) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/reduced-p-selmer-rank-bounds-the-corank`); [Only finitely many quadratic twists have rational odd p-torsion](#st5-finitely-many-twists-with-rational-p-torsion) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/finitely-many-twists-with-rational-p-torsion`); [Distribution of p^∞-Selmer coranks in a quadratic twist family](#st5-p-infinity-selmer-corank-distribution-in-twist-families) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/p-infinity-selmer-corank-distribution-in-twist-families`); `ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.1`; `SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2`; [The unweighted squareclass-height family of quadratic twists E^(t), t ∈ F×/F×²](#st0-quadratic-twist-squareclass-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/quadratic-twist-squareclass-family`)

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-1-isogenies-the-dual-the-invariant-differential-and-formal-groups-aec-ii2-iii46-iv; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-5-twists-aec-x2-x5; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-7-selmer-groups-and-sha-aec-x4

**Sources.** [P/burungale-converse-2026](#source-p-burungale-converse-2026), §3.2.2, Theorem 3.5, p. 7. Statement. [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §11, proof of Theorem 2.7, p. 19 (arXiv v2). The maximal-order case. [P/bhargava-3isogeny-2019](#source-p-bhargava-3isogeny-2019), §11, proof of Theorem 2.7, p. 19 (arXiv v2). The non-maximal case via an isogeny. [P/rubin-cm-1999](#source-p-rubin-cm-1999), Proposition 5.3 and proof, p.15. The ideal-kernel construction gives a curve isogenous over F with maximal endomorphism order; the proof correctly writes End_F(E′), correcting the displayed statement’s missing prime.

**Proof route.**

1.
