**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), §8.6, p.774 (Annals 183). The datum, generation; nonsplitting is cited from Lemma 3.2. [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), §8.6, p.774 (Annals 183). Property (v).

**API.**

- `inversionAction` (data): The homomorphism Z/2 → Aut(A) sending the generator to a ↦ −a.
- `generalizedDihedral` (constructor): G_A := A ⋊ Z/2 with the inversion action.
- `outsideInvolutions` (data): c_A := {x ∈ G_A : image of x in Z/2 is nontrivial}.
- `mem_outsideInvolutions_iff` (characterisation): For |A| odd: x ∈ c_A ⇔ orderOf x = 2.
- `outsideInvolutions_isConj` (characterisation): For |A| odd, any two elements of c_A are conjugate in G_A.
- `closure_outsideInvolutions` (structure): The subgroup generated by c_A is all of G_A.
- `center_generalizedDihedral` (structure): For |A| odd and A ≠ 0 the centre of G_A is trivial.
- `outsideInvolutions_nonsplitting` (other): For |A| odd and H ≤ G_A, c_A ∩ H is empty or a single H-conjugacy class.

**Checks.**

- `generalizedDihedral.test_card_Z3` (computation): For A = Z/3 the group G_A has 6 elements.
- `generalizedDihedral.test_trivial_center` (degenerate): For A = 0 the centre of G_A is the whole group (G_A is not centre-free).
- `generalizedDihedral.test_even_order_nonexample` (non-example): For A = Z/2 the two elements of c_A are not conjugate (G_A is abelian).
- `generalizedDihedral.test_involution_order` (characterisation): For A = Z/5 every element of c_A has order 2.

**Proof route.**

1. Construct the inversion action Z/2 → Aut(A) and the semidirect product (Mathlib SemidirectProduct); c_A is the preimage of the nontrivial element under rightHom.
2. (i) (aτ)² = a·τaτ^{−1} = a − a = 0, while an element a ≠ 0 of A has odd order; so involutions are exactly c_A.
3. (ii) b(aτ)b^{−1} = (a + 2b)τ and 2 is invertible on A, so A acts transitively on c_A; invertible powers of an involution are itself.
4. (iii) (aτ)(0τ) = a, so ⟨c_A⟩ contains A and τ.
5. (iv) a central element commutes with τ, forcing 2a = 0 hence a = 0 on the A-part, and aτ is not central when A ≠ 0.
6. (v) For H ≤ G_A meeting c_A, H = (H ∩ A) ⋊ ⟨a₀τ⟩ and c_A ∩ H = {(h + a₀)τ : h ∈ H ∩ A} = one (H ∩ A)-orbit by (ii) applied to the odd group H ∩ A. This is the instance of EVW Lemma 3.2 used in §8.6; the general odd-index lemma belongs to the Hurwitz homological-stability roadmap.

**Acceptance checks.**

- A = Z/3: G_A ≅ S_3 and c_A is the class of transpositions.
- A = 0: G_A = Z/2 is not centre-free.
- A = Z/2 (even order): c_A = {τ, aτ} consists of two central involutions of the Klein group, so (ii) and (iv) fail.

**Consumers.** EVW §8.6–8.8 (ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections) — G_A-covers with inertia in c_A are unramified A-covers of quadratic extensions ramified at ∞; EVW Theorem 6.1/Proposition 7.8 (stated input, gap) — (G_A, c_A) satisfies the nonsplitting and centre-free hypotheses of the uniform Betti bound

<a id="st5-class-group-surjection-pair"></a>

### 5.137 Pairs (L, α) of a quadratic extension and a class-group surjection

Let q be odd, n odd, L ∈ S_n with ring O_L (integral closure of F_q[t] in L), and A a finite abelian group. A pair (L, α) consists of L and a surjective homomorphism α : Cl(O_L) → A. Two pairs (L, α), (L', α') are isomorphic if there is a K-isomorphism φ : L → L' with α' ∘ φ_* = α. The nontrivial automorphism σ of L/K acts on Cl(O_L) by −1, so (L, α) ≅ (L, β) iff β = ±α. The moment m_A(L) := |Sur(Cl(O_L), A)| counts pairs with fixed L before identification.

**Hypotheses.** q odd; n odd; A finite abelian (in the application an ℓ-group, ℓ odd)

**Dependencies.** [The quadratic families S_n over F_q(t)](#st5-odd-degree-quadratic-function-field-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/odd-degree-quadratic-function-field-family`); [The number of surjective homomorphisms between abelian groups](#st5-surjection-count) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/surjection-count`); `mathlib:ClassGroup`; `mathlib:integralClosure`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proposition 8.7, p.775 (Annals 183). The isomorphism notion. [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proposition 8.7, p.775 (Annals 183). The sign identification.

**API.**

- `quadraticRingOfIntegers` (data): O_L as the integral closure of F_q[t] in L_f.
- `quadraticClassGroup` (data): Cl(O_L), a finite abelian group.
- `ClassGroupSurjectionPair` (constructor): Surjective homomorphisms Cl(O_L) → A, as a subtype.
- `ClassGroupSurjectionPair.neg` (structure): The involution α ↦ −α, induced by σ.
- `ClassGroupSurjectionPair.neg_ne_self` (characterisation): For A ≠ 0 of odd order, −α ≠ α.
- `classGroupMoment` (projection): m_A(L) = |Sur(Cl(O_L), A)| (zero if y² − f is reducible, which does not occur for odd n).
- `classGroupMoment_trivial` (simp): m_0(L) = 1.

**Checks.**

- `classGroupMoment.test_trivial` (degenerate): For the trivial group A, m_A(L_f) = 1 for every squarefree f of odd degree.
- `ClassGroupSurjectionPair.test_zero_not_surjective` (non-example): For A = Z/3 the zero homomorphism Cl(O_L) → A is not a pair.
- `ClassGroupSurjectionPair.test_neg_involutive` (characterisation): neg (neg α) = α.
- `classGroupMoment.test_even` (computation): For A = Z/3 and f squarefree of odd degree, m_A(L_f) is even.

**Proof route.**

1. Define the class group of O_L (Mathlib ClassGroup of the integral closure), the set of surjections and the involution α ↦ −α.
2. σ acts by −1 on Cl(O_L): for a fractional ideal I, I·σ(I) is the extension of the norm ideal from F_q[t], a principal ideal domain, hence principal.
3. For |A| odd and A ≠ 0, −α ≠ α for every surjection α (else 2α = 0, forcing α = 0), so the sign action on Sur(Cl(O_L), A) is free.

**Acceptance checks.**

- A = 0: m_A(L) = 1 for every L (the unique map is surjective).
- For A ≠ 0 of odd order, m_A(L) is even.

**Consumers.** EVW Proposition 8.7 (ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections) — points of the Hurwitz scheme are isomorphism classes of pairs; EVW Theorem 8.8 (ST.5/factor-two-point-count-identity) — Σ_L m_A(L) = 2|X_n(F_q)| by freeness of the sign action

<a id="st5-involution-quotient-of-the-unramified-pro-l-group"></a>

### 5.138 The σ-anti-invariant quotient of the unramified pro-ℓ group is the ℓ-part of the class group

Let q be odd, ℓ an odd prime not dividing q, n odd and L ∈ S_n with nontrivial automorphism σ over K = F_q(t). Let J_L be the Galois group of the maximal abelian everywhere unramified pro-ℓ extension of L, and J'_L := J_L/(1 + σ)J_L its largest quotient on which σ acts by −1. Class field theory gives an exact sequence 0 → Cl(O_L)_ℓ → J_L → Ẑ_ℓ → 0 on which σ acts trivially on Ẑ_ℓ and by −1 on Cl(O_L)_ℓ, and the snake lemma yields a canonical isomorphism J'_L ≅ Cl(O_L)_ℓ. Here Cl(O_L)_ℓ is the ℓ-primary part, and Cl(O_L) ≅ Pic⁰(C_L)(F_q) because C_L has a unique point over ∞.

**Hypotheses.** q odd, ℓ odd prime, ℓ ∤ q; n odd (so ∞ is ramified and has a unique, rational point above it)

**Dependencies.** [Pairs (L, α) of a quadratic extension and a class-group surjection](#st5-class-group-surjection-pair) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair`); `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4`; `mathlib:CommGroup.primaryComponent`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Proposition 8.7, p.775 (Annals 183). The CFT exact sequence. [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Proposition 8.7, p.776 (Annals 183). The isomorphism (8.7.3).

**Proof route.**

1. Import from the function-field class field theory owner (FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4): the unramified abelian pro-ℓ quotient sits in 0 → Pic⁰(C_L)(F_q)_ℓ → J_L → Ẑ_ℓ → 0 with the degree map to Gal(F̄_q/F_q)_ℓ.
2. Identify Pic⁰(C_L)(F_q) with Cl(O_L) via I ↦ D_I − deg(D_I)·∞ (unique rational point ∞ over ∞ of P¹).
3. σ acts by −1 on Cl(O_L) (ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair) and trivially on the constant-field quotient.
4. Apply the snake lemma to multiplication by 1 + σ on the sequence; since ℓ is odd, (1 + σ) is invertible on Ẑ_ℓ (acts by 2) and zero on Cl(O_L)_ℓ, giving J_L/(1+σ)J_L ≅ Cl(O_L)_ℓ/(1+σ)Cl(O_L)_ℓ = Cl(O_L)_ℓ.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Surjections onto an ℓ-group A factor through the ℓ-primary part, so Sur(Cl(O_L), A) = Sur(J'_L, A).
- For ℓ = 2 the quotient J_L/(1 + σ)J_L is not the 2-part of the class group (2 is not invertible).

<a id="st5-hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections"></a>

### 5.139 F_q-points of the dihedral Hurwitz scheme classify class-group surjections up to sign

Let q be odd, ℓ an odd prime with ℓ ∤ q, A a nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group, (G_A, c_A) the generalized dihedral datum and X_n = Hn^{c_A}_{G_A,n} ⊗ F_q, n odd. There is a bijection between X_n(F_q) and the set of isomorphism classes of pairs (L, α) with L ∈ S_n and α : Cl(O_L) → A surjective. Given (L, α), compose α with J'_L ≅ Cl(O_L)_ℓ, extend to Gal(F_L/K) = J'_L ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ → G_A (unique up to A-conjugacy), and take the fixed field F_α: a tame G_A-cover of P¹ over F_q, geometrically connected, branched exactly where L/K is (the n roots of f and ∞, since F_α/L is unramified), a point of Hn^{c_A}_{G_A,n}: n branch points in A¹ with inertia generated by elements of c_A, plus ramification at ∞; conversely a tame G_A-cover with inertia in c_A branched at n points of A¹ has X/A → P¹ ramified at ∞ (odd number of finite branch points) and X → X/A étale, giving (L, α) by class field theory.

**Hypotheses.** q odd; ℓ odd prime, ℓ ∤ q; A nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group; n odd; G_A centre-free, so F_q-points of the Hurwitz scheme are covers defined over F_q (not only Galois-stable geometric classes)

**Dependencies.** [The generalized dihedral group A ⋊ Z/2 and its involution class](#st5-generalized-dihedral-cover-datum) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/generalized-dihedral-cover-datum`); [Pairs (L, α) of a quadratic extension and a class-group surjection](#st5-class-group-surjection-pair) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair`); [The σ-anti-invariant quotient of the unramified pro-ℓ group is the ℓ-part of the class group](#st5-involution-quotient-of-the-unramified-pro-l-group) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/involution-quotient-of-the-unramified-pro-l-group`); `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5`; `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proposition 8.7, p.774–775 (Annals 183). Statement of Proposition 8.7. [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Proposition 8.7, p.776 (Annals 183). The inverse construction.

**Proof route.**

1. Import the Hurwitz scheme Hn^c_{G,n}, finite étale over Conf_n over Z[1/|G|], and, for centre-free G and any field k of characteristic prime to |G|, the bijection between Hn^c_{G,n}(k) and isomorphism classes of tame G-covers of P¹_k branched at n points of A¹ with finite inertia in c (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5; EVW §§7.1, 7.3; PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 items /63–/65).
2. Forward map: by ST.5/involution-quotient-of-the-unramified-pro-l-group and the splitting (8.7.1) of 1 → J'_L → Gal(F_L/K) → Z/2 → 1 (ℓ odd), α gives g_α : Gal(F_L/K) → G_A, well defined up to A-conjugacy since all involutions of G_A are A-conjugate (ST.5/generalized-dihedral-cover-datum (ii)).
3. Ramification: F_α/L is unramified, so the branch points are those of L/K; each inertia group maps onto an order-2 subgroup generated by an element of c_A; F_q is algebraically closed in F_α. Indeed the constant-field quotient of G_A is cyclic, hence factors through G_A^ab=C₂. The quadratic subfield L is geometric because it ramifies at infinity, so this quotient is trivial.
4. Inverse: for a tame G_A-cover X → P¹ with inertia in c_A branched at n points of A¹, X → X/A is étale over A¹ (local computation: inertia meets A trivially); X/A → P¹ has an odd number of finite branch points, hence is ramified at ∞, where the inertia is cyclic of order 2 mapping onto Z/2, so X → X/A is étale everywhere; class field theory (FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4) turns the étale A-cover into α.
5. Check the two constructions are mutually inverse on isomorphism classes, using that (L, α) ≅ (L, β) iff β = ±α (ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair).

**Acceptance checks.**

- A = Z/3: the points of X_n(F_q) are S_3-covers whose quadratic resolvent is in S_n.
- The bijection is with isomorphism classes of pairs, i.e. with pairs modulo α ~ −α; the marked count is twice the point count (ST.5/factor-two-point-count-identity).

<a id="st5-factor-two-point-count-identity"></a>

### 5.140 The moment sum is twice the number of Hurwitz points

In the setting of ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections (q odd, ℓ odd, ℓ ∤ q, A a nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group, n odd): Σ_{L ∈ S_n} m_A(L) = 2|X_n(F_q)|. For A = 0 the average of m_A over S_n is exactly 1.

**Hypotheses.** as in ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections

**Dependencies.** [F_q-points of the dihedral Hurwitz scheme classify class-group surjections up to sign](#st5-hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections`); [Pairs (L, α) of a quadratic extension and a class-group surjection](#st5-class-group-surjection-pair) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair`); [Size of the odd-degree quadratic family](#st5-size-of-the-odd-degree-quadratic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/size-of-the-odd-degree-quadratic-family`)

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.778 (Annals 183). The factor-two identity.

**Proof route.**

1. Σ_{L ∈ S_n} m_A(L) counts pairs (L, α) with α surjective, L running over S_n (each field once).
2. Isomorphism classes of pairs with fixed L are the orbits of α ↦ −α; for A ≠ 0 of odd order this action is free (ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair), so every class has exactly 2 elements.
3. Distinct L ∈ S_n are non-isomorphic over K, so the classes over different L are distinct; apply the bijection of ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections.

**Acceptance checks.**

- A = 0 is excluded from the factor 2: m_0 ≡ 1 and the sign action is trivial.
- Dividing by |S_n| = 2(q^n − q^{n−1}) (n ≥ 3) turns the identity into average m_A = |X_n(F_q)|/(q^n − q^{n−1}).

<a id="st5-empirical-l-primary-class-group-law"></a>

### 5.141 The empirical law of ℓ-primary class groups in S_n

Let q be odd, ℓ prime and n odd. The empirical law ν_n = ν_{q,ℓ,n} is the probability measure on the set of isomorphism classes of finite abelian ℓ-groups with ν_n(A) := #{L ∈ S_n : Cl(O_L)_ℓ ≅ A}/|S_n|, where Cl(O_L)_ℓ is the ℓ-primary part of the (finite) class group. Its A-moment Σ_B ν_n(B)|Sur(B, A)| equals the average of m_A(L) = |Sur(Cl(O_L), A)| over S_n, because surjections onto an ℓ-group factor through the ℓ-primary part.

**Hypotheses.** q odd, ℓ prime, n odd; classes of finite abelian ℓ-groups as in ST.5/isomorphism-classes-of-finite-abelian-p-groups

**Dependencies.** [The quadratic families S_n over F_q(t)](#st5-odd-degree-quadratic-function-field-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/odd-degree-quadratic-function-field-family`); [Pairs (L, α) of a quadratic extension and a class-group surjection](#st5-class-group-surjection-pair) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair`); [Isomorphism classes of finite abelian p-groups, indexed by partitions](#st5-isomorphism-classes-of-finite-abelian-p-groups) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/isomorphism-classes-of-finite-abelian-p-groups`); [Surjection moments of a measure on finite abelian p-groups](#st5-surjection-moment) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/surjection-moment`); `mathlib:CommGroup.primaryComponent`; `mathlib:ClassGroup`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Deduction of Theorem 1.2 after Theorem 8.8, p.777 (Annals 183). Definition of ν_n (corrected to the ℓ-primary part). [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Theorem 8.8 context, p.777 (Annals 183). The moment m_A.

**API.**

- `classGroupPrimaryIso` (characterisation): The proposition Cl(O_{L_f})_ℓ ≅ A (ℓ-primary component of the class group, additive form, isomorphic to the standard representative of A).
- `empiricalClassGroupLaw` (constructor): ν_n(A) = #{f ∈ P_n : Cl(O_{L_f})_ℓ ≅ A}/|P_n|.
- `empiricalClassGroupLaw_nonneg` (other): 0 ≤ ν_n(A) ≤ 1.
- `hasSum_empiricalClassGroupLaw` (structure): Σ_A ν_n(A) = 1 (q odd, n odd).
- `empiricalClassGroupLaw_eq_average` (compatibility): The A-moment of ν_n (ST.5/surjection-moment) is the average of m_A over P_n, equivalently over S_n.

**Checks.**

- `empiricalClassGroupLaw.test_degree_one` (degenerate): For n = 1, ν_1 is the Dirac mass at the trivial class: ν_1(trivial) = 1.
- `empiricalClassGroupLaw.test_mass_le_one` (characterisation): For every A, ν_n(A) ≤ 1.
- `empiricalClassGroupLaw.test_primary_not_whole` (non-example): classGroupPrimaryIso asks for the ℓ-primary part: a field with class group Z/2 × Z/3 counts toward A = Z/3 when ℓ = 3, although its class group is not a 3-group.

**Proof route.**

1. Class groups Cl(O_L) are finite (function-field class number finiteness, via Pic⁰(C_L)(F_q) finite); their ℓ-primary parts are finite abelian ℓ-groups, each isomorphic to exactly one class.
2. Define ν_n(A) as the proportion; computing it over polynomials P_n instead of S_n gives the same value since every class of S_n has (q − 1)/2 representatives.
3. Total mass one: the events Cl(O_L)_ℓ ≅ A partition S_n.
4. Moment identity: Sur(Cl(O_L), A) = Sur(Cl(O_L)_ℓ, A) for A an ℓ-group (restriction to the primary part is a bijection, the prime-to-ℓ part mapping to 0).

**Acceptance checks.**

- ν_1 is the Dirac mass at the trivial group (genus 0: Cl(O_L) = 0).
- Using the whole class group Cl(O_L) ≅ A instead of the ℓ-part does not define a probability measure on ℓ-groups (EVW p.777 prints Cl(O_L) ≃ A; sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E666).

**Consumers.** EVW deduction of Theorem 1.2 from Proposition 8.3 and Theorem 8.8 (ST.5/large-q-cohen-lenstra-theorem) — the moments of ν_n are controlled by Theorem 8.8 and fed into finite moment control; EVW §1 (ST.5/positive-proportions-of-l-divisible-and-indivisible-class-numbers) — ν_n(0) is the proportion with class number prime to ℓ

<a id="st5-lower-and-upper-degree-densities"></a>

### 5.142 Upper and lower densities along odd degrees

For a real sequence u : ℕ → ℝ, its upper (lower) odd-degree density is limsup (liminf) of u(n) as n → ∞ through odd n. For q odd, ℓ prime and A a finite abelian ℓ-group, δ^+(q, A) and δ^−(q, A) are the upper and lower odd-degree densities of n ↦ ν_{q,ℓ,n}(A). For fixed q they need not coincide; the degree limit n → ∞ is taken before q → ∞.

**Hypotheses.** u bounded (for ν_n(A) ∈ [0, 1] automatically)

**Dependencies.** [The empirical law of ℓ-primary class groups in S_n](#st5-empirical-l-primary-class-group-law) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/empirical-l-primary-class-group-law`); `mathlib:Filter.limsup`; `mathlib:Filter.atTop`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Theorem 1.2, p.730 (Annals 183). The densities δ^±. [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), After Theorem 8.8, p.777 (Annals 183). Why only upper and lower densities are used.

**API.**

- `upperOddDensity` (constructor): limsup_{m→∞} u(2m + 1).
- `lowerOddDensity` (constructor): liminf_{m→∞} u(2m + 1).
- `lowerOddDensity_le_upperOddDensity` (relation): For bounded u, lower ≤ upper.
- `oddDensities_eq_of_tendsto` (characterisation): If u(2m + 1) → c then both densities equal c.
- `upperClassGroupDensity` (data): δ^+(q, A) := upper odd density of n ↦ ν_{q,ℓ,n}(A).
- `lowerClassGroupDensity` (data): δ^−(q, A) := lower odd density of n ↦ ν_{q,ℓ,n}(A).

**Checks.**

- `upperOddDensity.test_const` (degenerate): For u ≡ c, upperOddDensity u = c and lowerOddDensity u = c.
- `upperOddDensity.test_alternating` (non-example): For u(n) = (−1)^{(n−1)/2} (on odd n), upperOddDensity u = 1 and lowerOddDensity u = −1, so the densities differ.
- `upperOddDensity.test_even_ignored` (characterisation): Changing u on even n does not change upperOddDensity u.

**Proof route.**

1. Define δ^± via Mathlib Filter.limsup (and its order dual liminf) of u(2m + 1) along m → ∞.
2. For bounded u, δ^− ≤ δ^+, with equality iff u converges along odd n, in which case both equal the limit.

**Acceptance checks.**

- For u constant, δ^+ = δ^− = that constant.
- For u(n) = (−1)^{(n−1)/2}, δ^+ = 1 and δ^− = −1 along odd n.

**Consumers.** EVW Theorem 1.2 (ST.5/large-q-cohen-lenstra-theorem) — the limit q → ∞ is taken of δ^±(q, A), not of a single-degree proportion; EVW Remark 7.9 — equality δ^+ = δ^− would need Frobenius-equivariant stabilization, which is not proved

<a id="st5-top-cohomology-counts-rational-components"></a>

### 5.143 Top compactly supported cohomology counts Frobenius-fixed components

Let X be a smooth separated scheme of finite type and pure dimension n over F_q, and λ a prime not dividing q. Then H^{2n}_c(X_{F̄_q}, Q_λ) ≅ Q_λ(−n)^{π₀(X_{F̄_q})}, the permutation representation on geometric connected components twisted by Q_λ(−n); hence Tr(Frob_q | H^{2n}_c(X_{F̄_q}, Q_λ)) = q^n · #{geometric components fixed by Frobenius}. In particular the trace is q^n exactly when one geometric component is defined over F_q.

**Hypotheses.** X smooth, separated, finite type, pure dimension n over F_q; λ ∤ q

**Dependencies.** `EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2`; `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.778–779 (Annals 183). Top-degree trace versus rational components. [P/liu-unramified-2024](#source-p-liu-unramified-2024), Proof of Theorem 1.4, p.40 (arXiv v2). The general form used by LWZB.

**Proof route.**

1. Decompose X_{F̄_q} into its connected components, which are smooth irreducible of dimension n and permuted by Frobenius.
2. For each geometrically connected smooth component C, Poincaré duality (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2) gives H^{2n}_c(C, Q_λ) ≅ H^0(C, Q_λ)^∨(−n) = Q_λ(−n).
3. Frobenius permutes the summands; only fixed components contribute to the trace, each contributing q^n (geometric Frobenius acts on Q_λ(−n) by q^n).

**Acceptance checks.**

- X = A^n: trace q^n.
- X = two conjugate copies of A^n over F_{q²} viewed over F_q (non-split): no fixed component, trace 0.

<a id="st5-uniform-trace-error-estimate"></a>

### 5.144 Uniform point-count error from a geometric Betti bound

Let X be a smooth separated finite-type F_q-scheme of pure dimension n, λ ∤ q a prime, and C ≥ 1 a real number with dim H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_λ) ≤ C^{i+1} for all i ≥ 1. If exactly one geometric connected component of X is fixed by Frobenius and √q > C, then |q^{−n}|X(F_q)| − 1| ≤ Σ_{i ≥ 1} C^{i+1} q^{−i/2} = C²/(√q − C). The numerical core: for reals t_j (0 ≤ j < 2n) with |t_j| ≤ q^{j/2} C^{2n−j+1}, |q^{−n} Σ_{j<2n} (−1)^j t_j| ≤ C²/(√q − C).

**Hypotheses.** X is smooth, separated and of finite type over F_q, of pure dimension n.; Betti bound dim H^i ≤ C^{i+1} for i ≥ 1; exactly one Frobenius-fixed geometric component; √q > C ≥ 1

**Dependencies.** [Top compactly supported cohomology counts Frobenius-fixed components](#st5-top-cohomology-counts-rational-components) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/top-cohomology-counts-rational-components`); `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`; `EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2`; `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.778 (Annals 183). Weight bound and the resulting geometric-series estimate (8.8.3).

**Proof route.**

1. Grothendieck–Lefschetz: |X(F_q)| = Σ_j (−1)^j Tr(Frob | H^j_c(X_{F̄_q}, Q_λ)) (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2).
2. The j = 2n term is q^n (ST.5/top-cohomology-counts-rational-components).
3. Deligne's weight bound (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7): every Frobenius eigenvalue on H^j_c has absolute value ≤ q^{j/2}; with Poincaré duality dim H^j_c = dim H^{2n−j} (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2), |Tr(Frob | H^j_c)| ≤ q^{j/2} C^{2n−j+1}.
4. Sum the finite range j < 2n first, then bound by the geometric series Σ_{i≥1} (C/√q)^i · C = C²/(√q − C) (put i = 2n − j).

**Acceptance checks.**

- C = 1, q = 16: the bound is 1/3.
- Only finitely many j occur; the infinite series is used only as an upper bound after the finite sum.

<a id="st5-hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system"></a>

### 5.145 The ℓ^k-torsion local system of the odd-degree hyperelliptic family

Let k be a field with 2ℓ invertible (ℓ an odd prime), n = 2g + 1 odd, and over Conf_n ⊗ k (monic squarefree degree-n polynomials f) let C_f be the smooth projective curve birational to y² = f(x), of genus g, with its unique point at ∞. For each m ≥ 1 the ℓ^m-torsion V_m := Jac(C_f)[ℓ^m] forms a locally constant étale sheaf of free Z/ℓ^m-modules of rank 2g on Conf_n ⊗ k, the Tate module T = lim V_m is a lisse Z_ℓ-sheaf of rank 2g, and the Weil pairing (from the canonical principal polarization) is a perfect alternating pairing V_m × V_m → μ_{ℓ^m}. Consequently geometric monodromy lies in Sp(V_m) and, over k = F_q, a Frobenius element acts in GSp_q(V_m) (similitude multiplier q).

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd prime, 2ℓ invertible on the base; n = 2g + 1 ≥ 3 odd; g = (n − 1)/2; k arbitrary (F_q or the function field of Conf_n); Frobenius on torsion points and Tate modules means arithmetic Frobenius, with cyclotomic multiplier q. The trace formula on compactly supported cohomology uses geometric Frobenius; these representations and conventions are not interchanged.

**Dependencies.** [The quadratic families S_n over F_q(t)](#st5-odd-degree-quadratic-function-field-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/odd-degree-quadratic-function-field-family`); `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-d-the-relative-picard-functor-and-the-jacobian-scheme

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.779 (Annals 183). The torsion local system and its rank. [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.780 (Annals 183). Frobenius multiplier q.

**Proof route.**

1. The Jacobian of the relative smooth proper curve y² = f(x) over Conf_n ⊗ k (completed at the unique point over ∞) is an abelian scheme of relative dimension g (tauceti JacobianChallenge Layer D: Pic⁰ and the Jacobian).
2. [ℓ^m] is finite étale of degree ℓ^{2mg} when ℓ is invertible, so V_m is a locally constant sheaf, free over Z/ℓ^m of rank 2g (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3).
3. The canonical principal polarization induces the Weil pairing V_m × V_m → μ_{ℓ^m}, perfect and alternating (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3); monodromy preserves it up to the cyclotomic character, which is trivial on the geometric fundamental group and equals q on Frobenius over F_q.

**Acceptance checks.**

- n = 1: g = 0 and V_m = 0.
- n = 3: V_m has rank 2 (elliptic curves y² = f(x) with the point at ∞).
- The Frobenius multiplier is q, not 1: over F_q the monodromy image is in GSp, not Sp.

<a id="st5-geometric-generic-fibre-of-the-unmarked-hurwitz-cover"></a>

### 5.146 The geometric generic fibre of X_n → Conf_n is Sur(V, A) modulo sign

Let ℓ be odd, A a nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group, m ≥ 1 with ℓ^m A = 0, and n = 2g + 1 odd. Over the function field K of Conf_n ⊗ F_q (or any field of characteristic prime to 2ℓ), the geometric generic fibre Σ of the finite étale cover X_n = Hn^{c_A}_{G_A,n} → Conf_n is identified, Gal(K̄/K)-equivariantly, with Sur(V_m, A)/{±1}, where V_m = Jac(C)[ℓ^m](K̄) with its monodromy action. The marked set Sur(V_m, A) has twice as many elements, and since −I ∈ Sp(V_m), the Sp(V_m)-orbit sets of Sur(V_m, A) and of Sur(V_m, A)/{±1} correspond bijectively.

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd prime; A ≠ 0 a finite abelian ℓ-group with ℓ^m A = 0; n odd; characteristic prime to 2ℓ

**Dependencies.** [F_q-points of the dihedral Hurwitz scheme classify class-group surjections up to sign](#st5-hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections`); [The ℓ^k-torsion local system of the odd-degree hyperelliptic family](#st5-hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system`); [Pairs (L, α) of a quadratic extension and a class-group surjection](#st5-class-group-surjection-pair) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair`); `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5`; `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.779 (Annals 183). The printed identification, corrected to the quotient by ±1.

**Proof route.**

1. Repeat ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections over K̄, replacing class field theory by geometric Kummer theory: étale abelian A-covers of the curve C over K̄ correspond to surjections Jac(C)[ℓ^m](K̄) → A (FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4, geometric form).
2. Pairs (C, α) and (C, −α) give isomorphic G_A-covers (the hyperelliptic involution acts by −1), so the fibre of the unmarked cover is Sur(V_m, A)/{±1}, not Sur(V_m, A) (EVW print Sur(V, A): sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E662).
3. Equivariance: the identification is canonical, hence commutes with Gal(K̄/K).
4. −I ∈ Sp(V_m) acts as the sign, so each Sp-orbit on Sur(V_m, A) is a union of sign classes; orbit sets correspond.

**Acceptance checks.**

- V = F_3², A = F_3: 8 surjections, 4 sign classes.
- The component count is unchanged by the correction; only the fibre description changes.

<a id="st5-hyperelliptic-boundary-degeneration"></a>

### 5.147 Degeneration of labelled hyperelliptic moduli to the boundary Δ_{1,1}

Let k be algebraically closed with 2ℓ invertible, g ≥ 3. The moduli space H̃_g of labelled hyperelliptic (Z/2-)curves of genus g degenerates to the boundary stratum Δ_{1,1}: there are clutching maps κ_L : H̃_{g−1} × H̃_1 → H̃_g^ct, κ_R : H̃_1 × H̃_{g−1} → H̃_g^ct and κ : H̃_1 × H̃_{g−2} × H̃_1 → H̃_g^ct factoring through both, whose images meet the closure of H̃_g. Along a clutching map the ℓ-torsion of Pic⁰ splits: κ^*Pic⁰(C_γ)[ℓ] ≅ Pic⁰(C_{γ1})[ℓ] × Pic⁰(C_{γ2})[ℓ] as symplectic local systems, and the monodromy group of the image contains the product of the factors' monodromy groups. Here H̃_g^ct is the compact-type locus of the compactification; the clutching images lie on its boundary, in the closure of the smooth locus H̃_g. They do not map into the smooth locus itself.

**Hypotheses.** k algebraically closed, 2ℓ invertible; g ≥ 3 (class vector (1, …, 1) of length 2g + 2 split as (1,1,1,1), (1,…,1) of length 2g − 2, (1,1,1,1))

**Dependencies.** [The ℓ^k-torsion local system of the odd-degree hyperelliptic family](#st5-hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system`); `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1`

**Upstream contracts.** tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-d-the-relative-picard-functor-and-the-jacobian-scheme

**Sources.** [P/achter-monodromy-2007](#source-p-achter-monodromy-2007), Lemma 2.5, p.7 (Achter–Pries author PDF). The degeneration. [P/achter-monodromy-2007](#source-p-achter-monodromy-2007), Lemma 3.1(a), p.11 (Achter–Pries author PDF). The splitting along clutching.

**Proof route.**

1. Achter–Pries Lemma 2.5: the class vector of H̃_g splits into γ1 = γ3 = (1,1,1,1) and γ2 of length 2g − 2, giving the Δ_{1,1} degeneration.
2. Achter–Pries Lemma 3.1(a): for a stable curve C = C1 ∪ C2 meeting in one section, restriction gives Pic⁰(C) ≅ Pic⁰(C1) × Pic⁰(C2) on stalks, hence an isomorphism of ℓ-torsion sheaves. The dual graph is a tree, so the nodal curve is of compact type and Pic⁰ is an abelian scheme; the displayed product is not a statement about a smooth glued curve.
3. Achter–Pries Lemma 3.1(b): the Galois cover trivialising the product local system has group H1 × H2, so the monodromy of the image of κ is the product.

**Acceptance checks.**

- g = 3: the middle factor has genus 1 and Δ_1 = Δ_2, so monodromy groups must be computed exactly (AP Remark 2.6).
- For g ≤ 2 there is no such degeneration; the base cases use full curve moduli.

**Interface qualification.** The moduli of labelled stable hyperelliptic curves with clutching maps is not planned by any atlas stage; see the gap 'Moduli of labelled stable hyperelliptic curves and clutching'.

<a id="st5-overlapping-symplectic-subgroups-generate"></a>

### 5.148 Two overlapping symplectic block subgroups generate Sp(V)

Let F be a finite field of odd characteristic and V = V1 ⊕ V2 ⊕ V3 a nondegenerate symplectic F-space with the V_i pairwise orthogonal and all nonzero. If a subgroup H ≤ Sp(V) contains Sp(V1 ⊕ V2) × Sp(V3) and Sp(V1) × Sp(V2 ⊕ V3), then H = Sp(V).

**Hypotheses.** F finite, char F odd; V_i ≠ 0, pairwise orthogonal, V nondegenerate

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:Matrix.symplecticGroup`

**Sources.** [P/achter-monodromy-2007](#source-p-achter-monodromy-2007), Lemma 3.2(b)(i), p.12 (Achter–Pries author PDF). The generation lemma (the displayed hypotheses are read as the block subgroups acting trivially on the complementary summand).

**Proof route.**

1. Sp(V) over a field is generated by the symplectic transvections t_{v,a}(x) = x + a⟨x, v⟩v (v ∈ V, a ∈ F): classical input recorded as the gap 'Generation of Sp(V) by symplectic transvections'.
2. Transvections along vectors of V1 ⊕ V2 or of V2 ⊕ V3 lie in H by hypothesis (they are the transvections of those nondegenerate summands, extended by the identity).
3. For v = v1 + v2 + v3 with v1 + v2 ≠ 0: Sp(V1 ⊕ V2) acts transitively on nonzero vectors of V1 ⊕ V2 and V2 ≠ 0, so some h ∈ Sp(V1 ⊕ V2) ⊂ H sends v1 + v2 into V2; then h(v) ∈ V2 ⊕ V3, t_{h(v),a} ∈ H and t_{v,a} = h^{−1} t_{h(v),a} h ∈ H. If v1 + v2 = 0 then v ∈ V3.
4. Hence H contains all transvections and H = Sp(V). This elementary argument replaces Achter–Pries's appeal to the maximality of Sp(V1 ⊕ V2) × Sp(V3) in Sp(V) (Kleidman–Liebeck), which needs V1 ⊕ V2 and V3 of different dimensions.

**Acceptance checks.**

- dim V1 = dim V3 = 2, dim V2 = 2g − 4 is the case used for g ≥ 3.
- The hypothesis V2 ≠ 0 is used: for V = V1 ⊕ V3, the subgroup Sp(V1) × Sp(V3) contains both block subgroups and is proper.

<a id="st5-mod-l-hyperelliptic-monodromy-is-symplectic"></a>

### 5.149 Achter–Pries: the mod-ℓ monodromy of hyperelliptic curves is Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ)

Let ℓ be an odd prime and k an algebraically closed field in which 2ℓ is invertible. For every g ≥ 1 the mod-ℓ monodromy groups of the labelled hyperelliptic moduli space H̃_g ⊗ k and of the hyperelliptic moduli space H_g ⊗ k (tautological curves, ℓ-torsion of Pic⁰) are both Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ).

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd prime; k algebraically closed, char k ∤ 2ℓ; g ≥ 1

**Dependencies.** [Degeneration of labelled hyperelliptic moduli to the boundary Δ_{1,1}](#st5-hyperelliptic-boundary-degeneration) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/hyperelliptic-boundary-degeneration`); [Two overlapping symplectic block subgroups generate Sp(V)](#st5-overlapping-symplectic-subgroups-generate) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/overlapping-symplectic-subgroups-generate`); [The ℓ^k-torsion local system of the odd-degree hyperelliptic family](#st5-hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system`); `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0`

**Sources.** [P/achter-monodromy-2007](#source-p-achter-monodromy-2007), Theorem 3.4, p.13 (Achter–Pries author PDF). Statement. [P/achter-monodromy-2007](#source-p-achter-monodromy-2007), Proof of Theorem 3.4, p.13 (Achter–Pries author PDF). Base cases.

**Proof route.**

1. H_g ⊗ k is open dense in its closure, which is dominated by H̃_g ⊗ k, so it suffices to treat H̃_g (restriction to a dense open does not change the image: InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0).
2. Base cases g = 1, 2: every curve of genus g is hyperelliptic, so M_ℓ(H_g) = M_ℓ(M_g) = Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) (Deligne–Mumford 5.15–5.16; gap 'Full mod-ℓ monodromy of M_1 and M_2'); pass to H̃_g by Achter–Pries Lemma 3.3, since the Galois group Sym(2g + 2) of H̃_g → H_g and Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) have no common nontrivial quotient (PSp_{2g}(F_ℓ) simple except PSp_2(F_3) ≅ A_4). In the exceptional base case (g,ℓ)=(1,3), SL₂(F₃) has abelianization C₃ and its nontrivial proper quotients have a C₃ quotient, whereas S₄ has no C₃ quotient; this excludes a common nontrivial quotient as well.
3. Induction for g ≥ 3: by ST.5/hyperelliptic-boundary-degeneration the image contains Sp(V1) × Sp(V2 ⊕ V3) and Sp(V1 ⊕ V2) × Sp(V3) with dim V1 = dim V3 = 2 (induction hypothesis for genera 1 and g − 1).
4. Conclude by ST.5/overlapping-symplectic-subgroups-generate.

**Acceptance checks.**

- g = 1: Sp_2 = SL_2(F_ℓ).
- At ℓ=2 the labelled family has trivial action on its labelled Weierstrass-point 2-torsion. The unlabelled image is the permutation image of S_{2g+2}; it is the full symplectic group for g=1,2, but is proper for g≥3. Thus the odd-prime theorem cannot be extended unchanged.

<a id="st5-integral-lift-of-full-mod-l-symplectic-image"></a>

### 5.150 A closed subgroup of Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) with full mod-ℓ image is everything (outside (g, ℓ) = (1, 3))

Let ℓ be an odd prime, g ≥ 1 and H ≤ Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) a closed subgroup whose reduction mod ℓ is all of Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ). If g ≥ 2 or ℓ ≥ 5, then H = Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ). For (g, ℓ) = (1, 3) the conclusion needs the extra condition that H mod 9 meets the kernel of SL_2(Z/9) → SL_2(F_3) nontrivially; without it the implication fails: the order-24 subgroup of SL_2(Z/9) generated by [[0, 1], [8, 0]] and [[1, 7], [6, 7]] maps isomorphically onto SL_2(F_3), and its inverse image in SL_2(Z_3) is a proper closed subgroup (of index 27) with full mod-3 image.

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd prime, g ≥ 1; H closed in Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) (images of profinite groups are compact, hence closed); (g, ℓ) ≠ (1, 3), or the congruence-kernel condition at (1, 3)

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:Matrix.symplecticGroup`; `mathlib:PadicInt`; `mathlib:ZMod`

**Sources.** [P/vasiu-surjectivity-2003](#source-p-vasiu-surjectivity-2003), Main Theorem 1.3, p.2 (arXiv math/0209237v2). Statement (cases a, b used). [P/vasiu-surjectivity-2003](#source-p-vasiu-surjectivity-2003), Main Theorem 1.3(b), p.2 (arXiv math/0209237v2). The ℓ = 3 condition, vacuous for Sp_{2g}, g ≥ 2.

**Proof route.**

1. Sp_{2g} is simply connected, so Vasiu's Main Theorem 1.3 applies with c(G) = 1: case (a) ℓ ≥ 5; case (b) ℓ = 3, where the extra condition concerns only normal SL_2/PGL_2 factors, i.e. only g = 1.
2. The mechanism (Vasiu §§3.7.1, 4.1.2, 4.5, 4.7; Serre's lifting argument): H mod ℓ² surjects onto Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ); the extension 0 → sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) → Sp_{2g}(Z/ℓ²) → Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) → 1 does not split and the adjoint module is irreducible, so H mod ℓ² contains the whole congruence kernel; then powering lifts congruence kernels level by level and H = Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) by closedness. This proof is recorded as the gap 'Vasiu's surjectivity criterion for Sp_{2g}'.
3. The (1, 3) witness: check by finite computation that the two matrices generate a group of order 24 mapping bijectively to SL_2(F_3) (whose order is 24), so its preimage in SL_2(Z_3) misses the nontrivial level-2 congruence kernel.

**Acceptance checks.**

- The (1, 3) subgroup of index 27 is a closed proper subgroup with full mod-3 image.
- Achter–Pries Corollary 3.5 invokes 'a standard group theory argument' at all (g, ℓ), which is insufficient at (1, 3) (sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E667).

<a id="st5-integral-hyperelliptic-monodromy"></a>

### 5.151 The ℓ-adic monodromy of hyperelliptic curves is Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ)

Let ℓ be an odd prime and k algebraically closed with 2ℓ invertible. For g ≥ 2, or g = 1 and ℓ ≥ 5, the ℓ-adic monodromy groups of H̃_g ⊗ k and of H_g ⊗ k are Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ). The case (g, ℓ) = (1, 3) is not covered by this argument.

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd prime, char k ∤ 2ℓ; g ≥ 2, or g = 1 and ℓ ≥ 5

**Dependencies.** [Achter–Pries: the mod-ℓ monodromy of hyperelliptic curves is Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ)](#st5-mod-l-hyperelliptic-monodromy-is-symplectic) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/mod-l-hyperelliptic-monodromy-is-symplectic`); [A closed subgroup of Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) with full mod-ℓ image is everything (outside (g, ℓ) = (1, 3))](#st5-integral-lift-of-full-mod-l-symplectic-image) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/integral-lift-of-full-mod-l-symplectic-image`); [The ℓ^k-torsion local system of the odd-degree hyperelliptic family](#st5-hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system`)

**Sources.** [P/achter-monodromy-2007](#source-p-achter-monodromy-2007), Corollary 3.5 and proof, p.14 (Achter–Pries author PDF). The integral statement; range-qualified here.

**Proof route.**

1. The ℓ-adic image is a closed subgroup of Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) (compact image of a profinite group; the Weil pairing gives the upper bound: ST.5/hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system).
2. Its reduction mod ℓ is Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) by ST.5/mod-l-hyperelliptic-monodromy-is-symplectic.
3. Apply ST.5/integral-lift-of-full-mod-l-symplectic-image in the stated range.

**Acceptance checks.**

- g = 1, ℓ = 3 is exactly the excluded case (sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E667).
- The eventual-n statement needed by EVW uses only large g.

<a id="st5-monodromy-of-the-odd-degree-polynomial-family"></a>

### 5.152 Full symplectic monodromy for y² = ∏(x − a_i) over Conf_n

Let ℓ be odd, k algebraically closed with 2ℓ invertible and n = 2g + 1 ≥ 5 (or n = 3 with ℓ ≥ 5). The geometric ℓ-adic monodromy of the Jacobian of y² = ∏_{i=1}^n (x − a_i) over Conf_n(A¹_k) is Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ).

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd, char k ∤ 2ℓ; n = 2g + 1 ≥ 5, or n = 3 and ℓ ≥ 5

**Dependencies.** [The ℓ-adic monodromy of hyperelliptic curves is Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ)](#st5-integral-hyperelliptic-monodromy) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/integral-hyperelliptic-monodromy`); [The ℓ^k-torsion local system of the odd-degree hyperelliptic family](#st5-hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system`); `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0`; `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.780 (Annals 183). The big-monodromy input for the family, supplied via Achter–Pries.

**Proof route.**

1. The family over the ordered configuration space PConf_n is a torsor under the smooth connected group B_n of affine changes (a, b, d) with d² = a^n, and [PConf_n/B_n] ≅ H̃_g^{sm} keeps the hyperelliptic involution (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1; PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 items /128–/131).
2. A representable smooth surjection with geometrically connected fibres induces a surjection on étale π₁ (IG.0; EVW items /132); restriction from the compact-type locus to the smooth locus does not change the image (IG.0; item /133).
3. Hence the image over PConf_n equals that over H̃_g, which is Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) by ST.5/integral-hyperelliptic-monodromy; PConf_n → Conf_n is finite étale Galois with group S_n, and the image over Conf_n contains the image over PConf_n and is contained in Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ).

**Acceptance checks.**

- n = 3, ℓ = 3 is excluded (genus 1).
- The statement is geometric: over F_q the arithmetic image lies in GSp with multiplier q.

<a id="st5-finite-level-monodromy-of-the-polynomial-family"></a>

### 5.153 Finite-level monodromy of the polynomial family

In the range of ST.5/monodromy-of-the-odd-degree-polynomial-family, for every m ≥ 1 the geometric monodromy image on V_m = Jac[ℓ^m] is Sp_{2g}(Z/ℓ^m), and the arithmetic image over F_q contains elements of GSp_q(V_m) lying over Frobenius. Any element of GSp_q(V_m) lifts to GSp_q(T) (T the Tate module), by smoothness of GSp.

**Hypotheses.** as in ST.5/monodromy-of-the-odd-degree-polynomial-family; m ≥ 1; Frobenius on torsion points and Tate modules means arithmetic Frobenius, with cyclotomic multiplier q. The trace formula on compactly supported cohomology uses geometric Frobenius; these representations and conventions are not interchanged.

**Dependencies.** [Full symplectic monodromy for y² = ∏(x − a_i) over Conf_n](#st5-monodromy-of-the-odd-degree-polynomial-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/monodromy-of-the-odd-degree-polynomial-family`); [The ℓ^k-torsion local system of the odd-degree hyperelliptic family](#st5-hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system`)

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.780 (Annals 183). Passage between finite level and the Tate module.

**Proof route.**

1. V_m = T/ℓ^m T equivariantly; reduction Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) → Sp_{2g}(Z/ℓ^m) is surjective (Sp_{2g} is smooth over Z_ℓ, Hensel lifting).
2. Frobenius acts with multiplier q (ST.5/hyperelliptic-torsion-local-system); GSp_q(T) → GSp_q(V_m) is surjective by smoothness of GSp and of the multiplier fibre.

**Acceptance checks.**

- m = 1 recovers Achter–Pries' mod-ℓ statement.
- This does not identify the unmarked Hurwitz fibre with the marked set (see ST.5/geometric-generic-fibre-of-the-unmarked-hurwitz-cover).

<a id="st5-symplectic-similitude-group"></a>

### 5.154 Symplectic similitudes of a lattice with a perfect alternating pairing

Let R be a commutative ring and V a free R-module of rank 2g with a perfect alternating pairing ω (in matrix form, V = R^{2g} with ω(x, y) = xᵀJy, J the standard alternating matrix). The similitude group GSp(V) consists of the R-linear automorphisms h with ω(hx, hy) = m(h)·ω(x, y) for a unit m(h) ∈ R^×, the multiplier; m : GSp(V) → R^× is a homomorphism with kernel Sp(V). For a unit m, GSp_m(V) := m^{−1}(m) is a coset of Sp(V). In matrices: h ∈ GSp_m ⇔ h J hᵀ = m J. The multiplier homomorphism and the assertion that its fibres are labelled cosets require g≥1. The displayed matrix subsets and their union remain defined at g=0, when every multiplier gives the same singleton subset.

**Hypotheses.** R commutative (in the application Z_ℓ or Z/ℓ^k, ℓ odd); ω perfect and alternating

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:Matrix.symplecticGroup`; `mathlib:SymplecticGroup.mem_iff`; `mathlib:Matrix.J`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.779–780 (Annals 183). The definition used in Lemma 8.9.

**API.**

- `similitudeCoset` (constructor): GSp_m = {h : h J hᵀ = m J} for a unit m.
- `similitudeGroup` (constructor): GSp = ⋃_m GSp_m, a submonoid of matrices (a group on units).
- `mem_similitudeCoset_iff` (characterisation): h ∈ GSp_m ⇔ h J hᵀ = m J.
- `similitudeCoset_one` (compatibility): GSp_1 is the carrier of Mathlib's symplecticGroup.
- `similitudeCoset_mul_mem` (structure): GSp_m · GSp_{m'} ⊆ GSp_{m m'}.
- `similitudeCoset_map` (functoriality): A ring homomorphism R → R' maps GSp_m(R) into GSp_{φ(m)}(R').

**Checks.**

- `similitudeCoset.test_diag` (computation): Over Z_ℓ, the block matrix diag(I, q·I) lies in GSp_q for every unit q.
- `similitudeCoset.test_neg_one` (degenerate): −1 lies in GSp_1 = Sp.
- `similitudeCoset.test_nonunit_multiplier` (non-example): Over Z_ℓ with g = 1, diag(1, ℓ) satisfies h J hᵀ = ℓ J but is not in similitudeGroup, since ℓ is not a unit.

**Proof route.**

1. Define the multiplier coset {h : h J hᵀ = m J} and GSp as their union over units m; closure under products and inverses is a computation (multipliers multiply).
2. For g≥1 a standard entry of J is 1, so mJ=m′J implies m=m′; invertibility of an empty matrix alone would not prove uniqueness. The equations hJhᵀ=mJ and hᵀJh=mJ are equivalent because J⁻¹=−J and h is invertible. The multiplier-one subset recovers Mathlib symplecticGroup.

**Acceptance checks.**

- diag(I_g, q I_g) ∈ GSp_q.
- −I ∈ Sp.
- A matrix with multiplier ℓ over Z_ℓ is not a similitude: the multiplier must be a unit.

**Consumers.** EVW Lemma 8.9 (ST.5/unique-similitude-stable-symplectic-orbit) — Frobenius-fixed components correspond to Sp-orbits stable under some element of GSp_q; EVW Theorem 8.8 proof (ST.5/monodromy-orbits-and-rational-components) — arithmetic monodromy lies in GSp with Frobenius in GSp_q

<a id="st5-monodromy-orbits-and-rational-components"></a>

### 5.155 Components of X_n are symplectic orbits; rational ones are GSp_q-stable orbits

In the range of ST.5/monodromy-of-the-odd-degree-polynomial-family (A a nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group, ℓ odd, q odd with ℓ ∤ q, ℓ^m A = 0): the geometric connected components of X_n ⊗ F̄_q correspond bijectively to Sp(V_m)-orbits on Sur(V_m, A), and an orbit O gives a component defined over F_q iff the stabilizer in GSp(V_m) of some (equivalently every) x ∈ O meets GSp_q(V_m). Via T → V_m these are the Sp(T)-orbits on Sur(T, A) whose stabilizer meets GSp_q(T).

**Hypotheses.** as in ST.5/monodromy-of-the-odd-degree-polynomial-family and ST.5/geometric-generic-fibre-of-the-unmarked-hurwitz-cover; Frobenius on torsion points and Tate modules means arithmetic Frobenius, with cyclotomic multiplier q. The trace formula on compactly supported cohomology uses geometric Frobenius; these representations and conventions are not interchanged.

**Dependencies.** [The geometric generic fibre of X_n → Conf_n is Sur(V, A) modulo sign](#st5-geometric-generic-fibre-of-the-unmarked-hurwitz-cover) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/geometric-generic-fibre-of-the-unmarked-hurwitz-cover`); [Finite-level monodromy of the polynomial family](#st5-finite-level-monodromy-of-the-polynomial-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/finite-level-monodromy-of-the-polynomial-family`); [Symplectic similitudes of a lattice with a perfect alternating pairing](#st5-symplectic-similitude-group) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/symplectic-similitude-group`); `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0`; `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.780 (Annals 183). The orbit description.

**Proof route.**

1. Connected components of a finite étale cover of a geometrically connected base are orbits of the geometric fundamental group on the geometric generic fibre; a component is defined over F_q iff Frobenius preserves the orbit (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0, IG.1).
2. The fibre is Sur(V_m, A)/{±1} (ST.5/geometric-generic-fibre-of-the-unmarked-hurwitz-cover); since −I ∈ Sp, the orbit sets agree with those on Sur(V_m, A).
3. The geometric image is Sp(V_m) (ST.5/finite-level-monodromy-of-the-polynomial-family) and a Frobenius element lies in GSp_q(V_m); Frobenius fixes the orbit of x iff some element of Sp·F = GSp_q ∩ (image) fixes x, i.e. the stabilizer of x meets GSp_q.
4. Lift to T using surjectivity GSp_q(T) → GSp_q(V_m) and Sur(V_m, A) = Sur(T, A).

**Acceptance checks.**

- A = 0 has one orbit (the empty surjection set is replaced by the single trivial map).
- The equivalence 'some x' ⇔ 'every x' holds because stabilizers along an orbit are Sp-conjugate and Sp is normal in GSp.

<a id="st5-primary-decomposition-for-a-multiplier-q-similitude"></a>

### 5.156 Primary decomposition of a similitude with multiplier q

Let ℓ be odd, V free of rank 2g over Z_ℓ with a perfect alternating pairing, q ∈ Z_ℓ^× with q − 1 ∈ Z_ℓ^×, and h ∈ GSp_q(V). Let V_1 (resp. V_q) be the set of v ∈ V with (h − 1)^N v → 0 (resp. (h − q)^N v → 0) ℓ-adically, and W := ⋂_N (h − 1)^N (h − q)^N V. Then V = V_1 ⊕ V_q ⊕ W as Z_ℓ-modules, each summand is h-stable, h − 1 is invertible on V_q ⊕ W and h − q is invertible on V_1 ⊕ W.

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd prime; q and q − 1 units of Z_ℓ; h ∈ GSp_q(V)

**Dependencies.** [Symplectic similitudes of a lattice with a perfect alternating pairing](#st5-symplectic-similitude-group) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/symplectic-similitude-group`); `mathlib:PadicInt`; `mathlib:Module.End.maxGenEigenspace`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Lemma 8.9, p.781 (Annals 183). The decomposition (8.9.3).

**Proof route.**

1. Factor the characteristic polynomial of h mod ℓ into its (x − 1)-primary part, (x − q)-primary part and a coprime remainder (1 ≠ q in F_ℓ); lift the coprime factorisation by Hensel's lemma to Z_ℓ[x].
2. The corresponding idempotents in Z_ℓ[h] give an h-stable decomposition V = V_1 ⊕ V_q ⊕ W with the stated invertibility (a polynomial coprime mod ℓ to the char. poly. of h on a summand acts invertibly on it).
3. Identify the idempotent summands with the limit descriptions (EVW's definitions): on V_1, h − 1 is topologically nilpotent; on the complement it is invertible.

**Acceptance checks.**

- h = diag(I, q I): V_1 = V_−, V_q = V_+, W = 0.
- If q ≡ 1 mod ℓ the decomposition V_1 ⊕ V_q fails (the primary parts coincide mod ℓ); this is why q − 1 must be a unit.

<a id="st5-symplectic-normal-forms-over-z-l"></a>

### 5.157 Symplectic bases and Lagrangians over Z_ℓ

Let M be a finite free Z_ℓ-module with a perfect alternating pairing. (i) M has a symplectic basis; any basis x_1, …, x_g of a Lagrangian direct summand extends to one; hence Sp(M) acts transitively on Lagrangian direct summands. (ii) Each factor in an orthogonal direct-sum decomposition of M inherits a perfect pairing. (iii) M = M_+ ⊕ M_− with M_± Lagrangian. (iv) If M = P ⊕ Q with P, Q isotropic, both are Lagrangian (of rank half of M). (v) Every automorphism of a Lagrangian M_+ extends, by inverse transpose on a complementary Lagrangian M_−, to an element of Sp(M).

**Hypotheses.** ℓ prime (odd in the application); M finite free over Z_ℓ, pairing perfect and alternating

**Dependencies.** [Symplectic similitudes of a lattice with a perfect alternating pairing](#st5-symplectic-similitude-group) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/symplectic-similitude-group`); `mathlib:PadicInt`; `mathlib:Matrix.symplecticGroup`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Lemma 8.9, p.780–781 (Annals 183). Fact (i); facts (ii)–(iv) follow in the text. [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Lemma 8.9, p.782 (Annals 183). Fact (v).

**Proof route.**

1. (i) Given a basis x_i of a Lagrangian summand, choose y_j with ω(x_i, y_j) = δ_ij by perfectness, then correct y_j by combinations of the x_i to make ⟨y_i, y_j⟩ = 0 (EVW's argument); transitivity follows by mapping one symplectic basis to another.
2. (ii) Choose bases of the two orthogonal direct summands. The Gram matrix is block diagonal, and its determinant is a unit by perfectness. Each block determinant is therefore a unit in Z_ℓ, proving perfectness of both restricted pairings; absence of a radical alone would not suffice over Z_ℓ.
3. (iii) Take the spans of the two halves of a symplectic basis.
4. (iv) Reduce mod ℓ and use the field statement (isotropic subspaces have dimension at most half).
5. (v) With respect to a symplectic basis adapted to M_+ ⊕ M_−, the block matrix diag(a, (aᵀ)^{−1}) is symplectic.

**Acceptance checks.**

- M = Z_ℓ²: every primitive vector spans a Lagrangian.
- Over Z_ℓ the summand condition matters: ℓZ_ℓ·e₁ is isotropic but not a direct summand.

<a id="st5-orthogonality-and-a-killed-lagrangian"></a>

### 5.158 Isotropy of the primary parts and a Lagrangian in ker f

In ST.5/primary-decomposition-for-a-multiplier-q-similitude: V_1 and V_q are isotropic, V_1 ⊕ V_q is orthogonal to W, and W is nondegenerate; W = W_+ ⊕ W_− with W_± isotropic, and then W_+ ⊕ V_1 and W_− ⊕ V_q are complementary maximal isotropic (Lagrangian) direct summands of V. If f : V → A satisfies f ∘ h = f, then the Lagrangian W_− ⊕ V_q lies in the image of h − 1, hence in ker f.

**Hypotheses.** as in ST.5/primary-decomposition-for-a-multiplier-q-similitude; f : V → A a homomorphism with f ∘ h = f

**Dependencies.** [Primary decomposition of a similitude with multiplier q](#st5-primary-decomposition-for-a-multiplier-q-similitude) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/primary-decomposition-for-a-multiplier-q-similitude`); [Symplectic bases and Lagrangians over Z_ℓ](#st5-symplectic-normal-forms-over-z-l) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/symplectic-normal-forms-over-z-l`)

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Lemma 8.9, p.782 (Annals 183). The killed Lagrangian.

**Proof route.**

1. For x ∈ V_1 and y ∈ V_1 ⊕ W write y = (h − q)^N z_N; using ω(hx, hy) = q ω(x, y), ω(x, y) ∈ ω((h − 1)^N x, V) for all N, hence 0 (EVW's iteration). Symmetrically for V_q. More explicitly the adjoint of h−q is −q h⁻¹(h−1). Its N-th power puts the pairing in the ideal generated by the coordinates of (h−1)^N x; the integral factors q^N h⁻N preserve divisibility. Those coordinates tend to zero ℓ-adically, forcing the pairing to vanish.
2. W is nondegenerate as an orthogonal summand of a perfect pairing (EVW fact (ii)); decompose W into two isotropic summands (EVW fact (iii), a symplectic basis: ST.5/symplectic-normal-forms-over-z-l).
3. (V_1 ⊕ W_+) ⊕ (V_q ⊕ W_−) = V with both summands isotropic, so both are maximal isotropic (fact (iv)).
4. h − 1 is invertible on V_q ⊕ W, so V_q ⊕ W_− ⊆ im(h − 1); f ∘ (h − 1) = 0 gives V_q ⊕ W_− ⊆ ker f.

**Acceptance checks.**

- Let h be q on V_+ and 1 on V_−, and let f factor through projection to V_−. Then V_+=V_q is the killed Lagrangian.
- Without q − 1 invertible the conclusion fails for h = I.

<a id="st5-linear-group-transitive-on-lattice-surjections"></a>

### 5.159 GL_g(Z_ℓ) acts transitively on surjections Z_ℓ^g → A

Let A be a finite abelian ℓ-group generated by at most g elements. Then GL_g(Z_ℓ) acts transitively (by precomposition) on the set of surjective homomorphisms Z_ℓ^g → A.

**Hypotheses.** A finite abelian ℓ-group with dim_{F_ℓ}(A/ℓA) = k ≤ g

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:PadicInt`; `mathlib:Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), End of proof of Lemma 8.9, p.782 (Annals 183). Statement of the reduction. [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), End of proof of Lemma 8.9, p.782 (Annals 183). The index misprint i > g.

**Proof route.**

1. Fix x_1, …, x_k ∈ A whose classes form a basis of A/ℓA; by Nakayama they generate A.
2. For a surjection f, lift x_i to y_i ∈ Z_ℓ^g; the y_i are independent mod ℓ, so extend to a Z_ℓ-basis y_1, …, y_g, and replace y_i for k < i ≤ g by y_i − Σ_{j ≤ k} c_{ij} y_j so that f(y_i) = 0 (possible since the x_j generate A). (EVW print 'i > g' for 'k < i ≤ g': sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E664.)
3. Doing the same for f_2 gives a basis y'_i; the automorphism y_i ↦ y'_i carries f_1 to f_2.

**Acceptance checks.**

- A = 0: the unique map; transitivity is trivial.
- g < dim A/ℓA: there are no surjections.

<a id="st5-unique-similitude-stable-symplectic-orbit"></a>

### 5.160 EVW Lemma 8.9: a unique Sp-orbit of surjections fixed by a multiplier-q similitude

Let ℓ be odd, V a free Z_ℓ-module of rank 2g with a perfect alternating pairing, A a finite abelian ℓ-group and q ∈ Z_ℓ^× with q − 1 ∈ Z_ℓ^×. Let O be the set of surjections f : V → A such that f ∘ h = f for some h ∈ GSp_q(V). If g ≥ dim_{F_ℓ}(A/ℓA), then O is nonempty and Sp(V) acts transitively on O.

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd prime; q, q − 1 ∈ Z_ℓ^×; A finite abelian ℓ-group; g ≥ dim_{F_ℓ}(A/ℓA)

**Dependencies.** [Primary decomposition of a similitude with multiplier q](#st5-primary-decomposition-for-a-multiplier-q-similitude) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/primary-decomposition-for-a-multiplier-q-similitude`); [Isotropy of the primary parts and a Lagrangian in ker f](#st5-orthogonality-and-a-killed-lagrangian) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/orthogonality-and-a-killed-lagrangian`); [Symplectic bases and Lagrangians over Z_ℓ](#st5-symplectic-normal-forms-over-z-l) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/symplectic-normal-forms-over-z-l`); [GL_g(Z_ℓ) acts transitively on surjections Z_ℓ^g → A](#st5-linear-group-transitive-on-lattice-surjections) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/linear-group-transitive-on-lattice-surjections`); [Symplectic similitudes of a lattice with a perfect alternating pairing](#st5-symplectic-similitude-group) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/symplectic-similitude-group`)

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Lemma 8.9, p.780 (Annals 183). Hypotheses. [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Lemma 8.9, p.780 (Annals 183). Conclusion; the proof shows g ≥ dim A/ℓA suffices.

**Proof route.**

1. Nonempty: write V = V_+ ⊕ V_− with Lagrangians (ST.5/symplectic-normal-forms-over-z-l (iii)); h := q on V_+ and 1 on V_− lies in GSp_q; any surjection factoring through the projection to V_− (exists as rank V_− = g ≥ dim A/ℓA) is fixed by h.
2. Given f ∈ O with h, ker f contains a Lagrangian direct summand (ST.5/orthogonality-and-a-killed-lagrangian).
3. By transitivity on Lagrangians (normal forms (i)) move it to V_+, so f factors through V → V_−.
4. Automorphisms of V_− extend to Sp(V) (normal forms (v)), reducing to GL_g(Z_ℓ)-transitivity on surjections Z_ℓ^g → A (ST.5/linear-group-transitive-on-lattice-surjections).

**Acceptance checks.**

- A = 0: O = {0}.
- Without q−1 invertible the conclusion can fail even in the stated rank range: take q=1, g=2, V=Z_ℓ⁴ with coordinates (x₁,x₂,y₁,y₂), and A=F_ℓ². The surjections f₀=(x₁,x₂) and f₁=(x₁,y₁) are both fixed by I. Their dual images modulo ℓ have respectively zero and nondegenerate restricted alternating pairings, so they cannot be Sp-conjugate. Here g=dim(A/ℓA)=2.

<a id="st5-one-rational-geometric-component"></a>

### 5.161 Exactly one geometric component of X_n is defined over F_q

Let ℓ be odd, A a nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group and q an odd prime power with ℓ ∤ q(q − 1). For every odd n larger than a bound depending only on A (n ≥ 5 and g = (n − 1)/2 ≥ dim_{F_ℓ}(A/ℓA)), exactly one geometric connected component of X_n = Hn^{c_A}_{G_A,n} ⊗ F̄_q is fixed by Frobenius.

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd; A ≠ 0 finite abelian ℓ-group; q odd, ℓ ∤ q(q − 1); n odd with n ≥ 5 and (n − 1)/2 ≥ dim_{F_ℓ}(A/ℓA)

**Dependencies.** [Components of X_n are symplectic orbits; rational ones are GSp_q-stable orbits](#st5-monodromy-orbits-and-rational-components) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/monodromy-orbits-and-rational-components`); [EVW Lemma 8.9: a unique Sp-orbit of surjections fixed by a multiplier-q similitude](#st5-unique-similitude-stable-symplectic-orbit) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/unique-similitude-stable-symplectic-orbit`)

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proof of Theorem 8.8, p.780 (Annals 183). The claim.

**Proof route.**

1. By ST.5/monodromy-orbits-and-rational-components, Frobenius-fixed components correspond to Sp(T)-orbits of surjections T → A whose stabilizer meets GSp_q(T).
2. Since ℓ ∤ q(q − 1), q and q − 1 are units of Z_ℓ; ST.5/unique-similitude-stable-symplectic-orbit gives exactly one such orbit (nonempty and transitive).

**Acceptance checks.**

- q ≡ 1 mod ℓ: excluded; several orbits may be rational, giving a different limit.
- The bound on n depends only on A, not on q.

<a id="st5-uniform-function-field-surjection-moment-estimate"></a>

### 5.162 EVW Theorem 8.8: uniform moment estimate over F_q(t)

Let ℓ be an odd prime and A a finite abelian ℓ-group. There is a constant B(A) such that for every odd prime power q with ℓ ∤ q(q − 1) and √q > B(A), and every odd n > B(A), | (Σ_{L ∈ S_n} m_A(L))/|S_n| − 1 | ≤ B(A)/√q, where m_A(L) = |Sur(Cl(O_L), A)|. For A = 0 the left side is 0.

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd prime; A finite abelian ℓ-group (abelian is a standing hypothesis; sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E661); q odd prime power, ℓ ∤ q(q − 1) (domain as corrected: sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E663); n odd, n > B(A), √q > B(A)

**Dependencies.** [The moment sum is twice the number of Hurwitz points](#st5-factor-two-point-count-identity) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/factor-two-point-count-identity`); [Size of the odd-degree quadratic family](#st5-size-of-the-odd-degree-quadratic-family) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/size-of-the-odd-degree-quadratic-family`); [Uniform point-count error from a geometric Betti bound](#st5-uniform-trace-error-estimate) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/uniform-trace-error-estimate`); [Exactly one geometric component of X_n is defined over F_q](#st5-one-rational-geometric-component) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/one-rational-geometric-component`); [The generalized dihedral group A ⋊ Z/2 and its involution class](#st5-generalized-dihedral-cover-datum) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/generalized-dihedral-cover-datum`); [The empirical law of ℓ-primary class groups in S_n](#st5-empirical-l-primary-class-group-law) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/empirical-l-primary-class-group-law`); `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5`

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Theorem 8.8, p.777 (Annals 183). Statement of Theorem 8.8 (the displayed inequality (8.8.1) follows). [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Proposition 7.8, p.769 (Annals 183). The uniform Betti bound used as a stated input.

**Proof route.**

1. A = 0 is immediate (m_0 ≡ 1). Assume A ≠ 0 and let G = G_A, c = c_A (ST.5/generalized-dihedral-cover-datum), X_n = Hn^c_{G,n} ⊗ F_q.
2. By ST.5/factor-two-point-count-identity and ST.5/size-of-the-odd-degree-quadratic-family (n ≥ 3), the average equals |X_n(F_q)|/(q^n − q^{n−1}); so it suffices to bound |q^{−n}|X_n(F_q)| − 1| (then absorb the factor (1 − 1/q)^{−1}).
3. Stated input, not planned in ST.5 (gap 'EVW homological stability and uniform Betti bound'; owner: the accepted Part II InverseGaloisPartIIHurwitzHomologicalStability): EVW Proposition 7.8 — if (G, c) is nonsplitting, G centre-free and c a rational conjugacy class generating G, there is C(G, c) with dim H^i_ét(Hn^c_{G,n} ⊗ F̄_q, Q_λ) ≤ C(G, c)^{i+1} for all i, n and all q prime to |G|, for primes λ > max(|G|, q, n); it rests on EVW Theorem 6.1 (for (G, c) nonsplitting and k a field with |G| invertible there are A, B with U : H_p(Hur^c_{G,n}, k) → H_p(Hur^c_{G,n+deg U}, k) an isomorphism for n > Ap + B, also on the connected loci CHur) and Corollary 6.2 (the same for the quotients by G when G is centre-free).
4. Proposition 7.8 gives the Betti hypothesis of ST.5/uniform-trace-error-estimate with C = C(G_A, c_A) (EVW write C(A) = C(G, c)² to put the bound as C(A)^i), for a prime λ > max(|G|, q, n) chosen for each (q, n); the trace formula and the weight bound hold for every prime λ ∤ q, so this choice costs nothing.
5. For n larger than a bound depending only on A, exactly one geometric component of X_n is Frobenius-fixed (ST.5/one-rational-geometric-component).
6. Combine to get |q^{−n}|X_n(F_q)| − 1| ≤ 2C(A)/√q for √q ≥ 2C(A), and take B(A) = 2C(A) enlarged to cover the (1 − 1/q) factor and the degree threshold.

**Acceptance checks.**

- A = Z/3, q = 7 (ℓ = 3 divides q − 1 = 6): excluded; the method gives a different (Malle-type) answer there.
- Averages over ⊔_{m ≤ n} S_m follow from the same bound.

**Interface qualification.** The Hurwitz scheme Hn^c_{G,n} and its comparison properties are imported from IG.5; the Betti bound is a stated input recorded as a gap (owner: InverseGaloisPartIIHurwitzHomologicalStability).

<a id="st5-large-q-cohen-lenstra-theorem"></a>

### 5.163 EVW: the Cohen–Lenstra distribution over F_q(t) as q → ∞

Let ℓ be an odd prime and A a finite abelian ℓ-group. As q → ∞ through odd prime powers with ℓ ∤ q(q − 1), both the upper density δ^+(q, A) and the lower density δ^−(q, A) — taken over odd n → ∞ of the proportion of L ∈ S_n (imaginary quadratic extensions of F_q(t), ramified at ∞) with Cl(O_L)_ℓ ≅ A — converge to the Cohen–Lenstra mass μ(A) = ∏_{i≥1}(1 − ℓ^{−i})/|Aut A|. Precisely: for every ε > 0 there is Q such that |δ^±(q, A) − μ(A)| ≤ ε for all such q > Q.

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd prime; A finite abelian ℓ-group; q odd, ℓ ∤ q, ℓ ∤ q − 1 (the printed domain 'q ≢ 1 mod ℓ' also allows q even and q a power of ℓ, which the proof does not cover: sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E663)

**Dependencies.** [EVW Theorem 8.8: uniform moment estimate over F_q(t)](#st5-uniform-function-field-surjection-moment-estimate) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/uniform-function-field-surjection-moment-estimate`); [The empirical law of ℓ-primary class groups in S_n](#st5-empirical-l-primary-class-group-law) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/empirical-l-primary-class-group-law`); [Upper and lower densities along odd degrees](#st5-lower-and-upper-degree-densities) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/lower-and-upper-degree-densities`); [Finitely many approximate moments control finitely many masses (EVW Proposition 8.3)](#st5-finite-moment-control-of-masses) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/finite-moment-control-of-masses`); [The Cohen–Lenstra measure μ_{p,u}](#st5-cohen-lenstra-measure) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cohen-lenstra-measure`)

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Theorem 1.2, p.730 (Annals 183). Statement of Theorem 1.2 (domain corrected here). [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), Deduction after Theorem 8.8, p.777 (Annals 183). The deduction from Proposition 8.3 and Theorem 8.8.

**Proof route.**

1. Fix A₀ and ε > 0. Apply finite moment control (ST.5/finite-moment-control-of-masses, EVW Proposition 8.3) with the finite set {A₀}: it yields δ > 0 and a finite set L' of finite abelian ℓ-groups such that any probability measure ν with |⟨Sur(−, A)⟩_ν − 1| ≤ δ for all A ∈ L' satisfies |ν(A₀) − μ(A₀)| ≤ ε.
2. The measures ν_n (ST.5/empirical-l-primary-class-group-law) are probability measures whose A-moments are the averages of m_A over S_n.
3. By ST.5/uniform-function-field-surjection-moment-estimate, choose Q > max_{A ∈ L'} max(1, B(A), B(A)²) with B(A)/√Q < δ for all A ∈ L'; then for q > Q allowed and odd n > Q, |ν_n(A₀) − μ(A₀)| ≤ ε.
4. Hence every limit point of ν_n(A₀) along odd n lies in [μ(A₀) − ε, μ(A₀) + ε], i.e. δ^±(q, A₀) are within ε of μ(A₀) (ST.5/lower-and-upper-degree-densities). The quantifiers are in this order: finitely many moments first, then uniform thresholds in q and n.

**Acceptance checks.**

- ℓ = 3, A = 0: δ^±(q, 0) → ∏_{i≥1}(1 − 3^{−i}) ≈ 0.560, the limiting proportion of class numbers prime to 3 (EVW §1.1 calls 0.440 the indivisible proportion; it is the divisible one: sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E665).
- The theorem gives bounds at every sufficiently large allowed fixed q; equality of the upper and lower degree densities, or an exact Cohen–Lenstra law at that q, is not proved by this argument.
- q ≡ 1 mod ℓ is excluded; there the method gives a different limiting distribution.

<a id="st5-positive-proportions-of-l-divisible-and-indivisible-class-numbers"></a>

### 5.164 Positive proportions of class numbers divisible and not divisible by ℓ

Let ℓ be an odd prime. There is Q₀(ℓ) such that for every odd prime power q > Q₀(ℓ) with ℓ ∤ q(q − 1), the lower odd-degree density of the proportion of L ∈ S_n with ℓ ∤ |Cl(O_L)| is positive, and the lower odd-degree density of the proportion with ℓ | |Cl(O_L)| is positive. Quantitatively both lower densities tend to c_ℓ = ∏_{i≥1}(1 − ℓ^{−i}) > 0 and 1 − c_ℓ > 0 respectively as q → ∞.

**Hypotheses.** ℓ odd prime; q odd, ℓ ∤ q(q − 1), q > Q₀(ℓ)

**Dependencies.** [EVW: the Cohen–Lenstra distribution over F_q(t) as q → ∞](#st5-large-q-cohen-lenstra-theorem) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/large-q-cohen-lenstra-theorem`); [The Cohen–Lenstra measure μ_{p,u}](#st5-cohen-lenstra-measure) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cohen-lenstra-measure`)

**Sources.** [P/ellenberg-hurwitz-2016](#source-p-ellenberg-hurwitz-2016), §1.2 after Theorem 1.2, p.730 (Annals 183). The corollary.

**Proof route.**

1. ℓ ∤ |Cl(O_L)| iff Cl(O_L)_ℓ is trivial, so the first proportion is ν_n(0); the second is 1 − ν_n(0).
2. By ST.5/large-q-cohen-lenstra-theorem with A = 0, δ^−(q, 0) → μ(0) = c_ℓ and δ^+(q, 0) → c_ℓ; the lower density of 1 − ν_n(0) is 1 − δ^+(q, 0).
3. c_ℓ ∈ (0, 1) for ℓ odd (the infinite product converges and each factor lies in (0, 1)); choose Q₀ with |δ^±(q, 0) − c_ℓ| < min(c_ℓ, 1 − c_ℓ)/2.

**Acceptance checks.**

- ℓ = 3: c_3 ≈ 0.560, so asymptotically about 56% of class numbers are prime to 3 and 44% are divisible by 3 (the EVW §1.1 wording swaps these: sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E665).
- Positive lower proportions hold at each sufficiently large allowed fixed q. No exact fixed-q Cohen–Lenstra law or assertion for every q is claimed.

<a id="st5-eventual-degree-large-q-limit"></a>

### 5.165 The convergence mode 'fixed large degree, q → ∞'

For m ≥ 1 let A_m be the filter on N of prime powers q coprime to m, tending to infinity. For a function E(q, n) of a prime power q and a degree n, and a target c(n), say E has eventual-degree large-q limit c if there is n₀ such that for every fixed n ≥ n₀, E(q, n) → c(n) as q → ∞ along A_m. Wood (2019) uses this mode. EVW’s final distribution theorem instead takes upper/lower degree densities first and then q→∞; these are distinct convergence modes; it is not the fixed-q, large-degree limit of the direct function-field analogue of the number-field conjectures, and the two limits may not be interchanged without a new uniform estimate.

**Hypotheses.** m ≥ 1 (the moduli excluded from q); E : prime powers × N → R, c : N → R

**Dependencies.** `mathlib:Filter.Tendsto`; `mathlib:Filter.atTop`; `mathlib:tendsto_nhds_unique`

**Sources.** [P/wood-nonabelian-2019](#source-p-wood-nonabelian-2019), §1 after Theorem 1.2, p.3 (arXiv v2; Duke 168, p.380). The convergence mode, and its difference from the fixed-q limit.

**API.**

- `allowedPrimePowers` (constructor): The filter A_m of prime powers coprime to m tending to infinity.
- `allowedPrimePowers_neBot` (instance): A_m is a proper filter when m≠0; its Lean instance requires [NeZero m]. At m=0 it is bottom.
- `EventualDegreeLargeQLimit` (constructor): The predicate ∃ n₀, ∀ n ≥ n₀, E(·, n) → c(n) along A_m.
- `EventualDegreeLargeQLimit.unique` (extensionality): For m≠0, two targets of the same E agree for all sufficiently large n.
- `EventualDegreeLargeQLimit.mono` (relation): If m divides m′, the allowed filter for m′ refines that for m, preserving the limit. Numerical m≤m′ alone is insufficient.

**Checks.**

- `EventualDegreeLargeQLimit.test_const` (degenerate): E(q, n) = c(n) has eventual-degree large-q limit c.
- `EventualDegreeLargeQLimit.test_not_fixed_q` (non-example): For E(q, n) = n/(n + q) the eventual-degree large-q limit is 0, although for every fixed q ≥ 1, E(q, n) → 1 as n → ∞.
- `allowedPrimePowers.test_mem` (characterisation): The set of prime powers coprime to m belongs to A_m, and A_m ≤ atTop (every cofinite set of integers belongs to A_m).
- `allowedPrimePowers.test_zero` (non-example): A_0=⊥ because no prime power is coprime to zero. Consequently every function converges to every target along A_0; uniqueness and liminf consequences must require m≠0.

**Proof route.**

1. Define A_m := atTop ⊓ principal{q : q a prime power, gcd(q, m) = 1}; it is a proper filter (infinitely many primes are coprime to m).
2. Define the predicate ∃ n₀, ∀ n ≥ n₀, Tendsto (q ↦ E(q, n)) A_m (nhds c(n)).
3. Limits are unique along the proper filter A_m, so c(n) is determined for n ≥ n₀.

**Acceptance checks.**

- E(q, n) = n/(n + q): the eventual-degree large-q limit is 0 at every n, while for each fixed q, E(q, n) → 1 as n → ∞.
- Constant functions have their constant as limit.

**Consumers.** Wood 2019, Theorems 1.2 and 4.8 (ST.5/imaginary-normalized-nonabelian-moment, ST.5/real-normalized-nonabelian-moment) — the proved function-field moments are limits in this mode; Wood 2019 printed bad-type limit (ST.5/printed-bad-type-ordinary-limit-assertion) — the unproved assertion is an existence claim in this mode; EVW Theorem 1.2 (ST.5/large-q-cohen-lenstra-theorem) — the degree densities are taken first, then q → ∞; contrasted with this mode

<a id="st5-imaginary-per-component-unit-moment"></a>

### 5.166 Wood Theorem 4.8, imaginary good case: unit moment per component invariant

Let G be a finite group, G′ ≤ G ≀ S₂ admissible, good and centre-free, c the set of order-2 elements of G′ outside ker(G′ → S₂). For each prime power q coprime to |G′| choose a Frobenius-fixed component invariant f_q with f_q(u_q) = (x, 2n − 1), x ↦ (1, 1, σ) in G′. Then for n sufficiently large, the number of pairs (K, ρ) with K ∈ IQ_{=q^{2n}} and ρ ∈ Sur(G_K^{un,∞}, G) of type G′ and component invariant f_q, divided by #IQ_{=q^{2n}}, tends to 1 as q → ∞ with (q, |G′|) = 1. The invariant f_q may vary with q; n is fixed before q → ∞; it is a rigid average (no |Aut_{G′}(G)| factor).

**Hypotheses.** G′ admissible, good (c is one G′-class), Z(G′) = 1; q prime to |G′| (hence odd); n ≥ n₀(G′)

**Dependencies.** [Imaginary discriminant slices over F_q(t) are monic squarefree polynomials of odd degree](#st5-imaginary-exact-slice-parametrization) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/imaginary-exact-slice-parametrization`); [The convergence mode 'fixed large degree, q → ∞'](#st5-eventual-degree-large-q-limit) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/eventual-degree-large-q-limit`); `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4`; `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5`; [Rigid finite-height and exact-slice averages](#st0-wood-average-normalizations) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-average-normalizations`); [Marked global extensions and infinity conventions](#st0-wood-infinity-and-type-adapter) (`ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/wood-infinity-and-type-adapter`)

**Sources.** [P/wood-nonabelian-2019](#source-p-wood-nonabelian-2019), Theorem 4.8, p.22 (arXiv v2; Duke 168, p.406). The imaginary good case (the displayed limit equal to 1 follows). [P/wood-nonabelian-2019](#source-p-wood-nonabelian-2019), Proof of Theorem 4.8, p.24 (arXiv v2; Duke 168, p.408). Uniformity only in q at fixed n.

**Proof route.**

1. Proposition 4.4 (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4; PAPER-WOOD-19 /73, /75): pairs (K, ρ) of the given type correspond to marked (G′, c)-extensions of F_q(t) of imaginary infinity type, with Disc M = Disc K^{|G′|/2}, so discriminant norm q^{2n} ⇔ Σ n_i = 2n − 1.
2. Theorem 4.5(2)–(3) (IG.5; PAPER-WOOD-19 /79, /80): these marked extensions are the F_q-points of CHur^{c,(1,1,σ)}_{G′,2n−1}, and for n ≥ N₀ the points with component invariant f_q are those of one Frobenius-fixed geometric component C.
3. Theorem 4.7 (IG.5; PAPER-WOOD-19 /88): |#C(F_q) − q^{2n−1}| ≤ K_{2n−1} q^{2n−3/2} uniformly in q.
4. #IQ_{=q^{2n}} = q^{2n−1} − q^{2n−2} (ST.5/imaginary-exact-slice-parametrization); the ratio is 1 + O_n(q^{−1/2}).

**Acceptance checks.**

- G = C_3, G′ = C_3 ⋊ C_2 (the dihedral case): recovers the unit 3-moment of the imaginary Cohen–Lenstra heuristic in this mode.
- The limit is in the mode of ST.5/eventual-degree-large-q-limit.

**Interface qualification.** ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0 stands for Wood's type, admissible/good, IQ and component-invariant bookkeeping definitions routed to ST.0 (PAPER-WOOD-19 /2–/12).

<a id="st5-real-per-component-unit-moment"></a>

### 5.167 Wood Theorem 4.8, real good case: unit moment per component invariant

With G, G′, c as in ST.5/imaginary-per-component-unit-moment, for each q coprime to |G′| let f_q be a Frobenius-fixed component invariant with f_q(u_q) = (x, 2n), x ↦ 1 in G′. For n sufficiently large, the number of pairs (ρ, y) — ρ ∈ Sur(G_K^{un,∞}, G), y a twist for ρ, (ρ, y) of type G′ with component invariant f_q — summed over K ∈ RQ_{=q^{2n}} and divided by #RQ_{=q^{2n}}, tends to 1 as q → ∞ with (q, |G′|) = 1.

**Hypotheses.** as in ST.5/imaginary-per-component-unit-moment, with trivial infinity type
